The Duchess of Sussex last year wrote to her father last year telling him she knew about sex abuse claims against him and that she would never allow him to meet his grandchildren, it has been reported.

Meghan told Thomas Markle, 82, that it was the last time she would contact him in the letter, understood to have been sent while he was in hospital in the Philippines after having his leg amputated, sources close to her told the BBC.

Authorities in the Philippines are currently investigating allegations that Meghan’s estranged father kept a hoard of child sex abuse images at his former home there – claims he denies and has called a “bunch of lies”.

It is understood details of the letter sent by Meghan, first reported in the Sun on Sunday, included her telling him that he would never meet her children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, and and her insisting she would never contact her father again. She also reportedly told him that authorities were aware of the claims made against him.

The Metropolitan Police on Saturday confirmed it passed a letter featuring claims of alleged offending outside the UK by Thomas Markle Sr to Meghan and her husband Prince Harry, but in an astonishing admission, said it did not pass those claims on to other relevant law enforcement.

open image in gallery The Duchess of Sussex wrote a letter to her father last year saying she was cutting off contact over the claims ( Instagram )

The force said it received a letter in 2019 about a “number of claims” relating to Mr Markle, adding it was “reviewing the handling of this matter”, including whether it needs to be referred to the police watchdog over its conduct.

On Friday, Meghan revealed she was made aware of “disturbing allegations” about her father in 2018. She said she was shown a letter sent to Scotland Yard eight years ago making “troubling” allegations against Thomas Markle Sr and she was assured that these were being investigated.

A spokesperson for the Duchess of Sussex addressed the discrepancies in dates and said if police had a time-stamped record confirming the letter was reviewed in 2019, then that “should be treated as the accurate reference point for when it was received and shared with the Duchess”.

They said on Saturday afternoon that it was “understandable” because of the passage of time that Meghan “may have been mistaken by a few months”.

A Met Police spokesperson said on Saturday afternoon: “Following a thorough review of Met Police systems and records, we have confirmed that in January 2019, we received a letter containing a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom.

“It was sent to the MPS Protection Command to raise concerns in relation to the security of the Duchess of Sussex. The letter was reviewed and a decision was made that it should be passed to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness.

“The details of the allegations in the letter were not shared with other law enforcement agencies. The MPS is reviewing the handling of this matter in 2019 and considering whether a referral to the IOPC is necessary to review our approach.”

open image in gallery Thomas Markle has admitted paying for sex but denies claims he has a stash of child sex abuse images ( Instagram )

Mr Markle has admitted to paying for sex in the Philippines but has continued to deny allegations he had a hoard of child sex abuse images.

According to The Sun, Meghan’s half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, alleged that he found a stash of images belonging to their father at his former home in the Philippines.

He reportedly told police in the country that he discovered the child abuse pictures and videos mixed up with innocent family mementos. The newspaper said he also contacted FBI investigators in the US in July.

Authorities in the Philippines said they are investigating the allegations.

In an interview with the Mail on Sunday, Thomas Markle Sr said he has “never had sex with anyone under the age of 18”.

He told the paper that when he was single he travelled to the Philippines at least twice and “slept with prostitutes”.

“I like Asian women but that is not a crime,” he said.

“I am not well enough to go to the Philippines but I will speak to anyone who wants to talk to me. I have nothing to hide.”

Mr Markle is learning to walk again at a nursing facility in Florida after he had his leg amputated during life-saving surgery in 2025.

He said he would also welcome any forensic examination of his computer, telling the Mail on Sunday: “If there is anything bad on there, it was put there by someone else.”

Mr Markle’s eldest daughter Samantha Markle defended her father, telling the paper: “I believe this is a set-up.”

News.title: All 8 of Slovakia’s regional heads were reelected
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The heads of all eight of Slovakia's regions were reelected, according to results released Sunday.

Incumbents supported by populist Prime Minister Robert Fico's ruling coalition retained two regional leadership posts in the election on Saturday. The candidates of parliamentary pro-Western opposition retained four regions while independents kept the remaining two posts.

In a notable contest in the eastern Prešov region, the head of the opposition Christian Democrats, Milan Majerský, won with over 48% of the vote, beating a candidate nominated by the far right Republic party, who received 35%. The Republic is currently the third most popular party in Slovakia, according to polls.

A parliamentary election in Slovakia, a country of 5.4 million people and a European Union and NATO member, will take place next year.

In a separate election traditionally dominated by independent candidates, Matúš Vallo, representing the opposition, was reelected for the third time as mayor of the capital, Bratislava.

News.title: All of the new driving licence rules introduced in October – including key update for older drivers
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

New driving licence restrictions have come into effect, banning young people from carrying certain passengers at night and restricting when learner drivers can take a test.

The changes, which have been launched in Northern Ireland, are aimed at reducing fatal road crashes involving young people.

According to official figures, 17- to 23-year-old drivers were responsible for almost a quarter of all collisions in Northern Ireland in 2024. That is despite them only accounting for 8 per cent of licence holders.

Data also shows that 251 people were killed or seriously injured in collisions involving a young driver in 2024. In 65 per cent of cases, the young driver was at fault.

The changes come after the government announced in January that learner drivers in England and Wales could face a wait of six months between sitting their theory and practical tests.

Here are the changes that have been made to driving licences.

open image in gallery The photocard driving licence was introduced to the UK in 1998 ( PA )

What changes have been made in Northern Ireland?

Northern Ireland has become the first part of the UK to introduce new rules for new drivers.

Graduated driver licensing (GDL), for learner and newly qualified drivers, now applies to all new drivers, but the changes are aimed at those aged 17 to 23 years old.

Learners must spend at least six months getting driving experience before they can take a practical test, and those under 24 face restrictions on carrying young passengers at night.

The rule changes were announced in January 2026, and drivers who do not follow the restrictions could receive three penalty points or a fine of up to £1,000.

What proposals are being considered for drivers born after 2002?

As part of the Road Safety Strategy that was initially developed under Sir Keir Starmer's former government, drivers born after 2002 may face stricter measures.

Andy Burnham’s new government is weighing proposals to implement a "minimum learning period for learner drivers".

Learners, the majority of whom are in their late teens and early 20s, could have to wait six months between their theory test and practical driving test as part of the plans.

Drivers under the age of 25 represent 6 per cent of licence holders but were involved in 24 per cent of fatal and serious crashes in 2024, according to Government figures.

Ministers believe minimum learning periods could help to reduce such collisions by up to 32 per cent, based on evidence from other countries.

Currently, someone can start learning to drive from the age of 17 with lessons on the road.

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

What has been proposed for older drivers in their 70s?

Rather than take a whole new test, the proposal plans for drivers in their 70s to have their vision checked every three years to keep driving on UK roads.

This is also not a new policy announced by Mr Burnham but a policy which was first discussed in August 2025 during Sir Keir Starmer’s premiership, as part of a new road safety strategy.

The proposal went to consultation earlier this year between January and May.

What are the current rules for older drivers over 70?

Currently, drivers aged 70 and over must renew their licence every three years and self-declare that they can meet the eyesight standards required to drive. Drivers also must declare any listed medical conditions.

However, the new proposal means drivers will no longer be able to simply say that their eyesight is good – instead, there will be mandatory eyesight tests as part of the licence renewal process.

News.title: Amgen says 'breakthrough' drug improves lung cancer survival rate by 58 per cent
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Combining the Amgen drug Imdelltra with AstraZeneca’s immunotherapy Imfinzi reduces the risk of death by 58 per cent compared to using the Astra drug alone in patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, according to data presented at a major medical conference on Saturday.

Imfinzi is currently the standard of care following chemotherapy for patients suffering from the aggressive and hard-to-treat disease, whose cancer does not progress after initial treatment.

The study showed that patients given both therapies had a median survival of 21.1 months, compared with 12.7 months for those treated with Imfinzi on its own.

"If you give Imdelltra earlier and earlier, you get bigger clinical benefit," said Dr Paul Burton, chief medical officer at California-based Amgen.

The results are "unprecedented in advancing the treatment of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer", he said.

open image in gallery The drug combination drastically reduces the risk of death, Amgen says ( Reuters )

Imdelltra's US list price is about $30,000 per cycle, or over $390,000 a year (about £292,000).

Wall Street analysts have estimated annual sales reaching more than $2.5 billion (£1.87 billion) by 2030, according to LSEG data.

The Amgen drug is currently approved for adults in the advanced stages of small cell lung cancer that has worsened despite chemotherapy, based on data showing that Imdelltra reduced the risk of death by 40 per cent.

Full results of the 563-patient trial were presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting in Madrid and published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Amgen had previously announced that the Phase 3 study was successful.

Imdelltra belongs to a dual-target class of drugs called bispecific antibodies, which are designed to pull immune system T cells into contact with cancer cells to destroy them.

open image in gallery Most people with small-cell lung cancer are given radiotherapy and chemotherapy ( Getty/iStock )

Imfinzi is an older type of immunotherapy that essentially blocks the mechanism tumors use to hide from immune-system assault.

Most lung cancer cases are non-small cell, while up to 15 per cent are the small cell variety targeted by Imdelltra. About 250,000 new cases are diagnosed worldwide each year, according to the US National Institutes of Health.

Very few people diagnosed with small-cell lung cancer are candidates for surgery, and most are initially given radiotherapy and chemotherapy, Dr Burton said.

Survival rates depend on when the cancer is diagnosed, but the overall five-year rate is only around nine per cent, according to the American Cancer Society.

Amgen said that nearly 80 per cent of trial patients treated with the combination were alive after one year, compared with 53 per cent of those on Imfinzi alone, as patient follow-up continues.

Serious side effects, including low white blood cell counts, occurred in 20.9 per cent of patients on the dual therapy and 10.8 per cent with the single therapy. A potentially dangerous condition known as cytokine release syndrome, an aggressive inflammatory response, was reported in 49.6 per cent of patients who received Imdelltra. But only one case was serious and there were no CRS-related deaths.

Adverse events led to discontinuation of the combination therapy in 5.7 per cent of trial patients and 5.8 per cent of patients given only Imfinzi.

News.title: Antonelli takes another step closer to F1 title with US GP pole position
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas, just outside of Austin. This is one of the finest tracks that we have on the Formula One calendar and is a fitting place for the US Grand Prix. The races are usually entertaining, the drivers love the track (though have complained about the bumps this year) and it comfortably the best on-track action of the three races in the US.

What might we see this weekend? Well, Kimi Antonelli could be crowned world champion if results go his way. The way the results need to go make that fairly unlikely, but stranger things have happened in F1 and they often do. In any case, it would take a catastrophic implosion for Antonelli to lose the championship from here, so it is a case of when rather than if.

Who looks in good form? Well, Ferrari do. They have brought an updated car here this weekend it, so far, is paying off. Charles Leclerc had good pace yesterday and Lewis Hamilton, his team-mate, was fastest earlier today in final practice. Hamilton’s time of 1min34.893sec was a tenth or two quicker than the Red Bull of Max Verstappen, with Leclerc not too far behind. Then it was Antonelli, George Russell in the second Mercedes and Oscar Piastri making up the top six, though the Australian was nearly half a second off the ultimate pace of Hamilton.

Qualifying begins in about 50 minutes and we will be here with all the updates from that.

News.title: Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head
News.content:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

News.title: Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

News.title: Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa
News.content:
Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

News.title: ‘Tactical genius’ Emery outsmarts Maresca as City crash to first league defeat
News.content:
It was four years ago to the day that Emery grabbed this famous club by the shirt and collar and gave them an almighty shake. After a summer of much instability including many player sales, he appears to have already struck a formula with his newly assembled team.

There were a number of fine individual performances from many of the summer arrivals, such as Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi.

Emery said: “We were very motivated and Manchester City is the best team in the world so this is the level. This year we started so poorly and we needed time to understand how we improve. The players showed the capacity to retrieve the level we’ve had over the last few years.

“Nicolas is more mature and very demanding of himself to improve. Earlier this season he was shooting over the crossbar but he is now finding the corners. There is still work to do and 11 points is not enough but we are feeling better.”

Villa were fierce from the start and ahead after six minutes. Guéhi’s mistake was punished by John McGinn, with the ball dropping to Jackson who crashed a shot into the roof of the net.

The home team did require Suzuki to produce saves to stop efforts from Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov as City responded. Ndiaye also struck the outside of the post and City were level seven minutes into the second half with Erling Haaland nodding in Ndiaye’s cross at the far post. Haaland had touched the ball just eight times in the opening 45 minutes but invariably only needs one chance.

News.title: England hammer France to keep Rugby League World Cup hopes alive
News.content:
With Samoa beating Papua New Guinea 64-6 earlier on Saturday, England’s task was put into stark and imposing focus. The Pacific Islanders have a points difference of plus-132. Courtesy of this mauling, England’s is plus-64. So they must see off Papua New Guinea by a big number next Friday and then pray that Tonga defeat Samoa two days later. That is their only route through.

In truth, that is as much as McDermott could hope after their initial shortcomings, as they seek to avoid missing out on the last four for the first time in the World Cup’s 72-year history.

“What we’ve done today, given the context, is just enormous,” McDermott said. “We had to win big but, as any coach will tell you, nobody thinks like that. You think, ‘we’ve got to win’.

“We had some real good, candid conversations this week about what that actually means and we’ve been able to do that without getting distracted in chasing points.”

It should be remembered that this was only McDermott’s second game in charge and, even allowing for the poor opposition, they were dramatically improved.

“We’ve been together for five field sessions only,” he said. “We’re building something here and there was a little bit of that on show today.

“Certainly the six tries we scored in the last 17 minutes or so before half-time are what we’ve been chasing. We can see how good that’s going to be.

“If this group’s together for a process or a long build-up to a tournament, we could achieve some special things but, over a short space of time, it’s been remarkable really.”

It is incredible to think that England took 22 minutes to break the deadlock, when the ever-excellent Dom Young burst through. From there, they averaged a try every four or so minutes, with France looking increasingly forlorn and fatigued.

News.title: How an aid initiative maimed thousands of children in war-torn Africa
News.content:
Tormented by pain from severe internal burns, Amza Kebbie is one of thousands of children in Sierra Leone damaged for life by an aid intervention which went horribly wrong.

It has been five days since the four-year-old boy drank caustic soda, one of the two main ingredients for making soap, after mistaking it for drinking water. The highly corrosive liquid, also known as sodium hydroxide, has stripped the lining of his oesophagus and part of his stomach, causing life changing damage.

He’s now in intensive care, clinging precariously to life. An intravenous drip provides fluids and there’s a nasal cannula that enables him to breathe. Medics and relatives look over him around the clock.

If he can gather enough strength (which the nurses say is by no means guaranteed) the dangerously sick child will undergo a gastrostomy, an operation that will see a tube directly inserted into his stomach so that he can be fed long term.

Amza drank caustic soda while being looked after by a neighbour who was making soap at home Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

He can no longer swallow properly and may never be able to do so again, say his doctors.

This is not an isolated tragedy. Across Sierra Leone, there are thousands of children like Amza, and their number is growing every year.

At the Goderich Surgical Centre in the capital Freetown, around 200 children are admitted annually with caustic soda poisoning. Many more are thought to die in remote regions where emergency medical treatment is unavailable.

Behind the calamity is a humanitarian initiative that has spectacularly backfired. It’s a prime example of the law of unintended consequences; of a seemingly sensible and undoubtedly well meaning public health intervention doing more harm than good.

Fatmata Kamara accidentally drank caustic soda at her grandmother’s house in 2014 and has had a feeding tube ever since Credit : SImon Townsley

The story starts in the aftermath of Sierra Leone’s vicious civil war, which ran between 1991 and 2002.

Fought between the government and the Revolutionary United Front – backed by Liberian warlord Charles Taylor – the war claimed an estimated 50,000 to 70,000 lives, displaced 2.5 million people and left the country brutalised and in ruins.

In its aftermath, international aid agencies and NGOs desperately sought ways to revive the country and alighted on DIY soap making as a way of killing two birds with one stone.

Siblings Aminata Fofana and Salieu Bangura help out with the family soap-making business Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Organisations including UNHCR, UNICEF and World Vision thought the practice would both improve sanitation in the country’s disease-ridden shanty towns and provide home-bound women with the means to earn a sustainable income.

It seemed like an obvious “win-win”, and schemes to help women set up in the soap making business rapidly proliferated.

An annual report by the International Federation of the Red Cross, published in May 2002, promoted a micro-finance scheme to fund small-scale soapmaking.

Saieu Bangura, 13, with a tub of soap flakes Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

In 2005, the Centre for War Affected Women in Sierra Leone’s Kono district, backed by the UNHCR, listed soap making as one of the main training courses for war widows and female amputees.

And at about the same time, the Freetown-based Safer Future Youth Development Programme, supported by UNICEF and the charity War Child, provided “a tool kit for soap production” at its training workshops.

As recently as 2020, Action Aid ran a promotional article on its Sierra Leone website showing how soap making had enabled women to become financially independent of their husbands.

The article ran under the headline: “With Soap Making Skills – I'm Empowered!”

Mabinty Bangura is taken to theatre for an endoscopy Credit : Simon Townsley

It is for good reason that the ancient Greek physician Hippocrates urged doctors “first, do no harm”.

To follow the rule literally is not possible as all health interventions entail some risk but it's a reminder never to underestimate the capacity of a new intervention to backfire.

There are plenty of examples from history to choose from.

During the British Raj in India, the government offered a cash bounty for every dead cobra as a way of reducing the danger of venomous snakes.

The surgical team examine the internal damage via an endoscopy Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

But rather than leading to a decline in snake numbers, the plan resulted in entrepreneurial individuals breeding cobras just so they could kill them and then claim the reward.

Once officials realised what was happening and the scheme was stopped, thousands of the then worthless cobras were released into the wild, greatly increasing the risk of snakebite.

In the late 1950s, the Chinese Communist regime introduced an equally calamitous public health campaign involving sparrows.

They issued a directive ordering the birds to be destroyed because they were thought to spread disease and destroy crops.

A child’s gastrostomy scar with a feeding tube in place Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

What those behind the idea failed to consider was that sparrows are natural predators. As their numbers declined, the locust population exploded, decimating agriculture and contributing to the Great Chinese Famine in which millions died.

So what went wrong in Sierra Leone? What did those behind the soap making scheme fail to foresee?

Experts say the initiative simply failed to consider the danger inherent in encouraging people to use toxic chemicals in their homes.

The brightly coloured buckets in which caustic soda is made, and then mixed with oil and scent to make soap, are the same buckets used across the country to fetch and hold drinking water. And just like drinking water, the lethal solution is cool, clear and inviting.

Just a drop is enough to cause the most horrific burns. So when a thirsty young child like Amza runs in from play and mistakenly scoops up a cup of it to quench their thirst they will lose their oesophagus, if not their lives.

Giuseppe Meucci, chief surgeon at the Goderich Surgical Centre Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Giuseppe Meucci, chief surgeon at the 56-bed Goderich hospital in Freetown where four year old Amza is being cared for, has been treating patients burned by sodium hydroxide nearly every day since arriving in Freetown in 2019.

Three quarters of patients seen by the hospital’s specialist programme for oesophageal burns, set up in response to the crisis and run by the Italian medical charity Emergency, are under five.

“It’s a struggle in this country,” says Dr Meucci. “Almost every family knows someone who has suffered because of this problem. But they just keep coming.”

Hospital director Jasna Sundic Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

“In most countries you remove the source of danger for the child, but here that doesn’t seem to happen,” he says.

“It’s one of the main health problems of this country. Soda is there with malaria, malnutrition and typhoid complications. It’s one of the reasons why so many children die before they reach five years old.”

Hospital director Jasna Sundic agrees.

“This is a very severe issue but one which is very preventable,” she tells the Telegraph. “[But] however much we do here, we have not been able to decrease the overall number of soda patients being admitted.

“We cannot stop mothers who have no other source of income except making soap.”

Ibrahim Kerah is fed by his father Mohamed Credit : SImon Townsley

In a handful of rare cases, burns victims are sent abroad for complex oesophageal reconstruction surgery but this is not an option for the vast majority of children injured in Sierra Leone.

More than 60 per cent require surgery, but for these children, like Amza, a feeding tube that bypasses the oesophagus is the only option.

The hospital has many of these gastrostomy patients.

Critically underweight Mabinty Bangura Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

In a ward dedicated to soda burns, four-year-old Ibrahim Kerah is being fed through his stomach tube by his father Mohamed.

The Telegraph watches as Mohamed carefully prepares his son’s meal, adding spinach leaves to the porridge-like mix which is fed into a syringe at the end of the tube.

At an adjoining bed two-year-old Mabinty Bangura is critically underweight after ingesting soda about six months ago. Nurses have put her on a high protein drip so she can regain enough strength to undergo the same bypass surgery.

In the courtyard outside, mothers whose children have just had a gastrostomy are being taught how to prepare the liquid food.

Ibrahim and his father Mohamed endured a 10-hour motorbike journey to attend his hospital check-up Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

A small proportion of the patients needing treatment following caustic soda burns are adults.

Mothers are taught how to prepare liquid food; Junisa Bundeh shows his feeding tube Credit : SImon Townsley

In the muddy lanes of Freetown’s Waterloo district there are makeshift soap making operations all over.

The coloured plastic buckets full of either soda or water are everywhere.

Against the backdrop of the rainy season’s persistent gloom, the containers symbolise a measure of cleanliness for families sheltering from torrential downpours under mouldy concrete awnings.

As the Telegraph watches Yabom Kapro, a village elder, making soap, the risks involved are immediately obvious.

Chief Yabom Kapro makes soap at her Waterloo town home, near Freetown Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

As she tips a purple bucket of caustic soda solution into a large basin and then adds palm oil from a plastic jerrycan, local children hover round the cluster of colourful containers.

Once set, the beige-coloured cake of soap is cut into blocks which are then grated on a wire mesh contraption to be sold at the local market.

“When you dilute the caustic soda, it is completely clear like water at first,” says another soap maker, 43-year-old Cilina Bangura.

“Afterwards a white scum forms on the top, but you cannot be watching all of the time, [even] with all of these children around.”

Cilina knows the risks but says she can't afford to stop making soap. It has, as the NGOs intended, become an economic lifeline for her and her family.

“I want my children to continue making soap when I stop working,” she says. “I took out a loan to buy everything I needed, and now it is the only way I can make a living.

“Of course, I know how dangerous soda is – it has burned my skin many times – but I don’t have another option.”

Home-made soap, in Waterloo Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

Maimunatu Sankoh, three, whose family lives in a nearby tin-roof shack, is sadly too well aware of that danger from her own bitter experience of soda poisoning.

As she feeds her daughter through a stomach tube, Maimunatu’s mum Iyesatu complains: “I have never seen any public information about soda.

“There are warnings on the packets but that is no use once the product is dissolved in water. They need to tell people to keep buckets out of the way.”

Iyesatu Kamara feeds her daughter Maimunatu Sankoh at their home Credit : SImon Townsley

Incidents of children consuming harmful chemicals are not confined to developing countries and were once common in the west.

In the US, the Poison Prevention Packaging Act was introduced in 1970, mandating childproof containers and the labelling of harmful household products.

The UK followed suit in 1975 with the introduction of child-resistant safety caps on containers of caustic soda and most other noxious household substances.

Despite the risks, Cilina says she can't afford to stop making soap Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Such legislation is still a long way off in Sierra Leone and is anyway far too late for four-year-old Amza.

Under heavy sedation in the intensive care unit, his glazed eyes open only occasionally.

The only visible evidence of his injuries is some scarring on his lips, but the doctors say his throat, oesophagus and stomach have all been seared by several large gulps of soda.

The boy’s mother, Mamie Kebbie, 30, keeps a watchful vigil, stroking his listless head tenderly. She says he used to be a playful and vivacious child.

If they are taken to hospital quickly, children with soda burns are normally given an oesophageal dilation endoscopy – a procedure which aims to keep the oesophagus open – but for Amza this has not been possible.

Freetown, Sierra Leone Credit : Simon Townsley

“This is a very severe case,” explains nurse Annette Turay, who heads the hospital’s intensive care unit. “When he was brought in, about 10 hours after he had ingested the soda, we were unable to conduct an endoscopy because he already had respiratory problems.

“He has pneumonia and he cannot feed through his mouth. He cannot even swallow his own saliva.

Mamie Kebbie keeps a vigil at her son's bedside Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

“It will be a week before he is strong enough for us to be able to operate. We will insert a gastric tube into his stomach. He will have to keep this as his main way of being fed for a long time, potentially forever.”

But nurse Turay has seen worse.

“I have seen so many children suffering a lot after ingesting soda, so many dying too.

“A few weeks ago, we had a child in the ward who died because his stomach was completely gone”.

The Telegraph contacted all the NGOs involved in the setting up of and promotion of soap making schemes in Sierra Leone that are mentioned in this story for comment.

News.title: How an aid initiative maimed thousands of children in war-torn Africa
News.content:
Tormented by pain from severe internal burns, Amza Kebbie is one of thousands of children in Sierra Leone damaged for life by an aid intervention which went horribly wrong.

It has been five days since the four-year-old boy drank caustic soda, one of the two main ingredients for making soap, after mistaking it for drinking water. The highly corrosive liquid, also known as sodium hydroxide, has stripped the lining of his oesophagus and part of his stomach, causing life changing damage.

He’s now in intensive care, clinging precariously to life. An intravenous drip provides fluids and there’s a nasal cannula that enables him to breathe. Medics and relatives look over him around the clock.

If he can gather enough strength (which the nurses say is by no means guaranteed) the dangerously sick child will undergo a gastrostomy, an operation that will see a tube directly inserted into his stomach so that he can be fed long term.

Amza drank caustic soda while being looked after by a neighbour who was making soap at home Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

He can no longer swallow properly and may never be able to do so again, say his doctors.

This is not an isolated tragedy. Across Sierra Leone, there are thousands of children like Amza, and their number is growing every year.

At the Goderich Surgical Centre in the capital Freetown, around 200 children are admitted annually with caustic soda poisoning. Many more are thought to die in remote regions where emergency medical treatment is unavailable.

Behind the calamity is a humanitarian initiative that has spectacularly backfired. It’s a prime example of the law of unintended consequences; of a seemingly sensible and undoubtedly well meaning public health intervention doing more harm than good.

Fatmata Kamara accidentally drank caustic soda at her grandmother’s house in 2014 and has had a feeding tube ever since Credit : SImon Townsley

The story starts in the aftermath of Sierra Leone’s vicious civil war, which ran between 1991 and 2002.

Fought between the government and the Revolutionary United Front – backed by Liberian warlord Charles Taylor – the war claimed an estimated 50,000 to 70,000 lives, displaced 2.5 million people and left the country brutalised and in ruins.

In its aftermath, international aid agencies and NGOs desperately sought ways to revive the country and alighted on DIY soap making as a way of killing two birds with one stone.

As recently as 2020, Action Aid ran a promotional article on its Sierra Leone website showing how soap making had enabled women to become financially independent of their husbands.

The article ran under the headline: “With Soap Making Skills – I'm Empowered!”

It is for good reason that the ancient Greek physician Hippocrates urged doctors “first, do no harm”.

To follow the rule literally is not possible as all health interventions entail some risk but it's a reminder never to underestimate the capacity of a new intervention to backfire.

There are plenty of examples from history to choose from.

During the British Raj in India, the government offered a cash bounty for every dead cobra as a way of reducing the danger of venomous snakes.

Once officials realised what was happening and the scheme was stopped, thousands of the then worthless cobras were released into the wild, greatly increasing the risk of snakebite.

In the late 1950s, the Chinese Communist regime introduced an equally calamitous public health campaign involving sparrows.

They issued a directive ordering the birds to be destroyed because they were thought to spread disease and destroy crops.

A child’s gastrostomy scar with a feeding tube in place Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

What those behind the idea failed to consider was that sparrows are natural predators. As their numbers declined, the locust population exploded, decimating agriculture and contributing to the Great Chinese Famine in which millions died.

So what went wrong in Sierra Leone? What did those behind the soap making scheme fail to foresee?

Experts say the initiative simply failed to consider the danger inherent in encouraging people to use toxic chemicals in their homes.

The brightly coloured buckets in which caustic soda is made, and then mixed with oil and scent to make soap, are the same buckets used across the country to fetch and hold drinking water. And just like drinking water, the lethal solution is cool, clear and inviting.

Just a drop is enough to cause the most horrific burns. So when a thirsty young child like Amza runs in from play and mistakenly scoops up a cup of it to quench their thirst they will lose their oesophagus, if not their lives.

Sports.title: Premier League star opens up on how booze started to take over his life and reveals what has got him back on track
Sports.content:
Next

FABIO CARVALHO claims he quit booze for Jesus – and that reading the Bible saved his career.

The Portugal midfielder spent an unsuccessful spell at Liverpool before switching to Brentford in August 2024, during which he partied at nightclubs and drank too much on Merseyside.



His situation grew worse as his playing time was limited and he was in danger of wrecking his chances of continuing as a professional footballer at the top level.

Carvalho, 24, went to church as a kid but was not as committed as he could have been.



But towards the end of his time at Anfield he found solace in religion.

He said: “I started to go out. I started to drink; I was doing crazy stuff off the pitch.



“I would come home from the clubs and start crying my eyes out. I just felt empty.

“Then I picked up my Bible. That’s not to say I changed instantly but I just knew there was an emptiness in my heart that only Jesus could fill.”

Carvalho, who posted a video of his baptism in January 2025, is part of a close-knit group of players at Brentford.

The trio of Carvalho, Brazilian striker Igor Thiago and Englishman Josh Dasilva turn to scripture during difficult moments, and all three listen to gospel or worship music.



He added: “It’s good to be able to fellowship and carry each other’s burdens. It just makes life easier.”

Boss Keith Andrews is the least surprised of anyone that Brentford went into this weekend in a European spot.

The Bees face Hull today and Andrews said: “Some fans, particularly those of a certain age, have been Brentford supporters for such a long time.



“So it’s nice for them to enjoy these times, competing against some of the biggest clubs in the world.

“We’re able to embrace the challenge on a weekly basis, and we’re constantly growing.

“I don’t find it hard to believe because I feel it most days. I really enjoy it.”

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard tipped for new manager’s role with Liverpool legend ‘missing’ football – ‘we need people like him’
Sports.content:
Next

STEVEN GERRARD has been tipped for a return to management as he is “missing” football.

The Liverpool legend has been out of the dugout since leaving Saudi side Al-Ettifaq in January 2025.



Gerrard, 46, had previously managed Aston Villa in the Premier League and Rangers in Scotland.

He had different levels of success as he landed the Scottish Premiership title in 2021 but failed to improve Villa.



The Burnley job has now opened up after Nicky Hayen was sacked following the 4-1 defeat at Lincoln City.

The result has left the Clarets 22nd in the Championship with the target of an immediate return to the Prem looking more difficult by the week.

Djibril Cisse has claimed that his former Liverpool captain getting the job would be “good for football”.

Speaking with Mr Gamble: “I’d love that, for two reasons.

‘He’s a friend, someone I like and respect a lot, and he loves football. He needs to be on the pitch, in contact with players.

“I hope he finds a project that suits him because he misses it. As a player he already had a coach’s mind.

Sports.content:

CHELSEA boss Xabi Alonso was bemused by claims Joao Pedro’s injury was leaked – by fantasy football.

There were claims online that family members of some Blues stars removed Pedro from their teams for the Premier League’s official fantasy game.



And some believe it gave Spurs an advantage in preparing for the clash at Stamford Bridge which Roberto De Zerbi’s team won 2-0.

Chelsea boss Alonso was asked whether he was annoyed about Pedro’s injury becoming public knowledge in such a way.



The Blues manager said: “I am not into the fantasy team thing so I didn’t know that.”

But Alonso is sure to be furious if he finds out any of his players shared the Pedro news to friends or family, who then made it public by changing their FPL teams.



The Spaniard has been trying to crack down on the dressing room leaks which have sometimes dogged Chelsea.

Last season there was even the suggestion a Blues player had told his barber about Cole Palmer and Pedro being unavailable for a match, with the scissor-wielder then passing on the news to others.

It was a truly miserable evening in the rain for Alonso and the thousands of Chelsea fans packed inside the Bridge.

Goalkeeper Mike Penders handed Tottenham an historic win on his first Premier League start.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And Palmer earned the first red card of his career before Mathys Tel ensured Spurs would emerge triumphant from a small-scale re-enactment of the Battle of the Bridge.

Nothing will ever make up for the 2-2 draw here which ended Tottenham’s title hopes in 2016.

But Penders’ own goal with 12 minutes left set Roberto De Zerbi’s side on the way to achieving a rare distinction in this London derby.

Elliott, 23, was shipped out on loan to Valencia on transfer deadline day as he didn’t figure into the Reds’ new manager Andoni Iraola‘s plans.

The ex-England youth international’s fortunes haven’t really improved at Valencia as he has only managed a total of 152 minutes in all of his six appearances for the club.



And Elliott’s misfortunes extended during the Derbi de la Comunitat with rivals Villarreal at the Mestalla Stadium.

The score was 1-1 as Villarreal’s Alex Freeman cancelled out Pepelu’s opener for the hosts.

And Javier Aguirre’s side soon picked up an advantage as the visitors lost Pape Gueye to a red card.

However, Elliott was booked in the 89th minute for seemingly committing a tactical foul on Georges Mikautadze, who tried to play the ball after the Yellow Submarine earned a foul.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick baffled by fascination with Man Utd’s running stats as boss insists he trusts players ‘100 per cent’
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED are one of the worst running sides in the Premier League.

But do not mention the word “pressing” to under-fire boss Michael Carrick.



Fitness has been a recurring issue at Old Trafford since David Moyes told the players at one of his first-team meetings he would “make them run more”.

Carrick was in the dressing room when Moyes outlined his blueprint in July 2013 and took exception to it.



United players — like former midfielder Carrick — felt their tendency to end games strongly was down to LIMITING their workload in the first hour.

However, a string of bosses post-Sir Alex Ferguson have wanted their sides to run more.



Ole Gunnar Solskjaer wanted his United players to be the “hardest-working”.

Jose Mourinho praised Marcus Rashford in December 2018 for running like a “mad dog”.

And six years later, Ruben Amorim urged his Old Trafford stars to “run like mad dogs”.

Ralf Rangnick attempted to incorporate ‘gegenpressing’ into United’s style but gave up after two Premier League games in December 2021.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Erik ten Hag inflicted a punishing 13km run on his stars in training after Brentford outran them by the same distance in a 4-0 thrashing in August 2022. This term United players have covered 487.4 miles across their seven Prem games.

Only Liverpool (482.5) have run fewer miles but Andoni Iraola’s men are fifth while United are 15th.

Carrick’s men have been outrun by every opponent this season except one — Manchester City in the 1-0 defeat at Old Trafford.

And Enzo Maresca’s side played with ten men from the 23rd minute after Phil Foden’s red card.

Carrick, whose struggling team host Bournemouth today, is clinging to his job, with Brighton’s Fabian Hurzeler considered the standout Prem coach to replace him although Eddie Howe remains favourite with the bookies.



The 48-year-old has been without a club since leaving Newcastle in the summer.

Hurzeler’s high-flying Seagulls went viral last month for a pressing sequence in their 3-0 dismantling of champions Arsenal.

Little wonder Carrick has downplayed the concept of pressing.

The former Middlesbrough boss said: “I think you’ve got to be careful with saying ‘not running’.



“We’ve won a lot of games over a period of time.

“And this pressing thing that suddenly everyone thinks about pressing . . . pressing is one small part of football.

“There’s all sorts of different ways of what people class as a press. What actually is it?

“What are you doing it for? Is it to your strength? Is it covering up other spaces?



“You don’t necessarily need to press to win games of football.

“Sometimes you do, sometimes you don’t. It’s just a word that gets thrown about. We’ve got to be a bit careful with that. It’s not necessarily just running stats that define football games, either.”

Despite United’s horror start putting him in grave danger of the sack, Carrick said: “I trust them 100 per cent. I definitely trust the players.

“It wasn’t a good night in Como for many reasons, we all know that.



“We will be a different team on Sunday. We have to be a different team.”

Captain Bruno Fernandes questioned Carrick’s tactics when the Champions League capitulation to Como left them winless in seven games.

It came days after Lisandro Martinez was fined for an astonishing blast at director of football Jason Wilcox.

Old Trafford boss Carrick has refused to rule out dropping Fernandes for this afternoon’s Prem visit of Bournemouth.



Changes are inevitable after Wednesday night’s debacle.

Carrick bickered with forward Matheus Cunha in the first half of United’s 4-1 thrashing before hooking him at half-time.

Fernandes has played in four different positions in as many games and was taken off in Italy.

Carrick’s emotional address on Friday lasted almost six minutes before he took questions in a press conference that ran to almost 20 minutes.

The gaffer explained he wants United’s history to provide inspiration.



He stressed: “I fully understand the situation and my position and I know what this club means to so many people.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The history doesn’t give you the right to keep winning. Teams that win earn the right to win, so it’s important we draw inspiration from the past.

“But our responsibility is to carry that forward and it’s so important to me that we do that.”

Sports.title: 'Dream come true!' - Britain's Palmowski becomes 2026 F1 Academy champion
Sports.content:
Britain's Alisha Palmowski became the 2026 F1 Academy champion with three races to spare after building an unassailable lead in Austin.

Palmowski followed up victory in Friday's Opening Race at the Circuit of the Americas with second in the Reverse Grid Race behind Alba Larsen to take a 70-point lead over her closest championship challenger, Emma Felbermayr, with only a maximum of 67 points remaining.

The Red Bull-backed driver has dominated this season by winning five of the 11 races so far with six pole positions to become the second Briton after Abbi Pulling in 2024 to win the F1 Academy title.

Palmowski, 20, is the youngest F1 Academy champion and praised the team and her family, who were in attendance in Austin.

"We did it guys! It's incredible. I don't know what to say. I'm trying not to cry!" she said.

"There's so much hard work gone on behind the scenes, not just from myself, but all the people you won't see. They have lived it day and night.

"We have worked so hard as a team, Campos Racing and Red Bull Racing. We have left no stone unturned. I don't want to name names but my engineer Diego has lived this with me every day and night."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the second F1 Academy race at the 2026 United States Grand Prix

Palmowski has won the title in her second full campaign after an impressive rookie season where she won the 2025 season-opener and took another four podiums.

She has been backed by Red Bull since the start of last year after finishing as runner-up in the 2024 GB4 Championship.

"I've learned so much in the last 18 months to two years being with Red Bull," she said.

"I learned about things I didn't know. I've developed so much, not only as a driver but a person as well. I've matured so much in the last 12 months. It's a dream come true."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Alisha Palmowski get the biggest winning margin in F1 Academy history in Canada earlier this year, and then broke it again a few races later!

What next for Palmowski?

Previous F1 Academy champions Marta Garcia, Pulling and Doriane Pin have gone on to race in other motorsport categories in endurance racing and Formula Regional.

Palmowski, who starts on pole for Sunday's main race in Austin at 5pm, live on Sky Sports F1, may now look to make a similar move in 2027.

"There are conversations happening in the background but I'm leaving that to my management team," she told Sky Sports F1.

"I want to go as far up the single-seater ladder as possible but I'm aware motorsport is a results-based business.

"I'm a big believer that when you go in a car, the helmet goes on, the car doesn't have a gender and we are fighting for the same thing."

Sports.title: ‘Night and day different’ – why did Ferrari's pace evaporate again?
Sports.content:
Ferrari's wait for a first Grand Prix pole position since August 2025 continued in the United States on Saturday as Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton qualified outside the top three in a session the team had appeared favourites for.

For the first time this season, Ferrari went into qualifying having topped all three practice sessions in Austin, on a weekend their car features the team's final significant upgrade of the season.

Leclerc finished second fastest to McLaren's Lando Norris in Q1, but only after the McLaren driver completed a second run to do so, and then returned to the head of the field in Q2.

But the Scuderia found themselves on the back foot immediately from the start of Q3 with Leclerc holding a provisional fourth and Hamilton sixth after the first runs of the decisive final phase.

Hamilton improved one place to fifth on his final run, but Leclerc stayed where he was, to leave the Ferraris behind the two Red Bull drivers and Mercedes polesitter Kimi Antonelli for the start of Sunday's 56-lap race.

Yet had Leclerc matched his benchmark time from the theoretically-slower Q2 session, he would have qualified second.

Team principal Frederic Vasseur told Sky Sports F1: "Bit of mixed feelings for sure. The potential was there over the weekend. We had good pace in free practice.

"Until the last corner we are fighting for pole but it is like it is."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix

So where did Ferrari's pace go?

On team radio after ending up fifth, 0.276s away from pole, a bemused Hamilton said: "These guys must be turning up [their engines] for that last Q3 because where did that time go?"

Speaking to Sky Sports F1 afterwards, Hamilton said that his car's handling had felt consistent through all three sessions, suspecting that the team's straight-line speed deficit had again played a central role in them being usurped.

"We did a really good job overnight. The car felt really good in FP3 - competitive," said Hamilton, who had topped that final practice session.

"Q1 and Q2 both felt pretty strong. It felt like we were right there in the fight and the car was just as good as... we didn't make any changes, the car didn't flip upside down in Q3. It was a really good lap.

"Those guys just somehow took another step. I don't know what it is. Ultimately we do lose, I think we are a few tenths off on the straight as we usually are, but a great lap by Kimi and the power deficit to the Red Bull and Mercedes is still significant.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli takes pole for the United States Grand Prix - could this be a championship winning drive?

"Our car is clearly as good as theirs through the corners but we lose that down the straights."

Leclerc, though, offered an alternative suggestion, believing that a decrease in track temperature for the start of Q3 had made a pivotal difference to their competitiveness, causing tyre warm-up issues.

Asked if it was again a case of rivals finding something extra to them at the end of qualifying, Leclerc replied: "This time I think it's slightly different in that I don't think the others have changed anything from Q2 to Q3. Where we have lost is on ourselves and that is mostly the tyres.

"The out lap was extremely difficult. There was a bit more cloud in Q3. We lost one or two degrees of track temp and, for us, it was night and day difference, and already from the out lap I felt I was having lots of difficulties.

"It's a shame that it happened in Q3 because I strongly believe that we had the pace to be fighting in front but unfortunately not today again."

Ferrari last started a Grand Prix from pole in 2025 in Hungary.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Powered by Audi: Martin Brundle takes to the iconic Circuit of the Americas track in a high-performance Audi, combining real laps with advanced sim data to break down racing lines, braking points, and elite-level performance

Why Ferrari are not out of victory hunt yet

All is not yet lost, however, for Ferrari in terms of fighting at the front in Sunday's race on a track where overtaking is possible and tyre degradation is predicted to be high.

Leclerc felt they could even still repeat his Austin victory from the same starting berth two years ago.

"Yeah [Ferrari can still win the race]. The last time I think I started from fourth here I won so I hope we can do the same," he said.

"Just a good start and then where you position your car and trying to anticipate what is going to happen [is key] because there are many different scenarios that can happen in such a turn one with very wide entry.

"Then if you are doing the right choices you can get a lot more than any other track, so I'm looking forward to that."

Image: Leclerc and Hamilton are both former winners at COTA, the latter on a record five occasions

Hamilton was staying cautious given the pace of the cars ahead, but expressed hope that Ferrari could still be a threat over the full race distance.

"Starting position isn't everything. You have to have really good pace to overtake," he added.

"It's a long race. There was more degradation than anticipated on Friday on the long runs. Our car will hopefully be decent and we will do the best job we can to apply pressure.

"To beat the Red Bulls and Mercedes will be challenging, for sure, but we will give it absolutely everything."

Sports.title: Antonelli takes surprise pole to boost chances of sealing title in USA
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli beat Max Verstappen to pole position for the United States Grand Prix to boost his chances of sealing a maiden world championship in Sunday's race.

The 20-year-old Mercedes driver is all but certain to become Formula 1's youngest ever champion but could clinch the title with five rounds to spare if he wins in Austin on Sunday and other placings go his way.

It was perhaps the most unlikely of Antonelli's seven poles this season as he came from nowhere in Q3 to surge ahead of Verstappen, who had appeared for most of the weekend to be battling Ferrari for the front-row positions.

Antonelli's pole time of 1:34.035s was good enough to beat Verstappen by 0.179s, with neither driver managing to improve on the second of their two Q3 flying laps.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater explains how Kimi Antonelli can clinch the F1 world title this weekend at the United States Grand Prix

Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar equalled his best qualifying result by taking third, leaving Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton a hugely disappointing fourth and fifth, respectively.

George Russell will start from sixth, with the Brit needing to finish in the top eight to ensure Antonelli won't be crowned champion if he wins on Sunday. Hamilton would also need to finish fifth or lower in the event of an Antonelli victory for the title to be confirmed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli admits taking pole at the United States GP was 'tricky' and eyes up a 'tough' battle with Max Verstappen

"We got pole, so we will try to win tomorrow," Antonelli said. "Max has been very quick and Isack did an incredible job, so it won't be easy.

"We will try to get a good start and hopefully we lead into Turn 1, then set the pace, even though it will be very tight.

"Very happy with qualifying. Q3 was very tough with the wind. Very gusty and unpredictable but happy to put it on pole."

United States GP Qualifying: Top 10 1) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



2) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



3) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



5) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



6) George Russell, Mercedes



7) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



8) Lando Norris, McLaren



9) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls*



10) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



*five-place grid penalty to be applied

Oscar Piastri took seventh ahead of his McLaren team-mate Lando Norris as the latter was demoted from sixth after having his final effort deleted for breaching track limits.

Racing Bulls took the final two top-10 places but Liam Lawson will inherit ninth from his team-mate Arvid Lindblad, who has a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine component allowance.

Antonelli delivers as Ferrari fall away

Ferrari came into the session as favourites for pole having topped all three practice sessions, and the only driver who appeared to be capable of challenging them was the in-form Verstappen.

That form appeared to be holding as qualifying began with Leclerc setting the early pace. It was only an extra run at the end of Q1 from Norris that knocked the Ferrari driver and Verstappen down from the top two places.

It was in Q2 that the picture began to change, with Verstappen appearing to separate himself from his rivals as he eased through with just one run on a used set of tyres.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli takes pole for the United States Grand Prix - could this be a championship winning drive?

Leclerc finished the period fastest ahead of Antonelli and Russell, who had shown improvement for Mercedes but still couldn't match the Ferrari as all three ran on fresh tyres.

The Silver Arrows' dominance during the first half of the season enabled Antonelli to build a big championship lead and his team to do the same in the constructors' standings, but the recent upgrade package they brought had to this point failed to deliver.

That all changed on the first runs in Q3 when Antonelli put together a fine lap to sit almost two tenths clear of Verstappen, with Leclerc behind Hadjar, three tenths down and seemingly suddenly out of contention.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff admits the car is still 'on the edge' despite encouraging signs of their Mercedes upgrades.

With gusting winds making for challenging conditions, Antonelli made a mistake in the final sector on his second run that appeared to have opened the door for Verstappen to snatch pole, but the Dutchman was also caught out and failed to improve his time, before the lap was deleted in any case for a track limits breach.

"Just Q3 was not good," Verstappen said. "Q1, Q2 was nice but then, for whatever reason on both sets [of tyres], just didn't have a good balance.

"There were no mistakes but just no grip and started to slide a lot and then the final lap, you can see that it's not really happening with the tail wind in places so you try to push a bit more, you hit the bump wrong the car is like a kangaroo and you have a massive slide so you know the lap is over."

Behind the top two on track, Leclerc managed to improve but not enough to improve his position, while Hamilton could only get above Russell for fifth.

Hamilton questioned over team radio whether Ferrari's rivals 'turning up their engines' had caused the turnaround, but Leclerc insisted after the session that it was down to other factors.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton explain what went wrong for Ferrari during qualifying, despite them looking on pace

"This time I think it's slightly different in that I don't think the others have changed anything from Q2 to Q3," Leclerc said. "Where we have lost is on ourselves and that is mostly the tyres.

"The out lap was extremely difficult. There was a bit more cloud in Q3. We lost one or two degrees of track temp and, for us, it was night and day different and already from the out lap I felt I was having lots of difficulties.

"It's a shame that it happened in Q3 because I strongly believe that we had the pace to be fighting in front but unfortunately not today again."

Sports.title: 'Not realistic' - Can Wolff's assessment of Antonelli's title chance be trusted?
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff believes it is "not realistic" for Kimi Antonelli to win the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday at the United States Grand Prix, despite the Italian starting on pole position.

Antonelli was not expected to claim top spot in qualifying but produced a superb lap in Q3 to beat Red Bull's Max Verstappen and take his first pole since July's Belgian Grand Prix.

Should Antonelli win Sunday's race in Austin with Lewis Hamilton finishing fifth or lower and George Russell no better than ninth, he will seal the title with five rounds remaining.

Hamilton will start fifth and Russell sixth when the lights go out at the Circuit of the Americas at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event.

However, Wolff has warned Mercedes will not have the pace to win as they did not have the pace in Friday practice's long runs.

"We are not talking about that [the championship]. It's not realistic," he told Sky Sports F1.

"I don't think we are quickest in the race, so it's about scoring points and eventually, hopefully, winning."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli takes pole for the United States Grand Prix

Antonelli is also wary of Red Bull's race pace and the possibility that Verstappen in second and Isack Hadjar in third can also work together.

He admits this week has been "a bit different", knowing it is the first opportunity to become the sport's youngest world champion at 20 years old.

"The goal stays the same. I just need to keep doing my job, and actually, I feel like I can enjoy the driving and everything more," said Antonelli.

"But of course, we still have to do the race, still have to try and win, and then, of course, we'll see what happens. But, I feel like I can enjoy it a bit more because obviously I'm in a very good position. But still, the mindset is always the same."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix

Verstappen plans to 'keep it respectful' against Antonelli

The uphill run towards the wide Turn 1 at the start provides a good opportunity for the driver in second to steam up the inside of the pole-sitter, something Verstappen may look to do if he has a strong getaway.

Verstappen, who has won the last two races, effectively has nothing to lose but suggested he will not be excessively aggressive against championship leader Antonelli.

"Kimi wants to go for the win right? That helps his position in the championship," he told Sky Sports F1.

"We keep it respectful and try to win the race."

United States GP: Top 10 Starting Grid 1) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



2) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



3) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



5) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



6) George Russell, Mercedes



7) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



8) Lando Norris, McLaren



9) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls

Tyre degradation was high in Friday's practice sessions in Austin but that has been the case at several races this season, only for the Grand Prix to turn into a one-stop race as the teams have changed the setup on their cars and the track has gripped up over the weekend.

Nevertheless, overtaking is possible and Verstappen cut a quietly confident figure to make it a hat-trick of wins and deny any chance Antonelli has of winning the title on Sunday.

"We have been happier in the long runs, and I hope that it will be the same tomorrow," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ahead of the United States Grand Prix, Max Verstappen discusses Red Bull's Championship title aims for next season

As for Russell, it has been another tricky weekend and he faces a big challenge to overtake Ferrari's Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in front of him, who have both been quick in practice, to get into the podium fight.

Russell has been unable to get to grips with Mercedes' new upgrade package but admits he simply just did "two bad laps in Q3".

"I think I could have been in the top three. My Q2 lap was two and a half tenths quicker than what I achieved in Q3 but that obviously isn't good enough from my side," he told Sky Sports F1.

Asked about his race prospects, he said: "I think it's a long race, a lot happens here in Austin. Strategy plays a role so still opportunities."

Sports.title: Foster drops Navarrete twice to unify three world titles
Sports.content:
O'Shaquie Foster unified the WBC, WBO and IBF super-featherweight world titles with a decisive unanimous decision win over Emanuel Navarrete at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.

Navarrete was relentless, as he always is, but he could scarcely land punches cleanly on Foster, who mixed in footwork and counters to keep the Mexican at bay.

As the rounds progressed, Foster grew more confident and began standing his ground to trade. By the championship rounds, Foster's corner was asking him to end the show.

The 33-year-old native of Orange, Texas, scored two knockdowns in the 12th, but Navarrete survived.

Image: O'Shaquie Foster overcame Emanuel Navarrete by unanimous decision.

Foster won with scores of 118-108 twice and 115-111.

Foster said, "It was a great performance. I finished strong, and I put him down twice in the end.

"A lot of people were saying that I didn't have power and that I wouldn't be able to keep him off me. But I showed that I am a complete fighter.

"I want to become undisputed. That's my dream. I want to make history, and all I need is one more [title]."

Navarrete said: "In this sport, it's about styles. And his style was better than mine today. Congrats to him. I knew he was an exceptional and complete fighter. I knew what we were facing.

"Perhaps I could have pushed more, but I'm content with my performance."
