Sports.title: Glitch in Chelsea’s coding costs Alonso while resurgent Spurs are all systems go | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
There was an odd interlude at Stamford Bridge with 76 minutes gone and the score still 0-0, one of those moments where suddenly your brain seems to be on inside out, like trying to walk the wrong way down an escalator.

Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row.

Fittingly it took a glitch in the coding to break this game open. Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s set-piece coach, was, as ever, up on his touchline semaphoring his instructions. Except this time he was ordering Chelsea players out of their own box. Get upfield. We need fewer people defending. We must, for some reason, vacate that space and initiate some kind of counterattack chess game.

This had already happened at another corner on 52 minutes. On that occasion 10 players were arranged in various upfield positions, leaving just a small gaggle in the box doing the actual try-to-score stuff. The ball landed in one of the huge vacant spaces. Everyone cheered.

Who started this habit? It seems like one of those things that just happens and you don’t know how or why, like driverless cars, or Howard Webb suddenly having his own ref-based TV show. But it was decisive here.

The second corner came howling in right through that vacated area. Again it looked strange, not least on a wet, blustery day, the kind of day where the rain just seems to want to get inside the neck of your coat, up your trouser turn-ups, in your pockets. The ball kept travelling, right through all that open space. At which point Mike Penders punched it into his own net.

MacPhee came to Chelsea in the summer after the club activated his release clause at Aston Villa, the most remarkable part of which is that the bloke who waves at corners actually has a release clause (fee: undisclosed). Here his response to the goal was to walk pensively down the touchline, stroking his chin. Hmm, yes, need to log this. Look at the data on that.

To be fair, this was a goalkeeping mistake by Penders, a random variable. Although not really if you zoom out. Penders is not best equipped to deal with no protection, with rain, wind and a soaking ball. Penders is good with his feet, famous for stepping out to play centre-half sometimes at Strasbourg. Maybe he should have been waved upfield by MacPhee to mark the counterattack. Anything but this in fact.

MacPhee’s gambit, now safely in the data bank as Counter-Bluff Own Goal No 34, did at least open up the game. A few minutes later Cole Palmer was sent off for a second yellow after a foul on Conor Gallagher. And on 87 minutes Mathys Tel scored a lovely goal, surging upfield and shooting low inside the near post, signal for Roberto De Zerbi to invade the pitch in a strange capering run, cramped over at the waist, cackling provocatively, like a stylised martial arts pose. Enter: Haemorrhoid Warrior.

View image in fullscreen Roberto De Zerbi was wild, passionate, his heart on his sleeve, but also obsessed with patterns and systems. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Until that point the entire afternoon had felt like an overload of systems-ball. Sometimes games like this are described as a fascinating tactical battle. This was something else, a dull tactical battle. At times in the first half the Stamford Bridge crowd got to watch a press being baited when there was no press, just a bait. Essentially, just people standing around.

By the end two things had happened. First, Chelsea were terrible. Maybe this is still a structural thing. After the years of wild overspend this has now become a high-speed talent trading house, new faces, old faces, faces you didn’t know were there, all simultaneously coming and going. End result: Chelsea had no cutting edge at all here in the absence of João Pedro, an entire system thrown by the lack of a focal point in attack. Danny Welbeck stayed on the bench for whatever reason.

Xabi Alonso played Palmer and Morgan Rogers in a strange, liminal forward role, ghost tens, nonexistent nines. There has been a lot of talk about the freedom Alonso likes to give his attack, the hard positional stuff reserved for the block behind. Sometimes freedom’s just another word for standing around in the rain, not sure which run to make.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea were static all game, lacking in edge, fire or urgency. There was even something a little sad in the crowd reaction on 69 minutes as Palmer earned his first yellow card, signal for a bust-up between the benches, basically a load of men in puffer jackets jostling and prancing. The home crowd leapt up, absolutely delighted to see some kind of edge finally. This is what they like here. In the end people just want to feel something.

Instead Chelsea had kicked off this London derby in cold systems-ball mode, and never got the engine hot. Forty minutes in Palmer had touched the ball eight times, Chelsea were on 27 per cent possession at home to Spurs, and the only real element of tension was the sight of Alonso’s weirdly inadequate golfing blouson steadily saturating with rainwater. Not his only misjudgment of the afternoon.

The second thing, Tottenham were good. Allowed to dominate the ball, and with Mateus Fernandes very good in deep midfield, this turned into their best result of the season, and a huge tick for the manager, who clearly loved every second.

De Zerbi is a funny concept. Wild, passionate, heart on his sleeve. But also obsessed with patterns and systems. He’s basically wildly excited about maths. But he was great to watch here. On the hour mark something complex happened in his team’s movements. Someone stood in the wrong space. A chance to swarm-press was passed up.

In response De Zerbi leapt in the air and let out a strange baying noise, the sound of an alpaca being garrotted. Moments later, Omar Marmoush passed straight to a Chelsea player and De Zerbi didn’t even flinch. We see things you’ll never see.

For a while James Maddison seemed to be playing a different game to everyone else, one where you’re allowed to make forward passes, carry the ball and make the game up in front of you a little. With 49 minutes gone he sat down in the centre-circle, his game done, which will be a concern. But this was still an excellent afternoon for De Zerbi’s Spurs; albeit one that turned on a missed punch and a moment of unnecessary helicopter coaching.

Sports.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
Sports.content:
When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year.

A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.”

The switch of venue to England from its usual home in Paris is a mark of respect to the man who became the first active player to receive a knighthood in 1965, a few months before retiring at the age of 50. It also provides an opportunity to recall an astonishing career that began with his local side Stoke in 1932 and made the “Wizard of Dribble” the most famous player on the planet.

View image in fullscreen In September 1956, Stanley Matthews shows his son Stanley Jr a scrapbook of cuttings from newspapers and magazines going back over 25 years of his career in football. Photograph: Popperfoto/Getty Images

“He was so far ahead of his time,” says Matthews Jr, a former winner of junior Wimbledon who had a successful tennis career. “The way he trained, his football boots … they were so light, they were like slippers so that he could move quicker. Towards the end of his career, when he was back at Stoke, he had the fire brigade come and water the pitch before the game so it would be a little slick, which was better for him. Now they water the pitches all the time, you know. So he was very revolutionary in all the things he did, plus his diet and his training.”

Matthews’ father, Jack, was a renowned boxer known as the Fighting Barber of Hanley and it was from him that he is said to have developed his work ethic. Matthews owned a Blackpool hotel that regularly welcomed celebrities including the comedian Charlie Chester, and was known for his early morning fitness routines on the beach that helped to prolong his career.

View image in fullscreen Stanley Matthews (right) visits a boot and shoe factory in 1951 where he is pictured discussing his own design with two experts. Photograph: Popperfoto/Getty Images

He remains the oldest Ballon d’Or winner and won the last of his 54 England caps – a number that would have been higher but for the second world war – in 1957 at the age of 42. Matthews Jr thinks his father could have lasted even longer in today’s possession-based game. “He would probably have thought: ‘My goodness, if all I had to do was pass the ball around, I could have played until I was 70,’ because a lot of the players just seem to be doing that, passing out from the back,” he says.

Whereas Harry Kane and the rest of the favourites for this year’s Ballon d’Or are all multimillionaires, Matthews had to make do with at most £20 a week until the maximum wage was abolished in 1961. “We compared it to the top sportsman in the US at the time, which was [baseball player] Joe DiMaggio” says Joe Pierce, who produced the 2017 film Matthews. “He was at the height of his career, and he had just signed a contract for $100,000 a year.”

View image in fullscreen Stoke City’s Sir Stanley Matthews is chaired off the pitch by World Stars XI’s Lev Yashin and Ferenc Puskas as Josef Masopust (left) leads the applause for the Wizard of Dribble after his testimonial in April 1965. Photograph: Empics/PA/Alamy

That meant there were a few successful and not so successful business ventures, including his own football boot brand, hats and various books, not to mention vegetable juice. “He tried to do it in cans, but it didn’t work out,” says Pierce. “There was a problem because it went bad in the cans.”

Another way of supplementing his income was coaching overseas in the off-season and between 1953 and 1978 Matthews visited an African country each summer. His love affair with the continent grew a few months after he had won the Ballon d’Or when he arrived in Ghana to play a series of exhibition matches to celebrate its independence. He was presented with an ivory sword and crowned as a “soccerhene” (soccer chief). “The King of Ghana – that’s what they called him,” says Matthews Jr. “My sister still has the stool that he was crowned on.”

Matthews developed a particular affinity for South Africa. He started coaching a team in Soweto during the mid-70s who became known as Stan’s Men and secured them sponsorship from Coca-Cola before taking them to play in a tournament in Brazil. Pierce was surprised when he discovered the lengths Matthews went to under significant pressure from the apartheid government not to travel.

View image in fullscreen Stanley Matthews coaching in Soweto. Photograph: Courtesy of Stanley Matthews Jr

“There was real drama and back and forth. The UK government was involved. The South African government was involved. There were spies involved – the South African spies at the camps and around – and he just kept pushing forward. He was good friends with the Duke of Edinburgh – they would get invited over for tea and things like that. So he had connections in high places that probably helped quite a bit.”

Matthews Jr says: “He was very proud of the fact that at one stage he was banned. He said: ‘Frank Sinatra was banned as well.’ So he thought that was kind of funny. I remember him saying that the South African players had so much speed and so much talent. Dad just liked people. And he knew that they had or he thought that they had a good talent. He just wanted to see if he could help them improve.”

His association with Stan’s Men ended after the 1976 Soweto Uprising, with one player in the film describing how ending contact with Matthews left a “hole in my heart”. Matthews’ death in 2000 at the age of 85 also evoked strong emotions, with more than 100,000 people turning out in Stoke for what the Guardian called the biggest public funeral since Winston Churchill.

View image in fullscreen Some former members of Stan’s Men. Photograph: Courtesy of Stanley Matthews Jr

“He’s probably sitting there saying: ‘I told you so,’” Pierce says of the record 78 African players in the Premier League last season. Only one African player – George Weah – and three Englishmen – Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen – have followed Matthews in winning the Ballon d’Or. Whoever is chosen this year will be following in the footsteps of one of the sport’s most celebrated figures.

Sports.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s outbursts are no laughing matter for fans
Sports.content:
In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.”

To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest.

The clip was widely shared, there is every chance you saw it earlier this month. The general perception, from those of a neutral stance, was that one of football’s great characters had lost the plot. To those in the room, there was a sense that it was merely the exuberant mannerisms of a quirky manager during a tricky period. But for a large section of Swindon fans, it prompted an unamused eye roll. Here we go again. The circus tent is pitched firmly in town.

Supporting a Holloway-led club is an interesting assignment. Within weeks of taking the Swindon job two years ago on Sunday, he began constructing a hostile wall towards fans by reminding them that they could “go bowling” if they did not like his methods. Last December, he had to be restrained by his players during an altercation with a fan, while he has made a habit of telling them to “jog on” if overly vocal in their criticism.

When his side picked up a much-needed point against Walsall last week, the goalkeeping coach held him back from another confrontation with supporters. Asked about it, he goaded reporters into putting his address online so that disgruntled fans could have it out with him: “I don’t really care anymore.” So, when season-ticket holders found their phones pinging with amused messages containing the same viral Holloway zombie clip, their lack of laughter could be forgiven.

“When you get these soundbites from Ian Holloway, outside the Swindon Town world it’s all about what a great character he is, how he says it like it is, and how it must be great to have him as manager,” says Rich Pullen, founder and co-host of the largest Swindon podcast, Loathed Strangers. “But, to a growing percentage of the Swindon community, it’s exhausting and it takes away from any of the good.

“If Swindon win, post-match he often uses it as an opportunity to have a go at the fans. It’s got to the stage where you can’t even enjoy a win without Ian Holloway being unable to hold himself from criticising fans. The easy thing to do is ignore him, but it’s almost impossible because he is everywhere. He goes viral and everyone always thinks: ‘Oh, isn’t that funny.’ Well, no. People are tired of the excess noise.”

This time last week, there was a thought that Saturday’s M4 derby homecoming trip to Bristol Rovers might hasten a possible end to Holloway’s Swindon tenure. Winless in eight games in all competitions, the discontent was not expected to abate on the preceding midweek trip to high-flying Barnet. The 3-1 victory that followed – Barnet’s first league defeat of the season – was a huge shock, thanks in no small part to the heroics of the goalkeeper, Connor Ripley, who recently declared the whole squad would “run through a brick wall” for Holloway.

View image in fullscreen Disheartened Swindon fans stand solemnly in the pouring rain at the Memorial Stadium. Photograph: Jeremy Landey/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Swindon might have followed it with another win, at Rovers’ Memorial Stadium, only for Matty Virtue to miss an open goal 90 seconds into the match. The forgettable goalless draw that played out at least extended Swindon’s unbeaten run to three games and kept them safely mid-table in League Two. Holloway was right to savour the improved performances, but the malaise runs deeper.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The manager had said something far more significant immediately after his viral soundbite when he continued: “The owner’s a dead man walking as well and that over-complicates everything here.”

Even those seeking a more composed figure in Holloway’s place agree the manager is just one cog in a machine many argue has been misfiring for some time. Days after the zombie rant, the Swindon Town Supporters Trust declared the club had “lost our soul, our hope, our passion”, and urged Holloway’s comments about the Australian owner, Clem Morfuni, to “be a wake-up call”.

Since saving the club from probable administration in 2021, Morfuni has become a target of increasing fan indignation, failing to sell up and adding millions to the club’s debt. “Whilst the short-term focus may be on Ian Holloway, the bigger picture is above the role of the manager,” concluded the Trust, pointing to “a wedge with supporters so obvious that even the manager openly talks about it”.

In such a context, the uptick in form is merely one – albeit very welcome – aspect among wider misgivings. Because what fans really want is a united club and manager they can get behind; not to go jogging on.

Sports.title: Clinical Arsenal earn precious win against Everton thanks to Konsa and Gabriel
Sports.content:
The wait goes on for David Moyes. The 63-year-old Scot must have been hoping that on his 14th visit to this stadium as Everton’s manager, his luck would change. Yet from the moment Ezri Konsa slammed home his first goal for Arsenal as the Premier League champions rediscovered their knack of scoring from set pieces, the writing was on the wall.

While it took until midway through the second half for Gabriel Magalhães to make sure of the victory, Arsenal were never going to let slip the chance of moving level on points at the top with Manchester City after their defeat by Aston Villa earlier in the day.

Asked whether it was strange that his side are again going toe-to-toe with their great rivals but with the added uncertainty of what punishment City will receive after being found guilty of 115 charges by the Premier League, Mikel Arteta said: “[We are] just focusing on what we can do. We are very pleased with 90% of the results and performances that we have.”

This was hardly a vintage performance from the clinical home side after a testing week but it did not need to be against opponents who offered precious little in attack, even if they defended for their lives at times.

Having gone six matches without defeat to start the season, a second in succession will only add to Everton’s concerns after confirmation that the club’s American owners want out.

“It was always going to be hard after conceding the early goal,” said Moyes, whose solitary victory at the Emirates was as West Ham’s manager in 2023. “I want us to challenge the top teams but it’s difficult when you see the strength of their bench.”

Everton’s record at this stadium is almost as bad as their manager’s. They arrived in north London having won twice in 35 matches here and had to do without Jarrad Branthwaite and Jack Grealish, who was ruled out with illness. It did not bode well for them when Arsenal took the lead in the seventh minute with a third corner in succession.

View image in fullscreen Ezri Konsa (No 15) squeezes the ball home for Arsenal’s early first goal against Everton. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Gabriel made the crucial first contact at the near post and Jordan Pickford tipped the ball on to the crossbar, only for Vitaliy Mykolenko’s failed clearance under pressure from Viktor Gyökeres to allow Konsa to ram home from close range. After a record-breaking 25 goals from set pieces last season, it was their first of this campaign.

It was a measure of Arsenal’s exertions against Bayern Munich on Wednesday that Arteta rotated his side more than usual for a Premier League match, making five changes.

Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke spurned good opportunities to extend the lead in front of the watching England head coach, Thomas Tuchel. The latter was left out of the last squad, but could well benefit from Bukayo Saka’s expected long absence due to a thigh injury. He was inches away with an instinctive effort with his right foot from the edge of the area on the half-hour mark and was consistently Arsenal’s most dangerous threat.

Everton must have feared the worst as yet another Arsenal corner – 10 during the first half – was launched into the area. Yet the defence just about stood firm.

A moment’s lapse of concentration from Ben White just before half-time almost gave Everton an equaliser but Thierno Barry could not get enough on his attempt to flick the ball past David Raya in their clearest opening.

Gyökeres looked determined to make an impression on his first Premier League start of the season but the Sweden striker, who has yet to score for his club this term, looked laboured.

Quick Guide Arsenal 2-0 Everton key facts Show • With both Arsenal and Manchester City doing so this season, this is just the third top-flight campaign to have two teams win at least seven of their opening eight matches after 1892-93 (Preston and Sunderland) and 1913-14 (Blackburn and Manchester United). • This was David Moyes’s 400th defeat across all competitions in his managerial career with all clubs. 31 of these have come against Arsenal, more than against any other opponent. • The opener from Ezri Konsa (pictured celebrating) was Arsenal’s first set piece goal (excluding penalties) since May against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one. Opta Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

He could not believe it when Tony Harrington penalised him for a foul on James Tarkowski and a sheepish Arteta earned himself a booking for protesting. Unsurprisingly, Gyökeres’ number was up soon after as Arsenal turned to their bench.

It took less than 60 seconds for Gabriel to head in at the back post as White offered Tuchel a timely reminder of his qualities with a brilliant cross.

Moyes’ frustration meant he joined Arteta in the referee’s notebook. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall could have made things interesting but his header fizzed just wide of a post.

Arsenal are now breathing down City’s necks, although whether this title race lasts the course remains unknown.

Sports.title: Relief for Slegers as Russo rescues Arsenal against Tottenham in WSL
Sports.content:
Alessia Russo’s contentious second-half penalty delivered relief, a reprieve and a chance for a reset as Arsenal came from a goal down to earn their second win of the WSL season in the north London derby.

At a rain-lashed Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Gunners were again their own worst enemy, forced to come from behind after Cathinka Tandberg’s headed opener. Georgia Stanway levelled and Russo powered in the penalty that gave them the lead they protected defiantly.

The Tottenham manager, Martin Ho, queried the penalty decision, with the ball hitting the raised arm of substitute Ella Morris from the clearance of one of her teammates. “My interpretation of the rule is if your teammate hits it and it hits your player, if you’re one yard away, the time and distance is taken into account, so there’s no penalty,” he said. “That’s my understanding of it, from when we were told to start the season. I want to understand what they’re saying, because then I can accept the decision.

“I don’t want the game to be about that, but when it decides a game it’s frustrating because it’s not within the law of the game.”

Arsenal’s manager, Renée Slegers, said she was glad to give the fans a win. “They sing us and fight us through the game,” she said. “At the end it’s scrappy, it’s game management and it’s scenarios, and they’re all with us.”

With the pressure building on her and her players after five games without a win, at times it felt like they were trying to disprove the phrase “you can’t dig yourself out of a hole”.

Quick Guide Brighton cruise to victory against West Ham Show Maisie Symonds’ first-half stunner sent Brighton on their way to a 3-0 win against West Ham at the Amex Stadium. The midfielder Symonds’ thunderbolt gave the Seagulls a half-time lead before Fran Kirby and Kiko Seike struck quickfire goals midway through the second period. It was a first clean sheet this season for Arturo Ruiz’s side and lifts them up to eighth in the table, two points above West Ham, who slipped to 12th after their fifth league defeat of the campaign. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Arsenal had looked a little shaky in the opening few minutes but they settled, built possession and started to pose a threat. A failure to carve out clearcut chances and capitalise on any period of dominance has been the running theme of their season. They lacked fight and there was sloppiness too, with too many overhit passes putting the ball out of play or giving away possession.

That the opener came from a Tottenham corner was unsurprising. Victoria Pelova swung the ball in and Tandberg rose above her two markers, Stanway and Emily Fox, who failed to even to jump and challenge, and headed home.

Spurs’ joy was short lived as Stanway made up for her marking error four minutes later by arriving to meet Russo’s cut back and powered the ball in off the crossbar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway equalises for Arsenal in the 17th minute. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

After the break there was concern for Tottenham when Alice Sombath’s leg seemed to twist awkwardly as she stretched for the ball. The club’s record signing left on a stretcher to be replaced by Morris, who made her return from an anterior cruciate ligament injury towards the end of last season.

After the lengthy stoppage, Russo forced a huge save from Lize Kop as she attempted to turn in Caitlin Foord’s cross from close range, the forward putting her hands to her head and screaming in frustration at the missed opportunity.

It did not take long for that frustration to transform into elation. The resulting corner from Kyra Cooney-Cross was headed on by Leah Williamson at the near post and Lisa Baum’s effort came back off the post. Spurs’ clearance bounced off the raised arm of Morris and the referee pointed to the spot. Russo sent Kop the wrong way and drove the ball low into the corner.

Arsenal were clinging on as the final whistle loomed but they had “found their fight,” said Slegers. “We had a run of games where results haven’t been good enough. It was frustrating for everyone. I’m so happy we got to win on this occasion, in the north London derby, away from home in the rain and we showed that character in the team.

“This will definitely energise us. We need to back this up in the next couple of games.”

Sports.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season.

Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend.

“No, I’m not worried about Marc at all,” Maresca said. “I know that he’s played every minute since the season started with us, with the international team, so it’s not easy. But again, the change was also because he was on a yellow card and in the way we want to be aggressive, sometimes to have one yellow card can be dangerous, but I’m not worried at all.”

City had 15 shots to Villa’s eight as they dropped points for the first time this season. Zion Suzuki made a number of important saves to keep City at bay in the second half, and Villa scored with their only two shots on target.

“I think we deserved more from the game, for the amount of chances that we created and for the chances that we conceded,” Maresca said. “We lost because probably we have not been clinical enough in their box and sometimes when you concede the first goal because of the mistake, the second goal again comes from transition in 45 minutes. It’s difficult to avoid that every time, but we learn from the game and we try to move on and to improve.”

View image in fullscreen Nicolas Jackson scores Aston Villa’s first goal past Gianluigi Donnarumma. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Jackson’s double takes him to seven goals since his move from Chelsea. He was a constant threat to the City centre-backs, who were unable to cope with his speed, physical presence and clinical finishing. Unai Emery said of his forward: “He’s very demanding of himself to improve things. Today he scored two goals, in the last matches he scored goals – but at the beginning of the season, what happened to us was more difficult and he was shooting a lot of balls over the corner.

“Now, he’s getting better at shooting. He’s working fantastically tactically, he’s understanding as well where we need him. Today, he scored two goals, but the most important thing is how he did his work, his task.”

His fellow summer signing Suzuki challenged Jackson for the player of the match award and is starting to show why Villa were so keen to acquire him as Emiliano Martínez’s replacement. Matty Cash told TNT Sport: “He’s brilliant, his first session when he came in, in the possession drill I thought we’d signed a midfielder. His vision is unbelievable, he catches crosses really well which as a full-back is a dream.”

Sports.title: Burnley sack Nicky Hayen after Lincoln rout leaves them in bottom three
Sports.content:
Burnley have sacked Nicky Hayen after only 14 games in charge, in the wake of a 4-1 defeat at Lincoln that left the Clarets in the Championship’s relegation zone.

The Belgian was appointed in the summer as the permanent successor to Scott Parker, who left in April with relegation from the Premier League inevitable. He leaves having won just one match, a 4-0 league victory at Watford on 10 October.

Burnley edged past Notts County on penalties in the Carabao Cup in his first match in charge and recovered in the last seven minutes from 2-0 down to draw at home to West Ham in their opening game of the Championship season. However, they then lost badly at West Brom and Norwich, sandwiching a shootout exit from the Carabao Cup at Bradford, and the pattern was set.

Burnley were fancied to push for promotion, which was achieved in their past two Championship seasons, but are now at risk of relegation. Wolves’ come-from-behind win at Turf Moor last weekend left Hayen on the brink and now the club have acted.

A terse, two-sentence statement on the club website said: “Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect. The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.”

Hayen had earlier said in his post-match press conference, before news of his dismissal emerged: “It’s frustrating for everyone, especially the fans. I want to apologise to them, but I know it doesn’t matter because it’s another hard defeat for them and I can understand their criticism.

“We haven’t got the results. I will keep on working hard as long as I have the chance. But there will be a day if it carries on like this that it stops. I know it’s a really tough defeat and something to think about for the board.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta gathering evidence on rival Premier League managers as he calls for new technology
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta gathering evidence on rival Premier League managers as he calls for new technology

Mikel Arteta is one of the most passionate bosses in the Premier League, buzzing around inside, or often outside, his technical area.

The Arsenal manager never stands still, racing around the area near the dugout - so much so, that he was punished on Saturday.



2 Arteta was shown a yellow card for leaving his technical area during Arsenal's win over Everton at a stormy Emirates on Saturday afternoon Credit: Getty

Arteta was shown a yellow card in the second half of his side's 2-0 win over Everton at the Emirates for leaving his technical area.

And that comes as no surprise for those who keep an eye on the Spaniard, who regularly encroaches past the white lines.

But when asked about the booking, which was his second of the season so far, Arteta defended himself by revealing some bizarre research into his rivals.



Arteta reveals manager investigation

"I do have to be careful," Arteta admitted in his press conference before claiming he has collected evidence of other Premier League managers doing the same as he did without being booked.

"There are managers that have the record in the league - 36 times in 10 minutes leaving the touchline, no yellows.



"I'm clipping all of that. I have a massive storage of images.

"So if somebody comes to me I can say: 'I'm not in the record yet, somebody else has the record'.

"Then it's 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers. I don't know what we're going to do. Let's see."



Arteta also mentioned that he wants to see some new technology added to the technical area to prevent breaches.

"We need to have good sensors there," he stated.

2 Arteta revealed he has already been looking into how many times his rival managers leave their technical area during a match Credit: Getty

What else did Arteta say on Saturday?

As well as admitting he'd been investigating his fellow Premier League bosses, Arteta discussed the win over Everton.

"We’re very happy with the victory, the performance and the week, because we were given a terrible schedule," he said.



"Playing Sunday afternoon, then Wednesday night in Munich, coming here really late on Thursday and then having to play again in the Premier League against a really tough opponent on Saturday at 3pm.

"We have overcome some injuries, and I’m really proud of the mentality of the team in the conditions today."

One of the injuries he mentioned was to Bukayo Saka, who sat out at the 2-0 victory of the Emirates with his issues.

And Arteta told talkSPORT post-match that Saka is going to be out for 'weeks' amid reports he could be sidelined for two months.

Sports.title: James Maddison suffers devastating injury blow as Tottenham secure historic win at Chelsea
Sports.content:
Tottenham pulled off an historic win over Chelsea after a devastated James Maddison picked up another injury.

Maddison, who has not long returned from a nine-month lay-off, was substituted after 50 minutes on Saturday evening.

4 Maddison looked defeated as he appeared to hold back tears while being treated and walking off the pitch on Saturday Credit: Getty

4 But Spurs went on to win the game without one of their key men, making history with a 2-0 victory away at rivals Chelsea Credit: Getty

At the start of the second half, cameras cut to the Spurs midfielder being surrounded by some of his teammates on the pitch.

He then sat down on the grass, looking emotional and holding back tears as the realisation of another potential issue set in.

Maddison recently opened up to talkSPORT about the 'dark days' of his recovery from an ACL injury after making his first start in a competitive match since May 2025 on Monday.

As he left the pitch at Stamford Bridge, he was hugged by some Chelsea players as well as multiple Tottenham stars.

And even Blues boss Xabi Alonso gave him a hug as he walked, head down, off the grass and straight down the tunnel.

Thankfully, Maddison later came out of the dressing room and returned to the bench to celebrate the huge 2-0 victory.

Maddison injury update

Speaking post-match, De Zerbi gave an update on Maddison.

He told talkSPORT: "We have to manage Maddison like a diamond.

"He's a special player, but not just about his qualities, as a personality, as an experienced player.

"Now we have to make the medical check to understand what the problem is. But we need him, absolutely."

4 Maddison pulled up with no player around him and walked off the pitch looking forlorn Credit: Getty

History made at Stamford Bridge

Losing Maddison would be a huge blow for Spurs of course, but they managed to end Saturday evening on a high.

De Zerbi's men went on to beat Chelsea 2-0, picking up just their second ever Premier League win at Stamford Bridge.

It was also their first victory while keeping a clean sheet at Stamford Bridge since December 1986.

An own goal from Blues goalkeeper Mike Penders and a late second from Mathys Tel made history for Tottenham.

The victory came against ten men in the end, as Cole Palmer was shown his first career red card after two yellows.

Chelsea have now received nine red cards in the Premier League since the start of last season, at least four more than any other side.

4 Spurs won at Stamford Bridge for just the second time ever in the Premier League Credit: Getty

The result has the Blues now just four points clear of Spurs, who have now gone three unbeaten and won two in a row.

They are now up to 12th in the top flight after the 2-0 win.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta issues fresh Bukayo Saka update amid reports he faces two months out
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has revealed that Bukayo Saka is facing 'weeks' out in a fresh update on his star winger's worrying injury.

Saka went down in the opening minutes of the Gunners' Champions League draw against Bayern Munich under no pressure.



2 Saka pulled up in pain immediately after making a pass in midweek and went on to miss Arsenal's clash against Everton on Saturday afternoon Credit: Getty

With the score at 0-0, he pulled up after attempting to play a crossfield ball, immediately going ground and indicating that he was unable to continue as medics came on to assess him.

He clutched his thigh as fell over and was then replaced by Eberechi Eze, who went on to score in the match in Munich.

The game finished 2-2 in the end, but concerns remained over Saka after he picked up what looked to be a serious knock.



And Arteta confirmed post-match on Wednesday: "They [the medical staff] are a bit concerned. The player having to come off feeling a sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see."

Saka hasn't trained since and went on to miss Arsenal's 2-0 win over Everton at the Emirates on Saturday afternoon.



How long will Saka be out for Arsenal?

After that victory, Arteta then gave another update on the England international amid reports he could be out for two months.

The Gunners boss told talkSPORT: "We have to wait. It will be weeks.

"I think in a week or ten days we're going to have another scan because there's so much fluid at the moment.



"So the picture is not that clear to give you an exact amount of time.

"But it looks like it's going to be weeks."

2 Arteta has revealed that Saka is going to be out for 'weeks' and he is due to have another scan on his injury soon Credit: Getty

Arsenal and England's injury blow

Saka has made ten appearances in all competitions at club level this season, scoring four goals and assisting once.

Three of his goals have come in the Premier League, while has scored and provided an assist in the Champions League.



Noni Madueke played in his place against Everton, with Arsenal coming out on top with ease, even without Saka.

The Gunners may be able to cope without him, but England are also set to be without one of their stars next month.

If Saka is out for multiple weeks, then manager Thomas Tuchel will be missing him for the upcoming November internationals.

The Three Lions face Croatia and Spain in their final two Nations League group stage fixtures in just three weeks time.



Saka started in three of England's four games in the previous international break, and scored a double in the 7-0 thumping of Croatia.

Sports.title: EFL boss immediately sacked just hours after latest defeat
Sports.content:
Burnley have sacked manager Nicky Hayen following their 4-1 defeat away at Lincoln in the Championship.

Hayen was unable to prevent the Clarets from picking up their sixth loss in 12 games on Saturday.



3 Burnley manager Hayen only won one game in the league since being appointed in the summer Credit: Getty

Burnley, who were only relegated from the Premier League last season, are currently sitting in the relegation zone.

Their loss to newly-promoted Lincoln, in another game in which they took the lead, leaves them in 22nd spot in the second tier having won just one game all campaign.

And Burnley, who haven't won at home since October 2025 - the longest streak in the top four tiers of England - have wasted no time in announcing the axing of Hayen just hours after their latest loss.



A club statement read: "Burnley Football Club has dismissed Head Coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect.

"The Board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season."



talkSPORT understands that Kenny Miller is one of several names appreciated by Burnley for the now vacant position, with the Sotsman impressing in charge of Maccabi Tel Aviv.

Hayen's axing comes shortly after he told talkSPORT that his future at the club is in the balance, where he also apologised to fans.



What did Hayen say after the defeat to Lincoln?

When asked post-match if he fears being sacked, Hayen told talkSPORT: "Fear? I know how it goes in football, especially with the results we have had in the last few weeks.

"I spoke with the owner last week in terms of the injuries that we had and the upcoming game, and also that we had a good training week.

"But for one or another reason, we can't bring the same quality in the game that we show on the training pitch.

3 Burnley were easily beaten by Lincoln in the Championship on Saturday to compound the misery of Hayen and his side Credit: Getty



"That's a little bit of a shame because the boys deserve much better and that is unfortunately the reality."

Then, on whether he hopes to continue in his role as manager, he added: "Yes, of course you hope to continue. But I know how it goes.

"I also feel sorry for the fans as there were a lot of fans here, so I do apologise.

"I know even if I apologise to them it doesn't matter because again we have a big loss and I know they're frustrated and I totally accept it."



'Absolute disaster'

Hayen spoke honestly about his and Burnley's woeful start to the Championship season, but unfortunately for the Belgian, it wasn't enough to save his job.

Burnley legend Ben Mee had declared after the Lincoln defeat that the writing was on the wall for the manager.

3 Hayen failed ti impress during his spell in charge of Burnley Credit: Getty

Speaking on talkSPORT's GameDay Live, Mee, who made 367 appearances for the Clarets, said: "Absolute disaster today.



"Going there and capitulating as they did, going 1-0 up, the quality in the group, the attitude of the group, it seems to be a theme this season.

"Lose a goal, heads go down, whether the players' mentality is right, whether they want to be at the club...

"I think there's players in there that were trying to leave in the summer, maybe didn't get the wish, the heads and the focus aren't quite there.

"The manager's gone in and maybe taken over a squad that's not as together as what he would have liked.



"He's going to find out, he's going to get the brunt of it, I think."

Sports.title: Chelsea name surprise striker for Tottenham clash after unexpected Joao Pedro blow
Sports.content:
Chelsea name surprise striker for Tottenham clash after unexpected Joao Pedro blow

Joao Pedro was not in the Chelsea squad for their derby defeat to Tottenham, with a surprise name taking his place.

Rather than Danny Welbeck taking Pedro's spot leading the line for the Blues, Geovany Quenda was handed a start.

3 Quenda made his first Premier League start against Spurs, replacing Pedro in the Chelsea team over Welbeck Credit: Getty

It was Quenda's first Premier League start since arriving at Stamford Bridge, having played just 28 minutes this season so far.

The natural right winger was preferred to Welbeck, despite the latter being an out-and-out striker to replace Pedro.

Welbeck remained on the bench for Xabi Alonso's side, with Quenda coming in and him, Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto and Morgan Rogers playing fluidly across the front line.

Why is Pedro not in the Chelsea squad?

Chelsea's top scorer Pedro was missing from their squad for their clash against rivals Spurs due to an injury.

His new issue is currently being assessed.

Alonso confirmed pre-match: "Yesterday in training he felt something, and at the moment he has some liquid, so we have to do some tests to know how big the injury is.

"It's disappointing, but we need to carry on."

Pedro had started Chelsea's last two games, scoring two against Bournemouth before playing against Everton.

But he did previously miss international duty with Brazil due to a knock that reportedly saw him visit a knee specialist.

And that came after he also sat out of the Blues' clash against Brentford before the extended international break.

3 Pedro was missing for Chelsea after picking up an injury that is currently being assessed Credit: AFP

Who is Geovany Quenda?

Quenda took Pedro's place in a surprise decision, considering the 19-year-old wide man hasn't started a Chelsea game before.

The Portugal U21 international joined the Blues this summer from Sporting Lisbon in a deal that was agreed last year.

Since his £43.5million move, Quenda hasn't managed to break into Alonso's line-up, competing with Pedro, Rogers and Palmer.

But with Pedro out, he was given a chance.

On deciding to start Quenda, Alonso explained: "He has many qualities, he attacks the space well, he has been training well and all the players will have their opportunities at times.

"Geo has been patient and today's a big game for him."

3 Quenda has never started a game for Chelsea, but he was part of the attacking unit in a huge clash against Spurs Credit: Getty

He ended up playing 72 minutes of the game at Stamford Bridge.

Estevao took his place for the final stages as Spurs shocked Chelsea and came away 2-0 winners in the London derby.

Sports.title: Championship star breaks English football record just 15 minutes into match
Sports.content:
QPR's Richard Kone stunned Swansea on Saturday with the fastest hat-trick from kick-off since English football records began.

Kone took less than two minutes to open the scoring at Loftus Road, before doubling the hosts' lead seven minutes later.



2 Kone's hat-trick is the earliest in the top four divisions of English football for at least 22 years Credit: Getty

And when QPR were awarded a penalty, he did the business from 12 yards to put Julien Stephan's side seemingly out of sight within a quarter of an hour.

In doing so, Kone recorded the earliest hat-trick from the start of a match in England's top four divisions since records began (in the 2004/05 season when the EFL rebrand took place).

He beats the previous record held by Sadio Mane for Southampton against Aston Villa in 2015 by a minute.



Mane still boasts the fastest hat-trick in terms of time elapsed between the first and third goals - scoring all three within two minutes and 56 seconds in that famous 6-1 victory for Saints.

But Kone now has his own little slice of English football history.

Kone out of nowhere

Kone's quickfire treble was made all the more remarkable by the fact that Swansea came into the game boasting the league's best defensive record.



Swansea had conceded just eight goals in 11 Championship matches prior to Saturday.

It's certainly some way to get off the mark for the season – Kone had only scored once in 13 games since March.



But he wasted no time in drawing level with Paul Smyth as QPR's top league goalscorer this term.

This was Kone's second professional hat-trick – and his first at Championship level.

2 Kone's goalscoring talent became clear during his time at Wycombe, where he scored 21 goals in the 2024/25 campaign Credit: Getty

He previously helped himself to three goals for Wycombe Wanderers against Peterborough United in League One in October 2024, completing that hat-trick within 11 minutes of coming off the bench.



The 23-year-old has now scored 34 EFL goals, having been given his big break by Wycombe.

Kone's story so far

The Chairboys signed Kone from non-League Athletic Newham in January 2024.

Born in the Ivory Coast, the striker had initially come to England to play in the 2019 Homeless World Cup.

And since banging in an utterly prolific 42 goals in 48 games in his first season in the Essex Senior League, he's gone from strength to strength.



Kone left Wycombe for QPR in August last year and earned his first senior international cap that November.

Victory for QPR will keep them firmly in the Championship play-off hunt.

This season's play-offs have been expanded from four teams to six, meaning eighth place will be enough for a shot at promotion come May.

Sports.title: National League match abandoned after 14 minutes of chaos
Sports.content:
Barrow's National League match against Forest Green Rovers was abandoned on Saturday after just 14 minutes.

Referee Stuart Morland took the decision to end the game after the pitch became waterlogged due to Storm Boelo.



1 The match was deemed unplayable after just 14 minutes following a pass that held up completely on the waterlogged pitch Credit: Forest Green Rovers

The huge storm has hit the UK this weekend, leading to incredibly windy and rainy conditions across the country.

Barrow, who are based in Barrow-in-Furness, play their football right on the North West coast and the weather has been severe.

A wind warning had been announced for Northern England by the Met Office before kick-off, but the National League clash went ahead.



That was despite the green light being given by referee Morland after a lengthy pitch inspection.

But the game didn't last long, with officials calling time just 14 minutes in after Barrow had already taken an early lead.



With the score at 1-0 to the hosts, they posted on X: "Due to circumstances beyond our control, the game has been abandoned."

Meanwhile, after announcing the same, Forest Green wrote: "We understand this is very frustrating for the FGR supporters who have travelled to Barrow today. We wish you all safe travels back home."



The club then posted a video to X showing just how chaotic the conditions were for both teams at Holker Street.

It showed a Barrow player attempting to pass the ball back to his goalkeeper, but it completely held up in the waterlogged pitch, allowing Forest Green forward Sean Etaluku a chance on goal.

That was the moment that Forest Green labelled the 'deciding factor', and the referee subsequently called the game off.

'It was quite farcical'

Forest Green do not have a manager, but one of their coaches, Yan Klukowski discussed the abandonment post-match,



"It was the right decision," he began. "But it was quite farcical in the end, the game should never have started with the conditions of the pitch.

"It was quite clear in the warm-up that the ball wasn't rolling correctly or truly."

Klukowski added: "The referee had been here two, three hours before kick-off, he had his concerns which he highlighted before we arrived.

"His communication was good...at that point you could sense there was an element of him being extremely worried.



"He had the initial inspection, there was a lot of doubt but he decided we were going to give it a go, but looking back it looks like a poor decision and one he should have made then."

Will the match be rearranged?

According to FA rules, the match will be replayed fully as it was abandonded due to circumstances out of the clubs' control.

A new date will be agreed by the clubs and the National League.

Sports.title: Chelsea 0-2 Spurs PLAYER RATINGS: Which Blues star endured a nightmare outing? Who was an 'absolute nuisance' for the visitors? And how did Cole Palmer rate after red card?
Sports.content:
Chelsea 0-2 Spurs PLAYER RATINGS: Which Blues star endured a nightmare outing? Who was an 'absolute nuisance' for the visitors? And how did Cole Palmer rate after red card?

Tottenham beat Chelsea at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in 36 years on an evening to remember for Roberto De Zerbi's men.

A dreadful error from Blues goalkeeper Mike Penders gave Spurs the lead 13 minutes from time as he punched a corner into his own net.

It went from bad to worse for Chelsea shortly after as Cole Palmer was sent off for two yellow cards in quick succession.

Mathys Tel then sealed the three points for Spurs as he beat Penders from distance to cap a perfect outing for the visitors and leave Xabi Alonso with questions to answer.

Daily Mail Sport's KIERAN GILL and BOBBY MANZI were there to run the rule over both sides.

Roberto De Zerbi's men secured a famous victory at Stamford Bridge on Saturday night

CHELSEA (3-4-2-1)

Mike Penders – 3

Is there a worse way to mark your full debut in the Premier League than this? He tried to punch clear a Tottenham corner, but only sent the ball backwards for an own goal. He was then beaten from 20 yards by Mathys Tel to cap an unfortunate afternoon for the 21-year-old understudy.

Josh Acheampong – 5

Tottenham seemed to target this 20-year-old academy graduate’s side, especially in the first half. Acheampong had his hands full with Tel, who got away from him to score Spurs’ second, while James Maddison was also drifting into his area.

Maxence Lacroix – 5

Performed an acrobatic clearance in a bid to try to save Penders from his humiliation, but the ball had crossed the line. Among those Chelsea players who took turns fouling Maddison before he exited injured.

Levi Colwill – 5

Had an easier time of it defending-wise than Acheampong. Super ball in behind from deep nearly left Pedro Neto one-on-one. But this was a substandard afternoon for all those associated with Chelsea.

A dreadful error from Mike Penders gifted Spurs the lead 13 minutes from time as he punched into his own net

Pedro Neto – 6

Wing back. Winger. Call him what you want. Neto works hard. Tel tried to buy a penalty out of him, but he won the ball fairly. Tested Antonin Kinsky several times – just couldn’t score.

Moises Caicedo – 5

If you were in his way, he’d barge into you, as Maddison discovered here on the odd occasion. Maddison was allowed too much space throughout. Captained Chelsea to a derby defeat.

Jordan Henderson – 5

Almost scored in what was his fourth successive start in the Premier League. Kinsky managed to stop his 18-yard crack after some – rare – nice one-touch football from Chelsea.

Jorrel Hato – 5

When Spurs had the ball – as they often did – he was expected to be a left back. When Chelsea had it, he was supposed to get forward to help the attack.

Cole Palmer – 3

He flirted with a second yellow last week at Everton and got away with it then. But he did not here. He earned his two bookings. He barged into Mateus Fernandes to be cautioned for dissent after 71 minutes. Then stood on Conor Gallagher’s foot after 80. Both were acts of idiocy from Palmer.

Cole Palmer was sent off for two yellow cards in quick succession after a moment of madness

Morgan Rogers also struggled in a different role as the Blues rued the absence of Joao Pedro

Geovany Quenda – 5

First start for Chelsea, replacing the injured Joao Pedro, but hardly contributed to the attack. Tried swapping wings with Neto for a while. Huge roar for Estevao when the Brazilian replaced him.

Morgan Rogers – 5

Chelsea missed the hold-up play of a striker. Rogers largely filled in as a false nine, though the set-up was rather fluid as players moved around positions. Showed his frustration towards the end when he was on the pitch without his mates, the red-carded Palmer and the injured Joao Pedro.

SUBS USED

Marco Palestra (for Hato, 65 minutes) – 5

Came on at 0-0. Chelsea lost 2-0. But hardly his fault. The Blues were not competitive enough throughout this match and Spurs left saying they outplayed their opponents.

Estevao (for Quenda, 73 minutes) – 5

You do not hear many roars this loud for a substitution as Estevao was introduced before the 80th minute for the first time this season. But he could not deliver that big moment.

Danny Welbeck (for Neto, 88 minutes) – N/A

SUBS NOT USED

Teddy Shawman-Lowe

Wesley Fofana

Valentin Barco

Malo Gusto

Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli

Romeo Lavia

MANAGER

Xabi Alonso – 4

This was not a performance worthy of Chelsea when Tottenham come to town. They are supposed to try to take control, but they were weak here, and deserved to lose.

TOTTENHAM

Antonin Kinsky - 7

Slightly questionable with his feet but brilliant otherwise. Made a fantastic save to deny Palmer, tipping over the bar. A few good stops from Neto chances, too.

Archie Gray - 6

Played both left-back and right-back, neither fazed him. Managed Palmer and Quenda well. Didn’t offer bundles going forward, though.

Jan Paul van Hecke - 7

Pressured Penders into a mistake as he punched into his own net, giving Spurs their first win at Stamford Bridge in eight years. Spurs fans won’t care how it was scored, van Hecke will go down as their hero. Was a rock at the back.

Sandro Tonali helped Spurs run the midfield in a dominant display as they claimed a 2-0 win

Micky van de Ven - 7

Strong. A misfiring Chelsea front line could not get past him. Formed a fine partnership with his compatriot at centre-back.

Andy Robertson - 6

Combined well with Tel, particularly in the first half. Played an exquisite cross into Marmoush’s feet and was robbed of an assist by poor finishing.

Mateus Fernandes - 8

Was up for it and pivotal to Spurs’ midfield control. Expertly broke up play and acted as the anchor between defence and attack. Solid.

Sandro Tonali - 7

Covered the most ground of any player. Offered a durable platform with his defensive work. Dominated midfield alongside Fernandes and that was vital.

Mohammed Kudus - 7

Missed narrowly inside the area, bending wide of the post from a tight angle. Got on the ball plenty and showed his dribbling quality.

Tonali's midfield partner Mateus Fernandes put in his best performance since joining Spurs

James Maddison - 8

Ran the show on his second start of the season until he was forced off injured minutes into the second half. He just cannot stay fit.

Kept it ticking in midfield; Moises Caicedo could not get near him. Was the main creative outlet while on the field, with the most touches in the opposition box. Found Tel in space on the left with a wonderful outside-of-the-boot pass. Their link-up was effective.

Mathys Tel - 8

Absolute nuisance down the left. Chelsea could not handle him at all. Topped it off with an exceptional drilled finish from outside of the box in the dying minutes, guaranteeing a rare Spurs win over Chelsea.

Omar Marmoush - 5

Should have given Spurs the lead after he was found free in the six-yard box but hit his effort straight at Penders. Anywhere else, it was 1-0 Spurs. Disappointing.

SUBS

Conor Gallagher (51’ for Maddison) - 6

Was fouled as Cole Palmer was sent off for a second yellow card. Viscerally booed by the home fans on return to his former employers. Didn’t do much.

Dominic Solanke (65’ for Marmoush) - 5

Didn’t manage a shot in his 25-minute cameo. It was a good job those around him took the initiative.

Pedro Porro (65’ for Robertson) - 6

Active up and down the touchline. Helped keep Spurs’ energy high.

Ben Davies (89’ for Kudus) - N/A

Dejan Kulusevski (89’ for Tel) - N/A

Now give your ratings...

Sports.title: The night Mateus Fernandes finally came of age in a Spurs shirt: Talented £85m star shone in Chelsea win as he showed Roberto De Zerbi what he is made of after tough start to Tottenham career, writes MATT BARLOW
Sports.content:
The night Mateus Fernandes finally came of age in a Spurs shirt: Talented £85m star shone in Chelsea win as he showed Roberto De Zerbi what he is made of after tough start to Tottenham career, writes MATT BARLOW

There were heroes in all quarters and Roberto De Zerbi lavished praise freely, but the rain-drenched triumph at Stamford Bridge will go down as the night Mateus Fernandes came of age in a Tottenham shirt.

Expectations have been sky high since Spurs paid West Ham what was at the time a club-record £85million for Fernandes in July.

Perhaps unnaturally high expectations went with an unnaturally high fee for a young midfielder who did not make Portugal's World Cup squad, wall all about potential and still playing most of his international football at Under-21 level.

His talent was clear, but Fernandes suffered relegation in successive relegations with Southampton and West Ham, and Spurs, despite flirting with the drop last season, have different ambitions.

'He needed to understand the club,' said De Zerbi on the eve of the trip to Chelsea. 'To better understand the environment of a bigger club, a different club. He's a good guy. I don't change my idea of him. And the club don't change their idea.

'We pushed together to bring him. We are convinced of his qualities. He has to stay with a calm head, have confidence and enjoy himself on the pitch. Enjoy it with the ball, show his qualities because he will be one of the most important players of Tottenham for the future. For the present and the future.'

Mateus Fernandes enjoyed his best night in a Spurs shirt since signing for £85million

The Portuguese midfielder came of age during the 2-0 win that stunned Stamford Bridge

Fernandes was hooked at half-time in a 3-2 defeat against Aston Villa.

'I have a big confidence in Mateus, but I didn't like the performance of Mateus today,' said De Zerbi at the time. 'He knows. But it's normal. It's not an attack on Mateus, I love Mateus, it's not a problem. But we need more from Mateus.'

The Villa defeat was the final game before the international break, when Spurs were marooned at the bottom of the Premier League with just two points from their first five games.

The team has progressed, making improvements but Fernandes had barely been involved.

He missed some training for the birth of his son between the draw with 10 men at Manchester United and the win against Coventry on Monday, when he was overlooked despite the absence of Rodrigo Bentancur, who was banned.

De Zerbi preferred to tweak his formation to a back-three and play Archie Gray in midfield with Tonali and James Maddison.

At Chelsea though, Fernandes was back, restored in a deep central role and it did not start well.

There was an early mistake. Looking for a free-kick near in a left-back area, he was easily dispossessed by Pedro Neto and it led directly to a chance for Cole Palmer.

Fernandes was also involved in the game's main flashpoint after being caught by Cole Palmer

Toni Kinsky made a save to keep Spurs level but from that point on, Fernandes displayed the personality to impress De Zerbi and grew in confidence.

For long spells, he and Sandro Tonali bossed midfield against Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson. This is how it was meant to be when Spurs invested so much in the pair.

They rippled with power and bristled with energy. They won the ball and zipped it about with pace and poise. They snapped into tackles and shielded their back four as Spurs kept Chelsea's creative forces at bay.

De Zerbi thought it was Tonali's best game since arriving at Spurs for £100m from Newcastle just days after Fernandes.

The Spurs boss also hailed the performance of captain Micky van de Ven and he said: 'We won the game with the two wingers. Mo Kudus and Mathys Tel made the difference.'

The performance will do wonders for Fernandes, though.

He was also caught in the 72nd minute flashpoint with Palmer, which supercharged the closing stages of the game.

Tumbling to the floor as he failed to halt Palmer on a dangerous break and he hooked the ball away with a hand as a last resort.

It was cynical but it was critical. Palmer reacted angrily barging Fernandes back to the deck as he tried to get up.

De Zerbi lost it on the touchline and the benches emptied.

Fernandes displayed the personality to impress Roberto De Zerbi and grew in confidence

Both players were shown yellow cards and Palmer picked up a second when he was late into a tackle on Conor Gallagher in the 80th minute, three minutes after Spurs had taken the lead when Chelsea's rookie goalkeeper Mike Penders punched a corner into his own net.

Fernandes, the initial culprit emerged as the cold-eyed hero.

'I love watching my players fighting on the pitch,' said De Zerbi. 'But Mateus Fernandes played 90 minutes with a big, big quality. I want to see him with personality. I want to see him enjoy with the ball. Even if he makes a mistake, it doesn't matter. It's not a problem, a mistake. But I want to see this personality from my team.

'We are a big club. In the last period the results have been not so good. But we are a top club in the Premier League.'

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi's new Tottenham: Spurs often crumble when the going gets tough but this group showed they are stronger and more mature in deserved win over petulant Chelsea, writes MATT BARLOW
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi's new Tottenham: Spurs often crumble when the going gets tough but this group showed they are stronger and more mature in deserved win over petulant Chelsea, writes MATT BARLOW

When filthy conditions produce a filthy game of football the clever money is seldom on Tottenham to prevail.

Conventional wisdom dictates Spurs will go under when the going gets tough. They will lose their focus, commit errors and crumble and they fail to impose their quality.

Roberto De Zerbi can take great satisfaction that on this occasion Chelsea were the team who lost their cool and reacted with childish petulance when things conspired against them in a frenetic closing sequence of events.

In doing so, Xabi Alonso's Blues missed the chance to capitalise on Manchester City's first defeat of the Premier League season and close the gap at the top of the table.

It was Spurs with the look of maturity. Stronger in body and mind. They were the better team for most of the contest.

They resisted when required and seized on a moment of good fortune when Chelsea's rookie goalkeeper Mike Penders punched a corner into his own net for the opener.

Mike Penders had a moment to forget on his full debut, punching in a Tottenham corner

Chelsea's miserable evening was capped by Cole Palmer being sent off for a second yellow card

The delivery by Mateus Fernandes was exquisite, fizzed across with pace and swerve and Penders was under pressure from Jan-Paul van Hecke.

The home team claimed a foul for the Van Hecke challenge, but the mistake belonged to the 'keeper not the referee. Maxence Lacroix hooked the ball out, but it had crossed the line.

Within three minutes, Cole Palmer had been sent off for a second yellow card for a late tackle on Conor Gallagher.

Palmer had been lucky not to be sent off for his first offence, a yellow card for retaliation when he barged into Fernandes as the Spurs midfielder climbed up from the floor having conceded a free kick for a deliberate handball to halt a dangerous Chelsea break.

Palmer was right to be annoyed but his fiery reaction caught Fernandes flush in the face and threw him back to the floor.

De Zerbi and his staff completely lost it on the bench, demanding a red card. De Zerbi picked up a yellow for his protests.

It was not exactly the Battle of the Bridge, the infamous skirmish between these London rivals in 2016 but it brought the game to the boil, but Spurs held their nerve as Chelsea lost theirs.

Morgan Rogers might easily have followed Palmer off, cutting down Gallagher from behind with a cynical foul. Rogers escaped with a yellow card.

Maxence Lacroix was unable to prevent the ball from crossing the line

Mathys Tel added to Chelsea's misery with a brilliant solo goal, a strong run and a crisp low finish flashed across the turf for the second in the 87th minute.

Spurs celebrated wildly in the rain with their fans. Who can blame them? In the previous 41 visits to Stamford Bridge, they had won only once. That was in April 2018, a fading memory.

The only blow was an injury to James Maddison.

Spurs are up into the comfort of mid-table and gradually bonding under De Zerbi.

They have been on an upward curve since the international break. First a battling point with 10 men at Manchester United. Then the first win in the Premier League at the seventh attempt, at home to Coventry on Monday.

These results either side of a secretive training break in Spain helped replenish the confidence tanks and they made a strong opening at the Bridge.

SPURS' 'COMPLETE' DISPLAY Roberto De Zerbi hailed Tottenham's heroes as a 'complete team' after beating Chelsea at Stamford Bridge for the first time in eight years. Two goals in the final 15 minutes capped off a dominant Spurs performance, as Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net before Mathys Tel drilled a superb strike into the bottom corner from outside the box. The victory marked just Tottenham's second away victory at Chelsea in 35 league meetings. Cole Palmer compounded Chelsea's misery after he was dismissed for a second yellow card for a late challenge on former teammate Conor Gallagher. He was fortunate to escape a red card for his first booking, having clattered into Mateus Fernandes off the ball. Spurs dominated the ball with nearly 70 per cent possession and De Zerbi waxed lyrical after his team brushed aside their usual inferiority complex at the Bridge. 'Great individual and collective performance,' said De Zerbi. 'We did something different to what Tottenham had in the last period. Not a different attitude but a different relationship with the players – changing the group's spirit changed the performance. 'Now we are a complete team. The players are playing better and we have improved our style. I believe in this group. I never lost confidence in my players. We have to keep working hard and improving. 'The character was great, but we have many, many new players. The players who stayed here from last season and two or three seasons ago suffered from the results, including two 17th-place finishes. 'We are working to change the last part of the club's history. We are lucky because we have many great people in the dressing room and many great players. 'When you work with smart and sensitive people, they already know what we have to do to improve the situation. If we work hard, we can do something important. 'The negative record here was the last problem we thought before the game. Normally we want to make our fans happy but the past results are not our responsibility. 'Winning the game, we are very happy for the fans and proud of the club. We have been working to change the club's mentality in the last seasons. 'We are a big club. In the last period, the results haven't been so good. But we are a top club and we must show personality, mentality and the quality of the players.' Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso was frustrated by Palmer's red card with his dismissal marking Chelsea's ninth red since the start of last season. The Chelsea boss conceded he must sort out their disciplinary record. 'Absolutely,' Alonso replied when asked if Palmer's red card is a learning moment. 'I've not seen it but I've been told it's right. I need to check the action before speaking with Cole but it's one to learn from. 'We need to work and improve our emotional control. We spoke yesterday about those things. One first yellow can be decisive. It's a process of maturity.' Bobby Manzi

De Zerbi, having dabbled with a back three against Coventry, reverted to a back four and those who came in delivered for the boss.

Fernandes excelled alongside Sandro Tonali as Spurs dominated midfield and Tel was lively from the outset, linking up to good effect with left back Andy Robertson.

Tel created the first real chance for the visitors, with a low cross cut back for Omar Marmoush. Unmarked, 10 yards out in the centre of goal, Marmoush should have scored but he was unable to beat Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian starting in goal for Chelsea after coming off the bench at Everton when Emi Martinez was carried off with a broken jaw.

Penders made another save to deny Tel, released by Marmoush, although the flag went up for offside.

At the other end, Antonin Kinsky's distribution was erratic and kept Chelsea in the game even when they did not have the ball. Twice Kinsky gave the ball away to Pedro Neto. On the second occasion he had to react with a splendid save from Jordan Henderson.

Kinsky also made the first save of the game, flying to his right to push wide a shot from Palmer after Neto had won the ball.

Spurs enjoyed more than 70 per cent of possession in the first half but Chelsea had grown into the game as the interval approached. Kinsky was forced to make saves from Rogers, who started at centre forward with Joao Pedro absent with injury, and from Neto.

Maddison went down five minutes into the second half, signalling to the bench as he sank onto his haunches. He knew immediately he could not continue.

De Zerbi admitted on the eve of the game that Maddison had barely trained since Monday when he started a game for the first time in nearly 18 months and scored against Coventry.

The Spurs boss promised to take no risks but with a player who has had no luck with injuries. First the cruciate knee injury, then a setback, then a hip problem in preseason and a shoulder jarred at Brentford on the opening day.

The only sour note for Tottenham was James Maddison limping off in the second-half with a groin injury

Maddison was replaced by Gallagher, a former Chelsea captain, booed onto the pitch by those who once adored him. There were cheers when he was shown a yellow card for a foul on Rogers.

Kinsky produced another excellent save from Neto as the clock ticked past the hour mark.

Then came a flurry of substitutions and tempers frayed as the flashpoint featuring Palmer and Fernandes brought the game to the boil.

Who would have thought it would be Spurs to prevail.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer 'lost his head' in Chelsea's defeat by Spurs: Gary Neville hits out at Blues star after sending off and claims Morgan Rogers should also have seen red
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer 'lost his head' in Chelsea's defeat by Spurs: Gary Neville hits out at Blues star after sending off and claims Morgan Rogers should also have seen red

Gary Neville has claimed Cole Palmer 'lost his head' after the Chelsea star was sent off for two quick yellow cards in the defeat by Spurs on Saturday.

Palmer was booked after shoving Mateus Fernandes to the ground before being given his marching orders for what Neville called a 'very naughty' challenge on Conor Gallagher just minutes later.

His dismissal came after Chelsea had fallen behind when Mike Penders inadvertently punched the ball into his own net from a corner.

Ten-man Chelsea's misery was compounded as Mathys Tel doubled Spurs' lead late on as Roberto De Zerbi's side became only the second Tottenham team to win at Stamford Bridge in 36 years.

Speaking on Sky Sports during the game, Neville said: 'Cole Palmer has lost his head. To do that five minutes after the challenge on Fernandes is just silly.

'He sticks his studs in on him, he knows exactly what he's doing. It's not a good challenge. It is naughty, very naughty. He's experienced enough to know.'

Cole Palmer was sent off for two quick yellow cards in Chelsea's defeat by Spurs on Saturday

Neville said Palmer was fortunate not to see red for the push on Fernandes with the Blues forward furious at the midfielder's deliberate handball.

'Why has Palmer done that? I'm not sure why he reacts,' Neville said.

'Fernandes has handballed it and it's a clear yellow card. Palmer's reaction looks silly. He's asking for trouble.'

A frustrated Morgan Rogers was then booked in the dying moments for kicking Gallagher, a challenge Neville felt should have seen Chelsea reduced to nine.

'I think that's a red. I do,' Neville said.

'He's absolutely wellied him with no intent. That's ludicrous from Rogers. They have lost it. Xabi Alonso needs to get them off.'

Palmer will be available for Chelsea's next league game, at home to Manchester United on Saturday, despite the red card as he will serve his suspension when Alonso's men travel to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday.

Sports.title: Kimi Antonelli secures pole in Austin to boost chances of becoming world champion at US Grand Prix amid F1 calendar chaos
Sports.content:
Pole for Kimi Antonelli under the Texan sun. And so there is a decent chance this breezy, curly-haired kid could become world champion today, the youngest ever at 20, without anyone knowing it’s a fact for sure.
