Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Questions WBO Over Voluntary Defense Reversal
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley is challenging Gustavo Olivieri to explain what changed after claiming the WBO president publicly agreed to let him make a voluntary defense before facing mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez next year.

Bentley’s response follows Olivieri’s explanation that the organization never received a formal petition to approve the proposed fight against Shane Mosley Jr. The dispute leaves two different accounts of how Bentley’s planned voluntary defense reached this point.

“Whether I had an opponent or not this guy agreed and tweeted I get a voluntary defence before the end of the year then fight yo-yo next year which I was happy to do so the question everyone needs to ask is what changed,” Bentley wrote on X.

That is the question Bentley wants answered. His argument is that Olivieri had already accepted the sequence: a voluntary before the end of 2026, followed by Hernandez in 2027.

Olivieri, speaking to Tru School Sports, described a process that still required formal approval.

“We never received a formal petition. From Zuffa, from team Bentley, or from team Mosley for this particular fight.”

The WBO president added that every championship defense requires the approval of its championship committee, whether the opponent is a mandatory challenger or a voluntary selection.

According to Olivieri, Bentley had no date, opponent, or venue when the mandatory obligation needed to be addressed. Hernandez had been the designated challenger since July, and his team submitted a petition seeking enforcement.

Bentley is scheduled to face Mosley on November 7 in London, but the WBO rejected his appeal to take a voluntary defense and instructed him to commit to Hernandez. sports.yahoo.com

The wording of Olivieri’s earlier post is therefore crucial. An explicit agreement allowing Bentley to fight a voluntary before Hernandez would give the British fighter a reasonable basis to question the subsequent ruling. Permission dependent on committee approval would leave Bentley’s team responsible for completing that process.

A public conversation with the president and formal authorization from the championship committee may be separate steps. Bentley’s latest response does not explain whether his team submitted the details needed to secure that authorization.

Hernandez has his own interests to protect. He pursued his mandatory opportunity and asked the WBO to enforce it. Accepting Bentley’s preferred timetable would require him to wait while the champion takes another fight.

Bentley says he was willing to face Hernandez next year. The disagreement is over whether he had permission to take another opponent first—and whether Olivieri’s earlier words support the permission Bentley believes he received.

Sports.title: Alberto Puello Falls Short Against Dalton Smith
Sports.content:
Dalton “Thunder” Smith (20-0, 14 KOs) retained his WBC light welterweight title with a split decision over former champion Alberto “La Avispa” Puello (25-2, 11 KOs) on Saturday at a sold-out Utilita Arena in Sheffield, England.

Two judges scored the fight 115-113 for Smith, while the third had Puello ahead 115-112. Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Boxing promoted the event, which aired on DAZN.

The opening six rounds were closely contested, with this writer’s unofficial card even after Puello took the fifth and sixth.

Smith responded well in the seventh and eighth, edging the action as swelling appeared beneath Puello’s left eye. Puello answered with stronger work in the ninth and tenth before Smith took the 11th.

In the final round, a left hand from Puello opened a small cut on Smith’s right cheek. Smith began celebrating during the final 30 seconds, although the divided scorecards showed how close the contest had been.

Lee Every refereed.

Giorgio Visioli Edges Maxi Hughes

Unbeaten southpaw Giorgio “The Italian Job” Visioli (12-0, 6 KOs) defeated veteran Maxi “Maximus” Hughes (29-10-2, 6 KOs) by majority decision over ten rounds to win the vacant WBC International Silver lightweight title.

Two judges scored it 96-94 for Visioli, with the third returning a 95-95 draw.

Visioli’s effective jab helped him through much of the first seven rounds. Hughes opened a cut over Visioli’s left eyebrow with a right jab in the eighth, but Visioli responded and finished strongly enough to secure the decision. Kieran McCann refereed.

Shannon Ryan Stops Emma Dolan In Rematch

Shannon “Kaos” Ryan (12-1, 3 KOs) avenged her previous defeat to Emma Dolan (9-2, 1 KO) with a first-round stoppage in their scheduled ten-round super flyweight rematch.

Around 20 seconds into the fight, Ryan dropped Dolan with a right hand to the side of the face. Dolan rose, but another right followed by a left sent her down again.

Referee Howard Foster stopped the contest at 40 seconds after Dolan regained her feet.

Edward Hardy Outpoints Diego Ruiz

Edward Hardy (9-0, 3 KOs) remained unbeaten with an eight-round points victory over Diego “El Profeta” Ruiz (28-16-1, 14 KOs).

Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick scored it 79-73 for Hardy, who controlled most of the action from the second round onward.

Both fighters maintained a high work rate during an active final round, but Hardy finished with a clear points win.

Joe Hayden Defeats Will Harrison

Joe Hayden (25-0, 4 KOs) handed Will “The Thrill” Harrison (8-1-2, 0 KOs) his first professional defeat in their eight-round welterweight bout.

Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick scored it 79-72 for Hayden.

Leo Atang Scores Three Knockdowns In First-Round Stoppage

Nineteen-year-old heavyweight Leo Atang (9-0, 8 KOs) dropped Jonathan “Chicito” Vergara (9-5, 5 KOs) three times before stopping him in the opening round of their scheduled six-round contest.

A right hand dropped Vergara within the first minute. Atang scored another knockdown with a right to the side of the head with approximately 30 seconds remaining.

A third right hand sent Vergara down again in the closing seconds. Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick waved off the fight after Vergara rose, just before the bell.

Chris Mulunda Shuts Out Harley Collison

Chris “Mulla” Mulunda (5-0, 0 KOs) defeated Harley Collison (3-9-2, 0 KOs) by points over six rounds.

Referee Michael Alexander scored every round for Mulunda, returning a 60-54 verdict.

Divine Omojor Wins Professional Debut

Cruiserweight Divine Omojor (1-0, 1 KO) began his professional career with a second-round stoppage of Goran Kozul (8-13, 2 KOs).

Referee Michael Alexander stopped the scheduled four-round bout at 1:52 of the second.

David Diamante served as ring announcer.

Sports.title: Emanuel ‘Vaquero’ Navarrete Loses to O’Shaquie ‘Ice Water’ Foster!
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie “Ice Water” Foster defeated Emanuel “Vaquero” Navarrete by unanimous decision Saturday night at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, adding the WBO and IBF super featherweight titles to his WBC championship.

Foster scored two knockdowns in the final round and won by scores of 118-108, 118-108, and 115-111. The Top Rank event aired on DAZN.

Foster improved to 26-3 with 12 knockouts, while Navarrete fell to 40-3-1 with 33 knockouts.

Navarrete spent the opening round following Foster without consistently cutting off the ring, allowing Foster to land counters and move away. The second round became scrappier, with Foster tying Navarrete up when he closed the distance.

Navarrete had success with pressure in the third, but Foster’s movement and counterpunching helped him control much of the action over the following rounds. Foster hurt Navarrete during the seventh, forcing him to hold.

Both landed well in the tenth, with Navarrete producing some of his better offensive work. Navarrete also hurt Foster with a heavy shot late in the 11th, giving him encouragement entering the final round.

Foster responded with two knockdowns in the 12th. A counter right sent Navarrete to one knee, and referee Mark Nelson administered the count. Another counter right dropped Navarrete again in the final minute.

Navarrete rose both times and reached the bell, but Foster’s strong finish secured the victory.

Albert Gonzalez Knocks Out Edward Vazquez

NABF featherweight champion Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez improved to 19-0 with 12 knockouts by stopping Edward “Kid” Vazquez at 1:04 of the second round of their scheduled ten-round bout.

Vazquez, of Fort Worth, Texas, fell to 20-4 with six knockouts.

Gonzalez overwhelmed Vazquez with a prolonged attack in the second round, then followed him to another corner. Heavy punches to the body sent Vazquez to one knee, where referee Laurence Cole counted him out.

Frank Martin Stops Tarik Zaina

Southpaw Frank “The Ghost” Martin stopped Tarik “El Camello” Zaina at 2:38 of the seventh round to win the vacant NABO light welterweight title.

Martin improved to 20-1-1 with 14 knockouts, while Zaina dropped to 18-4-1 with 12 knockouts.

Martin had success early, but Zaina’s lead right hands helped keep the middle rounds competitive.

In the final minute of the seventh, Martin landed a combination beginning with a left to the chin that dropped Zaina. Zaina beat referee Angel Mendez’s count, but Martin immediately followed with a flurry that forced Mendez to stop the fight.

Deric Davis Shuts Out Joaquin Silva Faccio

Deric “Scooter” Davis defeated Joaquin Silva Faccio by unanimous decision in their eight-round lightweight bout, winning 80-72 on all three scorecards.

Davis improved to 13-0 with ten knockouts, while Faccio fell to 10-2 with four knockouts.

Davis consistently attacked the body and controlled the action. He hurt Faccio with a body shot late in the seventh, but the Uruguayan remained on his feet.

Faccio fought back in an active final round, though Davis completed the shutout. Laurence Cole refereed.

Samuel Contreras Outpoints Oscar Pedroza Padilla

Samuel Contreras remained unbeaten with a six-round unanimous decision over Oscar “El Perro” Pedroza Padilla in their lightweight contest.

All three judges scored it 60-54 for Contreras, who improved to 9-0 with three knockouts. Pedroza Padilla dropped to 8-3-1 with three knockouts.

Contreras hurt Pedroza Padilla with a flurry midway through the second round, leaving him with a bloody nose. Pedroza Padilla answered with an overhand right that rocked Contreras during a competitive fourth.

Contreras finished strongly, landing the cleaner punches over the closing rounds to secure the decision. Angel Mendez refereed.

Daniel Cortez Edges Joshua Montoya

Daniel III Cortez won a six-round split decision over Joshua “Spotlight” Montoya in their super bantamweight bout.

Two judges scored it 58-56 for Cortez, while the third had Montoya ahead by the same score.

Cortez improved to 14-1 with nine knockouts, while Montoya fell to 8-6-2 with one knockout.

Cortez’s work rate helped him through several close rounds, but Montoya stayed competitive and finished well in the sixth. His late effort wasn’t enough to secure the verdict. Laurence Cole refereed.

Joseph Almajdi Defeats Miqal Dolphus

Joseph Almajdi defeated Miqal Dolphus by unanimous decision in their six-round super welterweight opener, winning 60-54 on all three cards.

Almajdi improved to 6-1 with three knockouts, while Dolphus suffered his first professional defeat and fell to 6-1-1 with four knockouts.

A right hand from Almajdi buzzed Dolphus near the end of the third round. Almajdi also landed a left hook late in the fifth that drove Dolphus backward, helping him complete a clear points victory.

Angel Mendez refereed. Ralph Velez Jr. handled the preliminary ring introductions, with Jimmy Lennon Jr. announcing the main card.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Targets O’Shaquie Foster After Undisputed Run
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson called for a future fight with O’Shaquie Foster after watching him defeat Emanuel Navarrete, describing the newly unified super featherweight champion as an opponent who would motivate him to return to the ring.

Shakur left the timing open, indicating he would wait until Foster finishes pursuing undisputed status at 130 pounds. His challenge came after Foster collected Navarrete’s WBO and IBF belts to go with his WBC championship Saturday night.

“Helluva fighter he will never give me my credit but I’ll be real tonight he showed his level,” Shakur wrote on X. “That’s a challenge that would get me out of bed. Let’s do it whenever he’s ready.” He added: “I’ll be here after his undisputed run!”

Shakur’s challenge initially sounded immediate, but waiting until Foster becomes undisputed suggests he wants the fight to marinate before committing.

Foster earned the attention with a performance built on accurate counters, movement, and a strong finish. He dropped Navarrete twice in the 12th round and won by scores of 118-108, 118-108, and 115-111.

That was the kind of opponent Shakur could appreciate: a boxer who made an aggressive, awkward champion miss and repeatedly punished him for reaching. Foster also recovered from being hurt late in the 11th to deliver his most decisive round.

There was a competitive edge beneath Shakur’s praise. His claim that Foster would never give him credit made the message more than a congratulatory post, although he still recognized what Foster had accomplished.

The practical questions remain unanswered. Shakur did not name a weight, propose a date, or suggest negotiations had begun. Foster has just secured three belts at super featherweight, while Shakur holds the WBO light welterweight title.

A meeting would therefore require decisions about weight as well as timing. For now, Shakur has identified Foster as a challenge worth pursuing, while giving him room to chase the remaining championship at 130 before discussing a fight.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Drops Emanuel Navarrete Twice To Unify
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster knocked Emanuel Navarrete down twice in the final round to complete a unanimous decision victory and unify three super featherweight titles Saturday night at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.

The judges scored it 118-108, 118-108, and 115-111 for Foster, who retained his WBC belt and took Navarrete’s WBO and IBF championships. He also claimed the vacant Ring Magazine title in the DAZN main event.

Foster’s accuracy and movement frustrated Navarrete through much of the contest. He landed leaping left hooks early, followed with straight punches, and stepped away before Navarrete could bring his heavier attacks into play. Navarrete kept advancing but frequently found himself reaching and missing.

The third round offered Navarrete a route back into the fight. He caught Foster near the ropes, landed to the body, and threw a prolonged combination that forced the American onto defense. His pressure was more effective when he closed the distance before letting his hands go.

Foster adjusted in the fourth, taking the initiative with body jabs and counters. Over the middle rounds, he repeatedly beat Navarrete to the punch, landing straight shots and a sharp counter uppercut while using movement and clinches to interrupt the return attacks.

Navarrete remained dangerous despite struggling to sustain his offense. He landed some of his cleanest punches during a competitive tenth round, then hurt Foster with a heavy shot near the end of the 11th. That moment gave the closing stages an uncertainty the earlier rounds had often lacked.

Foster removed it in the 12th. With Navarrete chasing a knockout, Foster landed counter right hands that produced two knockdowns. Navarrete rose both times, but he couldn’t turn the fight around.

The finish strengthened a performance built on cleaner punching and better control of distance. Navarrete’s persistence kept him threatening late, but Foster made him pay for the risks he took and left with three world titles at 130 pounds.

Sports.title: Emanuel Navarrete vs. O’Shaquie Foster Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Albert Gonzalez (19-0, 12 KOs) knocked out Edward Vazquez (20-4, 6 KOs) with a second-round body attack to retain his NABF featherweight title. Gonzalez had a quiet opening round before increasing his aggression sharply in the second.

He hurt Vazquez early in the round and followed with short, compact combinations that left the challenger struggling to recover. Gonzalez kept attacking downstairs, landing heavy body punches, including a left hook, before Vazquez went to the canvas. Vazquez couldn’t beat the count, with referee Laurence Cole counting him out.

The unbeaten Gonzalez needed fewer than two rounds to defeat a former world title challenger in the scheduled ten-round co-main event. The knockout ended Vazquez’s three-fight winning streak and gave Gonzalez another early finish following his second-round victory over Aaron Alameda in July.

Frank “The Ghost” Martin (20-1-1, 14 KOs) stopped Tarik Zaina (18-4-1, 12 KOs) in the seventh round to win the vacant NABO light welterweight title. Martin started cautiously, allowing the taller Zaina to keep the early rounds competitive with his reach and awkward style.

Zaina landed a couple of solid power shots in the third, giving Martin more to consider as he searched for openings. Through five rounds, Martin had yet to take firm control, with his opponent continuing to find occasional success at long range.

That changed in the seventh when Martin stepped back and dropped Zaina with a hard left hand. Zaina beat the count, but Martin immediately attacked with follow-up punches that forced the referee to stop the fight.

The finish handed Zaina his first stoppage defeat and gave Martin a needed victory after his February draw with Nahir Albright.

Deric “Scooter” Davis (13-0, 10 KOs) swept all eight rounds against Joaquin Silva Faccio (10-2, 4 KOs), winning a unanimous decision in their lightweight bout. All three judges scored it 80-72 for Davis, who controlled the action from the opening round.

Faccio came forward aggressively, but Davis picked him off with straight punches and used defensive movement to avoid much of the return fire. Davis continued landing the cleaner shots as Faccio’s awkward footwork did little to disrupt his accuracy.

In the sixth, Davis attacked the body with hard punches that left Faccio trying unsuccessfully to match his work. Faccio absorbed considerable punishment but kept fighting back through an active finish. There were no knockdowns, with Davis having to settle for a wide points victory against an opponent tough enough to last the distance.

Super bantamweight Daniel III Cortez (14-1, 9 KOs) edged Joshua “Spotlight” Montoya (8-6-2, 1 KO) by split decision. Two judges scored it 58-56 for Cortez, while the third favored Montoya by the same score. Cortez entered as the favorite but had to work for the victory against an opponent who kept the contest close.

Cortez’s busier work helped him in the third round, although Montoya came on toward the end of it. Neither fighter scored a knockdown, leaving the judges to separate them after six competitive rounds.

Montoya made a strong case for the decision, with ringside observer Francisco Salazar scoring the fight 58-56 in his favor. Cortez ultimately secured his 14th professional victory, but the divided scorecards reflected how little separated the two fighters.

Lightweight Samuel “Sammy” Contreras (9-0, 3 KOs) remained unbeaten with a six-round unanimous decision over Oscar Pedroza Padilla (8-3-1, 3 KOs). All three judges scored it 60-54 for Contreras, who controlled most of the action.

Contreras punished Pedroza Padilla through the first three rounds, leaving the Mexican fighter struggling to find an answer. Pedroza Padilla rallied in the fourth, getting inside and landing enough shots to draw a response from the crowd. Contreras regained control in the fifth, delivering more punishment and stopping his opponent from building on that success.

The fight went the distance without a knockdown, giving Contreras his ninth professional victory.

Joseph Almajdi (6-1, 3 KOs) handed Miqal Dolphus (6-1-1, 4 KOs) his first professional defeat, winning a six-round unanimous decision in their junior middleweight bout. All three judges scored the opening preliminary contest 60-54 for Almajdi.

Using his height and reach, Almajdi established distance with his jab and followed with straight right hands. Dolphus pressed forward and attacked the body, trying to get inside the taller fighter’s reach.

The middle rounds brought lively action, with Dolphus finding some success but Almajdi producing the cleaner work. Almajdi’s footwork and timing helped him control the distance often enough to sweep the scorecards.

Neither fighter scored a knockdown, with Almajdi earning his sixth professional victory and Dolphus going the distance despite struggling to impose his pressure.

Sports.title: Albert Gonzalez Knocks Out Edward Vazquez In Two
Sports.content:
Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez broke through Edward Vazquez’s defenses with a punishing body attack, scoring a second-round knockout to retain his NABF featherweight title Saturday night at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.

The unbeaten Gonzalez improved to 19-0 with 12 knockouts in the scheduled ten-round co-main event on the Emanuel Navarrete–O’Shaquie Foster card on DAZN. Vazquez dropped to 20-4 with six knockouts, losing his three-fight winning streak.

Gonzalez gave little away about the approaching finish during a quiet opening round. The 24-year-old allowed Vazquez to be the more active fighter while taking time to find his distance. There was no sustained attack from Gonzalez, and the veteran challenger had an opportunity to get started without immediately being forced into survival mode.

That changed quickly in the second.

Gonzalez hurt Vazquez early and moved straight into his finishing work, throwing short combinations rather than giving the challenger time to recover. His punches downstairs did the most damage, with a left hook to the body among the blows that sent Vazquez to the canvas.

Referee Laurence Cole completed the ten-count with Vazquez unable to rise in time. Once Gonzalez increased his output, the fight went from a cautious start to a one-sided finish.

The result followed Gonzalez’s second-round body-shot knockout of Aaron Alameda in July, when he won the vacant NABF belt. Trained by Robert Garcia, Gonzalez again showed how quickly his compact punches can become decisive when an opponent remains within range.

Vazquez brought experience against Joe Cordina and Rafael Espinoza, along with recent winning form, but neither helped him absorb Gonzalez’s body attack. He had entered after three consecutive victories, including a decision over Daniel Lugo.

Gonzalez still needs tougher tests before his championship potential can be judged fully. This performance, however, gives his team reason to seek a higher-level opponent: Vazquez never had time to make his experience count once Gonzalez began landing heavily.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia vs Teofimo Lopez Targets February 6
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are targeting February 6 for their next fight, with negotiations continuing despite uncertainty over Lopez’s WBA title and Garcia’s pursuit of Floyd Mayweather Jr.

Mike Coppinger reports that neither the WBA’s decision nor the possibility of a Mayweather fight is expected to interfere with those discussions. That puts Garcia–Lopez ahead of the Mayweather matchup, which has generated plenty of talk without producing an agreement.

“Would be surprised if Garcia-Teofimo didn’t take place next,” Coppinger wrote on X. “Feb. 6 is the targeted date right now as talks continue.”

The date is still a target. There is no confirmed fight announcement, but the report gives Garcia’s next move a clearer direction after his attorney and adviser, Guadalupe Valencia, promoted the financial potential of facing Mayweather.

Valencia’s comments left the timetable dependent on Mayweather becoming available. Coppinger’s reporting places that possibility further down the road, with Teofimo first.

A Garcia–Lopez fight would give Ryan an opponent whose threat comes from what he can do today. Mayweather’s name would sell the event, but Teofimo offers a competitive fight between two active stars with something to lose.

The WBA situation remains a separate question. Jack Catterall has been pursuing his ordered fight with Lopez, while Teofimo has sought permission to pursue Garcia instead. Coppinger’s report indicates negotiations can continue regardless of the ruling; it does not establish whether Lopez will retain his championship.

That affects how the fight can eventually be promoted. Garcia–Lopez has an appeal with or without two belts, but calling it a confirmed unification would be premature until Lopez’s title position is settled.

Garcia also has reason to keep his attention on the opponent closest to becoming a reality. Selling a Mayweather fight before reaching terms with Teofimo risks making the more competitive matchup sound like a preliminary step.

For now, February 6 is the date to watch. Mayweather remains a possible later payday, while Garcia and Lopez work toward the fight Coppinger expects to happen next.

Ghana News.title: MUSIGA warns musicians against glorifying online fraud
Ghana News.content:
The Musicians Union of Ghana (MUSIGA) has cautioned musicians against making public statements that could be interpreted as encouraging or glorifying online fraud and other cyber-related crimes.

In a statement signed by its President, Bessa Simons, MUSIGA said it respected musicians’ right to express opinions on governance, unemployment, corruption and the administration of justice, but stressed that such concerns should not be used to justify criminal conduct.

“While MUSIGA respects every musician’s right to express opinions on governance, unemployment, corruption, and the fair administration of justice, we state emphatically that no grievance against public institutions justifies statements that may appear to normalize fraud, portray suspected offenders as heroes, or discourage cooperation with lawful investigations,” the statement said.

The Union’s statement follows comments Shatta Wale made during ShattaFest in Accra on 17 October 2026, which suggested that he was encouraging young people to engage in fraud.

“Me I do my music for over 25 years. I buy Rolls Royce, I buy Lamborghini all from my music. Then somebody go go talk somebody say Shatta Wale he dey do fraud.

“Make I tell you today. I get plenty fraud boys who be my friends but me I no be snitch wey I go snitch anybody. The country no good so if you go fraud, fraud,” he said in Pidgin English.

Shatta Wale’s comments have since generated widespread discussion, with some critics expressing concern that his influence could negatively affect society, particularly young people.

MUSIGA warned that online fraud causes real harm to victims, damages Ghana’s international reputation, threatens legitimate digital businesses and endangers the future of young people.

It therefore urged musicians, particularly those with large followings and influence among young people, to avoid statements, performances and social media posts that could be construed as promoting or defending internet fraud, money laundering, romance scams, identity theft and other forms of cybercrime.

“Musicians must understand that their words carry weight. A stage, concert platform, interview, or social-media account is not a private space; it is a powerful channel of public influence,” the statement added.

The Union said using such platforms to excuse criminal conduct, attack lawful enforcement actions or indirectly encourage fraudulent activities was irresponsible and inconsistent with the values of the music profession.

However, MUSIGA acknowledged that concerns about selective justice, corruption, youth unemployment and accountability were legitimate national issues that musicians had every right to raise.

It maintained that criticism of public institutions and demands for justice should be pursued constructively without appearing to endorse unlawful behaviour.

“However, criticism of injustice must never become a justification for crime,” the statement stressed.

The Union called on artistes to channel their influence towards addressing the challenges confronting young people by advocating employment opportunities, supporting digital-skills training, promoting financial literacy and entrepreneurship, and speaking out against corruption and fraud.

It urged the music industry to contribute to solutions that would help young people pursue lawful and productive livelihoods rather than expose themselves to criminal activities.

MUSIGA also cautioned musicians against making statements that could expose them or their fans to legal, reputational or professional consequences.

“Every musician must remember that fame does not place them above the law, and artistic freedom does not include the freedom to encourage unlawful conduct,” the statement said.

The Union reaffirmed its commitment to protecting the rights and welfare of musicians but warned that it would not remain silent when public statements by members threatened the credibility of the profession and the safety of Ghanaian youth.

It called on musicians to use their platforms responsibly, defend the dignity of Ghana’s creative industry and inspire young people to pursue success through lawful and productive means.

Ghana News.title: Mahama describes AfCFTA as Africa’s ‘greatest architecture for conflict prevention’
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama

President John Dramani Mahama has called for deeper economic integration among African countries, describing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) as a major instrument for preventing conflict and strengthening peaceful relations across the continent.

Speaking at the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Peace in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, President Mahama presented the 2026 State of Peace and Security in Africa Report, covering developments from January 2025 to June 2026.

He argued that the AfCFTA should not be viewed solely as a commercial initiative, but also as a framework for reducing tensions by making African countries more economically interdependent.

“We often view the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) purely as a commercial project. That is a mistake. The AfCFTA is perhaps our greatest architecture for conflict prevention,” he said.

President Mahama explained that stronger trade links could increase the economic cost of conflict and encourage countries to see their neighbours as valuable trading partners and suppliers rather than adversaries.

He also said integrated and traceable value chains could help dismantle illicit economies associated with smuggled minerals, illegal taxation at roadblocks and the activities of warlords.

The President further highlighted the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), which facilitates cross-border payments in African currencies, as another mechanism for strengthening regional economic ties and reducing Africa’s exposure to external economic shocks.

However, he cautioned that economic integration alone could not resolve conflicts, stressing that political agreements and settlements remained necessary for lasting peace.

“Trade cannot replace political settlement, but poverty and border friction will always guarantee war,” he said.

President Mahama urged African countries to strengthen regional cooperation and address the economic conditions that fuel instability, arguing that sustainable peace must be supported by both security measures and economic justice.

Ghana News.title: Africa needs stronger digital payment links to unlock regional trade – Femi Osinbajo
Ghana News.content:
Professor Yemi Osinbajo, a former Vice-President of Nigeria, has called for stronger cooperation among African countries to improve cross-border payments, strengthen digital integration and support trade and investment across the continent.

He said although African countries had made progress in developing domestic payment systems, transferring money across borders remained difficult and costly for traders, businesses and individuals.

Prof. Osinbajo was speaking at the opening of the Mobex Africa Conference 2026 on the theme: ” Resetting Africa’s Digital Identity and Sovereignty from Promise to Practice.”

He said some transactions still depended on correspondent banking arrangements outside the countries involved, often introducing additional intermediaries and costs.

The former Vice-President said the challenges could undermine efforts to deepen regional economic integration and expand opportunities for businesses operating across national borders.

He said initiatives such as the African Continental Free Trade Area and digital transformation programmes demonstrated the continent’s commitment to integration, but their success depended partly on efficient, secure and accessible payment systems.

He called for stronger collaboration among central banks, financial institutions, governments, and other relevant authorities to improve connections between national payment systems.

He said integration required more than technical partnerships, stressing the importance of trust, common standards and effective regulatory cooperation among African countries.

The former Vice-President said digital integration must also protect financial stability and ensure that improved connectivity did not introduce risks into national financial systems.

He urged governments to establish supportive policy environments, while central banks strengthened the resilience of financial infrastructure and financial institutions developed services that responded to the needs of households and businesses.

He said digital financial services could create opportunities for traders and small businesses by improving access to financial information and enabling lenders to make better-informed decisions.

He, however, stressed the need to protect customers, ensure fair lending terms and provide safeguards when technology failed or payment transactions encountered problems.

The former Vice-President said accessible digital identification and straightforward verification processes were also important to making financial services available to more people.

He noted that concerns about data exposure and increased visibility to authorities could discourage some traders from participating in formal digital financial systems.

He called for safeguards to protect personal and business information and ensure that users could benefit from digital services without compromising their privacy or rights.

Mr Owureku Asare, Director of the Fintech and Innovation Office at the Bank of Ghana, highlighted Ghana’s experience in developing payment infrastructure to improve connectivity among banks, microfinance institutions and other service providers.

He said Ghana’s experience demonstrated that public investment, strong institutional leadership and enabling regulation could support secure and accessible payment systems while allowing financial institutions to innovate and compete.

Mr Asare said Ghana remained committed to working with other central banks, regional institutions and industry partners to improve the efficiency and connectivity of payment systems across Africa.

Ghana News.title: Africa must prove climate adaptation is saving lives, not just spending money
Ghana News.content:
When floods leave roads impassable, water supplies become contaminated and children fall ill, the consequences of climate change are measured in more than damaged infrastructure or financial losses. They are measured in lives disrupted, household incomes lost and families struggling to cope.

For Dr Richard Munang, Director of the United Nations University Institute for Natural Resources in Africa (UNU-INRA), these are the realities that must shape how Africa measures progress on climate adaptation.

“Adaptation is not what we spend. Adaptation is who we protect,” he told participants at the African Technical Workshop on the Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA) Indicators in Accra.

The three-day workshop, held from 22 to 24 October 2026 at the West African Genetic Medicine Centre, brought together African climate negotiators, government officials, technical experts and representatives of the United Nations University and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

Its central task was to test whether the global adaptation indicators can adequately reflect Ghana’s national priorities, what existing data systems can measure and where gaps must be addressed.

The exercise comes as countries begin working with the 59 Belém Adaptation Indicators adopted under the Global Goal on Adaptation process. For African countries, the challenge is no longer simply to agree on a framework for measuring adaptation, but to determine whether it captures the results that matter to people and communities.

Measuring what matters to people

Dr Munang argued that climate adaptation must be judged by its impact on people’s lives, rather than by the amount of money allocated or spent.

Drawing on his childhood in north-western Cameroon, where failed maize harvests left his family struggling to find food, he recalled how climate pressures can deepen the vulnerability of households already facing economic hardship.

That experience, he said, reinforced the need to connect adaptation policies and investments to tangible improvements in people’s lives.

“Because if you don't count what is failing, you cannot fix it,” he said, calling for evidence that identifies both successful interventions and those that fall short.

He pointed to the links between disaster risks and public health, arguing that poorly maintained drainage systems, flooded roads and delayed early-warning messages can have consequences that extend well beyond the immediate disaster.

A flooded road can prevent an ambulance from reaching someone in need. Contaminated water can expose children to waterborne diseases. When early warnings fail to reach communities in time, the consequences can be devastating.

These connections underpin the workshop’s decision to focus on disaster risk reduction and health, two areas where the effectiveness of adaptation measures can have direct consequences for human wellbeing.

For UNU-INRA, working with the United Nations University International Institute for Global Health offers an opportunity to examine these connections more closely and strengthen the evidence used to assess adaptation outcomes.

Ghana’s national priorities take centre stage

Ghana is serving as the pilot country for the exercise, providing an opportunity to compare its National Adaptation Plan and sector priorities with the global indicators.

The assessment is intended to establish where national priorities align with the indicators, where important outcomes may be missing and whether the data and institutional arrangements needed for reporting are already in place.

Director of the United Nations University International Institute for Global Health, Dr Revathi Phalkey, said the exercise should help countries determine whether their existing systems can adequately measure progress towards their adaptation ambitions.

“What we really need to measure is where do we need to go and how fast we can get there,” she said.

Her remarks underscored the importance of looking beyond historical performance to assess the pace and scale of action needed to meet future adaptation goals.

Representing the Chair of the Africa Group of Negotiators, Stella Okoh of Ghana’s Environmental Protection Authority said the workshop would help institutions identify how existing national reporting systems could be used to track the indicators.

“The conversation is not to create different reporting formats,” she said, explaining that the priority was to build on existing national systems, identify gaps and determine what needed to improve.

She also highlighted the importance of monitoring whether adaptation interventions were actually building resilience in Ghana.

The approach is expected to bring together institutions responsible for climate adaptation, health, disaster management and reporting, helping them assess what information is available and where additional work is required.

From global indicators to national action

For the UNFCCC Secretariat, the exercise forms part of the wider effort to establish how the global indicators can be applied across different national contexts.

Motsomi Maletjane of the Secretariat’s Adaptation Division said countries had agreed to test the indicators voluntarily following their adoption at COP30. The resulting experience will help inform the development of indicator metadata and methodologies, as well as assessments of their applicability to national circumstances.

“These exercises by Ghana, many other countries that are doing similar exercises are very key to being able to tell how countries can start to work with the indicators,” he said.

The findings are also expected to contribute to countries’ reporting on adaptation progress and inform their own planning processes.

For Ghana, the workshop’s practical work centres on mapping national adaptation priorities against the relevant indicators, examining data availability and identifying methodological, institutional, technical and financial gaps.

Participants are also expected to develop recommendations for addressing those gaps and identify lessons that could be adapted by other African countries.

Building an evidence-based African position

Beyond the technical assessment, the exercise carries implications for Africa’s engagement in international climate negotiations.

Dr Munang said the continent needed evidence to demonstrate whether adaptation investments were delivering results and whether the global indicators adequately reflected African priorities.

He argued that indicators should not be accepted simply because they form part of an international framework. Where they fail to capture national ambitions or outcomes, countries should be able to demonstrate the shortcomings and make the case for improvement.

“Africa is not poor. Africa is uncounted,” he said, stressing the importance of strengthening the evidence available to African policymakers and negotiators.

The workshop is expected to produce an assessment of Ghana’s alignment with the indicators, a review of implementation gaps, practical guidance for future country-level exercises and policy messages to support African engagement ahead of COP31 and COP32.

The wider ambition is to develop an approach that other African countries can use to assess the indicators against their own adaptation plans, priorities and reporting systems.

For Dr Munang, however, the ultimate test remains whether adaptation makes a measurable difference to ordinary people.

“We can only say we have adapted if that child who is playing aside today will not end up in a clinic tomorrow,” he said.

That challenge places the focus firmly on outcomes of whether communities are better protected from disasters, whether health risks are reduced and whether public investments are building resilience where it is needed most.

As Ghana undertakes the pilot assessment, its findings could help shape a more practical approach to measuring adaptation across Africa, one that connects international commitments to national priorities and, ultimately, to the lives those commitments are intended to protect.

Ghana News.title: PIAC seeks details of petroleum funds allocated to Big Push projects
Ghana News.content:
The Public Interest and Accountability Committee (PIAC) released its 2026 semi-annual report on Ghana’s petroleum revenue management, noting that additional information on how the government uses petroleum revenues allocated to the national budget would strengthen its assessment of government expenditure.

Mr Richard Ellimah, Chairman of PIAC, said the Committee had yet to receive information from the Ministry of Finance on the utilisation of the Annual Budget Funding Amount (ABFA), which limited its ability to fully assess expenditure under the programme.

He made this known at the launch of PIAC’s 2026 semi-annual report in Accra, explaining that the Committee had requested the data from the Ministry but was still awaiting a response.

Mr Ellimah said the information was particularly important for monitoring expenditure on infrastructure projects, including the government’s Big Push Agenda, which includes the construction of the Accra-Kumasi Expressway.

He said the concentration of a significant proportion of the ABFA in the Big Push programme could also influence how PIAC conducted its project inspections.

“We are hoping very much that the Ministry of Finance will give us the data so we can understand what is going on,” he said.

“It is something new for us because it is going to change the way we also do our project inspections.”

Mr Ellimah also called for greater attention to compliance with the legal provisions governing the provision of information to PIAC.

He said in the Committee’s 15 years of operation, he was not aware of any prosecution for failure to comply with the Petroleum Revenue Management Act (PRMA).

PIAC intended to engage the Attorney-General for guidance on addressing recurring compliance concerns, he said, noting that the Committee could not independently initiate legal action to enforce its recommendations or compliance with the Act.

“These are clearly legal infractions,” he said, adding that the Attorney-General’s advice would help determine the appropriate course of action.

PIAC was established under Section 51 of the PRMA to promote transparency and accountability in the management and use of petroleum revenues.

Its mandate includes monitoring compliance with the Act and providing independent information to the public to support informed debate and Parliament’s oversight responsibilities.

Mr Isaac Dwamena, PIAC’s Executive Secretary, said the Petroleum Revenue Management Regulations specified the timeframe within which institutions were expected to respond to the Committee’s requests for information.

Regulation 25 requires institutions requested to provide information for PIAC’s annual and semi-annual reports to do so within 15 days of receiving the request.

Despite the outstanding information, the report assessed developments in petroleum revenue collection, production, expenditure and the management of the country’s petroleum funds during the first half of 2026.

It said petroleum revenue receipts increased to US$561.4 million in the first half of 2026, from US$370.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

The increase was attributed largely to higher crude oil prices and a rise in corporate income tax receipts.

The average achieved crude oil price was US$92.80 per barrel, above the benchmark price of US$76 per barrel.

PIAC, however, cautioned that the increase in revenue was driven substantially by higher prices rather than a corresponding rise in production.

It highlighted the vulnerability of petroleum receipts to fluctuations in the international oil market.

Ghana News.title: NRSA praises Sunyani inner ring road project, raises concern over tricycle speeding
Ghana News.content:
The National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) in the Bono Region has lauded the quality of work on the Sunyani-Inner Ring Road Project, being funded by the government's “Big Push” Road Infrastructure programme.

Mr Gabriel Kwame Okyere, the Public Relations Officer at the Bono Regional Office of the NRSA, however, cautioned tricycle riders in particular against reckless riding.

Kofi Job Constructions Limited, contractors executing the 9.2-kilometre Road Project from Fiapre Roundabout, connecting the Sunyani Technical University, has asphalted the road.

In an interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA) in Sunyani, Mr Okyere said: “Our major concern now is how tricycle riders are speeding on the road since it was asphalted”.

“In fact, the office continues to receive complaints of recklessness by the tricycle riders, using portions of the asphalted road project”, he stated.

He commended the government for the ‘Big Push’ programme, saying that the inner ring road project had opened the Sunyani Municipality for economic growth.

Mr Okyere said small-scale businesses had started springing up along the road project, since it was asphalted, thereby creating economic opportunities for the locals.

In a separate interview, Mr Kofi Kamkam, the site engineer of Kofi Job Construction Limited, said 2.5 kilometres of the road project had been asphalted for use, assuring that the project would be completed within the two-year stipulated period.

Ghana News.title: Mahama warns foreign powers against treating Africa as a ‘chessboard’
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama

President John Dramani Mahama has urged African leaders to unite against foreign interference and protect the continent’s sovereignty, warning that external powers are seeking strategic influence and access to Africa’s resources.

Speaking at the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, he said African countries must take greater control of their political, economic, and security priorities instead of allowing foreign interests to determine their future.

“External powers, from the East, the West, and the Gulf, are actively seeking leverage, access, and client states on our soil,” President Mahama said.

He warned that Africa risked becoming a battleground for competing foreign interests if its leaders failed to act collectively and establish a common vision for the continent.

“Africa is not an empty chessboard for foreign powers to play their games. We are not spectators,” he added.

President Mahama stressed that African countries must take the initiative in shaping their own future, cautioning that failure to do so could leave the continent at the mercy of decisions made by others.

“But unless we consciously decide to take up the pen and write our own script, someone else will write it for us, and we will not like how the story ends,” he said.

The President called for stronger continental unity and greater African ownership of political, economic and security decisions, arguing that the continent must define its priorities and safeguard its sovereignty amid growing competition for influence.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod will not compromise LBMA certification for galamsey – Minkah
Ghana News.content:
Prince Kwame Minkah, Media Relations Officer

The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has rejected suggestions that it would support illegal mining, insisting that doing so would undermine its efforts to secure certification from the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA).

The Board’s Head of Communications, Prince Kwame Minkah, said responsible sourcing was a key requirement for the certification, which demands that gold entering the market comes from legitimate sources and is produced without causing environmental destruction.

He explained that GoldBod’s ambition to meet international standards meant it could not endorse mining activities that violate the law or damage the environment.

“Nobody should fall under any delusion that the CEO of GoldBod, whose institution is aspiring for LBMA Certification, would endorse illegal mining, especially when the prerequisite for LBMA Certification is responsible sourcing,” he said.

Mr Minkah’s comments follow public criticism of GoldBod Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi over remarks concerning efforts to formalise unlicensed small-scale miners.

Mr Gyamfi subsequently clarified that his position was to bring eligible operators into a regulated system, rather than endorse illegal mining.

Speaking on Channel One TV on Saturday, October 24, Mr Minkah said his intervention was intended to reinforce Mr Gyamfi’s position on transitioning eligible miners into lawful operations.

The LBMA is a global authority in the precious metals market, with standards covering the quality of gold and silver as well as responsible sourcing.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Israeli forces turn Hebron homes into military posts amid lockdown
World.content:
Israeli forces have turned Palestinian homes in the city of Hebron into barracks and observation posts after forcing residents to leave, as a military operation in the southern occupied West Bank continues, the Palestinian news agency Wafa has reported.

They took over homes in the Khallat Manna and Dahiyat al-Zaytoun areas of southern Hebron to use them as barracks, and forced residents from homes in other neighbourhoods to use the properties as observation posts, Wafa said, citing sources.

The Israeli military has imposed a lockdown in Hebron and conducted hundreds of raids since two armed Palestinian men allegedly carried out an attack on an Israeli army reserve base on Friday, killing two soldiers. The two suspects were also killed.

The evictions follow the forced displacement of hundreds of families amid extensive raids, road closures and tight restrictions on movement.

According to the Palestinian Prisoner’s Society, Israeli forces have detained at least 47 Palestinians across Hebron since Friday, while forcibly displacing 293 families, comprising about 2,200 people.

Among those displaced from Hebron are 127 infants, 81 pregnant women and 26 people with disabilities, the NGO told Al Jazeera. The displaced also include 134 Palestinians with chronic illnesses and 265 elderly people over the age of 60.

Israeli troops also conducted hundreds of field interrogations, subjecting Palestinians to detention and abuse, the group said.

New settler outposts

Meanwhile, Israeli settlers began establishing two new outposts on Palestinian-owned land in the town of Yatta, south of Hebron, Wafa reported.



Activist Osama Makhamra told Wafa that settlers began setting up an outpost in the Khallet al-Fara area, west of Yatta, where they pitched a tent, brought in bulldozers and excavation machinery, and started levelling and digging the land in preparation for construction.

He added that another outpost was established in the Yatta desert area, on Palestinian-owned land between the villages of az-Zuweidin and Umm Qussa, where settlers pitched several tents and began installing infrastructure, including water and electricity networks.

Near Bethlehem, Israeli forces continued to close roads and entrances across the governorate for the third consecutive day on Sunday, affecting several towns and villages, Wafa reported.

On Saturday, Israeli forces shut down dirt roads leading to Tuqu to block access, firing tear gas canisters and stun grenades towards Palestinian vehicles travelling along rough alternative routes near the town.

The latest attacks and closures come days before Israel’s general elections and as tensions remain high across the occupied Palestinian territory, where settlers, backed by the military, have carried out a wave of pogroms targeting olive harvesters.

World.title: Australian Grand Prix called off as rain spoils Phillip Island sendoff
World.content:
Race delayed by two hours before being cancelled due to low visibility despite a sellout crowd at Phillip Island.

The final Australian MotoGP at the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit has been called off due to heavy rain, ruining the farewell for one of the championship’s most beloved circuits.

It was a crushing blow for the sold-out crowd at Phillip Island on Sunday before the Australian Grand Prix moves to the streets of Adelaide next year.

The Moto2 and Moto3 races were cancelled first, and the MotoGP race was delayed by two hours due to the weather before organisers threw in the towel and finally called it off at 3:40pm (04:40 GMT).

“Due to limited visibility affecting the operation of the medical helicopter the MotoGP Grand Prix race has been cancelled,” MotoGP said in a statement.

“The MotoGP riders will do a lap behind the safety car and stop on the main straight to greet the fans.”

Riders say farewell to fans in final parade

The dark clouds and pelting rain brought down the visibility around the circuit, affecting the medical helicopter, which would take 45 minutes to reach the circuit from mainland Melbourne in an emergency.

Other than two years lost to the COVID-19 pandemic, the seaside track south of Melbourne had been a fixture on the world championship calendar for 30 years and produced some of Australian motorcycling’s most memorable moments.

Australian two-time world champion Casey Stoner celebrated six wins there in succession from 2007 to 2012 while compatriot Mick Doohan sealed his fifth and final world title with victory in the 1998 race.

The raincoat-clad fans who persevered through the precipitation were treated to a farewell lap from the MotoGP riders, who waved as they slowly made their way around a soaking wet track.



Home racer Jack Miller did his best to entertain his supporters with a series of tricks, including a stand-up wheelie over the finish line, before heading over to the grandstand and throwing his gloves and boots into the crowd.

Miller dejected, sigh of relief for Martin

The Pramac Racing rider, a strong performer in the wet, cut a dejected figure when he was interviewed after completing his lap.

“This is a tough pill to swallow,” said the 31-year-old, who will be leaving MotoGP at the end of the season after more than a decade to join Pata Maxus Yamaha in the World Superbike Championship.

“You know, I was praying for rain all weekend. We got the rain, but obviously, we weren’t organised enough to get the racing going, so it’s a tough one.

“You guys deserve better. Honestly, all of you have done a fantastic job turning out for Phillip Island.”

Rain had been expected for the weekend, but MotoGP did not revive its 2023 strategy for the circuit when the Grand Prix was moved ahead to Saturday and the sprint scheduled for Sunday.

That sprint race three years ago was eventually called off.

The cancellation of the race also ended the opportunity for seven-time MotoGP champion Marc Marquez to extend his lead in the championship standings, particularly after his title rival Jorge Martin was declared unfit to compete in the race after fracturing his wrist.

Martin held the championship lead heading into the weekend but finds himself 10 points behind Marquez after failing to finish Saturday’s sprint following a gruesome crash.

On Sunday, Martin’s Aprilia team said he would not travel back to Spain to undergo treatment, however, boosting the 2024 champion’s hopes of racing at next week’s Malaysian Grand Prix and remaining in the title fight.
