World.title: My wife died two years ago, then grief opened door for madness
World.content:
My Peju Akande

Mywife died two years ago. Before then, she had been sick for a long time; the kind of sickness that drains everybody in the house. You know that saying: “The person caring for the sick is sometimes sicker than the sick person.” It’s true. It’s painfully true.

I won’t stand here and claim I did all the caring. Her children, our children, carried that burden with full chest. They were her hands, her legs and her nurses. But she was still mywife. I did what I could, in my own small way. I put all my manhood on hold and accepted it as destiny.

You know what I mean.

When she died, the house became quiet in a way that frightens even an old man. There used to be noise, you know, the good kind. People trooping in and out.

Neighbours, people from our mosque, alfas, children she helped, women she advised, men she encouraged.

Big tree

Mywife was a big tree. When she fell, the shade disappeared. People came for the burial, stayed for a while, then left one by one like leaves falling off a branch.

And I was alone.

My children begged me to come and stay with them, but grief is a stubborn companion. I said I wanted to be alone. I didn’t realise loneliness has teeth. Not that I feared ghosts, if mywife appeared, even as a ghost, she wouldn’t harm me. She would probably scold me for misplacing my glasses, or my phone or even money.

Eventually, my children arranged someone to cook and clean. I was turning 80; I needed help. Even if it was someone to quarrel with. That’s how I met this woman at the mosque.

The ‘eleha’ who hid her evil under a burqa. She was an eleha, fully covered, soft‑spoken, eyes lowered. But I was fooled in my old age!

I’m not saying women who wear hijab or burqa are evil. No.

But this particular one used that covering to hide her wickedness like a snake hiding under dry leaves.

She was 45 when we met. She said her husband left her with three children. At my age, I wasn’t looking for romance. I have 11 grandchildren. My prostate is enlarged — so that department is closed for renovation.

Companionship

All I wanted was companionship, you know, someone to talk to. Someone to sit with, someone to keep me warm in the evenings.

I told her clearly: “I will help you financially. But I cannot father your children. They cannot live with me.”

She agreed, or she pretended to.

We started “seeing” each other quietly. I didn’t introduce her to my children, they would never accept it. But I’m sure they suspected.

That woman entered my life like a thief in the night and she has been stealing me blind. She stole more than Shina Rambo!

Do you know Shina Rambo? Ah, you are young. Shina Rambo was the most notorious armed robber in Nigeria in the 80s and 90s.

This woman? She stole more than him, without gun, without knife, without breaking the door. She would take my money and claim I gave her myself. She lies like someone who practices lying as a profession. I would put money on top of the fridge, she would take it and swear I took it myself.

I don’t have an ATM card, so I withdraw large sums at once. Before I know what is happening, fiam! All the money is gone. I told her I would help her financially. I didn’t tell her to help herself to my money like a rat eating ‘breadi agege’.

She turned me into an ATM machine, and that is what I will not accept. So I told her not to come to my house again. And I will stand by it. Because as old as I am, I have learned one bitter truth: loneliness is not enough reason to invite madness into your home!

•Series, first published in thisislagos.ng, was written and edited by Peju Akande and based on true stories

World.title: Soludo in Tinubu’s Campaign: ‘Bitter truth’ is South-East must align with centre — Sly Ezeokenwa, APGA National Chair
World.content:
Sly Ezeokenwa, APGA National Chair

•Dismisses anti-party claim against Anambra gov

By Dickson Omobola

National Chairman of the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, Sly Ezeokenwa, in this interview first aired on Arise News, speaks on the reasons Anambra State governor and national leader of APGA, Professor Charles Soludo, has pitched tent with President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 elections, despite concerns over alleged anti-party activities. Excerpts:

Your party, APGA, has adopted President Bola Tinubu, and your governor, Professor Charles Soludo, has now been named on APC list. What should this tell the average voter? Is this merely a symbolic show of strength and dominance by the APC? Would the allegation of anti-party activity apply to Professor Soludo?

I think it would be good to state that the decision of Professor Charles Soludo, who, by the way, is the national leader of our party, to support the President transcends their personal relationship. Once you become the leader of a party, the Constitution imposes certain obligations and responsibilities on you. In a multi-party democracy such as ours, coalitions are inevitable.

When you have about 22 political parties, as we currently do, with people from diverse ethnic groups and different religious backgrounds, you can be certain that any presidential candidate seeking to meet the constitutional threshold faces a considerable task. You must recall that to be elected president of Nigeria, the Constitution requires you to secure a simple majority and at least 25 per cent of the votes cast in at least two-thirds of the states in the country. You will agree with me that this is not an easy task for any presidential candidate in a multi-party democracy.

That, therefore, calls for broader coalitions. Those who are well versed in our politics will know that such coalitions have historical precedents. There have been instances of alliances and coalitions before independence, after independence, during the 1979 elections and beyond. For me, this is nothing new. However, our decision as a party to support the President stems from three perspectives, and I must make that emphatically clear. First, it draws from history. APGA has a standing policy under which the party considers a cordial relationship with the ruling party part of its strategic alliances and survival. You know very well that this policy was adopted around 2011.

Incidentally, the only governor on the platform of APGA at the time was the current presidential candidate of the NDC. That was when APGA adopted the presidential candidacy of the then President Goodluck Jonathan, a decision it repeated in 2015. Even in 2019 and 2023, when the party nominated its own presidential candidates, it did not derogate from that tradition of supporting the incumbent. Beyond the policy and historical perspectives, we come to the more germane issue. Our leader popularised an aphorism that, in a multi-party democracy, it does not make sense for every political party in the country to field a presidential candidate when some of those candidates are unlikely to secure even 50,000 votes.

If our affiliations and alliances in a multi-party democracy should be ideologically driven, then there is nothing wrong with political parties that profess similar ideologies coming together to support a common presidential candidate. That was how our leader popularised the phrase that progressives are working together, which stemmed from his charge or call during the President’s visit to Anambra. For our party specifically, there is a strong, longstanding alliance with the administration of President Bola Tinubu. That alliance led to the appointment of a serving member of APGA’s Board of Trustees, BoT, Bianca Ojukwu, as a minister in President Tinubu’s cabinet, as well as the appointment of another APGA member.

If you look at the 2023 elections, despite having much of the influence in the South-East, Peter Obi of the Labour Party secured over 90 per cent of the votes in the region. How will APGA’s influence change that result in favour of the APC, bearing in mind that Obi was once a member of APGA and would still have some supporters in your party? Obi is from Anambra and still wields that level of influence in the South-East. How would you turn the region in favour of President Bola Tinubu now that APGA has aligned with his candidacy?

As a party, we have our position, which is that we have endorsed and adopted the candidacy of President Bola Tinubu. That is a fact. Now, we have a critical issue involving a proud son of Anambra, the first governor elected on the platform of APGA, who is also running in this election. However, in this context, it is better for us to be politically correct as we approach the 2027 presidential election. It is a question of whether to be politically correct or join the bandwagon of sensationalism surrounding a particular candidate.

We believe that, before the advent of the current Fourth Republic in 1999, the promoters and founders of the ruling party, the PDP, came together and crafted an agreement. It was more or less an unwritten agreement on power rotation or power sharing between the North and the South. We believe that, whatever the circumstances, it is now the South’s turn. Someone from Southern Nigeria, President Bola Tinubu, is currently in office. So, the South has another four years, and it only makes sense to allow the South, through President Tinubu, to complete its tenure. That is one fact.

For us as a party, we believe it is our responsibility to tell the people the bitter truth, regardless of whose ox is gored or how people feel about it. That bitter truth is that we believe it has not served the interests of the South-East to continue on this trajectory of political alienation.

If you look at the data or statistics recently released by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, showing the percentage of registered voters across the country, the South-East accounts for, I think, about 11 per cent of registered voters. The question is whether the South-East, on its own, can produce a President without building a broader coalition with other regions. We believe that the roadmap to the presidency, for the foreseeable future, requires the South-East to find a way to align with the centre. If we align with the centre and other regions, we can return to the question at the appropriate time. For now, it is the South’s turn to complete its remaining four years through the incumbent President.

We believe it serves the interests of the South-East better to align with other regions by supporting President Tinubu’s bid for re-election. We see this as a means of bringing the South-East back into the equation. Since 2015, it has been our belief that the South-East has been left out of the scheme of things in the country. No matter how anybody feels about it, that is the bitter truth. It ought not to be so, but that is the reality on the ground.

You called Obi your precious son from Anambra and the first person to win the governorship on APGA’s platform. Why denigrate him openly for political reasons? Win or lose, the 2027 elections will be over by January 15, but the impact of the damage you people would do to your fellow Igbo man would never be forgotten. How do you react to that?

Emotions will get us nowhere. I head a political party; I do not run a charity organisation. As a political party, we make decisions based on what our leaders believe serves our strategic interests at a particular time. At this point, that means supporting President Bola Tinubu’s candidacy. It is the party’s decision, and, as I said, it is driven by historical alliances, policy and other factors. I have not seen any former governor who was given the kind of pre-eminence Peter Obi enjoyed under APGA. When he joined the party, APGA gave him its platform on a platter of gold, and he contested the election.

Barely six months after completing his tenure, he left the party. Since then, he has continuously worked against APGA. His only mission, in our view, is to annihilate the party. APGA has survived various attempts by Peter Obi to undermine it. Let us start from 2015. Barely a year after leaving the party, he joined the PDP and became part of the coalition forces working against APGA’s National Assembly candidates. This was despite the fact that APGA had adopted the candidacy of President Goodluck Jonathan at the time. In 2017, Peter Obi was instrumental in the emergence of Chief Willie Obiano. However, that same year, he backed another candidate and took that candidate across the state. We have videos of him calling the then governor of the state a drunkard at a campaign rally.

In 2021, he repeated the same thing, supporting another candidate. Despite all this, Professor Charles Soludo, who became governor in 2022, recognised that Obi was a son of the state and a former member of the party. He invited him back to APGA because we believed that building that brotherly alliance was necessary if we were to have a shot at the presidency. President Bola Tinubu, the brother you referred to, built alliances across the South-West before taking office. Even when the time came for him to run for President, he stepped aside from his ambition to support another presidential candidate because he believed it was not the right time for him to contest. That is what a true leader who has the interests of his people at heart does.

A quick flaw in your argument: you said that when Peter Obi left, he still returned to work with the party to ensure Willie Obiano’s emergence. Did he not?

No, no, no. That is wrong.

Who worked for Obiano’s emergence?

He was still in the party when he worked for Obiano’s emergence.

The part of the story you have not mentioned is that all this started when they fell out.

You are wrong. They did not fall out before he left the party. Immediately after Peter Obi handed over to Obiano on March 17, 2014, some Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, governors visited him at his residence somewhere in Onitsha and invited him to join the party. If you recall, he never said at the time that he had fallen out with Obiano. He called APGA a special purpose vehicle.

But you have just made my point. He was elected, helped APGA win re-election and handed over an APGA government in the state when he left…

We have never denied that Peter Obi helped us to get re-elected. But you are putting the cart before the horse. The fact is that APGA first did someone a favour by offering him its platform in 2003. When he was rigged out, APGA members went to the tribunal to defend his mandate. They testified, presented certified true copies of result sheets and tendered them as evidence, leading to the historic overturning of the declaration of then Governor Chris Ngige. So, you must give APGA credit.

Now that your party is supporting President Tinubu, we have heard that in Edo State, the APC expects to deliver 2.5 million votes. In Osun, the Accord Party says it will deliver 1.8 million votes. How many votes will APGA deliver?

For me, it is not about figures. It is about presenting our people with the facts, the truth and, as it were, the bitter truth: that, in this election, there is no pathway for our so-called brother.

As painful as it is, that is our position. It is in the strategic interests of Ndi Igbo to align with President Bola Tinubu’s aspiration. That is what APGA stands for, and we will do everything possible to convince our people why they should vote for President Tinubu.

Vanguard News

World.title: Tinubu: I’m Working to Eradicate Inherited Hunger and Poverty
World.content:
•Shettima: President has consistently supported northern political interests

•Blaming opponents for hunger shameless attempt to dodge responsibility, Atiku replies Tinubu

• ADC mocks APC campaign flag-off over empty seats, rented crowd, recycled promises

• Tinubu’s Kaduna campaign flag-off ‘political theatre’, says Makinde

Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha, Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja and John Shiklam in Kaduna

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu yesterday flagged off his 2027 re-election campaign in Kaduna State, declaring that he was working to eradicate inherited hunger and poverty created by his political opponents when they were in power.

Tinubu, who spoke at the Ranchers Bees Stadium, the venue of the All Progressives Congress (APC) rally, promised that his administration would create prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity.

This comes as Vice President Kashim Shettima declared that President Tinubu has consistently supported northern political interests, citing historical instances when the president provided vital political backing to major northern figures facing political adversity.

Meanwhile, Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State has challenged opposition figures presenting themselves as northern candidates to show their track record.

Reacting to Tinubu’s claim that the opposition created hunger and poverty, African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku described it as a delusional and shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery Tinubu’s government has inflicted on Nigerians.

The ADC Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has also described the APC campaign flag-off in Kaduna as a monumental disappointment, accusing the ruling party of relying on rented crowds, empty seats and recycled promises.

Similarly, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has dismissed President Tinubu’s campaign flag-off as political theatre, accusing his administration of failing the North on security, economic welfare and political inclusion.

Speaking at yesterday’s campaign rally, Tinubu accused his political opponents of creating hunger and poverty, which his administration was tackling.

Tinubu stated: “I must thank you for your participation in the past elections. You gave me joy, and I will always remember the victory you gave me to become President. I have come again to thank you and seek your mandate for a second term to fulfill our promise of prosperity, continuity, progress and development.

“I hear my opponents talking about hunger. Who created it? They did. They created hunger and poverty. We are trying to eradicate them. We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working, and I am proud of them. They are developing their states.

“To you, the children of our country, we promise prosperity in our second term. You will not regret going to the polls.

“Do you have your PVC? This is not a matter of anger either. Our opponents are angry… They have nothing to offer you but heckling. We have prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity. I assure you of that.”

The president urged voters to vote for all the ruling party’s candidates during the election.

He noted: “Your prosperity is here. Your good fortune is in your hands. Your fingerprints will reflect this. Be careful. Watch them. Do not let them lie to you.

“What is past is past. Fuel subsidy is in our past. No more corruption, no more falsification of invoices, no more lies and no more smuggling.”

Shettima: Tinubu Had Consistently Supported Northern Political Interests

Also speaking at the rally, Vice President Shettima stated that President Tinubu had consistently supported northern political interests.

“And I want us to bear in mind and go back to the past. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has fiercely identified with the North over the years. It is pertinent to mention that when former Vice President Atiku Abubakar was harassed and chased out of the PDP, with his tail between his legs, he ran to the land of the Jagaban, who gave him political succour, support, and a platform to contest the presidency in 2007.

“Again, in 2011, President Tinubu supported another Northern man, Malam Nuhu Ribadu, to contest for the presidency of this country. You can also see that in 2015 and 2019, President Tinubu stood solidly behind the late President Muhammadu Buhari, who secured his first- and second-term victories. This is why we have all stood with him. This is a mark of honour, and our faith in a man of honour.”

Shettima said Tinubu’s administration had also kept the country together despite predictions of failure and had delivered on key promises.

Shettima also cited several projects delivered by Tinubu’s administration.

Gov Sani Challenges Northern Candidates to Show Records

Kaduna State Governor Senator Sani challenged opposition figures presenting themselves as northern candidates to show their track record, stressing that Tinubu had fulfilled key campaign promises made to Kaduna State in 2022, particularly on road reconstruction and security in Birnin Gwari.

He recalled Tinubu’s visit to Birnin Gwari LGA on December 22, 2022, when the area was the epicentre of insecurity in the North-west.

Addressing the President, Sani said: “At that time, a very senior officer advised you against going to Birnin Gwari because of security concerns. You instantly rejected the advice and travelled to Birnin Gwari with 27 armoured vehicles.”

According to the governor, two promises made during that visit have been met, adding that the 123km Kaduna-Birnin Gwari Road abandoned for over 40 years was under reconstruction.

Sani said the government had released N117 billion to the contractor.

He noted: “Today you can travel to Birnin Gwari with your eyes closed without a single police escort. That is progress.”

The governor challenged opposition figures to show their track record.

“When someone came to us and said we should vote for him simply because he is a northerner, we asked him, can you show us a track record?” Sani said.

Also, the Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, said the campaign would be based on records in the economy, infrastructure, health, education and cash transfers.

“We have been engaging all and sundry, our traditional rulers, our ulama and our imams, to understand the importance of your return in 2027 for continuity, for the peace of this country.”

He added: “The opposition have now upgraded their campaign from Facebook and Twitter to AI. So, I want to call the attention of our supporters to prepare, be watchful and be vigilant.”

For his part, the National Chairman of APC, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, declared that Tinubu has earned the confidence and support of Nigerians through his courageous leadership, commitment to national development, and promise of greater prosperity for the country.

Blaming Opposition for Hunger Shameless Attempt to Dodge Responsibility, Atiku Replies Tinubu

Meanwhile, Atiku has described Tinubu’s claim that the opposition created hunger and poverty as a delusional and shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery his own government has inflicted on Nigerians.

In a statement issued by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, the former Vice President argued that a President cannot light the fire of hardship with his own policies, then blame the neighbours for the smoke.

“Mr President, blaming the opposition for hunger is either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia. The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record.

“The hardship your administration has brought upon Nigerians is real. You cannot deny it by blaming others.

“Your decision to commission the unfinished Abuja to Kaduna Expressway from inside a stadium shows how far removed you are from the daily reality of Nigerians. A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon-cutting ceremony,” Atiku added.

ADC Mocks APC Campaign Flag-off Over Empty Seats, Rented Crowd, Recycled Promises

Reacting to the rally, the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC-PCC, Mr. Kola Ologbondiyan, said an event intended to demonstrate the APC’s political strength across the North-west had instead exposed what he described as the party’s declining public acceptance.

Ologbondiyan alleged that the APC mobilised people from the seven states of the North-west and beyond, with payments reportedly ranging from N50,000 to N100,000 per person. Yet, the stadium, which he put at a capacity of 5,000, remained sparsely occupied.

He added that the turnout, which he described as disappointing, was compounded by what he called the unenthusiastic reception given to the speeches and messages of APC leaders.

Ologbondiyan further alleged that some attendees expressed dissatisfaction with the ruling party after leaving the stadium, chanting the Hausa phrase “Ba mu yi,” which he interpreted as a rejection of the APC and its policies.

The ADC-PCC accused the APC of returning to Kaduna with promises similar to those made during the 2015, 2019 and 2023 election cycles, arguing that the ruling party had failed to account for its years in power adequately.

Tinubu’s Kaduna Campaign Flag-off ‘Political Theatre’, Says Makinde

On its part, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) said the APC campaign event would not erase what it described as broken promises, worsening hardship and declining public confidence in the ruling party.

In a statement issued by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, MDPCO challenged Tinubu to explain what the North had gained from his administration beyond persistent insecurity, economic difficulties and what it called marginalisation.

MDPCO alleged that at least 20,000 people had been killed in northern Nigeria since Tinubu assumed office in 2023, while millions had been displaced by insecurity. The statement did not independently verify the figures.

The organisation further alleged that the North had been marginalised in appointments to strategic federal positions, accusing the APC of treating the region primarily as a source of electoral support.

“No part of the country should be an electoral warehouse to be raided every four years and abandoned after victory,” the group said.

World.title: NDC Fixes Monday for Third NEC Meeting, Presidential Campaign Council Unveiling
World.content:
•Says 80% of candidates received free nomination forms amid economic hardship

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) will unveil its National Campaign Council on Monday as part of preparations for the 2027 general election, while presenting its financial accounts to demonstrate its commitment to transparency and accountability.

The party disclosed this in a statement issued yesterday by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, announcing that its third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting would be held at 10 a.m. on October 26 at JD Event Centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, Maitama, Abuja.

A major highlight of the meeting, according to the party, will be the National Treasurer’s presentation of the party’s statement of account, a move it said is intended to distinguish its financial management practices from those of other political parties.

The NDC challenged other political parties, particularly the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to adopt similar measures to promote transparency in managing party finances.

The party also attributed its financial limitations partly to the economic difficulties facing Nigerians, claiming that approximately 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the fees for expression-of-interest forms.

It said it had consequently issued the forms to the affected candidates free of charge to enable them to participate in the electoral process.

The party blamed the situation on what it described as widespread poverty, hunger and deprivation under the APC-led federal government, criticising its economic policies.

Beyond the financial disclosures, the NEC meeting will give the party an opportunity to unveil its National Campaign Council, which it said would coordinate its campaign activities across all levels of government.

According to the statement, the council will encompass the presidential, National Assembly, governorship and state Houses of Assembly campaign structures.

The party also announced plans to present certificates of return to its candidates contesting the various elective positions.

The developments come as political parties intensify preparations for the 2027 general election, with campaign structures, candidate mobilisation and party organisation expected to play important roles in the contest.

For the NDC, the planned unveiling of its campaign council and disclosure of its accounts are intended to project organisational readiness and distinguish the party’s approach to internal financial accountability.

The NDC expressed confidence in its preparations for the forthcoming elections, saying it was determined to offer Nigerians what it described as altruistic leadership.

The statement read, “The leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) wishes to announce that its 3rd National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting will hold on Monday, 26th October 2026, at JD event centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, opposite A-class park, Maitama, Abuja. The time is 10 am prompt.

“A major highlight of the meeting will be the release and presentation of the party’s Statement of Account by the National Treasurer. This reflects our avowed commitment to the principles of transparency and accountability. In this regard, we challenge other political parties, especially the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to emulate this level of openness and transparency in managing their finances.

“For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual.

“Our finances would have been more robust. However, contrary to speculations in the public domain, and due to the level of poverty, hunger and deprivation in the country occasioned by the rudderless APC and its amorphous economic policies, about 80% of our candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms. The party had to issue forms to such candidates free of charge.

“The party will also use the opportunity of the NEC meeting to unveil its National Campaign Council (NCC).

“As a party of innovation, our NCC is all-encompassing. It covers the Presidential, National Assembly, Governorship, and State Houses of Assembly Campaign Councils.

“Our various candidates will be presented with Certificates of Return for their respective offices.

“The NDC is turbo-charged and ready to give Nigerians the altruistic leadership the nation deserves. A New Nigeria is Possible. We can do it!”

World.title: Crude Oil Price Surges Above $117 Over Fears of Fresh US Strikes on Iran
World.content:
• Oil theft slumps 82.9% to 17,600bpd in five years amid fresh uptick in losses

• Navy uncovers 132,000 litres of stolen crude oil in Bonny

Emmanuel Addeh and Linus Aleke in Abuja

Crude oil prices surged above $117 a barrel at the weekend, reaching their highest level since April, as fears of renewed US military strikes on Iran and escalating threats to energy infrastructure across the Middle East heightened concerns about global crude supplies.

This comes as oil theft and pipeline losses in Nigeria fell by 82.9 per cent in five years, from 102,900 barrels per day (bpd) in 2021 to 17,600 bpd in the first seven months of 2026, amid fresh concerns about further increases in lost volumes after years of decline.

Meanwhile, the Nigerian Navy has uncovered 132,000 litres of stolen crude oil in Allison community, Bonny Local Government Area (LGA) of Rivers State, disrupting a potential storage point in the illicit petroleum supply chain as troops of Operation Delta Sentinel intensified their clampdown on oil theft and economic saboteurs in the Niger Delta region.

Nigeria’s oil benchmark, Brent crude, climbed by about 3.5 per cent to cross $117 a barrel during trading before easing to just above $116, still up approximately 2.7 per cent.

The latest rally followed reports that Washington was considering fresh military strikes against Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, raising concerns that the conflict, now in its eighth month, could escalate further rather than move towards a diplomatic resolution.

Iran had threatened to attack oil facilities, undersea cables, data centres and artificial intelligence infrastructure across the Gulf if the United States and Israel launched a new offensive against the country.

Brent crude traded at about $72 a barrel in February, before the war began, but surged to about $126 a barrel by the end of April as the conflict intensified and concerns mounted over supply security.

Tensions rose again during the week following claims by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) that it struck four commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday.

The US ordered some diplomats and family members of American government employees to leave Saudi Arabia, which had faced continued attacks by Houthi rebels operating from Yemen.

World.title: Oil Theft Slumps 82.9% to 17,600bpd in Five Years Amid Fresh Uptick in Losses
World.content:
Meanwhile, official operational statistics published by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) showed that daily crude oil losses, which fell to a five-year low of 9,100 bpd in 2025, rose by 93.4 per cent to 17,600 bpd between January and July 2026.

The figures in the commission’s fifth anniversary publication, ‘The Upstream Gaze’, highlighted both progress in curbing crude theft and the ongoing challenge of protecting oil production and transportation infrastructure.

According to the data, daily losses declined from 102,900 bpd in 2021 to 55,000 bpd in 2022, representing a 46.5 per cent reduction. The downward trend continued in 2023 when losses dropped to 22,900 bpd, before falling further to 11,200 bpd in 2024 and 9,100 bpd in 2025.

The federal government attributed the cut in crude losses to the combined efforts of the military, local pipeline surveillance groups in the Niger Delta, and the introduction of modern crude measuring devices in the region.

The figures showed that Nigeria’s total liquid hydrocarbon production, comprising crude oil and condensate, gradually recovered from the lows recorded in recent years.

Output averaged 1.63 million bpd in the first seven months of 2026, compared with 1.62 million bpd in 2025, 1.56 million bpd in 2024, 1.47 million bpd in 2023 and 1.38 million bpd in 2022. Production stood at 1.62 million bpd in 2021, the NUPRC data highlighted.

Crude oil production alone averaged 1.46 million bpd in the period under review, up from 1.43 million bpd in 2025, 1.35 million bpd in 2024, 1.24 million bpd in 2023 and 1.14 million bpd in 2022. The figure for 2021 was 1.31 million bpd.

In contrast, blended condensate production continued its downward trend, averaging 170,000 bpd in the first seven months of 2026, compared with 190,000 bpd in 2025, 210,000 bpd in 2024, 230,000 bpd in 2023, 240,000 bpd in 2022, and 310,000 bpd in 2021.

The gradual improvement in crude production also coincided with a significant shift in how the country allocates its oil, particularly the growing share supplied to domestic refineries as Nigeria expands its local refining capacity.

Supply to domestic refineries climbed to 460,000 bpd in the first seven months of 2026, up from 280,000 bpd in 2025, 220,000 bpd in 2024, 20,000 bpd in 2023, and just 10,000 bpd in 2022. Domestic refinery supply was virtually non-existent in 2021.

At 460,000 bpd, local refineries accounted for approximately 29 per cent of the 1.61 million bpd in total crude oil lifted during the period. The allocation represented a 64.3 per cent increase over the 280,000 bpd supplied to domestic refineries in 2025, underscoring growing demand for locally processed crude.

Similarly, the shift coincided with a decline in crude available for export, as the government struggled to meet local supply. Average daily crude exports fell to 1.15 million bpd in the first seven months of 2026, from 1.33 million bpd in 2025; 1.31 million bpd in 2024; 1.47 million bpd in 2023; 1.32 million bpd in 2022 and 1.51 million bpd in 2021.

The latest export figures were down 13.5 per cent from the 2025 level and 23.8 per cent from the 2021 volume.

In the same vein, total crude lifting averaged 1.61 million bpd in the first seven months of 2026, marginally below the 1.62 million bpd recorded in 2025. The figures suggested that the growing allocation to domestic refineries has been accompanied by a reduction in export volumes, rather than a comparable increase in total crude lifted.

World.title: Navy Uncovers 132,000 litres of Stolen Crude Oil in Bonny
World.content:
Meanwhile, the Nigerian Navy has uncovered 132,000 litres of stolen crude oil in Allison community, Bonny LGA of Rivers State.

According to a statement by the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, the Forward Operating Base Bonny discovered the stolen crude oil under Operation Delta Sentinel, following actionable intelligence.

He said the operation uncovered 10 dugout pits, adding that the site and the recovered products were handled in accordance with extant regulations.

“The operation reinforces the importance of intelligence-led action in identifying concealed petroleum stockpiles and disrupting the infrastructure that enables crude oil theft and the unauthorised movement of petroleum products.

“The Nigerian Navy will sustain efforts to locate and dismantle illegal refining infrastructure and disrupt the networks facilitating crude oil theft across the Niger Delta,” the statement said.

The Navy urged community leaders, residents, traditional institutions and other stakeholders to promptly report crude oil theft, illegal refining, suspicious petroleum storage and the unauthorised movement of petroleum products to the nearest security agency.

Timely, credible information, the statement said, could enable swift intervention and prevent illicit activities from expanding.

“Safeguarding the nation’s critical petroleum assets requires vigilance and active cooperation between security agencies and the communities they serve. The Navy therefore urges the public to remain alert and support lawful efforts to protect national resources,” Folorunsho concluded.

World.title: Amid Improved Economic Indicators, Foreign, Domestic Investors’ Transactions on NGX Hit N15.06tn
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

Foreign and domestic investors’ transactions on Nigeria’s stock market reached N15.06 trillion in the first nine months of 2026, amid key reforms and improved economic indicators.

The Nigerian Exchange Limited’s (NGX) report on domestic and foreign portfolio participation in equity trading revealed that domestic investors continued to dominate transactions, accounting for 89.74 per cent of the total. In comparison, foreign investors contributed 10.26 per cent.

Foreign investors’ share of transactions declined from 21.56 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025 to 10.26 per cent in 2026. Conversely, domestic investors, comprising retail and institutional investors, increased their share from 78.44 per cent to 89.74 per cent.

The report disclosed that domestic investors’ transactions rose to N13.52 trillion between January and September 2026, representing a 102 per cent increase over the N6.69 trillion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

Foreign investors, however, accounted for N1.55 trillion, representing a 16.01 per cent decline from N1.84 trillion recorded between January and September 2025.

The shift suggests that the surge in activity on Nigeria’s stock market this year has been driven largely by local capital, particularly institutional investors.

Capital market analysts attributed the growth in institutional investors’ transactions partly to the National Pension Commission’s (PenCom) decision to raise equity investment limits for pension funds in February 2026.

They said the policy had helped inject fresh liquidity into the stock market, supporting gains in the share prices of some blue-chip companies. On February 9, 2026, PenCom revised the investment limits for ordinary shares in Retirement Savings Account (RSA) Funds I, II, III and VI (Active).

The commission amended Section 9 of its investment regulations, raising equity allocation limits for RSA Fund I from 30 per cent to 35 per cent; RSA Fund II from 25 per cent to 33 per cent; RSA Fund III from 10 per cent to 15 per cent; and RSA Fund VI (Active) from 25 per cent to 33 per cent.

Institutional investors accounted for N8.36 trillion of domestic transactions between January and September 2026, compared with N5.15 trillion from retail investors. In the corresponding period of 2025, institutional and retail transactions stood at N4.09 trillion and N2.60 trillion, respectively.

The report also showed that foreign portfolio outflows rose to N913.61 billion between January and September 2026, up from N810.39 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, a 12.7 per cent increase.

Foreign portfolio inflows, however, fell to N632.35 billion, down about 38.6 per cent from N1.03 trillion in the corresponding period of 2025.

Capital market analysts said FTSE Russell’s 2023 downgrade of Nigeria contributed to foreign investors’ exit from the stock market. They described the upgrade in September 2026 as a first step towards attracting them back.

The report put foreign investor inflows in September 2026 at N925.20 billion, up 249.53 per cent from the N264.70 billion recorded in August.

Investors on the Nigerian stock market recorded strong returns in the first nine months of 2026, with market capitalisation gaining N63.73 trillion despite volatility.

Market capitalisation rose from N99.376 trillion at the beginning of the year to N163.105 trillion on September 30, 2026, representing an increase of N63.73 trillion, or 64.13 per cent.

Similarly, the NGX All-Share Index gained 95,598.64 points, or 61.43 per cent, rising from 155,613.03 points at the beginning of the year to 251,211.67 points at the end of September.

With fewer than five new listings, the NGX has recorded substantial growth in 2026, with market capitalisation reaching the N164 trillion mark amid improving macroeconomic indicators.

The report added: “Over 19 years, domestic transactions increased significantly by 160.83 per cent from N3.5560 trillion in 2007 to N9.2747 trillion in 2025, whilst foreign transactions also increased significantly by 329.87 per cent from N0.6156 trillion to N2.6475 trillion over the same period.

“Total domestic transactions accounted for about 78 per cent of the total transactions carried out in 2025, whilst foreign transactions accounted for about 22 per cent of the total transactions in the same period.

“As at 30 September 2026, year-to-date domestic transactions amounted to approximately N13.5159 trillion, representing 89.74 per cent of total market transactions, whilst foreign transactions amounted to approximately N1.5460 trillion, accounting for 10.26 per cent.”

World.title: APC Accuses Atiku, ADC of Plotting to Discredit Tinubu’s Campaign Flag-off in Kaduna With Fake News
World.content:
•Keyamo: ADC presidential candidate jittery over losing north to Tinubu

•Tinubu’s panic cannot erase APC’s terrible record, says ADC

Chuks Okocha, Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja and Chinedu Eze in Lagos

The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) has accused the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, of orchestrating a fake news campaign to discredit its presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna yesterday.

Similarly, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace development, Festus Keyamo, said Atiku was jittery over the flag-off of the presidential campaign of APC in Kaduna because he was afraid of losing the bulk votes which he was hoping to get from the north.

But is swift reaction, the ADC accused the APC of using allegations of fake news to divert attention from the economic hardship Nigerians were facing under President Bola Tinubu.

The APC-PCC in a statement issued statement by its spokesperson, Mr Dele Alake said it uncovered a “well-orchestrated, devious plan” to misinform the public through AI, deepfake videos and counterfeit documents targeted at the APC rally, President Tinubu, Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State and APC leaders.

According to the council, the plot began with the circulation of a picture of a security vehicle on routine patrol near an APC campaign billboard in Kaduna metropolis, which was twisted to claim security agents were deployed to protect APC billboards.

The council said the story was planted in a national newspaper and subsequently shared by Atiku on his social media handles.

Alake added that the second leg was the circulation online of a fake letter purportedly written by Sani to the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, on the purported release of N2.3 trillion by the Kaduna State Government to host the rally.

He added: “We are still at a loss as to how anyone can imagine and concoct this senseless and utterly baseless lie that defies logic and basic common sense.

“How much is the entire annual revenue of Kaduna State, or any state, for that matter, that a state would spend N2.3 trillion to host a rally?” Alake queried.

Alake noted that the alleged N2.3 trillion was more than Kaduna State’s annual budget for three years combined, citing the state’s budgets for 2024 at N458.271 billion, 2025 at N790.439 billion and 2026 at N985.9 billion, which he said were still less than N2.3 trillion.

The council claimed Atiku and ADC had also perfected plans to circulate old, doctored and deepfake videos during the rally to show purported resentment by the people.

Alake said: “We hereby use this opportunity to alert the general public about this malicious and ignoble plan. It is a fact that Atiku Abubakar and the ADC, his special-purpose vehicle, are incapable of winning any election.

“They will pull any strings, no matter how despicable and atrocious, to stay afloat in their desperate bid to grab power at all costs.”

The APC Campaign Council urged Nigerians to be vigilant and reject what it described as machinations of the opposition.

World.title: Keyamo: ADC Presidential Candidate Jittery over Losing North to Tinubu
World.content:
On his part, Keyamo, in a statement titled, ‘Why Atiku Abubakar is Particularly Jittery About the Kaduna Flag-off,’ posted on his verified Facebook account, alleged that the former Vice President had launched ‘blistering online attack’ against APC as the date of the launch got closer.

The minister accused Atiku of being behind the destruction of APC posters in Kaduna and other parts of the north.

“The common but cheap tactic is to position cameras in certain places, procure individuals to tear down the posters of the President, and then post the videos online. The other tactic is to disseminate disinformation claiming that any support the President is seen to receive in the North is procured only through the massive deployment of financial resources. Hence the fake letter alleging a N2.3 trillion deployment for the Kaduna rally. The intention is to generate a hoopla that will create a groundswell of public opinion that President Tinubu has been “massively rejected” in the North,” Keyamo said.

The Minister also said the reason why Atiku was allegedly doing this was because he did not want to lose the bulk votes which he was hoping to get from the north.

“The reason for this is simple: Atiku Abubakar was seriously banking on the bulk of Northern votes to see him through in 2027, knowing full well that he has no inroads at all into the South, given the mood of the country that the South deserves to complete eight years of the Presidency.

Tinubu’s Panic Cannot Erase APC’s Terrible Record, Says ADC

Meanwhile, the ADC has accused the APC of using allegations of fake news to divert attention from the economic hardship Nigerians were facing under President Tinubu.

The ADC Presidential Campaign Council said the ruling APC should focus on defending its record in government rather than accusing it and Atiku of plotting to discredit the APC’s presidential campaign flag-off.

In a statement, the council’s Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, described the APC’s allegations as an attempt to distract Nigerians from rising living costs and the administration’s economic policies.

Shaibu challenged the APC to provide evidence linking Atiku and the ADC to the alleged circulation of forged documents, manipulated images and deepfake videos ahead of the Kaduna rally.

“Until then, his ‘fake news alert’ is an empty political stunt,” Shaibu said, referring to the statement by Alake.

The ADC spokesperson argued that the economic difficulties confronting Nigerians could not be dismissed as propaganda, citing high petrol and diesel prices, food inflation and growing poverty.

He said the APC’s allegations would not change the daily struggles of households grappling with the cost of food, transportation and other essential needs.

On the security presence near an APC campaign billboard in Kaduna, Shaibu questioned the explanation that the vehicle was on routine patrol, asking why the issue had become a subject of political controversy.

He also raised concerns about reports that some APC supporters had travelled long distances to attend the rally and were left sleeping on the streets of Kaduna.

Shaibu further referred to reports of accidents involving APC supporters travelling from Sokoto and Abuja to the event. However, he acknowledged that details of the reported incidents remained unconfirmed.

The ADC spokesperson called on the APC to account for the safety of supporters travelling to the rally, arguing that political mobilisation should not come at the expense of citizens’ welfare.

“Making citizens endure long, hazardous journeys and sleep outdoors simply to create rally optics is political exploitation, not leadership,” he said.

Shaibu also questioned the scope of Tinubu’s campaign activities, alleging that the president was campaigning in only 12 states and suggesting that supporters were being moved between rallies.

He argued that the size of a rally crowd should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of widespread public support, particularly where attendees had been transported from other locations.

“You can hire buses, assemble a crowd and plaster the streets with billboards. You cannot hire consent,” he said.

World.title: Yellow Level 2 warning: Severe storms threaten Eastern Cape on Monday
World.content:
Yellow Level 2 warning highlights possible flooding, property damage and power disruptions during severe thunderstorms. Image: AI Illustration

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a Yellow Level 2 warning for severe thunderstorms in parts of the Eastern Cape on Monday.

The warning will remain in effect from 08:00 until 20:59.

According to SAWS, a deepening surface trough and an upper trough could trigger thunderstorms across the eastern half of the province.



Yellow Level 2 warning: Severe thunderstorms

Affected area: (eastern half of the Eastern Cape)

Validity period: 26 October 2026.#saws #weatheroutlook #southafricanweather pic.twitter.com/sTOgQAbJW0 — SA Weather Service (@SAWeatherServic) October 25, 2026

Some storms may become severe in the north-eastern parts, bringing heavy downpours, strong winds and hail that could cause damage.

Yellow Level 2 warning: What impacts can residents expect?

SAWS has warned that severe thunderstorms could damage homes, property and temporary structures in affected areas.

Heavy rainfall may also flood roads and low-lying bridges, making travel difficult.

Strong winds and hail could damage crops and lead to livestock losses.

The weather service also warned of possible disruptions to electricity and communication services, as well as danger to life.



Staying safe during severe thunderstorms

Residents should avoid crossing flooded roads and bridges and stay indoors during severe thunderstorms.

Motorists should drive carefully during heavy downpours, particularly in areas prone to flooding.

People living in vulnerable structures should take extra precautions.

Farmers should consider moving livestock to safer areas where possible.

Residents are encouraged to follow updates from SAWS as conditions develop throughout Monday.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs v TS Galaxy: Date, kickoff time, venue, predicted lineup
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs will turn their attention to the Carling Knockout Cup as they look to bounce back from their disappointing exit from the CAF Confederation Cup.

Amakhosi host TS Galaxy in the round of 16 on Tuesday (27 October) evening at FNB Stadium, with kick-off scheduled for 19:30.

The encounter presents head coach Fernando Da Cruz with another opportunity to guide the Soweto giants towards silverware after their campaigns in the MTN8 and CAF Confederation Cup ended in disappointment.



Chiefs will need to put their continental setback behind them quickly as they look to keep their season on track. Another early cup exit would increase the pressure on Da Cruz, who is under pressure to deliver results.

The Glamour Boys have a long wait to end in the Carling Knockout, having last lifted the trophy 16 years ago. Tuesday’s clash therefore offers them a chance to take a step closer to ending that drought.

TS Galaxy looking to spoil Kaizer Chiefs party

With Amakhosi eager to progress to the next round, TS Galaxy will be determined to spoil the party and book their place in the quarter-finals.



With the Soweto Derby also looming, Kaizer Chiefs cannot afford to lose momentum at a crucial stage of the season. Da Cruz and his players will need to rediscover their rhythm and build confidence ahead of their upcoming fixtures.

Progressing to the next round would provide a timely boost for Amakhosi, while another setback would leave the coach facing even greater scrutiny.

Here’s how Chiefs can lineup: Bvuma, Frosler, Migeul, Moloisane, Cross, Mthethwa, Maboe, Shabalala, Vilakazi, Silva and Duba.



Will Chiefs reach the next round?

World.title: Kwagga Smith’s injury return date confirmed
World.content:
It was confirmed this weekend that Kwagga Smith has signed with the Bulls on a three-year contract. The versatile loose forward has spent eight years there with Yamaha Júbilo, now rebranded as the Shizuoka Blue Revs, and he has remained an integral part of the Springbok team throughout this time, earning more than 60 Tests.

Smith suffered a major knee injury in May 2026, tearing his ACL and meniscus while playing for the Blue Revs. It ruled him out for the rest of the 2026 season. Medical experts have since cleared him to return to play at the end of December.

“I’m very excited to be joining,” said Smith, who mentioned that he was tracking well with his recovery. “I’m already jogging. I miss the rugby but I’m feeling good.



“My wife is pregnant, due in January, so the timing of joining the Vodacom Bulls is perfect. Playing under Johan Ackermann (previously) was one of my best experiences. I’m looking forward to getting back by early next year.”

Kwagga Smith set to boost strong Bulls team

Smith is bound to become a popular figure at Loftus Versfeld where the Bulls have an array of talent in the back row.

Bulls CEO Edgar Rathbone said: “Kwagga is a proven winner who has achieved just about everything the game has to offer, and he has never lost his hunger. His work rate, physicality and fearlessness are exactly what we want in Vodacom Bulls colours. He will drive standards inside our group, and our supporters will love the way he plays.”

Other injury news

Meanwhile, the Bulls will have to do without Springbok scrumhalf Embrose Papier for several weeks, after the 29-year-old underwent surgery on an ankle injury.

Papier, the reigning SA URC Player of the Year, was hurt after coming off the bench in the Bulls’ 56-20 Champions Cup win over Stade Français in Pretoria last Saturday.

His absence leaves Paul de Wet and Zak Burger as the scrumhalf options in the match 23.

World.title: Mpumalanga man missing in Ballito surf – NSRI
World.content:
A 35-year-old man from Mpumalanga, remains missing after being caught in rip currents at Salmon Bay in Ballito on Saturday. Image: NSRI

A 35-year-old man from Witbank, Mpumalanga, remains missing after reportedly being caught in rip currents at Salmon Bay in Ballito on Saturday.

The National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI) Ballito duty crew was activated at 08:00 following reports from IPSS Medical Rescue of a drowning in progress near the Salmon Bay launch site.

READ | Weekend tragedy as man drowns in Wilderness saving son



According to NSRI Ballito station commander Mike Bishop, an IPSS Medical Rescue member who was nearby witnessed the man in distress and raised the alarm.

The man is believed to have been caught in rip currents in an area that is not protected by duty lifeguards.

Brother-in-law injured in rescue attempt

The missing man’s brother-in-law entered the water in an attempt to reach him. However, the man disappeared beneath the water before his relative could get to him.



The brother-in-law sustained cuts and bruises during the rescue attempt. Paramedics treated him at the scene, and he did not require further medical care.

NSRI Ballito rescue swimmers, the South African Police Service (SAPS), Police Search and Rescue, Metro Police Search and Rescue, IPSS Medical Rescue and KwaDukuza lifeguards responded to the incident.

Search efforts continue

NSRI launched its rescue jet-ski and deployed a rescue swimmer into the surf zone as part of extensive search efforts.



Despite searches at sea and along the shoreline, there were no signs of the missing man.

Police have opened an investigation, while Police Search and Rescue teams continue searching with assistance from KwaDukuza lifeguards and Metro Police Search and Rescue.

The NSRI said its thoughts and care were with the missing man’s family during this difficult time.



Warning about rip currents

The incident highlights the dangers of rip currents, which can rapidly carry swimmers away from shore.

Beachgoers are urged to swim at beaches protected by lifeguards, heed safety warnings and avoid entering the water when conditions are dangerous.

World.title: Kwagga Smith signs for the Bulls
World.content:
The Bulls have signed Springbok Kwagga Smith on a three-year contract, boosting their depth in the loose forward position. Image: SA Rugby

The Bulls have signed Springbok loose forward Kwagga Smith on a three-year contract.

The two-time Rugby World Cup winner brings a serial winner’s pedigree and a fearless, abrasive edge to a franchise already rich in backrow talent.

READ | Sharks, Springboks suffer major injury blow



Smith, 33, has been in two World Cup-winning squads, in 2019 and 2023. He is a ferociously talented ball winner who plays at No 6 and No 8.

His athleticism and refusal to take a backward step have made him one of the most revered players in the Springbok group.

‘Delighted’

Bulls coach Johan Ackermann said he was delighted to team up again with Kwagga Smith, having coached him previously at the Lions.

“As a youngster, he showed character and fight and integrity. He’s a team man who has grown into a stalwart, and it’s been a privilege to watch his career unfold and establish himself as one of the best backrows in world rugby. Wherever he goes he makes a difference, and I look forward to him contributing both on and off the field.”

Made his name in Sevens

Kwagga Smith made his name in Sevens before he did so in the 15-man game. He won Commonwealth Games gold with the Blitzboks in Glasgow in 2014 and an Olympic bronze medal in Rio in 2016. He then took that pace and aggression into the 15s game.

His first big break came at the Lions, where he was part of the side that won the 2015 Currie Cup.



He moved to Japan in 2018 and has spent eight years there with Yamaha Júbilo, now rebranded as the Shizuoka Blue Revs. He kept his place in the Springbok set-up throughout and has played more than 60 Tests.

His honours include the 2019 and 2023 World Cups, the 2021 series win over the British & Irish Lions, and the Rugby Championship titles of 2019, 2024 and 2025.

He has played 63 Tests for the Springboks, scoring 11 tries. His most recent Test came in November 2025 against Wales at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, a match the Springboks won 73-0.

Knee injury

Kwagga Smith suffered a major knee injury in May 2026, tearing his ACL and meniscus while playing for the Blue Revs. It ruled him out for the rest of the 2026 season. Medical experts have since cleared him to return to play at the end of December.

“I’m very excited to be joining,” said Smith, who mentioned that he was tracking well with his recovery.

“I’m already jogging. I miss the rugby but I’m feeling good. My wife is pregnant, due in January, so the timing of joining the Bulls is perfect. Playing under Johan Ackermann [previously] was one of my best experiences. I’m looking forward to getting back by early next year.”

Bulls CEO Edgar Rathbone added: “Kwagga is a proven winner who has achieved just about everything the game has to offer, and he has never lost his hunger. His work rate, physicality and fearlessness are exactly what we want in Bulls colours. He will drive standards inside our group, and our supporters will love the way he plays.”

World.title: Weekend tragedy as man drowns in Wilderness saving son
World.content:
A man has died following a drowning incident in Wilderness, after two teenage boys were caught in rip currents on Saturday. Image: NSRI website

A man has died following a drowning incident at Leentjiesklip Beach in Wilderness, Western Cape, after two teenage boys were reportedly caught in rip currents on Saturday.

The National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI) Wilderness duty crew was activated at 17:31 after reports of a drowning in progress.

READ | Boy and his dog rescued at Yzerfontein Harbour – NSRI



According to NSRI Wilderness station commander Jonathan Britton, two fathers entered the water to help their sons after the teenagers got into difficulty in the surf.

The two families are friends. One father and his teenage son are local residents, while the other father and his 14-year-old son are from Germany.

Rescue operation launched

NSRI rescue swimmers, the South African Police Service (SAPS), Western Cape Government Health EMS, ER24 and George Fire and Rescue Service responded to the emergency.



One of the teenagers, a 14-year-old boy from Germany, managed to make his own way back to the beach. He was initially assisted by NSRI medics before being handed over to paramedics.

An NSRI rescue swimmer entered the water to assist the two adults and the remaining teenager, who were still in distress in the surf zone.

The NSRI duty crew also launched two rescue craft, Ann Stratford and Oscars Rescuer.



The German father and the local teenage boy were rescued and brought safely to shore. Both received assistance from NSRI medics before being handed over to paramedics.

Father declared dead despite CPR efforts

The second father, a local man, was found lifeless in the water by NSRI rescuers and brought to the beach.

NSRI medics immediately began cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), with paramedics joining the efforts to revive him.



Despite extensive resuscitation attempts, the man was declared deceased after all efforts to save his life had been exhausted.

His body was handed over to police and Government Health Forensic Pathology Services.

The surviving father and both teenagers were transported to hospital by ER24 ambulance and are recovering under medical care.



Police open inquest

Police have opened an inquest into the man’s death.

NSRI extended its condolences to the deceased man’s family and friends, adding that its thoughts were with both families during the difficult time.

The incident serves as a reminder of the dangers posed by rip currents, which can quickly place swimmers in serious danger and put those attempting rescues at risk.

World.title: Moving to Cape Town? Seven best areas for young professionals
World.content:
If you’re moving to the Mother City for work or looking to start a new chapter, choosing the right neighbourhood to live in can be quite overwhelming. Here is a look at seven of the best neighbourhoods for young professionals.

SEVEN BEST NEIGHBOURHOODS FOR YOUNG PROFESSIONALS

SEA POINT

One of Cape Town’s most popular neighbourhoods for young professionals is Sea Point, which offers a combination of the ocean and city living. Sea Point is located along the Atlantic Seaboard, the suburb offers a lively atmosphere, restarunts, coffee shops, fitness studios and easy access to the popular Sea Point Promenade.

If you work remotely, there are also great cafes or coworking spaces you could look into to enjoy a change of scenery. However, while Sea Point is a great area, it also comes at a price. One-bedroom apartments start at around R13 000 for rent and two bedroom apartments are around R20 000. If you earn a comfortable salary, then this could be the option for you.



GARDENS

Another popular option for young professionals in a central location is Gardens, situated near the Cape Town CBD and the slopes of Table Mountain. Gardens offers access to a variety of restaurants, entertainment, cultural attractions and green spaces. This is an ideal location for those who work in the city and want to avoid a long daily commute.

Gardens is definitely worth considering. However, the rental prices are also quite high, specifically for well-maintained buildings.

WOODSTOCK

Woodstock has been known to have been developed into one of Cape Town’s most well-known creative neighbourhoods. The suburb attracts young professionals, entrepreneurs, artists and those that works in the industry of design, media and technology.

The distance to the CBD is not too far, making it a good option for those who want to live close to work without paying Atlantic Seaboard rental prices. The area is also popular for its art galleries, restaurants and creative spaces. The Old Biscuit Mill is one of its best-known destinations, offering markets, food and opportunities to explore local businesses.



Rental prices start at arund R10 000 to R15 000.

OBSERVATORY

Observatory, often referred to as Obs, has a reputation for its alternative atmosphere and vibrant social scene. The neighbourhood attracts students, young professionals and people working in creative industries as well.

Its location near the University of Cape Town and several major hospitals also makes it convenient for academics, healthcare workers and people employed in nearby institutions. Observatory offers a mixture of restaurants, pubs, independent businesses and older residential properties.

For young professionals who enjoy socialising and meeting people, the suburb can provide a lively environment.

It is also worth considering for those looking for accommodation more affordable than Sea Point or Gardens. However, rental prices vary considerably depending on the property and its condition.

CLAREMONT

Claremont offers a different lifestyle from Cape Town’s inner-city neighbourhoods. Located in the Southern Suburbs, this area is particularly appealing to young professionals who want access to shopping centres, restaurants, public transport and residential amenities.

Cavendish Square is one of the area’s major shopping destinations, providing access to retailers, restaurants and entertainment. Rental prices can vary depending on whether someone chooses an apartment, townhouse or larger property.

The suburb is also worth considering for young professionals who want to establish a longer-term home rather than move between smaller city apartments.

DURBANVILLE

Durbanville is a great option for young professionals who want a quieter suburban lifestyle. Located in Cape Town’s Northern Suburbs, the area offers access to shopping centres, restaurants, residential developments and wine farms. It is particularly appealing to people who prefer a more spacious living environment.

Durbanville Wine Valley is a popular attaction in the area, where several wine estates provide opportunities for weekend outings.

For young professionals who enjoy outdoor activities and a slower pace of life, the suburb offers a different experience from the city centre. Rental prices can also be more affordable than areas like Sea Point and Gardens. However, commuting will take up more of your time and an added expense for fuel. Someone working in the Cape Town CBD may need to spend considerably more time travelling than a person living in Gardens or Woodstock.

SOMERSET WEST

Somerset West offers another alternative for young professionals who want to live outside Cape Town’s busiest areas. Located in the Helderberg region, the suburb is known for its residential developments, shopping facilities and access to the surrounding mountains and wine estates.

It has traditionally attracted families and older residents. Hover, more recent developments and changing employment patterns have also made it appealing to working professionals.

Rental costs are more affordable. A one-bedroom apartment in Somerset West starts at R8000 a month.

The suburb also offers access to Somerset Mall, restaurants and outdoor activities. For young professionals who work remotely or in the Helderberg area, Somerset West can provide a more relaxed lifestyle. However, commuting to central Cape Town will also take up more of your time and money. Therefore, it is important to factor in the cost of fuel.

TIPS FOR CONSIDERING WHERE YOU WANT TO LIVE IN CAPE TOWN

Choosing where to live in Cape Town requires more than comparing rental prices. The city’s different neighbourhoods offer different advantages and options for living. Therefore, the most suitable option depends on individual preferences. You should also consider:

Rental affordability should be the first consideration. A neighbourhood may offer an appealing lifestyle, but spending too much on accommodation can make it difficult to manage other monthly expenses such as groceries, transport, insurance and savings.

A neighbourhood may offer an appealing lifestyle, but spending too much on accommodation can make it difficult to manage other monthly expenses such as groceries, transport, insurance and savings. Commuting is equally important. Living closer to work could reduce fuel expenses and travel time, while choosing a cheaper suburb further away may create additional costs. With the current hike in fuel prices, it is important to run the math before making your choice.

With the current hike in fuel prices, it is important to run the math before making your choice. Public transport should also be considered, particularly for people who do not own a car. Access to MyCiTi buses and railway stations can influence how easily someone travels around the city and the affordability.

If you are looking to rent you should investigate the property’s security, parking arrangements, internet connectivity and amenities.

Rental prices should also be checked against current listings, as the market changes and advertised prices vary considerably between properties.

So, where is the “best area” to live in for young professionals? Well, there is no single answer. Sea Point is attractive for people who want coastal living and a lively social environment. Gardens offers central convenience, while Woodstock and Observatory appeal to professionals who enjoy creative communities and urban living.

Claremont provides suburban convenience, while Durbanville and Somerset West offer more space and a quieter lifestyle. However, these areas are further out.

World.title: Oil prices threaten to undermine fuel levy relief
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Rising oil prices are threatening to undermine the positive impact of government's fuel levy relief in November.

In the Medium-Term Budget, the Finance Minister announced the fuel levy relief.

It will temporarily fall by R3 per litre for Diesel and R1.50 per litre for petrol from 4 November.

The price change will be based on the month's average oil price and the dollar-rand exchange rate.

According to the latest Central Energy Fund data, 95 unleaded petrol is set to rise by R1.27.

With the R1.50 fuel levy relief, prices will fall, but only by around 23 cents per litre.

The relief will be more impactful for Diesel users.

Low sulphur diesel is set to increase by R1.24, but with the fuel levy relief, it will fall by around R1.76 per litre.

Both fuels hit record highs in October.

World.title: Political parties intensify campaigns ahead of November polls
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - With just over a week to go before the local government elections, political parties are stepping up their campaigns.

ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa is heading to Johannesburg on Saturday.

He's expected to address voters at City Hall and then take the party's message to residents door to door.

Meanwhile, the DA is KZN for its final election rally in eThekwini.

And EFF Leader Julius Malema is criss-crossing the Gauteng province.

He'll be campaigning in Emfuleni, Ekurhuleni and Tshwane.

Major metros are set to be the battleground for the country's biggest parties.

World.title: Five killed in Cape Flats mass shooting
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Five people have been killed and three others wounded in a shooting in Lavender Hill, on the Cape Flats.

Police said the victims were drinking at a house in Blonde Street at around 8pm on Saturday, when gunmen burst in and opened fire.

Four men and a woman, aged between 21 and 33, died at the scene. Three others were taken to hospital with gunshot wounds.

Police believe the shooting may be linked to gang violence. The Anti-Gang Unit has launched a manhunt for the suspects.

World.title: Honeydew police sergeant arrested for rape
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A Honeydew police sergeant will appear in the Protea Magistrate’s Court tomorrow.

The 49-year-old has been charged with rape and sexual grooming.

IPID arrested the officer for raping a young family member.

The alleged abuse started when the girl was just 14 and continued until October 2024.

The officer allegedly gave her money to buy her silence.

World.title: Four arrested in suspect drug lab raid near Sun City
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Police have bust another suspected drug lab, this time in Ramokokastad near Sun City in the the North West.

Police arrested four people after a raid on a property in Thabeng Section.

They seized 800 kilograms of drugs and chemicals and equipment used to make Mandrax and crystal meth.

A manhunt has been launched for a fifth suspect who escaped arrest.

The suspects are expected to appear in the Mogwase Magistrate's Court soon.

World.title: Mbalula tells voters what ANC plans to deliver
World.content:
MPOLWENI - ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula has been campaigning in Mpolweni, KZN.

It comes after he collapsed following a Constitutional Court ruling in the ANC's favour about disputed candidate lists.

Mbalula thanked the community for their continued support.

"Above all, the issues here are matters that relate to housing, which is being attended to. And then the school has been down. We're going to visit the school. And there's going to be mobile classes that are going to come next week to the school. We'll visit. We're going to talk to the community as well.

"The issues with regard to road situation on the ground, that too has been attended to. We are with the mayor here, who briefed us about some of the things that are outstanding. There are issues of the transformer in terms of Eskom. The other transformer has been brought in. And then we're going to be talking to Eskom to extend the transformer to the rest of the community so that they can all of them be covered. So these are things that are doable, that we can do. So we thank our people for keeping the faith and the belief in the people's movement."

World.title: Youth voter apathy under the spotlight
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - There’s a growing disconnect between South Africa’s youth and political parties.

That’s according to Rivonia Circle, a non-profit think tank focused on democratic reform, policy development and leadership.

With the 4 November municipal elections just days away, the concern is whether young people are losing faith in the ballot box or simply disengaging from the political process.

Rivonia Circle's Naledi Ngqambela said young people are disengaged.

"I think young people are aware of what’s happening in the country. I just think that they’re so disengaged because political leaders are not doing what they said they will do. So, that’s why young people are sort of seemingly looking like they’re not engaged on what’s going on around the country. But also, political parties or political leaders are not engaging young people the way that they want to be engaged.

"So, as you mentioned that young people are always online and I think that’s where also political leaders need to be. Be online. Go to schools and engage in the way they want to be engaged. So that it’s fun and it’s also fulfilling for them to be part of the electoral system. I’ve seen an advert by the IEC actually, where they’re working with one of social media influencers, Alfie, and I think that was such a great initiative to work with social media influencers so that young people are always engaged and that young people know what is happening in the country.

"Because it’s much easier as people they gravitate towards. So they always need to be online, need to do fun things. If young people are out at a party place, politicians have to be there and they need to engage and they should say ‘clock it’ they should, you know, engage them at a level that they want to be engaged. So, I like that initiative by the IEC and I think we need more of that.”
