World.title: Pregnant woman rescued from collapsed Eastleigh building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya Red Cross workers after rescuing a man who trapped in the rubble.

A pregnant woman was on Saturday evening rescued from the multi-storey building that collapsed in Nairobi’s Eastleigh estate on Friday, October 23 and rushed to the Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) for treatment.

She is the second person to rescued as earlier in the afternoon the Kenya Red Cross society announced the rescue of a man from the ill-fated building.

The man was also taken to KNH for treatment with the society saying that the rescue followed hours of work put in by the search and rescue multi-agency team.

“After hours of painstaking work alongside multi-agency partners, our search and rescue teams in Eastleigh brought a trapped man out of the rubble,” said Red Cross.

The rescue comes even as the fate of six people who were reported missing on Friuday remains unknown with rescue teams still continuing with the search at the site of the collapsed building along Yusuf Haji Avenue.

The society said that 66 of the 67 construction workers who were at the site had been traced and accounted for but the search continues for people who may have been near the site of the collapsed building.

The development comes as police announced that they had launched a manhunt for the for the owner and contractor of a building.

Police spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said that officers had launched a probe in collaboration with relevant bodies to establish the cause of the collapse and determine criminal liability.

“Any individual or entity found culpable of negligence or of violating building regulations will face the full force of the law,” he said in a statement.

Nyaga called on members of public to stay completely clear of Yusuf Haji Avenue and 9th Street to give access to heavy excavators, specialised canine units and rescue personnel to perform their duties.

Earlier Saturday, at least 31 families reported their relatives missing as coordinated rescue efforts entered their second day.

No deaths have been reported so far.

The National Construction Authority (NCA) on Friday evening identified the developer, contractor, architect and structural engineer listed for the collapsed building.

The Authority has faced scrutiny over its oversight role, as Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja said the project had failed to comply with construction guidelines.

He said the county had forwarded relevant information to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations for further investigation.

In a statement, the NCA said the building was registered on July 30, 2025, as a proposed development on 9th Street in Eastleigh.

It identified 9th Street Plaza Limited as the developer and Stromax Holdings E.A. Limited as the contractor.

Emmanuel Mwangi Maina was listed as the project architect, while Joseph Muturi Mugu was named as the structural engineer.

World.title: Several feared trapped in Eastleigh building collapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

What was supposed to be a usually busy Friday afternoon in Eastleigh's 9th Street turned chaotic after an 18-floor building that was under construction came down, tumbling.

By Friday evening, rescue operations were still ongoing, with cries from people believed to have been trapped being heard from a distance as bulldozers and rescuers continued the search operation.

Two victims, a man and a woman, who were injured in the building had been rescued and rushed to hospital as the search continued.

Asha Jilo, one of the witnesses, said the building collapsed around 1:09 pm just after the afternoon prayers.

"Immediately after the building collapsed, we started contacting some people we know who work there, one of them was still available on the phone until around 3 pm, when his phone went offline," Jilo shared

On Fridays, Eastleigh is usually a hive of activities, being the main market day, but all the businesses were shut as police were battling rowdy youths, some of them believed to be opportunists.

The building, whose height was said to be about 15 floors, had not been cleared for occupation as required, raising questions about why the investors had allowed it to be taken.

It is said that the ground and first floors were already occupied by businesses, raising fears that the number of victims could be high. Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

At the time of the collapse, it is said that some construction workers were busy on the upper floors.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, who visited the scene after the collapse, was still gathering information about the building. The first priority was about saving lives.

“The building that collapsed is around 16 floors, and we have got information about the building, but what is more concerned right now is for us to save lives,” said Sakaja

Adding, “Equipment has already been mobilized, excavators and breakers, so we can be able to remove the big debris and save lives,’

The Governor said some developers engage qualified professionals to secure construction approvals before dismissing them and disregarding approved plans and safety standards.

He urged professional bodies to strengthen oversight, investigate such cases and take appropriate disciplinary action, stressing that developers must comply with approved designs, engage qualified personnel and obtain occupation certificates after safety inspections.

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud, who was at the scene, said that, according to reliable information, several people were trapped inside the debris, inside the big boulders, and the rescue effort is ongoing.

The city police boss said investigations will be carried out to ascertain who is responsible for any negligence.

“If there will be any death, that is negligence by murder. Whoever is the owner, whoever authorized the building, all of them will be charged properly. But that will come after thorough investigation is done,” he warned

Adding, “We will not excuse anybody on this matter. This has become now and then, and we will make sure that people face the law accordingly for any criminal negligence,”

World.title: Ruto hands over COMESA chairmanship, pushes for levy to fund regional programmes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President Ruto and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa during the handover of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa chairmanship at the bloc’s 25th Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, on Thursday, October 22, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has handed over the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chairmanship to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Ruto took over the one-year chairmanship from Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye at the 24th COMESA Summit in Nairobi on October 9, 2025.

His tenure focused on using digital technology to deepen regional integration, expand trade and promote inclusive growth.

He handed over the role on Thursday, October 22, during the 25th Comesa Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, where he urged the regional bloc to fast-track a market levy to finance its programmes and institutions.

“We cannot be ambitious in our plans and timid in our financing. Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for,” Ruto said.

He urged the Comesa Secretariat to fast-track Article 168 of the COMESA Treaty, which provides for the Comesa Market Levy, as the organisation seeks sustainable and predictable financing.

The treaty establishes the levy to generate resources for financing the bloc’s activities.

Ruto said officials from finance ministries, central banks and other relevant agencies would meet to consider a draft COMESA Resource Mobilisation Strategy aimed at strengthening member states’ ownership of regional programmes and finding new ways to raise funds.

He called on member states to make financing central to their discussions, warning that the bloc’s institutions and integration agenda would depend on their ability to fund agreed commitments.

“Can we finance what we commit, and deliver what we finance?” he asked.

Ruto also urged African countries to channel more of their domestic financial resources into African institutions rather than leaving funds in foreign accounts while development projects lack capital.

He said Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets, arguing that regional financial institutions could mobilise more of these resources to support trade, infrastructure and development.

Ruto named the Trade and Development Bank (TDB), the African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) and ZEP-RE among the institutions that could mobilise capital for regional priorities.

He urged African governments to place more reserves with these institutions, finance more projects through them and support their bonds and guarantees.

The outgoing Comesa chairperson said the bloc needed stronger regional value chains and more trade among member states as global supply chains faced disruption and protectionism returned.

“Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity,” he noted.

Ruto said Comesa’s economic growth rose from 5.6 per cent in 2024 to 6.4 per cent in 2025, while inflation fell from 31 per cent to 13.2 per cent.

Exports among member states increased by 10.5 per cent to $14.7 billion, their highest level between 2020 and 2025, while exports to global markets rose by 6 per cent to $212 billion, he said.

He argued that African countries needed to process more raw materials locally instead of exporting them and importing finished products.

“To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: invest with us, process with us, build with us,” Ruto added.

He called for partnerships based on mutual benefit and equal treatment, saying African countries should have a greater role in determining how their resources and markets contribute to economic development.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: PM responds to claims that citizens do not feel development fruits
World.content:
CAIRO, Oct 24 (MENA) – Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly stated during the closing ceremony of the Egypt 2026 Forum today, under the auspices of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, that some attempt to project a mental image that the citizen does not feel the fruits of development, affirming that what the historical presentation included today is sufficient to answer this question.

Madbouly added before concluding his speech that to the great people of Egypt, what this historical presentation included is sufficient to answer this question, and for those who want details, the total beneficiaries targeted by the presidential initiative Hayah Karima is 61 million citizens, with the first phase ending now benefiting 18 million citizens including 11 million citizens in Upper Egypt, asking whether these did not feel the fruits of development.

He added that the state managed to eliminate unsafe areas by executing housing units for about 1.5 million citizens, asking whether they did not feel the fruits of development, noting that without state intervention with these citizens, their fate would have been like others who died under rocks, lost their lives in torrent paths, or were electrocuted under high voltage wires.

He continued that the fruits of development enabled the state to spend billions of pounds on our people without any return for the government except the greatest, most important, and best return, which is protecting them from death, protecting their children, and working to secure a better future for them, and the reward for this with God is great.

He noted that 5.5 million citizens are currently registered in the first phase of the comprehensive health insurance system in the governorates of Port Said, Luxor, Ismailia, South Sinai, Suez, and Aswan, asking whether these do not enjoy the fruits of development, and 63 million citizens were screened and those in need treated for Hepatitis C, asking whether these did not return to life once again after their future was threatened.

Madbouli stated that 3.3 million operations were conducted to eliminate waiting lists, asking whether these millions did not benefit from the fruits of development, and two million families benefited from Sakan Kol Al-Masryeen projects and developing governorate capitals, asking whether this unprecedented number did not benefit from the fruits of development, besides eight million residents inhabiting unplannned areas developed by the state.

He added that the Suez Canal Economic Zone attracted investments providing 164,000 job opportunities, asking whether these youth and hundreds of thousands of others did not benefit from the fruits of development, besides 50,000 job opportunities provided by industrial complexes.

He continued that 16.2 million families benefited from efforts to connect natural gas to homes, and 8.3 million families benefited from support efforts for families most in need, among them 4.7 million families currently benefiting from the cash support program, 2.2 million families exited after their social and economic conditions improved, and 1.4 million families exited as a result of changing circumstances.

He completed that current average classroom density reached about 45 students compared to 100 students per classroom before 2014, asking whether they benefited or not, and the 150,000 teachers initiative to solve the teacher shortage problem benefited teachers, their families, students, and even the entire society.

Madbouli stated that until 2014, 10 or 12 percent of Egypt’s villages had sewage, and currently the percentage has become approximately 60 percent, asking whether all these citizens did not feel the fruits of development, affirming they certainly felt it, and hundreds of thousands of citizens used to ride trains without doors or windows along with breakdowns, while currently we have air-conditioned trains passing through Egypt’s villages, and we have a high-speed electric train, a light rail transit, a monorail, and endless phases of the subway. (MENA)

World.title: Sisi: Egypt faces water challenges as Nile provides over 98% of renewable water resources
World.content:
CAIRO, Oct 25 (MENA) – President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said Egypt faces a unique water challenge due to its geographical location and heavy reliance on the Nile River, which it shares with other Nile Basin countries and which provides more than 98 percent of its renewable water resources.

With population growth, rising water and food needs and the escalating impacts of climate change, Egypt continues to work to improve water-use efficiency, develop its water resources, and maximize their utilization, Sisi said.

In a recorded address delivered on Sunday at the opening of the ninth edition of Cairo Water Week, Sisi said one of humanity’s greatest civilizations had flourished along the banks of the Nile in Egypt since the dawn of history.

The Nile had been the foundation of stability and a driving force for development and prosperity, he said, adding that it was not merely a river for Egypt, but had always been and remained the lifeblood of the country and a bridge for communication and cooperation among peoples.

Speaking from the land of the Nile and civilization, Sisi welcomed participants in the ninth edition of Cairo Water Week, which has become an international platform for dialogue, the exchange of expertise and the building of partnerships.

“This year, we meet under the theme ‘Water as a Catalyst for Peace, Shared Prosperity and a Sustainable Planet,’” he said, describing the theme as a reflection of Egypt’s belief in the role of water in achieving development and strengthening stability and cooperation among countries and peoples.

Sisi affirmed that water issues rank high on Egypt’s foreign policy agenda as a driver of cooperation and shared prosperity, rather than a political tool for fueling conflicts and disputes.

The President said Egypt fully recognizes that it is not alone in facing these challenges, as countries worldwide are threatened by water scarcity, rising risks of droughts and floods and mounting pressure on resources amid growing demand for water, food and energy.

Water security has become a shared responsibility requiring genuine international cooperation, mobilization of funding, technology transfer and capacity building, he said.

Sisi added that Egypt attaches great importance to strengthening water cooperation based on respect for relevant international law at both the African and Arab levels. He also stressed Egypt’s commitment to exchanging expertise and developing projects and partnerships that serve the interests of their peoples.

Sisi affirmed that Egypt respects and supports the right of all Nile Basin countries to development, noting that Cairo has translated this position into practical action through cooperation with fellow African countries on proposed projects under investment programs in the southern Nile Basin, particularly in energy, agriculture and irrigation.

He said the experience had demonstrated that prior notification, the exchange of studies and consultations are practical tools for mobilizing project financing, building trust and safeguarding the interests of all parties, rather than means of obstructing development or imposing guardianship over any country.

He said the experience showed that genuine cooperation was possible when political will was present, adding that Egypt sought to extend this approach to the eastern Nile Basin in a way that serves the interests of Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia.

Every country has the right to develop and benefit from its natural resources, provided that it exercises this right responsibly without harming other countries or jeopardizing their water security, Sisi said. The fact that a river’s headwaters lie within a country’s territory does not give it the right to exercise unilateral control over a resource shared by several peoples, he added.

Sisi said Egypt had consciously chosen the path of cooperation and dialogue, based on its confidence in the justness of its cause and the legality of its position. Protecting the interests of the Egyptian people was a responsibility that Egypt would not shirk, he said, stressing that any expectation that Egypt would accept a fait accompli or compromise its water security was misplaced.

He added that Egypt had taken the lead in advocating cooperation based on international law, consultation, coordination, good-neighborly relations and the principle of causing no harm.

“We are one family united by the Nile, and our shared interests are greater than our differences,” Sisi said, noting that the Nile Basin possesses extensive resources and potential that, if managed and developed effectively, could meet the needs and aspirations of its peoples.

He called for joint efforts to transform these resources into partnerships that maximize shared benefits, safeguard the rights of all countries, and make the Nile a source of development, prosperity and stability for all Nile Basin peoples.

Sisi said the Nile has been a cradle of civilization and a bridge between peoples since the dawn of history, expressing Egypt’s desire to preserve it as a river that unites rather than divides, a resource whose benefits are shared by its peoples, and a waterway that safeguards the rights of all rather than an arena for imposing unilateral will.

Sisi renewed Egypt’s call to make water a catalyst for peace and shared prosperity, and to work together to move from crisis management to developing solutions and from commitments to implementation.

Announcing the opening of the ninth edition of Cairo Water Week, Sisi wished participants success in their deliberations and expressed hope that joint efforts would yield tangible results that strengthen peace and help secure a safer, fairer and more prosperous future for their peoples. (MENA)

World.title: President Sisi attends closing ceremony of Egypt Forum 2026
World.content:
President Abdel Fattah Sisi attended the closing ceremony of the Egypt Forum 2026 on Saturday, which featured presentations reviewing the country’s development achievements, discussions on economic and energy challenges, and young Egyptians’ aspirations for the future.

The ceremony opened with a recitation from the Holy Quran, followed by a documentary titled “What Took Place at the Forum,” which reviewed key discussions and ideas raised during the forum’s sessions, Presidential Spokesperson Ambassador Mohamed al-Shennawy said.

President Sisi also greeted Mahmoud Mohamed, a young man with hearing and speech disabilities, who had expressed his wish to meet the president in a film screened during the opening session. The president also greeted Talia, a young girl who had performed with the opening ceremony choir.

Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly then delivered a presentation beginning with a chronological overview of major developments in Egypt between 2011 and 2014.

He subsequently presented an interactive map showcasing projects and achievements implemented from 2014 to 2026.

At the end of his presentation, Madbouly presented President El-Sisi with a book documenting the country’s achievements over the past 12 years.

The second part of the ceremony featured a presentation titled “The Journey,” which reviewed the process of state-building and development projects implemented across various sectors, Shennawy said.

An economic commentator then delivered a presentation on the challenges facing the energy sector amid recent regional crises and their economic repercussions.

Three young influencers also presented key achievements made in recent years, each in their respective fields.

The ceremony also featured a film titled “The Dream of a Generation,” in which children under the age of 13 from Generation Alpha spoke about their aspirations and dreams for the future and their vision of the Egypt they hope to see in the coming years.

Prime Minister Madbouly subsequently announced the outcomes of the Egypt Forum 2026.

President Sisi then invited former Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy Mohamed Shaker to review achievements in the energy sector during a critical period and within a record timeframe.

Shaker highlighted the president’s pivotal personal role in helping Egypt overcome an energy crisis, including securing the best possible prices from international companies and addressing the country’s severe electricity shortage.

The presidential spokesperson added that the ceremony also featured success stories of outstanding Egyptians who had achieved international recognition in various fields. President al-Sisi joined them for a commemorative group photograph.

In his speech, the president said: “Over the past few days of this Forum, we have together witnessed chapters of our nation’s journey. We have spoken extensively about Egypt; about a reality we live with all its challenges; about truths we sought to lay bare before you with complete transparency and clarity; about a State whose protection commands our every effort to solidify its foundation and safeguard its resources and national assets; and about a bright future, by the grace of Allah Almighty, to which we aspire and toward which we work with unwavering resolve and steadfast devotion.”

“Through figures and facts, we reviewed the unprecedented achievements realized across our homeland, attainments that previously would have required long decades to accomplish.”

“Together, we engaged in a rich, constructive dialogue, giving full weight to views, proposals, and ideas that contribute to shaping a vision for the future of this nation.”

“I was keen to convene this Forum so that everyone may fully grasp the magnitude of the effort exerted, and continuing to be exerted, for Egypt, alongside our future aspirations within a collective framework that holds each and every one of us accountable to our responsibilities. For this nation belongs to all its sons and daughters, and upon every citizen rests the grave duty to safeguard it, preserve its stability, and chart its future,” the president said.

“In conclusion of this Forum, I wish to pause with you to reflect upon a meaning that runs deeper than mere numbers, and endures longer than projects and accomplishments; and to contemplate together two fundamental questions: Why did we embark on this journey? And where do we seek to arrive?”

“Since 2011, Egypt was not merely facing ordinary challenges or passing circumstances; rather, it stood at pivotal junctures in its modern history, wherein the Egyptian State came perilously close to the brink of collapse and downfall.”

“When I assumed the responsibility of leading the State in 2014, we were confronted with a formidable challenge, unprecedented in both scale and complexity. We were called upon to fulfill the legitimate hopes and aspirations of the Egyptian people to preserve their State, and to confront heinous terrorism and plots targeting the very existence of the State itself.”

“This had to be accomplished in parallel with managing the affairs of a great nation of Egypt’s stature, rebuilding infrastructure exhausted by decades of decline, upgrading public services burdened by long-standing neglect, addressing chronic, inherited crises, and reforming an administrative and governmental apparatus in dire need of comprehensive restructuring,” the president said.

“Above all else, we had to restore trust in State institutions, reinforce their foundation, and consolidate their stability, so that the wheels of daily life could turn once again across every corner of the Egyptian State.”

“Between merely protecting the present, or laying the groundwork for a future that the people of this nation truly deserve; between remaining captive to year-after-year crisis management, or possessing the courage and resolve to choose the harder, more enduring path: the true, root-cause confrontation of chronic problems, and addressing challenges through a comprehensive and responsible approach.”

“We chose the harder path. We did not possess the luxury of waiting or postponing tough decisions. We chose, with Almighty Allah’s support and the unwavering will of this great nation, to confront, to reform, and to build.”

“Thus, we embarked with sincerity and devotion upon a comprehensive course of reform and development within exceptional timelines, driven by our firm conviction that our national responsibility makes it incumbent upon us to ensure that our citizens do not continue to live through the problems of the past, nor pass them down as a burden to future generations.”

“The cost of this path has borne heavily upon the Egyptian citizen, who endured alongside us and served as the true cornerstone of this journey of development.”

“Allow me to extend a tribute of profound appreciation and pride to the great people of Egypt, who bore the burdens of this period with patience and fortitude, and whose awareness and steadfastness proved to be the State’s true anchor through its most formidable trials.”

“Allow me here to reaffirm that the State, the government, and the people constitute a single, indivisible entity and that the government, with all its institutions and agencies, is an integral part of the Egyptian people. It works tirelessly for their sake, serving their interests, and elevating their standard of living and quality of life within the limits of available resources and prevailing circumstances.

Duty compels us all to reject any and all attempts to portray State institutions as entities detached from the people or at odds with their interests, for such endeavors seek to undermine the cohesion of the Egyptian State, sow division, and fracture the internal front.”

“Our journey was never merely about projects constructed, roads paved, or cities expanding across our homeland; rather, it was a journey to rebuild the State’s capacity, awaken its latent strength, and lay the foundations for a renaissance whose impact reaches into the life of every Egyptian man and woman.”

“Our objective was not to alter the face of life on Egyptian soil, but to build a life that opens new horizons of hope, where a road becomes a gateway to opportunity, a factory a doorway to livelihood, a school the beginning of a dream, and urban development an expansion of hope.”

“I have always affirmed that popular awareness is the primary bulwark of nations, and that the building of states rests not solely on the resources they possess, but on the awareness, resolve, and devotion to work exemplified by their citizens.”

“Indeed, awareness is what enables us to comprehend the scale of our challenges relative to our available resources. And I stand fully confident that Allah Almighty observes the efforts we make, the sacred trust we bear, and the purity of our intentions; for He is all-knowing of what lies within hearts, and He never diminishes the reward of those who excel in good deeds.”

“Hence, our responsibility before Allah Almighty and before this great people demands that we spare no effort, that we seek utmost honesty and sincerity in every decision we take and every action we undertake, and that we remain steadfastly faithful to the sacred trust bestowed upon us by this nation. Together, we have navigated a path that was by no means easy. What we have achieved in our journey to consolidate the national State and anchor the pillars of the New Republic is an achievement of the entire Egyptian people, not of the government alone.”

“No one can claim that any human endeavor or developmental journey is devoid of lessons, errors, or challenges, for this is natural to all human experience. Yet our intentions remain sincere and faithful, backed by a genuine resolve to draw upon these lessons for the future.”

“I reaffirm once more that your awareness, steadfastness, and unity, Great People of Egypt, shall always remain the impenetrable fortress and first line of defense against all attempts to undermine the State or destabilize its security and stability. (MENA)

World.title: PM outlines government priorities for economic growth, public services at Egypt Forum 2026
World.content:
CAIRO, Oct 24 (MENA) – Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly outlined government plans to improve living standards, expand employment opportunities and strengthen public services during Egypt Forum 2026, held from October 19 to 24 under the patronage of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.

The six-day forum, held under the theme “A Look at Today, a Vision for Tomorrow,” was attended by government officials, experts and citizens to discuss economic challenges, development projects and their impact on everyday life.

Throughout the event, Madbouly addressed public concerns about education, housing, social protection, energy prices and economic reform, explaining the government’s spending priorities and plans to increase household incomes.

Madbouly said education remained a government priority, with efforts focused on reducing classroom overcrowding, addressing teacher shortages and improving teaching standards.

He discussed reforms to secondary education, including the introduction of the baccalaureate system, which provides students with additional opportunities to improve their examination results.

On urban development, the prime minister said Egypt’s national plan through 2052 included 39 new cities, with 27 already completed or under development.

He estimated that between 14 million and 15 million people currently live in new cities, explaining that the projects aim to reduce pressure on overcrowded urban areas and create employment opportunities.

Madbouly said the government had built more than two million housing units since 2014 and developed unsafe residential areas previously occupied by more than 350,000 families.

He added that the first phase of the Decent Life rural development initiative covered 1,477 villages, with investments exceeding LE450 billion.

The government is also preparing housing programs that include rental units, social housing and homes for middle-income families, with delivery planned over the next four years.

Addressing the rising cost of living, Madbouly said the government remained committed to protecting vulnerable households and improving the distribution of subsidies.

He said approximately 4.7 million families currently receive support through the Takaful and Karama program, which has assisted around 8.2 million families since its introduction.

Food and bread subsidy allocations have increased from LE 32.8 billion in the 2013/2014 financial year to approximately LE 178 billion this year, according to figures presented by the prime minister.

Madbouly also discussed the government’s response to higher global energy prices, explaining that the state had chosen to absorb additional costs rather than pass the full burden on to citizens.

He clarified that his earlier remarks about possible electricity cuts concerned hypothetical scenarios and did not constitute an announcement of planned power outages.

The prime minister said Egypt was accelerating its renewable energy plans, targeting a 45 percent share of the energy mix by 2028 and 50 percent by 2030.

He estimated that upgrading electricity networks to support the 2028 target would require investments of approximately LE 200 billion.

Madbouly presented the main objectives of Egypt’s proposed national economic transformation program for 2027–2030, which aims to increase production, strengthen private-sector participation and create more jobs.

The program targets economic growth of 6.8 percent by the 2029/2030 financial year, compared with 5.1 percent in the latest financial year.

It also aims to reduce inflation from 13.3 percent to between 5 percent and 7 percent, lower unemployment from 5.8 percent to 5.5 percent, and increase total investment from 12.7 percent to 20 percent of gross domestic product.

The government also plans to raise the private sector’s share of investment from 57.7 percent to 67 percent and increase tax revenues through a broader tax base rather than introducing new taxes.

Madbouly said the program would include measures to improve wages, increase personal income tax exemptions and expand access to healthcare, education and housing.

He reported that Egypt’s foreign currency reserves had reached $57.3 billion by the end of September 2026, compared with approximately $16.7 billion in the 2013/2014 financial year.

However, he said high debt-servicing costs, inflation, population growth and pressure on household purchasing power remained major economic challenges.

The prime minister announced that the program would undergo public consultations before its expected completion at the end of December.

During a session on entrepreneurship, Madbouly announced plans to establish a unit affiliated with the Cabinet to support startups and coordinate government efforts to address obstacles facing entrepreneurs.

The proposed unit would help emerging businesses secure support, access financing and expand into regional and international markets.

Madbouly said strengthening entrepreneurship and private investment would be important to creating employment opportunities and supporting economic growth.

Across the forum’s discussions, the prime minister maintained that the government’s development plans should produce measurable improvements in citizens’ lives, including better education, affordable housing, stronger purchasing power and more employment opportunities.

He said future economic policies would seek to balance long-term development with the immediate needs of Egyptian households, while directing more resources towards essential services and social protection. (MENA)

World.title: Egypt to experience rain, thunderstorms, and flash floods starting Sunday
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) predicts that the country will be affected by a low-pressure system and a widespread rainy spell, impacting various regions from Sunday through next Wednesday.

Satellite imagery indicates the presence of thunderclouds over parts of the southern Red Sea mountain ranges—specifically near Ras Banas and Abu Ramad—accompanied by rainfall of varying intensity.

Intermittent rains are also expected over the cities of Halayeb and Shalateen.

Rainy weather forecast

Weather maps suggest that this extensive rainy spell, which encompasses areas surrounding both the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, could potentially lead to flash floods.

The conditions are expected to begin this Sunday evening and continue into Monday, affecting the Red Sea region, South Sinai, and Upper Egypt.

Starting Wednesday, these conditions will affect the Mediterranean coast, the Nile Delta, the Suez Canal region, and North Sinai, potentially extending to parts of Greater Cairo, northern Upper Egypt, and the New Valley Governorate.

The EMA has also issued warnings regarding thunderstorms—including lightning and downdrafts—in these areas, with a particular focus on South Sinai, the Red Sea mountain range, Aswan, and the southern part of Upper Egypt (Aswan and the southern reaches of Luxor).

It has urged citizens to take necessary precautions and preparations to mitigate the impact of the weather, and to stay updated by following the latest bulletins issued by the EMA.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Saudi Arabia issues urgent decision over filming attacks and military sites
World.content:
Saudi Arabia on Saturday issued an urgent statement concerning the filming or documenting attacks against the country.

“Filming, publishing, or sharing information related to countering missiles and drones and their impact sites exposes you to legal liability,” the General Directorate of Saudi Civil Defense warned on the X platform.

Earlier on Saturday, the Saudi Civil Defense announced that the threat had passed for the governorates of Taif, Jeddah, and Yanbu, as well as the Makkah region.

It urged residents to continue following safety instructions and to strictly avoid gathering in crowds or taking photographs.

World.title: France sees another weekend of mass protests with nearly 1,000 detained
World.content:
Nearly 1,000 people were detained across France Saturday, the Interior Ministry said, as a wave of protests airing economic grievances returned to the streets of its major cities.

A massive police presence was met with some violent clashes in Marseille and Bordeaux as well as the capital, but the largely peaceful demonstrations were not marred by the scale of violence that erupted the previous weekend.

Around 110,000 of the over 410,000 protesters were in Paris, the ministry said, roughly the same number who demonstrated in the capital a week earlier.

Protesters have been calling for greater investment in the country’s education system, more opportunities for its young workers and solutions to surging living costs.

“In Paris, we had a major demonstration that took place peacefully, like most protest marches across the entire country,” Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez told reporters, saying that almost 1,000 people were detained nationwide.

Nuñez said the police had restricted protesters’ movements. “They were prevented from staging unauthorized roving protests or heading toward city centers,” he said.

“In certain cities there was some damage or looting of businesses, in very limited numbers,” Nuñez added, but far less than during protests a week ago.

Nuñez said there had been “no targeted attacks” on public buildings such as town halls and police stations, as seen last weekend.

However, security forces faced an “extremely high level of violence,” Nuñez added, “with projectiles constantly being thrown and mortar fireworks fired.” He said security forces would remain deployed until very late Saturday evening local time to guard against looting.

Some 70,000 police officers had been mobilized across the country Saturday, the Interior Ministry said, as French authorities launched an enormous security operation for the second round of protests.

Specialist SWAT units, helicopters, armored vehicles, police dogs and water cannon were at the ready as part of the operation, after more than half a million people took to the streets last Saturday.

After a peaceful march through Paris, a crowd of several thousand protesters confronted police, who used tear gas and a water cannon to block them, according to a CNN team at the scene.

The clashes broke out at the Porte de Vincennes, the endpoint of the march.

In France’s second city Marseille, protesters launched mortar fireworks toward police during running street skirmishes, and there were reports of looting in various parts of the city, including a jewelry store with smashed windows and a supermarket being pillaged, CNN’s French affiliate BFMTV reported.

Images from Bordeaux, on France’s Atlantic coast, showed tear gas being used against protesters in the famous Place de la Bourse. Videos showed some masked protesters hurling objects at police as the tear gas drifted across the square.

In Nice, dozens of far-right activists attacked people protesting peacefully Saturday, BFMTV reported.

The leader of far-left party La France Insoumise, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, warned that nationwide industrial action will take place on November 5 if French President Emmanuel Macron does not respond to protesters’ demands.

“A general strike… looms over the government for the 5th of November,” he told BFMTV, while speaking from the front line of Saturday’s demonstration in Paris.

As scores of protesters took to the streets in cities across France on Saturday, anti-government demonstrations were also taking place in a number of other European countries.

In the Italian cities of Naples, Rome and Milan, stores boarded up their windows ahead of planned protests, after looting at earlier demonstrations.

Protesters in the Albanian capital Tirana set fire to dumpsters and threw stones and tear gas canisters.

And in Brussels, students held up placards and barricaded streets. Police deployed a water cannon, according to Belgium’s public broadcaster VRT.

World.title: North Korea’s Kim crosses new bridge into China as trade ties warm
World.content:
Reuters —

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday, Xinhua reported, crossing a newly opened bridge in a symbolic move seen as highlighting Beijing and Pyongyang’s push to expand trade ties.

Kim was accompanied during his visit by China’s fourth-highest-ranked official Wang Huning, who conveyed greetings from President Xi Jinping, the official Xinhua news agency said.

Kim arrived in Dandong via the New Yalu River Bridge connecting North Korea and China, a South Korean government official said on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak publicly.

The new bridge is expected to help move heavy equipment, raw materials and energy products that North Korea needs for development. Its official opening this month is the latest sign of warming ties between Beijing and Pyongyang, after two summits between their leaders in the past 13 months.

China, which fought alongside North Korea in the 1950-1953 Korean War, remains Pyongyang’s main economic and diplomatic backer and accounts for most of its official trade.

Chinese TV shows Kim walking on bridge

But North Korea’s deepening military ties with Russia since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine have led analysts to question whether Pyongyang is becoming less reliant on Beijing.

Kim’s trip nevertheless points to a renewed push by China and North Korea to bolster their economic relationship.

South Korea’s Yonhap news agency had earlier reported that Kim was expected to return to North Korea after Saturday’s visit.

Footage from Chinese state broadcaster CCTV showed Kim walking on the bridge, lined by people waving flags, towards North Korea.

Xinhua said Wang accompanied Kim to a Korean War memorial in Dandong, where the North Korean leader paid tribute to Chinese People’s Volunteer Army soldiers who fought alongside North Korea during the three-year conflict. Kim also toured a Dandong automobile factory, it said.

New Yalu River Bridge boosts bilateral ties

China and North Korea opened the 3 km (2 mile) New Yalu River Bridge, their most significant land border crossing, this month after a long delay, aiming to rejuvenate trade and commerce after years of strained ties and ‌pandemic-related disruptions.

This photo taken on Oct. 15, 2026 shows trucks running on the new China-DPRK Yalu River bridge. The new China-DPRK Yalu River bridge officially opened to traffic on Thursday, with both sides jointly holding an opening ceremony on this cross-border artery. Pan Yulong/Xinhua/Getty Images

“Kim has given his imprimatur to bilateral trade by crossing the New Yalu River Bridge to enter China,” said Christopher Green, a Korea specialist at Leiden University in the Netherlands, saying the delayed opening had shown how dysfunctional the relationship had become.

During a meeting on Saturday, Wang told Kim that China was ready to use the bridge’s opening to expand personnel exchanges and economic and trade cooperation, Xinhua said.

A visit by Kim now is consistent with the current phase of closer economic ties and more frequent high-level exchanges between China and North Korea, said Lu Chao, an expert in China-North Korea relations at the Liaoning Academy of Social Sciences, a Chinese government think-tank in Shenyang.

“The opening of the bridge has resolved a major bottleneck in China-North Korea trade logistics,” Lu said. “With the logistics constraint eased, bilateral trade is likely to increase further.”

Trump waits for Kim to engage

Kim’s last known visit to China was in September 2025, to attend the 80th Victory Day celebrations in Beijing, when he held a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Xi made a state visit to North Korea in June.

US President Donald Trump has been eager to jump-start talks with North Korea, but US and South Korean officials see fading chances of him meeting Kim this year, Reuters reported on Friday.

China hosts a summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum next month in Shenzhen, which Trump is expected to attend.

World.title: Liberia: Judge Cites Evidence in Finding NSA Staff Peter Bon Jallah Guilty of Statutory Rape, Kidnapping
World.content:
Criminal Court E Acquits Him of Gang Rape; Orders Pre-Sentence Report Before Sentencing

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

Monrovia — Assigned Circuit Judge Wesseh Alphonsus Wesseh Sr. has found 63-year-old Peter Bon Jallah, a staff member of the National Security Agency (NSA), guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping, but not guilty of gang rape in a case involving a 16-year-old boy.



In a verdict delivered Friday, October 23, Judge Wesseh said he had reviewed the evidence presented by both parties and considered the arguments advanced during the trial before determining that the prosecution had established sufficient grounds to convict Jallah on two of the three charges.

The judge framed his decision around three central questions: whether the prosecution’s evidence justified a conviction for gang rape, statutory rape and kidnapping.

He answered the first question in the negative, acquitting Jallah of gang rape, but answered the other two in the affirmative, finding him guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping.

Following the verdict, Judge Wesseh ordered Jallah remanded at Monrovia Central Prison pending the submission of a pre-sentence and behavioral report by the Bureau of Probation Services at the Ministry of Justice.

The judge directed the clerk of court to communicate with the probation authorities to ensure that the report is made available as soon as possible to assist the court in determining the appropriate sentence.

Judge Identifies Three Decisive Questions

In his ruling, Judge Wesseh said the court had examined the facts and circumstances contained in the evidence presented at trial before identifying three issues that were decisive to the case.

On the gang rape charge, the judge concluded that the prosecution’s evidence did not provide sufficient and reasonable grounds to convict Jallah. He consequently declared the defendant not guilty and acquitted him of that charge.

However, on statutory rape, the judge found that the evidence presented by the prosecution provided sufficient grounds for conviction.

He reached a similar conclusion on the kidnapping charge, finding Jallah guilty on that count as well.

The ruling represents a split decision in a case that involved allegations of repeated sexual abuse of a minor and the alleged confinement of the complainant for several days.

Indictment Details Alleged Repeated Abuse

According to the indictment summarized in the court’s verdict, Jallah and two unidentified men were indicted by the Montserrado County Grand Jury during the February 2026 Term of Court for gang rape, statutory rape and kidnapping.

The indictment alleged that Jallah and the two other men acted individually and jointly in sexually abusing the complainant on multiple occasions.

It further stated that the complainant, who was 16 at the time of the alleged incidents, lived in the Airfield Shark Community in Monrovia and regularly visited Jallah’s residence to perform domestic work for which he received compensation.

The indictment alleged that on November 29 and December 24, 2025, Jallah lured the boy to his residence in the Sharks Community of Airfield Sinkor, where he allegedly sexually assaulted him.

The most serious allegations concerned an incident said to have occurred on January 1, 2026, after the boy participated in a community football league at the Kpelle Town football field.

According to the indictment, the boy encountered Jallah near his residence after the game. Jallah allegedly offered to purchase football boots for him and instructed him to return home to bathe before accompanying him.

The indictment alleged that the two subsequently travelled by car to a building in the Camp Johnson Road area of downtown Monrovia, where the boy was allegedly held for three days and sexually abused by Jallah and the two unidentified men.

It further alleged that on January 3, 2026, at about 10 p.m., the boy was concealed at the back of Jallah’s vehicle and abandoned along 15th Street in Sinkor.

The complainant was reportedly rescued by private security guards, who alerted his parents. His mother and other relatives subsequently took him to the John F. Kennedy Medical Center for medical examinations.

These details formed part of the allegations contained in the indictment and should not be interpreted as separate findings by the court unless expressly established in the judge’s ruling.

Case Faced Procedural Delays

The court’s verdict also outlined the procedural history of the case, which experienced several delays before proceeding to a full trial.

The case was initially before Criminal Assizes Court “A” for Montserrado County before being transferred to Criminal Court “E” for evidentiary proceedings and a full trial.

Jallah was arraigned on June 18, 2026, and pleaded not guilty to the indictment. He subsequently elected to be tried by a judge without a jury.

The trial was delayed after the prosecution filed a motion seeking a change of venue. Following the denial of that motion, the prosecution petitioned the Chamber Justice for a writ of certiorari, but the petition was denied and the case was ordered to proceed.

The proceedings encountered another setback when the judge previously presiding over the matter could not continue taking evidence after the regular sitting of the court expired.

On August 5, 2026, the case was reassigned for trial.

According to the written verdict, the prosecution presented 13 regular witnesses and six rebuttal witnesses, while the defense called eight regular witnesses and three subpoenaed witnesses from the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, Orange GSM and the John F. Kennedy Medical Center.

The prosecution’s witnesses included the complainant, police investigators, medical personnel and Rwandan forensic examiner Pascal Bavugirije.

The defense witnesses included Jallah himself and several other individuals who testified on his behalf.

The number of witnesses listed in the written verdict differs from earlier accounts that referred to 12 prosecution witnesses, making the court’s official record the appropriate reference for the final tally.

DNA and Medical Evidence Featured at Trial

The prosecution relied in part on forensic findings linking Jallah’s DNA profile to biological material recovered from four clothing exhibits.

However, testimony attributed to the forensic examiner indicated that the findings could not establish precisely when or how the biological material was deposited.

The defense challenged the prosecution’s interpretation of the evidence, pointing to alleged inconsistencies in the complainant’s account and limitations in the medical and forensic findings.

Medical evidence also featured prominently in the proceedings. Earlier accounts of the trial referenced a John F. Kennedy Medical Center report that reportedly found no visible signs of anal trauma, while the parties disputed the significance of the medical and forensic findings.

The precise weight the court assigned to each item of evidence should be established from the complete written ruling and trial record. The verdict provided identifies the court’s conclusions on the three charges but does not detail its assessment of every witness or exhibit.

Prosecution and Defense Clash in Final Arguments

During final arguments on Thursday, October 22, prosecution lawyer Cllr. Calvin H. Momolu urged Judge Wesseh to convict Jallah, maintaining that the evidence presented during the trial supported the charges.

Defense lawyer Cllr. Wilfred Sayeh argued that the prosecution had failed to prove its case to the required legal standard. The defense questioned the police investigation and challenged the interpretation of the medical, forensic and testimonial evidence.

The judge adjourned the proceedings until Friday morning to review the evidence and arguments before delivering the verdict.

In reaching his decision, Judge Wesseh found the prosecution’s evidence sufficient to convict Jallah of statutory rape and kidnapping, while concluding that it did not warrant a conviction for gang rape.

The two other men named in the indictment were not brought under the court’s jurisdiction and were not tried alongside Jallah in these proceedings.

Defense Plans Appeal

Following the verdict, defense lawyer Cllr. Sayeh announced plans to appeal the ruling to the Supreme Court of Liberia.

The planned appeal would give the defense an opportunity to challenge the lower court’s decision before the country’s highest court.

In the meantime, Jallah remains ordered remanded at Monrovia Central Prison while the Bureau of Probation Services prepares the report requested by Judge Wesseh.

The report is intended to assist the court in determining the sentence to be imposed following the guilty verdicts.

The case now enters the sentencing stage before the anticipated appeal, with the court having found Jallah guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping but acquitted him of gang rape.

Jallah had pleaded not guilty to all charges, while his defense challenged the prosecution’s evidence, citing alleged inconsistencies in the complainant’s account and limitations in the medical and forensic findings.

— Acquits NSA Staff of Gang Rape; Defense Announces Supreme Court Appeal

MONROVIA, Liberia — Criminal Court “E” at the Temple of Justice has found 63-year-old Peter Bon Jallah, a staff member of the National Security Agency (NSA), guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping but not guilty of gang rape in a case involving a 16-year-old boy.

By Victoria Wesseh



The verdict was handed down Friday, October 23, 2026, by Assigned Circuit Judge Wesseh Alphonso Wesseh Sr., following final arguments by the prosecution and defense on Thursday.

Following the verdict, Judge Wesseh ordered Jallah’s remand at Monrovia Central Prison. However, the court had not announced the sentence at the time of reporting.

Defense lawyer Cllr. Wilfred Sayeh has announced plans to appeal the ruling to the Supreme Court of Liberia, setting the stage for another legal battle over the verdict.

The court acquitted Jallah of gang rape. The two other individuals allegedly involved in the incident on Camp Johnson Road were not presented during the trial.

Prosecution Presented 12 Witnesses

During the trial, prosecutors presented 12 witnesses, including the complainant, police investigators, medical personnel, and Rwandan forensic examiner Pascal Bavugirije.

The prosecution also relied on DNA findings that linked Jallah’s DNA profile to biological material recovered from four clothing exhibits.

However, the forensic examiner reportedly testified that the findings could not establish when or how the biological material was deposited.

Jallah had pleaded not guilty to all charges, while his defense challenged the prosecution’s evidence, citing alleged inconsistencies in the complainant’s account and limitations in the medical and forensic findings.

Defense Challenges Evidence, Plans Appeal

During Thursday’s final arguments, prosecution lawyer Cllr. Calvin H. Momolu urged the court to convict Jallah, arguing that the evidence presented during the trial supported a guilty verdict.

Defense lawyer Cllr. Sayeh countered that the prosecution had failed to establish the allegations beyond a reasonable doubt. The defense questioned the interpretation of medical and forensic findings, as well as aspects of the police investigation.

The competing arguments centered on witness testimony, medical findings, forensic evidence, and whether the prosecution had sufficiently established the elements of the charged offenses.

With the guilty verdict on two charges and the defense’s announced intention to appeal, the case is expected to proceed to the Supreme Court, where Jallah’s lawyers will seek a review of the lower court’s decision.

World.title: Liberia Poised to Surpass 2026 Intellectual Property Registration Target
World.content:
The Government of Liberia, through the Liberia Intellectual Property Office (LIPO), has announced that it is on track to surpass its annual intellectual property registration target after recording 526 registrations by the end of the third quarter of 2026.

Speaking at the Ministry of Information’s regular press briefing on Thursday, LIPO Director General Hon. Garmai Koboi noted that the Office had achieved 95.6 percent of its annual target of 550 registrations — expressing confidence that the current pace of registrations would push the year-end figure beyond the projected benchmark.

According to Hon. Koboi, trademarks accounted for the overwhelming majority of registrations, with 483 recorded during the period, followed by 40 copyright registrations and three industrial designs.

Of the total, Hon. Koboi further disclosed that 174 of the registrations were by Liberian-owned businesses and foreign nationals with established business operations in the country.



“With 526 applications recorded against an annual target of 550, we have achieved 95.6 percent of our FY2026 intellectual property registration target, leaving an outstanding balance of just 24 applications, representing 4.4 percent of the annual target,” Hon. Koboi added. “This performance reflects the work we are doing to strengthen intellectual property awareness and engagement among businesses, entrepreneurs, and other key stakeholders through targeted outreach, capacity-building initiatives, and stakeholder collaboration.”

According to Hon. Koboi, the uptake in registration is down to LIPO’s ongoing efforts to make intellectual property services more accessible, particularly to entrepreneurs, creators, and small businesses seeking to protect and commercialize their innovations, brands, and creative works.

“These achievements reflect the progress we are making toward building a stronger and more inclusive intellectual property ecosystem in Liberia,” the Director General said. “By supporting enterprise development, promoting creativity and innovation, strengthening intellectual property protection, and expanding access to IP services for SMEs and creators, we are seeing a lot of uptake in our registration and use of the IP system.”

Highlighting LIPO’s other achievements, Hon. Koboi pointed to the implementation of the Business and Intellectual Property Management Clinic (BIPMC), undertaken in partnership with the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) through its GROW-2 Project.

The initiative, according to LIPO and UNIDO, reached 142 entrepreneurs across Lofa, Bong, Nimba and Margibi counties, providing practical training, business advisory support and technical guidance on intellectual property identification, registration and management.

At the closure of the clinic, 90 intellectual property applications were filed for the first time by enterprises in these counties, of which 39 resulted in the issuance of intellectual property registration certificates to applicants who satisfied the legal and regulatory requirements under the Liberia Intellectual Property Act of 2016.

The project, according to Hon. Koboi, forms part of a broader national effort by the Government to integrate intellectual property protection into business development, particularly in agriculture, food processing, fashion, manufacturing and other sectors where entrepreneurs increasingly rely on brands, creative designs and product differentiation to compete in the marketplace.

Speaking also, Hon. Koboi noted that LIPO, in collaboration with the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), has expanded the 2nd edition of the Intellectual Property Management Clinic (IPMC) to 40 SMEs in four counties, providing specialized one-on-one mentorship support to 40 small and medium-sized enterprises across Montserrado, Nimba, Bong and Lofa counties.

The initiative provides training and technical advisory support to participating businesses in order to help them strengthen their intellectual property management practices, minimize infringement risks and identify opportunities for business growth and market expansion.

“These projects support the government’s commitment under the ARREST Agenda to its 2029 vision of developing a robust intellectual property ecosystem, as they expand access to intellectual property protection services for businesses and creators while equipping them with the knowledge and practical guidance needed to understand, protect, and effectively manage their intellectual property assets,” Hon. Koboi noted.

Meanwhile, Hon. Koboi has noted that one of the greatest achievements for the office this year has been the successful completion of the national stakeholder validation of Liberia’s National Intellectual Property Policy and Strategy (NIPPS), describing the exercise as an important step toward establishing a coordinated framework for intellectual property development.

The document is intended to strengthen coordination among public institutions and other stakeholders while positioning intellectual property as a tool for innovation, enterprise development, creativity and economic diversification.

The completion of the validation exercise represents a key milestone in Liberia’s efforts to establish a more structured national approach to intellectual property development, although further steps will be required before the framework becomes fully operational.

The LIPO Director General has also disclosed that the institution is preparing to digitize its intellectual property registration services through the Intellectual Property Administration System (IPAS), with technical assistance from WIPO. The planned introduction of the system is expected to modernize the administration of intellectual property applications, streamline registration procedures, and improve the efficiency of service delivery.

In a separate development, the LIPO Director General has appealed to the Liberian Senate to give attention to outstanding international instruments submitted by the President for ratification, emphasizing their potential importance to the country’s agriculture, tourism and creative sectors.

Hon. Koboi noted that the ratification of relevant instruments could strengthen Liberia’s ability to benefit from international intellectual property protection frameworks, particularly in areas involving geographical indications and the protection of products associated with specific geographical origins.

“We also want to appeal to the Senate to look at all outstanding instruments submitted by the President for ratification,” Hon. Koboi noted. “These instruments are very cardinal to our agriculture sector, for example, looking at our potential geographical indications, including our Liberian coffee, the tourism sector, our local government and the creative industries.”

Geographical indications are intellectual property protections used to identify products whose qualities, reputation or other characteristics are linked to a particular geographical origin.

World.title: Liberia’s Supreme Court Weighs Whether Parliament Defied Its Order in Expelling Outspoken Lawmaker
World.content:
MONROVIA, Liberia — Liberia’s Supreme Court on Thursday reserved judgment in a case that could determine whether the country’s House of Representatives defied a court order when it expelled one of its most outspoken members, Yekeh Kolubah, in April.

By Victoria G. Wesseh

The case turns on a narrow but consequential question: was the House leadership legally served with a Supreme Court order instructing it to halt proceedings against Kolubah before it voted to remove him? If it was, the vote may have been taken in breach of a binding judicial directive. If not, the House may have been free to act.



How the Dispute Began

Kolubah represented District 10 of Montserrado County, which includes the capital, Monrovia, and was long one of the Legislature’s most combative voices. The disciplinary case against him followed a controversial statement he made about the Makona River boundary dispute, one that many considered provocative, even offensive.

Kolubah was formally notified on April 9, 2026, to appear before the House Committee on Rules, Order and Administration on April 13. He and his lawyers walked out of a later committee hearing after it refused to grant them an additional five days and access to evidence.

His lawyers then asked the Supreme Court for a writ of prohibition, an order used to stop a body from exceeding its authority. Associate Justice Yussif D. Kaba granted the petition on April 16, summoning House leaders to a conference on April 20 and ordering them to stay all further proceedings pending its outcome. The directive was addressed to Speaker Richard Nagbe Koon, Deputy Speaker Thomas Fallah, the House Chief Clerk, the Sergeant-at-Arms and everyone acting under their authority.

The next day, the House went ahead. Kolubah was expelled by the full House on Friday, April 17, after a resolution was signed by 49 of the chamber’s 73 members, the two-thirds majority the Constitution requires. The resolution said he was removed for acts and utterances deemed unpatriotic and detrimental to the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

The Service Dispute

The House says it was never properly served. Its lawyers cited Rule 26.5 of the House rules, which names the Sergeant-at-Arms as the only officer authorised to receive court orders on behalf of the House. Court records show the Supreme Court Marshal instead served the documents on a receptionist and a computer operator attached to the offices of the Speaker and the Chief Clerk.

That argument has already succeeded once. In May 2026, Justice Kaba dismissed Kolubah’s follow-up complaint, known as a bill of information, for improper service, reportedly finding that the House had not been properly served with the writ and stay order. Kolubah appealed to the full five-member bench, which heard arguments on Thursday.

Jonathan Massaquoi, who leads Kolubah’s legal team, told the justices that the validity of service should be judged by Liberia’s Civil Procedure Law, not by the House’s internal rules for handling correspondence.

He cited Section 3.38(9), which states: “Personal service upon a subdivision of the government subject to suit or upon a municipal corporation shall be made by reading and delivering the summons to the chief executive thereof.”

On that basis, the petitioners argued that delivering the order to the office of the Speaker, the House’s presiding officer, was sufficient. A court officer identified as Joshua B. delivered the document there, they said, and a receptionist acknowledged receipt and signed for a copy.

Whether the provision covers the House at all is an open question. It refers specifically to “a subdivision of the government subject to suit” or “a municipal corporation,” and the Court must decide whether a branch of the national Legislature falls into either category.

Did the House Defy the Court?

The justices must weigh the wording of the order, the Marshal’s report of service, the receptionist’s acknowledgment and the legal standing of the office that received it.

Even a clear answer on service may not end the dispute. If the Court upholds the dismissal, it will not necessarily have examined or endorsed the disciplinary proceedings; and a win for Kolubah on service would not automatically prove the expulsion unconstitutional.

Other questions hang over the vote itself. A Bomi County lawmaker has denied backing the expulsion, raising questions about whether the House reached the legally required majority. A media adviser to Speaker Koon also told FrontPage Africa the expulsion took place on April 22, not April 17, before abruptly ending the conversation. A later date could matter, because it would fall after the scheduled court conference.

The case has become a test of the balance between Liberia’s branches of government. Critics have likened it to the recent standoff over former Speaker Fonati Koffa, which tested the limits of legislative authority. Prominent lawyer Tiawan Saye Gongloe has said the Court’s options include voiding the expulsion, holding House leaders in contempt, or ordering Kolubah’s reinstatement pending a hearing that satisfies due process.

The Court did not say when it would rule.
