World.title: Liberia: PLP Elevates Zarwolo to Two Top Posts as Party Eyes New Political Framework With Bility’s CMC
World.content:
MONROVIA, Liberia — The People’s Liberation Party (PLP) has appointed education policy expert Tonzeah N. Zarwolo to two senior leadership positions, a move that could position him to help shape the party’s policy direction as it explores political collaboration with Musa Hassan Bility’s Citizens Movement for Change (CMC).

Zarwolo, a former PLP National Youth Chairman, has been named National Vice Chairman for Political Affairs and Acting National Secretary General, according to two appointment letters dated October 22, 2026.

The appointments come as the PLP engages in discussions with Bility’s CMC about a possible political collaboration intended to offer an alternative to the country’s established political blocs, the Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC) and the ruling Unity Party (UP).

While neither appointment letter explicitly links Zarwolo’s elevation to the discussions, his combination of political, administrative and education policy experience could make him a significant figure in developing the principles and policy priorities of any proposed arrangement.

A Possible Role in Policy Development

Zarwolo’s professional background could be particularly relevant if the proposed collaboration moves beyond political consultations toward developing a formal policy document.

An education policy expert, he has worked on national education projects involving the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and CODE Canada. He is also a university lecturer.

That experience could provide a foundation for contributing to discussions on education reform, public-sector performance, institutional accountability and national development priorities.

Zarwolo’s appointment as National Vice Chairman for Political Affairs could place him in a position to coordinate discussions on behalf of the PLP, while his role as Acting National Secretary General could give him a hand in documenting decisions and coordinating the party’s internal processes.

However, there is no confirmation in the appointment letters that he has been assigned to lead or draft a policy document for the proposed collaboration.

The Search for a Different Political Arrangement

The PLP’s reported discussions with Bility’s CMC come amid wider efforts by Liberian opposition parties to determine how they might cooperate ahead of the 2029 general and presidential elections.

In September, the CMC withdrew from a proposed opposition coalition process convened by former President George Weah, arguing that the draft arrangement did not adequately reflect its objectives. The party has emphasized the need for cooperation built around a clear reform agenda rather than political unity alone.

That position underscores a central question for any alternative political framework: whether participating parties can agree not only on political cooperation but also on a defined program for governing and addressing Liberia’s challenges.

For the PLP and CMC, a formal arrangement could require decisions on policy priorities, accountability mechanisms, internal decision-making, the roles of participating parties and how commitments would be communicated to the public.

Zarwolo’s policy background could be relevant to that process, particularly if the parties seek to develop proposals grounded in sectoral experience and implementable public policy rather than a general declaration of political unity.

Zarwolo Accepts Both Appointments

Zarwolo thanked the Political Leader, Tapple Doe, Bernard Blue Benson, National Chairman, David Woods Beyan Sr. National Vice Chair for Administration and the wider PLP membership for the confidence placed in him.

“I hereby formally accept these appointments and assure the Party of my unwavering commitment to discharging my responsibilities with diligence and loyalty,” he said.

He pledged to work with the party’s leadership and fellow partisans to advance its collective vision and strengthen its ideals.

World.title: Liberia: Commerce Minister Designate Plan Meets a Market That Isn’t Waiting
World.content:
MONROVIA — Stephen M. Yekeson Jr. told senators Wednesday that he wants to be “judged by what is delivered.” His confirmation statement gives the Senate one promise it can test within 100 days, and many more it cannot.

By Rodney D Sieh

Appearing before the Senate Committee on Commerce and Industry, the acting Commerce and Industry Minister set out a vision to have Liberia “produce more of what Liberia consumes” by 2029. He pledged to protect consumers, enforce Liberian-only business sectors and cut the cost of moving goods “between the ship and the shop.”



His firmest commitment: within 100 days, the ministry will publish weekly prices for rice, fuel and cement in all 15 counties. Beyond that, the statement leans on verbs such as “work with,” “engage” and “address,” with few numbers, dates or budgets attached. Set against the problems now pressing on traders and households, the distance between promise and mechanism is where the scrutiny belongs.

A stronger dollar that isn’t reaching the market

Yekeson’s most striking admission was that prices have kept rising “in spite of a stronger Liberian Dollar.” The Liberian dollar was Africa’s best-performing currency in September, closing the month at about L$172 to US$1.

Small traders in Monrovia say the gains are not passed on. They report that some wholesalers still price stock at about L$190 to the dollar while the market rate sits near L$170, a gap of nearly 12 percent.

On October 6, Yekeson announced a five-point plan under which the ministry would work with the Central Bank to require supermarkets, wholesalers and retailers to post the bank’s daily exchange rate. That measure does not appear in his Senate statement. Instead, he cites a “reengineered” Price Analysis Department and a better-resourced Inspectorate. Whether the posting rule is still coming, and when, is a question the committee should put to him.

Fuel: a review, but no formula

Fuel is where the Senate already has its own findings. A Senate probe found that diesel rose from L$840 to L$1,235 a gallon between October 2024 and September 2026, a 47 percent increase. Gasoline climbed from L$775 to L$985 over the same period. The probe also found that Bea Mountain paid nothing on 16.4 million gallons of diesel.

The senator leading that inquiry proposed that the Liberia Petroleum Refining Company (LPRC) publish its full pricing formula every week. Yekeson’s statement moves in that direction but stops short. He promises to review pricing with the LPRC, and says regulated prices should be “transparent, rule-based and regularly reviewed,” reflecting verified import costs, duties, transport and a reasonable margin.

He does not commit to publishing that formula. His weekly price list would show what motorists pay at the pump, not how the figure was reached. He also names the LPRC, a petroleum body, as his partner in reviewing rice and cement pricing, a pairing he did not explain.

Rice: a global squeeze is coming

The next test may arrive before his 100 days are up. World rice prices are up about 67 percent on the year and hit a 26-month high in early October.

At home, the price of the staple was last fixed in March. After an emergency meeting with six major importers, the ministry announced that a 25kg bag would stay at US$14.00 wholesale and US$14.50 retail.

With import costs climbing, importers are likely to push for an increase. Yekeson’s formula of verified costs plus a reasonable margin may justify one. His weekly price list will then put any rise in public view, county by county. The Senate should ask him now whether US$14.50 can hold, and on what basis it would change.

An Inspectorate that barely registers

Yekeson promises inspectors will pursue “hoarding, collusion, false invoicing and short measures.” The ministry’s own figures suggest little enforcement capacity today.

At a budget hearing last week, he reported that the ministry had collected about US$4.12 million by September 30. Of that, inspectorate fees and fines brought in roughly US$48,700, about 1 percent. He acknowledged those collections could improve.

The pledge is also not new. In 2024, his predecessor Amin Modad rolled out a rebranded Inspectorate Division to keep vendors from selling rice above the government ceiling. The committee should ask how many inspectors the ministry has, how many cases it opened this year, and what money comes with “resourcing” them.

Small business: right diagnosis, no deadlines

On Liberian enterprise, Yekeson’s diagnosis matches what traders report. He has said that women make up 75 percent of traders reporting financial constraints.

His answers are sensible but undated:

* Procurement set-aside. The law already reserves a quarter of qualifying public procurement for Liberian-owned small businesses. He promises to publish compliance “agency by agency,” but gives no date.

* Credit. A credit guarantee programme will come “only with the requisite approvals and clear fiscal safeguards,” a signal that no money is yet set aside.

* Late payment. He will “engage” concessionaires and “report progress,” with no target for how quickly government and companies must pay.

* Business registration. Service centres exist in seven counties, with nationwide expansion planned for 2027. His “every county” pledge carries no date.

* Liberians-only sectors. He will enforce the reservation of rice and cement retail, fuel stations and sand supply through ownership checks. He did not say how many such businesses are now foreign-owned.

The 2029 goal to “produce more of what Liberia consumes” has no baseline or target. He has also warned that a stronger currency can cut what farmers and processors earn, a tension his import-substitution plan does not address.

Questions of record

Yekeson told senators he will disclose all relevant interests, comply with the Code of Conduct and recuse himself where conflicts arise. He did not say whether he still holds shares or roles in South Atlantic Capital Group or Panchariya Group West Africa, where he previously served as CFO and president, respectively.

His appointment has also revived older questions. Smart News Liberia reported that his name appeared in a 2013 Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission asset verification that raised questions about deposits totaling more than US$300,000. His statement did not address it.

What the Senate should hold him to

Yekeson’s statement is the work of someone who knows the market’s pressure points. The question for senators is whether they will confirm the diagnosis or demand the mechanisms.

Five commitments would turn the speech into a record that can be checked:

1. Weekly county-level prices for rice, fuel and cement, published by the 100-day mark.

2. A date for the rule requiring traders to post the Central Bank’s daily exchange rate.

3. Publication of the full fuel pricing formula alongside pump prices.

4. An agency-by-agency report on the 25 percent procurement set-aside, with a deadline.

5. Full disclosure of his remaining business interests before confirmation.

He has offered quarterly reports to the committee. If confirmed, the first should show progress on each.

World.title: Liberia: Economist Samuel Jackson Appeals to Court for Permission to Travel Abroad Amid Health Concerns
World.content:
Jackson (center), who is seeking court permission to travel abroad for medical treatment, remains barred from leaving Liberia. He was seen being assisted by two men at the courthouse.

MONROVIA — Liberian economist and political commentator Samuel Jackson has appealed to Criminal Court “A” Judge Onesimus Barwon for permission to travel abroad for specialized medical treatment, citing concerns about his deteriorating health as he faces charges in connection with the death of his wife.

By Victoria Wesseh

Jackson was seen struggling to walk on the grounds of the Temple of Justice in Monrovia on Thursday, October 22, prompting renewed attention to his reported health condition.



The economist is seeking medical leave to obtain treatment outside Liberia but remains barred from leaving the country as his legal proceedings continue.

Jackson is facing charges in connection with the March 2026 death of his wife, Ntombi Khumalo Jackson, a South African attorney who was found dead in their Monrovia home.

Jackson told authorities that he discovered his wife semi-conscious in their bedroom after returning home from a television talk show engagement.

Khumalo Jackson, who was born in Gauteng, South Africa, was the founder of NK Attorneys. Her death attracted widespread public attention, particularly after images allegedly showing bruises and other injuries on her body circulated on social media.

Reports indicated that she suffered severe head injuries and required emergency brain surgery.

The circumstances surrounding her death have since become the subject of legal proceedings involving her husband.

Jackson’s request for permission to travel abroad for medical treatment now presents the court with a matter requiring consideration alongside the conditions imposed on him as the case proceeds.

The court’s decision on his request was not immediately available.

World.title: Liberia: War Victims, Survivors Protest at Court Office, Capitol as House Chairman Pledges to Put Court Bill Before Plenary Tuesday
World.content:
Some of the protesters at the war crimes court office. Credit: Anthony Stephens/New Narratives.

Hundreds of war victims, survivors and justice advocates protested at the war crimes court office and the Capitol Building, demanding approval of legislation to establish the long-awaited court.

A disagreement erupted at the Capitol after a lawmaker said a legislative committee had decided to exclude economic crimes from the proposed court. Protesters objected, prompting another lawmaker to assure them that both categories of crimes would be covered.

The House Committee Chairman pledged to bring the matter before plenary Tuesday, as the government’s timetable for establishing the courts faces uncertainty.

By Anthony Stephens, senior justice correspondent with New Narratives

Hundreds of victims and survivors of Liberia’s civil wars, joined by justice advocates, protested Thursday outside the government office overseeing the establishment of a war crimes court, temporarily disrupting operations, before moving to the Capitol Building, where a senior lawmaker pledged to place the long-delayed legislation before the House plenary on Tuesday.

The peaceful demonstrations drew people with disabilities, rural women, elderly victims and survivors, young people, and traditional and religious leaders. For hours, protesters gathered outside the Office for the Establishment of the War and Economic Crimes Court, holding placards demanding justice. One read: “REAL PEACE IS NOT THE SILENCE OF GUNS. REAL PEACE IS DISPENSING JUSTICE AND ENDING IMPUNITY. WE CALL ON THE EXECUTIVE AND LEGISLATURE TO GIVE THE PEOPLE JUSTICE & ACCOUNTABILITY NOW…”



“What’s going on wrong? We are suffering,” said Korpo Dennis, president of the Women in Peacebuilding Network, her voice cracking as she broke down in tears, burying her face in her lappa, a traditional cloth wrapped around her waist. Addressing Jallah Barbu, the office’s executive director, Dennis questioned why President Joseph Boakai had not raised the issue at the United Nations General Assembly, as she said he had promised. “He na come, we can hear nothing. We want answer today or else, we will sleep on this street.”

The protests underscored mounting frustration over Liberia’s failure to establish a court to prosecute atrocities committed during its civil wars, more than two decades after the fighting ended. Despite repeated government commitments and consultations, competing bills remain before lawmakers, leaving uncertain when those accused of wartime crimes will face prosecution.

Dennis’s organization was among the women’s peace groups widely credited with helping pressure Liberia’s warring factions to end the conflicts.

Barbu told protesters he remained confident that Boakai had not abandoned his commitment to establishing the court. Prevented from entering his office, along with other staff, he unsuccessfully attempted to reach House Speaker Richard Koon by telephone.

He then contacted James Verdier, the speaker’s chief of staff, who assured protesters that the legislation would be approved. Unsatisfied, the protesters moved to Capitol Hill to press lawmakers directly.

Kula Fofana, Boakai’s press secretary, did not respond to a request for comment on the protesters’ concerns.

“It has taken us too long,” said Jeremiah D. Cooper, a member of the Group of 77, an organization representing people with disabilities. “The same Liberian people who voted for you are the same Liberian people demanding that you pass certain documents in the interest of the country,” he added. “You people say you will not do it. Why?”

Jeremiah D. Cooper, one of the protesters.

But the gathering soon exposed a disagreement over whether the proposed court would prosecute both war crimes and economic crimes.

Prescilla A. Cooper, a Montserrado County representative and member of the House Committee on Claims and Petitions, told protesters that a joint legislative committee tasked with harmonizing the competing bills had agreed to proceed with legislation establishing a war crimes court, leaving economic crimes to be handled separately by the Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission.

The protesters rejected her account, insisting that economic crimes allegedly committed during Liberia’s civil wars must also fall within the proposed court’s jurisdiction.

Justice advocates have long argued that including economic crimes would allow the court to order convicted warlords and other perpetrators, including institutions found responsible, to pay restitution to victims and communities harmed by their actions.

Prince Toles, chairman of the House Committee on Claims and Petitions, sought to reassure the protesters, saying he shared their position that the legislation should establish a War and Economic Crimes Court.

“We signed it in 2024 (the joint resolution). We signed it 5G. But this one, we will give it 20G,” Toles said, referring to the Legislature’s earlier support for establishing the court. “If people did not rob the system, all of us would have lived better. I want to tell you that we are with you.”

“We will bring this matter before plenary,” Toles said. “But if they ask us to bring a paper signed by the different stakeholders, I will just propose that you draft something for us temporarily. Bring it here tomorrow (Friday), then I will put it on the floor on Tuesday.”

Plenary, the full membership of either legislative chamber, is its highest decision-making body. Toles’s pledge does not guarantee a vote or passage Tuesday.

House leaders subsequently invited protest organizers to a meeting.

“We feel a little bit relieved that it will work,” Peterson Sonyah, executive director of the Liberia Massacre Survivors Association, said by phone afterward. “We are impressed with the discussion. We are planning to be there on Tuesday.”

The protests came as Liberia approaches a deadline in its plans to establish the courts.

Under a 36-page roadmap submitted to Boakai in July 2025 , the court office projected that the National Anti-Corruption Court would be operational by November 2026, followed by the War and Economic Crimes Court in November 2027.

With neither court’s establishing legislation approved, the timetable faces uncertainty. The roadmap also envisaged completing trials by 2031, after which the war crimes court would transition to a residual mechanism.

Liberia is also preparing to assume the rotating presidency of the United Nations Security Council in December, a moment justice advocates say will draw international attention to the country’s unfinished accountability efforts.

A FrontPage Africa/New Narratives survey of 1,150 people across 11 counties found that 91 percent supported establishing the court, while 89 percent said they would not vote for lawmakers opposing it.

The survey was not scientifically sampled. Only 4 percent of respondents reported awareness of lawmakers’ consultations on the proposed court.

The legislative process has been complicated by six competing proposals.

They include a War Crimes Court bill from the Liberian National Bar Association ; a separate proposal from civil society organizations working with the Independent National Commission on Human Rights ; and two bills introduced by Senate President Pro Tempore Nyonblee Karnga-Lawrence and Senator Joseph Jallah , one proposing a War Crimes Court and another a Special Economic and Corruption Crimes Court.

The remaining two bills were prepared by the court office , proposing a War and Economic Crimes Court and a separate National Anti-Corruption Court. Boakai subsequently forwarded both proposals to the Legislature .

The senators’ proposals drew criticism from justice advocates , who warned that provisions concerning jurisdiction and appeals could weaken wartime accountability.

In June, more than 40 House members attended a two-day technical deliberation in Buchanan, Grand Bassa County , organized by the court office and its partners to examine the legislation.

Separately, the Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights, Claims and Petitions began consultations on the competing bills , seeking to resolve differences over senior appointments, prosecutorial independence and appeals.

The committee also outlined plans to harmonize the proposals , with further consultations and hearings expected before the legislative session ended.

Neither chamber approved the legislation before lawmakers departed for their constituency break.

The Legislature was scheduled to return October 9, but a dispute over lawmakers’ benefits delayed the House’s reopening. Regular business resumed October 13.

For Sonyah and the other organizers, Tuesday will test the assurances they received. They intend to return to the Capitol to see whether the matter reaches plenary — and whether the proposed legislation retains both war crimes and economic crimes.

This story was a collaboration with New Narratives as part of the Investigating Liberia project. Funding was provided by the U.N. Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights and the European Union. The funders had no say in the story’s content.

World.title: President Hicilema honours fisherman, Chalala Hero, other medal recipients
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has awarded Medal of Gallantry to Namwala fisherman who wrestled a crocodile to save a fellow fisherman and a civilian who risked his life to guide security agencies to rescue 13 young women abducted in Chalala.

President Hakainde Hichilema conferred the honours during the Investiture Ceremony held at State House where Newton Nalumino was honoured for exceptional courage and bravery on the night of April 2023 at around 04:00 hours while fishing in the Namwala River.

He said Mr Nalumino witnessed a crocodile attack in which a crocodile captured another fisherman, Without hesitation and at great personal risk, he confronted the reptile and repeatedly struck it with his paddling stick, forcing it to release the victim who he then pulled to safety.

“The injured fisherman was rushed to Namwala District Hospital and later referred to Livingstone Teaching Hospital, he survived but sustained permanent disability, he said

The second recipient of the Gallantry Medal was Robby Chitambo, who was recognised for compassion and selflessness during the 2022 abduction case that shook Lusaka, where young women were held captive in Chalala, causing widespread fear and anxiety.

Mr Chitambo, who was a civilian then, displayed remarkable bravery by assisting authorities and guiding them to the location where 13 young women were being held captive.

His courageous actions contributed to the successful rescue of the victims and subsequent apprehension of the perpetrators.

Mr Chitambo has since been employed in Government by Zambia Airforce.

President Hichilema also conferred others for their distinguished service among them is Chandra Desai and Lata Desai who received honours for significant contributions to education, healthcare, job creation and community development in Luanshya district where they settled in 1960.

“As a business couple, they established several enterprises including Desai Discount Centre, Quality Furniture, GMMI Limited and Gaurav Zambia Limited, creating over 500 employment opportunities,” he added.

Mr Hichilema added that their philanthropy has supported school infrastructure, computer laboratories, water and sanitation facilities and feeding programmes benefiting over 500 learners, as well as healthcare infrastructure at Thompson District Hospital and the Zambia Combined Staff Clinic, including assistive devices for children with special needs and tuition for over 600 vulnerable students.

A personal secretary by profession and early childhood education consultant born on 13th June 1953 in Mongu District, was awarded the President’s Insignia of Merit for outstanding contributions to education, youth empowerment and community development.

She personally financed the construction of a 1×3 classroom block and a fully equipped computer laboratory in Mongu District and through her Foundation has empowered women with sewing machines, provided housing support and assisted the elderly. Her initiatives have benefited over 2,000 people.

Meanwhile, Patrick Chinyemba, popularly known as Bado, the highly distinguished Zambian flyweight boxer born on 3rd January 2001 in Lusaka, was honoured for his consistent performance at national and international level, including representing Zambia at the Olympic Games, including Paris 2024, and winning several senior national titles.

Further, Carol Kanyemba, Head Coach of Zambia’s Under-17 Women’s National Football Team, the Copper Princesses, born on 23rd January 1988 in Kabwe, was honoured for exceptional commitment to youth development and advancement of women’s football, leading the team to major regional and international competitions including FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup qualifiers.

Moreover, Ashious Melu, the Zambian footballer, national team captain and coach, popularly known as Super Ash, was honoured posthumously.

Born on 16th June 1957 in Zambezi District, Melu began his career with Konkola Blades before joining Mufulira Wanderers in the late 1970s, became Zambian Footballer of the Year in 1983 after scoring 43 goals.

He again in 1987, captained Zambia from 1988 to 1992 leading the team to the 1988 Seoul Olympics quarterfinals with memorable wins over Italy and Guatemala, and later coached Wanderers to consecutive league titles in 1995 and 1996.

President Hichilema also conferred other national honours for distinguished service which include Trade Kings limited, Patel Iqbal, Wonderful group Limited Chief Executive Officer, Yaochi Huang and ambassador Cox Sikumba who was awarded posthumously.

The President said the honorees’ generosity, courage and exceptional service have advanced socio-economic development and elevated the Zambian flag, making them worthy of national recognition.

World.title: Government prioritises social sectors for economic independence-Bwalya
World.content:
Muchinga Province Permanent Secretary Tuesday Bwalya says Government is working hard to improve social sectors to achieve economic independence and ensure that citizens live dignified lives.

‎Dr Bwalya, who made the remarks during the commemoration of the 62nd anniversary of independence, said the government wants to transform the economy in a sustainable manner in line with the growing Zambia agenda.

The Province Permanent Secretary said the government is fully committed to boosting the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) with a sharp focus on sustainable job creation and rural industrialization.

‎Dr Bwalya emphasized that the ultimate goal of the province and the country’s economic expansion is to uplift ordinary citizens by revitalizing key social sectors.

‎”We want to improve social sectors so that we can improve the lives of the people.” he said

Dr Bwalya stressed that economic growth will not come at the expense of the environment.

‎He assured residents that the government is strictly pursuing green policies to ensure natural ecosystems are preserved for future generations.

‎”Government wants to ensure the environment is not damaged and will grow the economy in a sustainable manner,” he noted.

‎Dr Bwalya, who outlined the specific trajectory for Muchinga Province, said the region will no longer rely solely on exporting raw materials.

‎He indicated that the government will instead be pivoting toward value addition and the creation of local manufacturing enterprises to aggressively drive national development.

‎Dr Bwalya further underscored that true economic independence is impossible without local ownership.

‎He linked economic success directly to quality education, noting that an empowered workforce is the engine of development.

‎”Economic independence requires the involvement of the people. Hence, quality education is important so we can give skills to our people so we can develop,” he explained.

‎Dr Bwalya has since reiterated the government’s unwavering commitment to inclusive development, promising that no district or chiefdom in Muchinga Province or the wider nation will be left behind.

‎”We will ensure that development reaches all corners of the country,” he said.

‎‎Meanwhile, Dr Bwalya, who was responding to the concerns from freedom fighters, said the government has put up interventions to support them.

‎Dr Bwalya stated that all freedom fighters have been put on social cash transfer, and encouraged those who are not there to visit the relevant department for them to receive the support.

‎He also said that the freedom fighters have been encouraged to form cooperatives so that they can be supported with farming inputs such as fertilizer.

Meanwhile, Chinsali District Commissioner Brenda Silwembe said Chinsali is witnessing massive development facilitated through governmental development agenda and the increased Constituency Development Fund (CDF).

‎Ms Silwembe cited infrastructure development such as the construction of health facilities and schools and the delivery of youth and women empowerment, among others.

‎She added that as the Independence journey continues, President Hakainde Hichilema remains committed to fostering development in the district and the country at large.

‎”As we celebrated this year’s independence, I implore everyone to renew our commitment to hard work for us to honor the dreams of our founding fathers who fought for the nation to gain independence,” she said.

‎Ms Silwembe stated that with chinsali being a sacred place in the story of Zambia’s struggle for independence, there is a deliberate need to embrace unity, resilience, and the spirit of togetherness.

‎”As we gather to honor the liberation of Mother Zambia, the theme Zambia @62 Our Journey, Our Growth, Our Future challenges us to reflect deeply on where we are coming from and where we are heading to,” she said

‎Chinsali District Freedom Fighters Association Gremson Katongo said Zambia is enjoying freedom and unity today because of the founding fathers of mother Zambia who fought for the country’s liberty.

‎Mr Katongo said currently there are a few surviving freedom fighters who need to be taken care of.

‎Mr Katongo therefore, has called on the Government to look into the plight of freedom fighters and care for them.

World.title: Serenje DC calls for unity to boost Agriculture
World.content:
Serenje District Commissioner (DC), Ellen Mibenge has called on agricultural stakeholders to work together to unlock the district’s agricultural potential and contribute to the Grow Zambia Agenda.

Ms Mibenge says farmers, cooperatives, agricultural institutions, agro-dealers and private investors should strengthen collaboration to boost agricultural production and support the Government’s Grow Zambia Agenda.

Speaking during the commemoration of Zambia’s 62nd Independence Anniversary in Serenje, Ms Mibenge said the Government cannot not achieve its sector targets without the active participation of all stakeholders.

“The Government cannot realise this transformation alone. We need to contribute to the national agricultural targets under the Grow Zambia Agenda, which the Government, under the leadership of President Hakainde Hichilema, is implementing over the next five years,” Ms Mibenge said.

She said as the Government pursued national production targets for maize, soya beans, wheat and sugar, agricultural stakeholders in Serenje should ensure that agriculture remained a key driver of economic transformation and contribute meaningfully to national production.

Ms Mibenge added that all stakeholders have a responsibility to facilitate collaboration and ensure that national development priorities translate into tangible benefits for the people of Serenje.

On decentralisation, the DC emphasised the need to strengthen coordination between central and local government to ensure that district development priorities aligned with provincial and national objectives.

She also called on residents to uphold peace, unity and national values, saying these were essential to achieving the Grow Zambia Agenda.

Ms Mibenge further urged Serenje Town Council to manage public resources transparently and efficiently to ensure that development projects responded to the needs of local communities.

World.title: Southern Province PS calls for unity
World.content:
Southern Province Acting Permanent Secretary, Gift Monde has called for strengthened Collaboration among citizens in order to protect Zambia’s National Heritage and ensure that the Country upholds its identity.

Speaking during the Independence Day commemoration at Independence Stadium in Choma District too, Mr Monde said Zambia at 62 is a reflection of the Country’s progress made over the years.

“Over the years Zambia has made progress in education, infrastructure, healthcare, entrepreneurship and democratic participation ” he said.

He noted that the Grow Zambia Agenda is challenging the country to increase productivity, support local enterprises, create jobs and ensure economic progress for ordinary citizens.

” Let us move beyond celebrating independence and commit ourselves to practical actions,” he said.

And Choma District Mayor, Honest Mweemba, noted that as Zambia is celebrating 62 years of independence, Choma District is equally celebrating the development that has been achieved over the years.

He states that this development signifies a great milestone since Zambia gained its independence in 1964.

And Choma Central Member of Parliament, Cornelius Mweetwa added that the Grow Zambia Agenda is a strategic intervention aimed at developing the Country.

Meanwhile, Zambia United National Freedom Fighters Association Vice Chairperson for Southern Province, Earthwell Nkombalume has commended the government for the achievements that have been made since it was put into office.

” We pay a very special tribute to the new dawn administration for legal recognition of the freedom fighters, the first since we attained independence ” he said.

Mr Nkombalume has also appealed to the government to come up with a special provision for freedom fighters to ease access to boreholes for irrigation purpose as well as inputs and seeds.

World.title: Muza stun champions Power to go top
World.content:
F

C MUZA have beaten defending champions Power Dynamos 1-0 at Nakambala Stadium in Mazabuka to go top of Stream A in the MTN Super League Transitional Season.

Solomon Mpasela scored the solitary strike after 50 minutes as MUZA held on to stun Power.

MUZA top Stream A with 10 points from four games, at least for 24 hours before their closest rivals Nkana face Konkola Blades away at Konkola Stadium in Chililabombwe.

Power are fifth on the table with six points in four matches. This was their second defeat in the transitional season having lost to Konkola on the opening weekend.

Power coach Oswald Mutapa was left gutted by the defeat.

“Not a good result, not the result we wanted. We conceded through a deflection. We had a few chances we could have used to equalise and maybe win the match but it wasn’t to be. We move to the next game. We need to do more in terms of how to go and get the result,” Mutapa said.

In Stream B, Zesco United ended their winless run with a 5-0 win over Mutondo Stars at the Trade Fair Grounds in Ndola on Independence Day.

Coming into the match on the back of one defeat and two draws, Zesco gave their fans something to savour.

The net rippled inside the first minute when Anthony Shipanuka fired home from close range.

Shipanuka remained a constant threat and came close to doubling his tally 12 minutes later.

Zesco were rewarded in the 37th minute when Abraham Siankombo was brought down inside the penalty area. Kennedy Musonda stepped up and calmly converted from the spot to make it 2-0, before striking again a minute later to complete his brace.

On the hour mark, Happy Nsiku rose highest to head home from a corner to make it 4-0, before Elvis Addae completed the rout in the 88th minute after an error by Mutondo Stars goalkeeper Scotch Mwanza.

Assistant coach Tenant Chembo praised the performance.

“It is a good feeling, we are so happy we got the result and the goals that we wanted,” Chembo said.

In other results, Zanaco FC were 3-0 winners over Kansanshi Dynamos at Sunset, Kiala Wa Kiala scoring in the 34th minute before Araina Lambert bagged a brace on 40 and 58 minutes.

Nchanga Rangers edged Napsa Stars 1-0 away, with Mwiza Simwala scoring early in the 3rd minute to post their first win of the season.

Trident FC thrashed Makeni All Stars 6-1, while Nkwazi and Green Eagles drew 0-0.

World.title: Ashios Melu honoured posthumously
World.content:
29 years after his death, Zambia and Mighty Mufulira Wanderers legend Ashios Jordan Melu has been honoured posthumously for his outstanding contribution to sport and raising Zambia’s profile internationally.

Melu was honoured by President Hakainde Hichilema at the Investiture Ceremony on the occasion of the 62nd Independence Anniversary at State House.

He was recognised alongside boxer Patrick Chinyemba and Copper Princesses head coach Carol Kanyemba.

Melu captained Zambia from 1988 to 1992. In 1992 he turned to coaching as assistant coach at Wanderers before taking over as head coach.

In 1994, he was named Zambia national team assistant coach to Roald Poulsen. He then led Wanderers to back-to-back league championships in 1995 and 1996, giving the club its first league success since 1978.

Melu died in 1997.

Chinyemba was recognised for his achievements in amateur boxing and representation at major international competitions, including the Paris Olympic Games. Born on January 3, 2001, in Lusaka, he has won several senior national titles and competed in IBA and World Championship events.

Kanyemba, who leads the Under-17 women’s national team, the Copper Princesses, was honoured for her contribution to youth development and women’s football. Born on January 23, 1988, in Kateete, she has guided the team through regional and international competitions including FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup qualifiers.

Meanwhile, National Olympic Committee of Zambia President Alfred Foloko congratulated the trio, saying their achievements show talent, resilience and commitment that help raise Zambia’s profile internationally.

“We especially appreciate the focus on youth development, women’s football, and the lasting legacy of Zambian football. We also extend our sincere appreciation to President Hichilema for recognising and celebrating these sports personalities,” Foloko said.

World.title: Diplomatic Dean calls for Africa to Lead Its development
World.content:
The Dean of the Diplomatic Corps in Zambia Hawa Hassan Mohamed has called on African countries to take greater responsibility for their development, peace and prosperity, saying the continent must lead efforts to change perceptions about Africa.

Ms Mohamed said African countries needed to take ownership of their development agendas rather than depend on external actors to determine their priorities.

Speaking in an interview during Zambia’s 62nd Independence Anniversary celebrations, she said Africa had become more aware of global developments and was increasingly seeking to reshape narratives that had historically defined the continent.

She said Zambia’s development ambitions under the Grow Zambia agenda reflected the importance of countries taking charge of their own progress.

She described the agenda as one that Zambians should own and champion, stressing that the responsibility for achieving development goals rested primarily with the people themselves.

“It means that Zambia is going to grow. Zambia is going to do its own thing. The theme is going to be developing by themselves. It is something that we own, we are championing and we are going to do it,” she said.

Ms Mohamed also urged African countries to learn from one another by adopting successful practices from countries that had made progress in key areas of governance and development.

She cited elections as one area where countries could learn from one another, encouraging African nations to observe successful electoral processes and adopt positive practices that could strengthen democratic governance across the continent.

She pointed out that sharing experiences and replicating successful approaches could help African countries advance common development goals and strengthen cooperation.

And the United Kingdom (UK) reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Zambia’s development ambitions under the Grow Zambia agenda.

British Deputy High Commissioner to Zambia Simon ten Brinks-Jackson said the UK stood ready to continue supporting the country in achieving its development objectives.

He described the Grow Zambia agenda as forward-looking and optimistic, noting that the country had significant opportunities for growth and development.

“The Grow Zambia agenda is really forward-leaning, really optimistic, and the UK stands ready to continue supporting Zambia with those objectives,” the High Commissioner said.

The diplomat also congratulated the people of Zambia on the country’s 62nd Independence Anniversary, describing the occasion as special.

Freedom fighters also called on Zambians to safeguard the peace emphasizing that it was not easy to attain it.

Mr Stanely Mhlanga urged the young people to maintain Zambia’s peace if the country is to sustain its development.

Meanwhile, a youth, Pauline Bwalya, urged young people to remain peaceful, avoid abusive behaviour and contribute positively to national development as the country commemorates its 62nd Independence Day.

Ms Bwalya said Independence Day should remind citizens of the importance of preserving the freedom secured by those who fought for the country’s liberation.

Ms Bwalya encouraged young people to uphold peace, noting that their conduct was important to Zambia’s development and the country’s image internationally.

World.title: Muchinga PS calls for peace, unity
World.content:
Muchinga Province Permanent Secretary, Tuesday Bwalya has called on Zambians to uphold unity, peace, hard work and integrity as the country commemorates its 62nd Independence Anniversary.

‎

‎Dr Bwalya said Independence Day is an important reminder of the freedom the country enjoys and the collective responsibility of citizens to contribute to national development.

‎

‎He said this during the Independence Day flag-hoisting ceremony at Chinsali Municipal Council.

‎

‎Dr Bwalya said Zambia attained independence on October 24, 1964, following the courage and sacrifices of freedom fighters and founding leaders who fought for the country’s liberation.

‎

‎He said the nation should continue to honour those who contributed to the country’s independence by working towards a peaceful, united and prosperous Zambia.

‎

‎He also explained to the audience the meaning of all the colours on the Zambian flag.

‎

‎“Our flag tells our story. The green color reminds us of our land and natural resources, the red recalls the struggle for freedom, the black represents the people of Zambia, while the orange stands for our mineral wealth,” he said.

‎

‎Dr Bwalya added that the eagle on the national flag symbolises freedom and the country’s ability to rise above challenges.

‎

‎He said the national flag should serve as a reminder of the country’s motto, “One Zambia, One Nation,” which calls on citizens to promote unity and peaceful coexistence.

‎

‎“As we hoist the flag today, let us renew our commitment to unity, peace, hard work and integrity. Let us respect our laws, protect public property, care for our communities and give young people hope and opportunity,” Dr Bwalya said.

‎

‎He said independence should not only be regarded as a day of celebration but also as a responsibility for every citizen to contribute to building the nation.

‎

‎Dr Bwalya urged Zambians to serve the country with honour and ensure that their contributions laid a strong foundation for future generations.

‎

‎He said the 62nd Independence Anniversary provided an opportunity for citizens to reflect on the country’s journey, achievements and aspirations for the future.

‎

‎The flag-hoisting ceremony forms part of activities to commemorate Zambia’s 62 years of independence.

‎

‎This year’s independence is held under the theme, “Zambia @62: Our Journey, Our Growth, Our Future.”

World.title: Hwange champions, make PSL return
World.content:
HWANGE are the 2026 Pacific Breeze Southern Region Soccer League champions after edging Bulawayo Warriors 1-0 at White City Stadium yesterday, with Shawn Chabika scoring the decisive goal to seal the coal miners’ return to the Premier Soccer League.

The victory on Matchday 33 confirmed Hwange’s promotion to the top-flight league, completing a successful campaign for a club with a proud history in Zimbabwean football.

Chabika’s goal proved the difference in a tense encounter against Bulawayo Warriors, as Hwange secured the result they needed to finish the season as champions and end their stay in the Southern Region Division One league.

This story is for NewsDay subscribers.

World.title: Mapeza on the brink as Scottland’s CL dream ends in Luanda nightmare
World.content:
Football is a game of fine margins, but for Scottland, the final act in Luanda this afternoon was nothing short of a Greek tragedy.

Norman Mapeza’s future as head coach is now hanging by a thread after his side surrendered a comfortable first-leg advantage, suffering a harrowing 3-nil defeat away to Petro Atlético du Luanda to crash out of the CAF Champions League 3-2 on aggregate.

For a brief moment last week, the dream felt secure.

World.title: Congo-Kinshasa: As Ebola Spreads to 8th DR Congo Province, Families Battle to Feed Themselves
World.content:
A health worker carries a stretcher into an Ebola treatment centre in the DR Congo.

Geneva — Hunger in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo) is undermining efforts to combat Ebola as the deadly disease has expanded across borders and also to an eighth province of the huge central African country, the UN said on Friday.

Families facing Ebola in the DR Congo, which has a population of more than 105 million, can find that protecting themselves from the virus can also mean losing the means to feed their children, according to the UN’s World Food Programme (WFP).

“Today, the outbreak has spread to an eighth province, reaching communities already under immense pressure,” David Stevenson, the WFP's DRC country director, said during a UN press conference.

“As it spreads, hunger continues to undermine the measures needed to contain it.”

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

And earlier in the week, the World Health Organisation (WHO), on Oct. 20, said that Nigeria has confirmed one imported case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

It became the fifth country to detect the virus since the DRC declared an outbreak on May 15.

The spread of the disease comes as agencies fighting the escalating Ebola virus in the DRC constantly battle to win the trust of local communities, according to international groups in the field calling for the protection of health workers.

Stevenson said that the WFP has two critical roles: helping families seek care without sacrificing food and providing the logistics backbone that keeps the wider response moving.

“Without sustained support, we risk leaving families unable to follow health guidance when it matters most.”

The WFP official explained that in Ituri’s Mungbwalu, the epicentre of the outbreak, Francine Birungi Amoti has lost a child to Ebola.

“She is raising her six surviving children and another baby entrusted to her care. Violence has cut her off from her fields.

“She told me, ‘If you go, you may not even return alive, and I do not have money to buy food at the local market. So we stay at home, and WFP helps us enormously.’”

For Francine, food assistance means feeding the children in her care when reaching her fields could cost her life.

'INSECURITY AND HUNGER'

“This is what a crisis on top of a crisis looks like: disease and bereavement, compounded by insecurity and hunger,” said Stevenson.

He also cited the case in North-Kivu’s Butembo, where Isabelle Kyakimwa arrived at an Ebola treatment centre without strength.

“As she recovered, she told us: ‘Food is important for us as patients because it helps us regain the strength to keep going.’

Close 

Her words show what food assistance brings to a treatment centre: regular, safe, nutritious meals that support recovery, dignity, and continuity of care.

“Food does not treat Ebola. Medical teams do,” said Stevenson.

“But their work takes place amid severe food insecurity and continued violence that repeatedly displaces families, destroys livelihoods and complicates access to care.”

He said food assistance is vital to supporting patients through that care and that WFP needs $115 million over the next six months, including $79 million for hot meals and dry rations.

World.title: Kenya: Calls for Penalties Follow 12-Story Building Collapse
World.content:
A building under construction collapsed in the Eastleigh neighborhood of Nairobi.

Nairobi — Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has called for tougher penalties against rogue developers and the restoration of prosecutorial powers to county governments following the collapse of an incomplete 12-storey building in Eastleigh.

Sakaja said weak penalties for violating construction regulations undermine enforcement efforts and allow developers to compromise building safety, putting lives at risk.

Speaking as he led multi-agency rescue operations at the site along 1st Avenue, 9th Street, the Governor urged professional bodies representing architects, engineers and quantity surveyors to take action against developers who dismiss qualified experts after obtaining construction approvals.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said some developers engage licensed professionals to secure approvals but subsequently remove them from projects and proceed with construction using unqualified personnel, undermining safeguards intended to ensure buildings meet approved designs and safety standards.

"We have formally written to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, and we hope our request will be considered. Counties must be empowered to take firm action against rogue developers who disregard building regulations and put lives at risk," Sakaja said.

The Governor questioned the deterrent effect of existing penalties, noting that some developers found guilty of violating construction regulations could face fines as low as Sh5,000.

"Even when such offenders are arrested and taken to court, the penalties can be as low as Sh5,000, which is not a sufficient deterrent," he said.

Sakaja argued that restoring prosecutorial powers to county governments would strengthen enforcement and enable authorities to take firmer action against developers who disregard approved construction plans and safety requirements.

He called on professional associations representing architects, engineers, quantity surveyors and builders to collaborate with county governments in identifying and investigating cases where qualified professionals are withdrawn from construction sites under questionable circumstances.

The Governor said the bodies should take appropriate disciplinary action against professionals found culpable, adding that experts responsible for building design, supervision and safety must be allowed to discharge their duties without interference.

Sakaja also reiterated the need for developers to obtain occupation certificates before putting buildings into use. He said structures must undergo the necessary inspections to establish that they are safe and fit for occupation.

According to the Governor, developers are required to secure county approvals, engage qualified professionals and sign indemnity forms committing them to comply with approved plans and construction standards.

However, he said some developers disregard these commitments after obtaining approvals, compromising the integrity of construction projects.

The calls for stronger enforcement came after an incomplete 12-storey building collapsed in Eastleigh, triggering a multi-agency search and rescue operation amid fears that people were trapped beneath the rubble.

The building was still under construction, with the ground floor occupied at the time of the collapse.

Nairobi City County emergency response teams were coordinating operations alongside the National Disaster Operations Centre, the Kenya Red Cross, the Kenya Defence Forces and other agencies.

Heavy machinery had been deployed to clear debris and create access to sections where victims could be trapped, as additional resources were mobilised to support the rescue effort.

Sakaja urged families and members of the public with information about missing persons to report to designated centres established by rescue teams at the scene.

Close 

Residents were also advised to share information through the county's emergency hotlines, 1508 and 1199.

"Our health teams are on standby to provide immediate medical attention and support rescue efforts as soon as victims are reached. We are doing everything possible to ensure the operation proceeds as quickly and safely as possible," he said.

The collapse has renewed scrutiny of building safety enforcement in Nairobi, particularly compliance with approved construction plans, the engagement of qualified professionals and inspections at different stages of development.

Sakaja said stronger legal powers, tougher penalties and closer collaboration between county governments and professional bodies were necessary to hold developers accountable and prevent similar incidents.

He maintained that restoring county prosecutorial powers would complement existing inspection and enforcement mechanisms by strengthening the ability of local authorities to pursue violations of construction regulations.

World.title: Foster children's autism therapy at risk as Georgia lawmakers step into funding fight

A fight over cuts to autism therapy for Georgia foster children is escalating at the state Capitol, with a Republican lawmaker and families now calling for the 30% reimbursement reduction to be reversed as advocates warn children could lose hard-earned progress.

State Sen. Brian Strickland, R-McDonough, joined parents and providers Thursday to demand action over a reduction in reimbursement rates for applied behavior analysis (ABA) therapy that went into effect Sept. 1 through Amerigroup, which administers Medicaid coverage for children in Georgia's foster care system.

"As a parent of a child with autism, I know what ABA therapy means for a family and Georgia's foster children, which is why I stood at the Capitol to make clear that these cuts are indefensible," Strickland told Fox News Digital.

Strickland, who is running for state attorney general, also pledged to hold companies accountable if elected.

AUTISM PROVIDERS WARN FOSTER KIDS AT RISK FROM UNINTENDED CONSEQUENCES OF TRUMP'S MEDICAID FRAUD CRACKDOWN

The political pushback comes after Fox News Digital first reported earlier this month that autism advocates feared the reduction could force providers to stop treating foster children as an unintended consequence of the Trump administration's Medicaid fraud crackdown.

Taylor Sanders of the Autism Families Alliance told Fox News Digital on Saturday that families and clinicians have increasingly begun speaking out since the cuts took effect, emphasizing that "time is crucial to these families."

"Every moment where their child is not receiving services, we're seeing a regression in possible communication, safety skills," Sanders said. "Maybe we're seeing an increase in some of those challenging behaviors."

Sanders previously warned that as many as 75% of clinics could close or stop serving foster children because of the cuts.

AUTISM PROVIDERS CHEER TRUMP CRACKDOWN AFTER MILLIONS ALLEGEDLY STOLEN FROM CHILDREN THROUGH MEDICAID FRAUD

She described a family whose 3-year-old child had begun using words for the first time after receiving ABA therapy and whose mother now fears losing access to treatment.

"She was in absolute tears and so worried and frustrated," Sanders said, recalling their recent conversation.

The mother, Sanders explained, fears losing the consistent one-on-one therapy that she said helped the child begin communicating.

Sanders said the child had not received enough therapy to ensure those newly learned communication skills could be maintained across different settings.

"For these children and their families, time matters," Kelsey Bennett of the Autism Families Alliance told Fox News Digital. "Every day without critical care risks reversing hard-earned progress and limiting opportunities for continued development."

HOUSE GOP BILL MOVES TO CLOSE WHISTLEBLOWER GAPS EXPOSED BY MINNESOTA MEDICAID FRAUD SCANDAL

Bennett added, "Reverse the cuts."

Advocates are calling not only for the cuts to be reconsidered, but also for families, clinicians and other stakeholders to be involved in reviewing the policy rather than relying on a blanket approach.

In a statement to FOX 5 Atlanta, Amerigroup said it rebalanced ABA reimbursement rates based on service complexity and clinical expertise, increasing rates for treatment planning and caregiver-engagement services while decreasing rates for some technician-delivered services. The company also said rates for licensed clinicians did not decrease and that medically necessary autism services remain covered.

In response, Sanders emphasized that the reductions affected technicians who provide much of the one-on-one care.

COALITION OF 25 STATES SUES TRUMP ADMIN OVER MEDICAID WORK RULE DESIGNED TO PREVENT FRAUD

"Just because we put something down on paper doesn't mean that it's gonna be clinically effective or that these children are gonna be able to access care because companies are now having to maybe close their doors to these individuals because they can't afford the rate cut," Sanders said.

Sanders reiterated her concerns about the potential long-term consequences for children whose therapy is interrupted.

World.title: Inside the Pentagon's doomsday plan to keep America fighting if global war erupts
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

FIRST ON FOX — The Pentagon is preparing U.S. military bases to keep operating for at least 90 days without outside support as it prepares for the possibility of a major war that could cripple power grids, disrupt supply chains and threaten critical infrastructure on American soil.

The new requirement is part of FORTRESS, a broader military initiative aimed at ensuring American forces can continue fighting even if the civilian systems they depend on are disrupted, according to documents reviewed by Fox News Digital.

AMERICA'S NEXT WAR COULD REACH US SOIL, TOP ARMY GENERAL WARNS

"We don't want to rely on standard civilian municipal infrastructure to run our national defense. We just simply can't. It's an intolerable risk," Pentagon chief spokesperson Sean Parnell told Fox News Digital.

The Pentagon is also laying the groundwork for civilian factories to shift to defense production during a crisis, while preparing alternative supply chains and strategic reserves to keep weapons, fuel and other essential materials flowing.

"Power is combat now. Without electricity, you lose communications, water, logistics, assembly lines and just basic military command structures," Parnell said.

Under FORTRESS, every major military installation in the continental United States would be expected to sustain essential operations independently for at least 90 days, including access to electricity, water, fuel and communications.

TRUMP PENTAGON LAUNCHES COMPETITION FOR AMERICA'S NEXT GREAT MILITARY BASE

The requirement reflects a broader shift in how the Pentagon is preparing for threats to the American homeland, including the possibility that a major conflict could disrupt the infrastructure supporting military operations inside the United States.

"I realized that a lot of the way we think about homeland defense was built around the antiquated assumption that two oceans would protect us," Parnell said. "President Trump understands that world is gone, and he's already paved the way for new thinking: Golden Dome, a renewed focus on the Western Hemisphere, Greenland, Panama."

A central concern is the military's reliance on civilian power grids, which support everything from communications and logistics to weapons manufacturing.

FORTRESS envisions portable nuclear reactors, large-scale battery storage and microgrids capable of disconnecting military installations from the civilian electrical grid, allowing them to continue operating during prolonged power disruptions.

"Mission-critical power must be independent, hardened, and redundant," Parnell said.

The Pentagon has already announced plans to reduce major military installations' dependence on civilian power grids. The 90-day self-sufficiency standard goes further, extending the requirement beyond electricity to other essential services needed to sustain military operations.

The strategy also anticipates major disruptions to the global supply chains that provide the military with weapons, equipment and critical materials.

"The next conflict will likely be fought on multiple fronts. Look at the geopolitics behind any major war. When that happens, global supply chains will break," Parnell said.

To prepare, FORTRESS calls for strategic reserves of munitions, fuel, critical minerals, electronics, spare parts and medical supplies that could sustain military operations if international supply routes are disrupted or domestic manufacturers cannot keep pace with wartime demand.

Reserve targets would vary depending on how quickly supplies are consumed during a major conflict and how long manufacturers would need to replace them.

STARTUPS BRING INNOVATION TO DEFENSE INDUSTRIAL BASE

For the military's most critical defense dependencies, the initiative also establishes a requirement for at least two qualified supply or production pathways, reducing the risk that the loss of a single factory, supplier or industrial capability could interrupt military operations.

Another major component involves preparing America's civilian manufacturing sector to support a wartime mobilization.

Through the Civil Reserve Manufacturing Network, an existing initiative incorporated into FORTRESS, the Pentagon plans to identify commercial factories capable of shifting to defense production during a crisis.

The new details describe plans to assess manufacturers' capabilities and establish technical specifications, cybersecurity protections, contracting arrangements and conversion procedures in advance, rather than waiting until a conflict begins.

FORTRESS also calls for recurring industrial stress tests and mobilization exercises to assess whether manufacturers could maintain production through prolonged disruptions.

Beyond energy and manufacturing, the initiative includes efforts to strengthen military communications, navigation and satellite capabilities against interference, including preparations to maintain operations when GPS signals are jammed or space-based assets are disrupted.

Together, the measures are intended to reduce the military's dependence on civilian infrastructure and vulnerable supply networks during a prolonged conflict.

"You don't want to be making these decisions in the middle of a global multi-front conflict. We have to have a plan," Parnell said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

He described FORTRESS as an insurance policy for the homeland, designed to ensure American forces can continue operating even if a major war disrupts the infrastructure and supply chains they rely on.

World.title: Former Israeli army chief Gadi Eisenkot emerges as Netanyahu’s leading election challenger
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

JERUSALEM — Israel’s high-stakes election on Oct. 27 pits the longest serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, against the highly decorated retired Lt. Gen. Gadi Eisenkot. While fairly new to politics, Eisenkot has an impressive resume that could help him become the Jewish state's next leader.

According to a number of polls, Eisenkot's centrist political party, Yashar, has a narrow lead over Netanyahu's Likud. To form a government, Yashar or Likud will need to cobble together a 61-seat majority of parties to be able to form a new coalition government.

TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE

Who is the 66-year-old Eisenkot?

He was born in Tiberias in Israel’s north to a Jewish-Moroccan family who relocated to Israel’s southernmost city, Eilat, on the Red Sea when he was a toddler.

A career soldier, he opted to serve in the infantry. He was part of the elite Golani Brigade and reached the zenith of the military with his 2015 appointment to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) chief of staff in 2015 until 2019.

Yossi Melman, one of Israel’s most respected journalists on intelligence and defense reporting, told Fox News Digital that Eisenkot, "Is 100% a soldier. He is very brave and humble. He is an officer and gentleman."

Melman noted that when Eisenkot was chosen to be the next IDF chief of staff, he declined because he felt that then General Benny Gantz should receive the appointment. Melman asked, "How many people would do that? He was selected after Gantz. It shows his traits of modesty, honesty and not arrogant."

Melman said, "It is a miracle he is leading in the polls. He is the antithesis of a what a politician should be. He is not a great orator when you compare him to Netanyahu. He radiates honesty."

BENJAMIN NETANYAHU'S LEGACY AND POLITICAL FUTURE ON THE LINE IN ISRAEL'S OCT 27 ELECTION

Eisenkot’s Mizrahi background — Jews who originate from North Africa and the Middle East — would mean, if he prevails, that he would be the first Israeli Prime Minister of Moroccan origin. The Prime Minister’s office has been held by Israelis of Eastern European descent (Ashkenazi) since the rebirth of the Jewish state in 1948.

After Hamas invaded Israel on Oct. 7, 2023 and slaughtered over 1,200 people, including more than 40 Americans, Eisenkot joined Netanyahu’s war cabinet as a minister without portfolio.

Melman said Eisenkot "did not set any political conditions" and "his presence in the cabinet saved Netanyahu." After eight months of serving in the war cabinet, Eisenkot resigned, blaming the prime minister for failing to implement a comprehensive strategy.

The war against the Iran-backed terrorist movement Hamas took an enormous toll on the battle-hardened General Eisenkot and his family. Hamas killed his son, 25-year-old Master Sergeant Gal Eisenkot, in Dec. 2023. The terrorist organization also killed two nephews of Eisenkot. Netanyahu and his wife Sara said at the time that they were devastated by Gal’s death and Eisenkot was a "true hero."

ZIONISM EXPLAINED FROM ITS BIBLICAL ORIGINS TO THE REBIRTH OF THE STATE OF ISRAEL

Danny Orbach, a military historian from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, gave his take on the leading contender to replace Netanyahu. "I think his military record and his prospects as a national leader have both significant strengths and serious weaknesses. He bears considerable responsibility for shaping the IDF that existed on Oct. 7, 2023. And that was, paradoxically, both the army that proved capable of defeating Hezbollah, striking Iran and achieving unprecedented military successes in the extraordinarily difficult, tunnel-ridden battlefield of Gaza and the army that failed so miserably on Oct. 7."

He continued that, "Like other chiefs of staff, Eisenkot bears responsibility for the decisions that reduced the army's size and for the infamous ‘conceptzia’ [Hebrew word for concept] regarding Hamas. In that respect, I consider him just as culpable as Netanyahu."

Israel’s military, intelligence and political establishments bought into the ‘conceptzia’ that Hamas could be housebroken with massive infusions of economic aid. Hamas, however, was wedded to its radical Islamist ideology —the destruction of the Jewish state — and used the funds to advance its war aims.

Orbach noted that "I don't think most of Eisenkot's support stems from his energy, enthusiasm or even his political platform. My impression is that Eisenkot has emerged as the default ‘non-Bibi’ candidate, the politician who currently channels much of the camp's hopes and expectations."

Orbach added that "I also doubt that Eisenkot would have had the political determination to stand up to the Biden administration on such matters."

Netanyahu and former President Biden repeatedly clashed over Biden’s attempts to rope in Israel’s efforts to defeat Iran’s seven-front war against the Jewish state.

The military historian, however, noted that "I believe an Eisenkot government could address several of Israel's most urgent problems. It would remove Ben Gvir from power, confront the growing problem of Jewish extremist violence and terrorism in the West Bank, and begin repairing Israel's severely damaged international legitimacy."

Itamar Ben-Gvir is a controversial right-wing firebrand politician and the current minister of national security since 2022, who has outraged many Western European and foreign leaders with his heated rhetoric against the Palestinians.

TIMELINE OF DECADES-LONG ISRAELI-ARAB, PALESTINIAN CONFLICT

Eisenkot’s wife, Hannah, comes from an American Jewish family. U.S. General Joseph Dunford awarded Eisenkot the Commander of the Legion of Merit because of his "exceptionally meritorious service as chief of the General Staff of the IDF" and his "contribution to the strategic cooperation between the United States and Israel [that] will have a lasting effect on both countries," according to the Washington Institute, where Eisenkot served as a military fellow in 2019.

Nadav Eyal, an Israeli analyst and journalist for the mass circulation Israeli paper Yedioth Aharonoth, told Fox News Digital, Gadi Eisenkot is widely considered one of the most successful Chiefs of Staff that Israel has had in the last thirty years."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

He continued that "Chiefs of Staff in Israel, unlike in other countries, are really extremely capable, in general, to be prime minister. They are leading the country’s biggest organization, the IDF."

Eyal, who writes extensively about the IDF, credited Eisenkot’s military planning against the Iran-backed Hezbollah terrorist organization in Lebanon and the significant defeats the Lebanese Shiite entity experienced, including the "discovery of tunnels that Hezbollah built" to enter Israel. Hezbollah immediately joined Hamas’s war against Israel in Oct. 2023.

Given the nature of Israel’s electoral system, an outright winner won’t likely be known for several days, since the leading party will need to form a coalition to get to the 61-seat mandate to run the country.
