World.title: Nigerian Exchange Group Profit Jumps 83%
World.content:
Bridges linking Lagos Island and the mainland in Lagos, Nigeria, seen from above on 23 September 2015. Photo: Sir Demo, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

NIGERIA · LAGOS · MARKETS

The company that runs Nigeria’s stock exchange lifted its pre-tax profit 83% in nine months, but almost all of that gain came before July.

Key Facts — Profit Pre-tax profit rose 83% to ₦20.58 billion (about US$15.5 million) in nine months.

— Revenue Up 80% to ₦27.26 billion (about US$20.5 million); transaction fees were 76% of it.

— Third quarter Pre-tax profit rose just 1% to ₦5.83 billion (about US$4.4 million) against a year earlier.

— Dividends paid ₦8.23 billion (about US$6.2 million) in nine months, up 87% on last year.

— The company Holding company of the Nigerian Exchange in Lagos; shares trade as NGXGROUP.

Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX Group), the listed company that owns the stock exchange in Lagos, made a pre-tax profit of ₦20.58 billion (about US$15.5 million) in the nine months to Wednesday 30 September 2026, up 83% on a year earlier. The unaudited accounts, which the board approved on Tuesday 20 October, compare with ₦11.23 billion (about US$8.4 million) in the same period of 2025.

Transaction fees, which the group links to market activity, made up 76% of its revenue, so the accounts work as a rough gauge of how busy trading in Nigeria has been. For investors outside Nigeria the headline looks strong, but the quarterly figures show that growth slowed sharply after June.

In Plain English NGX Group: the company that owns the Nigerian Exchange (the market itself), its regulation arm and a property arm. Temi Popoola is its group managing director and chief executive.

the company that owns the Nigerian Exchange (the market itself), its regulation arm and a property arm. Temi Popoola is its group managing director and chief executive. Pre-tax profit: what is left after running costs and before income tax. At NGX Group it includes a share of the profits of companies it part-owns.

what is left after running costs and before income tax. At NGX Group it includes a share of the profits of companies it part-owns. Transaction fees: the group’s largest income line, which it ties to how much trading takes place on the exchange.

the group’s largest income line, which it ties to how much trading takes place on the exchange. CSCS: Central Securities Clearing System Plc, a depository and settlement agency for traded securities in Nigeria. NGX Group owns 43.52% of it.

The Nine-Month Results

Revenue rose 80% to ₦27.26 billion (about US$20.5 million) from ₦15.16 billion (about US$11.4 million), and total income including other income reached ₦29.57 billion (about US$22.2 million). Operating costs grew more slowly, up 57% to ₦14.71 billion (about US$11.0 million), so operating profit climbed 74% to ₦14.87 billion (about US$11.2 million).

Pre-tax profit of ₦20.58 billion (about US$15.5 million) is about 32% more than the ₦15.6 billion (about US$11.7 million) the group earned before tax in all of 2025. After tax, profit rose 86% to ₦14.69 billion (about US$11.0 million) from ₦7.88 billion (about US$5.9 million).

How We Converted Naira to Dollars Market close, Friday 23 October 2026: ₦1,331.58 per US$1, used for every dollar figure in this article, for both years.

₦1,331.58 per US$1, used for every dollar figure in this article, for both years. Central bank official rate, same day: ₦1,361.34 per US$1, which would put nine-month pre-tax profit at about US$15.1 million.

₦1,361.34 per US$1, which would put nine-month pre-tax profit at about US$15.1 million. Why it matters: last year’s figures use today’s rate, so the dollar comparisons show naira growth only.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Drove NGX Group Profit Growth

Transaction fees more than doubled, up 112% to ₦20.68 billion (about US$15.5 million) from ₦9.74 billion (about US$7.3 million), and they supplied ₦10.94 billion (about US$8.2 million) of the ₦12.10 billion (about US$9.1 million) rise in revenue. Listing fees, charged to companies with securities on the exchange, grew 24% to ₦3.73 billion (about US$2.8 million).

Income from treasury investments slipped 3% to ₦2.07 billion (about US$1.6 million), and other income fell 17% to ₦2.31 billion (about US$1.7 million) as net currency losses widened to ₦603.30 million (about US$453,000). The group also had no finance costs, against ₦708.85 million (about US$532,000) a year earlier.

Its share of profit from two part-owned companies rose 70% to ₦5.72 billion (about US$4.3 million), which is 28% of pre-tax profit. Almost all of it, ₦5.71 billion (about US$4.3 million), came from CSCS, in which NGX Group holds 43.52%, while NG Clearing, in which it holds 27.7%, moved to a small profit from a loss.

A Slower Third Quarter

“Our first-half results demonstrate the strength and scalability of NGX Group’s business model.”

Temi Popoola, group chief executive, in the first-half results statement, July 2026

The nine-month total hides a clear slowdown. Pre-tax profit for July to September was ₦5.83 billion (about US$4.4 million), up just 1% from ₦5.77 billion (about US$4.3 million) in the third quarter of 2025.

That compares with an average of about ₦7.38 billion (about US$5.5 million) a quarter in the first half, when pre-tax profit rose 170% to ₦14.76 billion (about US$11.1 million). Profit after tax for the quarter fell 7% to ₦4.33 billion (about US$3.3 million), and operating profit slipped 4% to ₦4.25 billion (about US$3.2 million), even though revenue grew 36% to ₦9.66 billion (about US$7.3 million).

Costs, not fees, explain the gap: operating costs rose 63% in the quarter and other income fell 43% to ₦573.76 million (about US$431,000), while transaction fees still grew 54%. Personnel expenses alone more than doubled to ₦3.38 billion (about US$2.5 million) from ₦1.63 billion (about US$1.2 million), and neither the statements nor any commentary available when this article was written explains why.

Dividends, Cash and the Share Price

The cash-flow statement shows ₦8.23 billion (about US$6.2 million) of dividends paid in the nine months, up 87% from ₦4.41 billion (about US$3.3 million) a year earlier. By The Rio Times’ own arithmetic, that matches the final dividend for 2025 of ₦2.00 (about US$0.0015) a share on the 2.20 billion shares then in issue plus the first-half interim dividend of ₦1.30 (about US$0.001) a share on all 2.94 billion shares now in issue.

NGX Group Shares at a Glance Closing price, Friday 23 October 2026: ₦152.50 (about US$0.11) a share.

₦152.50 (about US$0.11) a share. Shares in issue: 2.94 billion, after the one-for-three bonus issue.

2.94 billion, after the one-for-three bonus issue. Value of the company at that price: about ₦448 billion (about US$337 million), The Rio Times’ calculation.

about ₦448 billion (about US$337 million), The Rio Times’ calculation. Shares traded that day: about 1.08 million.

Shareholders approved a bonus issue of one new share for every three held on Wednesday 29 April 2026, which raised the number of shares to 2.94 billion. Cash and equivalents fell 37% to ₦1.61 billion (about US$1.2 million) from ₦2.55 billion (about US$1.9 million) at the end of 2025, while holdings of investment securities rose 28% to ₦35.70 billion (about US$26.8 million).

What It Means for US Readers

NGX Group shares are quoted in naira on the Nigerian Exchange under the ticker NGXGROUP, so a US investor’s result depends on the naira as well as on the company. On Friday the market rate and the central bank’s official rate differed by about 2%, which moves every dollar figure in this article by the same amount.

The company is small by US standards, with nine-month pre-tax profit of about US$15.5 million and a market value of about US$337 million. Because transaction fees supply most of its revenue, its results rise and fall mainly with trading activity on the exchange, which the group itself credited in July for the first-half jump in fees.

This is a company news report, not investment advice. Anyone weighing Nigerian assets should look at the naira and local interest rates as well as at a single company’s results.

Pre-tax profit rose 83% over nine months, but only 1% in the third quarter.

What Is Not Known

The statements are unaudited, and The Rio Times did not find a separate management commentary on the nine months. Why personnel costs doubled in the third quarter, and whether that level will last, is therefore not known.

The accounts do not set out how much was traded on the exchange or how much of it came from foreign investors. Nor did we find an announcement saying whether the board will declare another dividend for 2026 after the first-half interim payment.

It is also not known whether profit from part-owned companies such as CSCS, which supplied 28% of pre-tax profit, will keep growing. One company’s numbers cannot show where the Nigerian market goes next, and the third-quarter pause may prove temporary.

The Rio Times could not confirm exactly when the group first filed the statements with the exchange. The file on the group’s website is dated Friday 23 October 2026, and the board approved the accounts on Tuesday 20 October.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is NGX Group?

NGX Group is the listed holding company of the Nigerian Exchange in Lagos, formerly the Nigerian Stock Exchange. It became a shareholder-owned group in 2021 and owns the exchange, a regulation company and a real-estate company.

How much profit did NGX Group make in nine months?

Pre-tax profit was ₦20.58 billion (about US$15.5 million), up 83%, in the nine months to 30 September 2026. Profit after tax was ₦14.69 billion (about US$11.0 million), up 86%, and the figures are unaudited.

What drove the profit rise?

Transaction fees more than doubled to ₦20.68 billion (about US$15.5 million), and the group’s share of profit from part-owned companies rose 70% to ₦5.72 billion (about US$4.3 million). Listing fees grew 24%.

Did profit keep growing in the third quarter?

Growth almost stopped. Pre-tax profit for July to September rose 1% to ₦5.83 billion (about US$4.4 million), while profit after tax fell 7%.

Did NGX Group pay dividends in 2026?

Yes. The cash-flow statement shows ₦8.23 billion (about US$6.2 million) paid in the nine months, which matches the 2025 final dividend of ₦2.00 (about US$0.0015) a share plus the first-half interim dividend of ₦1.30 (about US$0.001) a share.

World.title: TV Says Ecuador Seized 100 Guns in Bunkers
World.content:
An Ecuadorian Army soldier salutes from an armored Cobra II vehicle at a delivery ceremony in Quito (file photo, 11 September 2023). Photo: Jonathan Miranda, Presidencia de la República del Ecuador, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

ECUADOR · GUAYAQUIL · SECURITY

Ecuadorian soldiers and police seized about 100 firearms from arsenals hidden in bunkers in less than a week, the television network Teleamazonas reported on Saturday, 24 October 2026.

Key Facts — Power Index Ecuador ranks 8th of 14 in Ecuador ranks 8th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 38.2 points (October 2026 edition).

— The haul An offensive of under seven days is credited with seizing about 100 firearms from hidden bunkers.

— Confirmed A north Guayaquil bunker held 13 mines, 10 C4 charges and two guns (Wednesday, 21 October 2026).

— US link Washington designated Los Choneros and Los Lobos, two Ecuadorian gangs, as terrorist organizations in 2025.

— Travel The State Department rates Ecuador Level 2, but parts of Guayaquil are Level 4, “do not travel”.

— Not known No itemised official tally of the 100 firearms could be found.

Ecuadorian soldiers and police seized about 100 firearms from arsenals hidden in bunkers during an offensive of less than seven days, according to a report by the television network Teleamazonas on Saturday, 24 October 2026. The report says the haul included rifles and weapons of war that were intended to cause terror in the country.

The seizures matter to Americans because Washington listed two Ecuadorian gangs, Los Choneros and Los Lobos, as foreign terrorist organizations, effective when the notice was published on Friday, 5 September 2025. The State Department also tells travelers not to go to large parts of Guayaquil, Ecuador’s biggest city and main port, and to reconsider travel to the rest of it.

In Plain English Bunker: a hidden, often underground room used to store weapons; the police called the Guayaquil one “sophisticated”.

a hidden, often underground room used to store weapons; the police called the Guayaquil one “sophisticated”. Los Choneros and Los Lobos: two Ecuadorian criminal gangs that the US government lists as terrorist organizations.

two Ecuadorian criminal gangs that the US government lists as terrorist organizations. Joint Command: the body that directs Ecuador’s armed forces, led by General Henry Delgado.

the body that directs Ecuador’s armed forces, led by General Henry Delgado. Curfew and state of exception: emergency rules the government has used in several provinces to fight organized crime.

What Teleamazonas Reported

Teleamazonas published the report, by journalist Catalina García, in the 24 Horas reports section of its website on Saturday, 24 October 2026, under the headline “Security forces seize arsenals with 100 firearms hidden in bunkers”. Its web page sums the story up in one sentence: a military and police offensive of less than seven days seized rifles and weapons of war.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Ecuador ranks 8th of 14 with 38.2 points. Strongest pillar: military means (55); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (14). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B); 51 homicides per 100,000. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The report is a video, and the text on the page does not list the bunkers, their locations or the number of firearms in each. On Sunday morning, 25 October 2026, The Rio Times found no itemised tally from the National Police, the Interior Ministry or the Armed Forces Joint Command on their public websites and social media pages that adds up to 100.

The headline number is therefore Teleamazonas’s own, not an official count. It is also unclear whether the 100 firearms combine army and police seizures, and whether every bunker was in Guayaquil, although the version of the headline in the network’s news feed says the forces acted there.

From the Teleamazonas Page “The military and police offensive deployed in less than seven days made it possible to seize rifles and weapons of war intended to cause terror in the country.” (translated from Spanish)

Download the PDF checklist

The Guayaquil Bunker That Is Confirmed

The National Police dismantled a hidden bunker in a house in the Samanes neighborhood of north Guayaquil on the afternoon of Wednesday, 21 October 2026, the news site Primicias reported the next morning. The Rio Times covered that raid in an earlier report.

Officers found 13 Claymore anti-personnel mines, 10 C4 plastic-explosive charges with detonation systems, a rifle, a shotgun, magazines and more than 690 cartridges. Nobody was in the house when officers entered, and the police did not name a gang.

Police chief Juan Espín of Guayaquil’s Distrito Modelo said intelligence officers had investigated the property for two months. The police called the bunker “sophisticated”, with a hydraulic system near the water tank, and called the raid a “hard blow to criminal economies”.

That bunker held two firearms, so it cannot account for most of the 100 in the Teleamazonas count. The other finds behind the figure are not described in any source The Rio Times could read.

Timeline Wednesday, 21 October 2026: the National Police dismantle the Samanes bunker in north Guayaquil.

the National Police dismantle the Samanes bunker in north Guayaquil. Thursday, 22 October 2026: Primicias publishes the police account of the raid.

Primicias publishes the police account of the raid. Saturday, 24 October 2026: Teleamazonas reports about 100 firearms seized in bunkers.

How It Fits the Wider Campaign

General Henry Delgado, chief of Ecuador’s Joint Command of the Armed Forces, said in an interview that El Universo published on Thursday, 1 October 2026, that the armed forces alone had seized 3,167 firearms so far this year. He added that they had carried out more than 1,000 raids since January, mostly in Guayas province, whose capital is Guayaquil.

Spread over the 39 weeks from January to the end of September, 3,167 firearms is roughly 80 a week, a Rio Times calculation. A haul of about 100 in under a week would therefore be large but not out of line, especially if it adds police finds to military ones.

President Daniel Noboa announced on Wednesday, 14 October 2026 a new series of special operations, and Executive Decree 519, signed on Thursday, 15 October, sets a curfew between 00:00 and 05:00 in Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos, El Oro and Esmeraldas from Sunday, 1 November to Tuesday, 10 November. He said the last curfew, which ran from Thursday, 17 September to Wednesday, 30 September in four provinces, came with 40% fewer crimes, according to El Universo.

The Campaign in Numbers 3,167: firearms the armed forces seized in 2026, as of the 1 October interview.

firearms the armed forces seized in 2026, as of the 1 October interview. More than 1,000: raids since January, mostly in Guayas province.

raids since January, mostly in Guayas province. About 80 a week: the average that implies, a Rio Times calculation.

Why It Matters to the United States

The State Department published the terrorist designations of Los Choneros and Los Lobos, dated Wednesday, 6 August 2025, in the Federal Register on Friday, 5 September 2025, and the foreign terrorist organization listing took effect on publication. A second notice the same day designated both groups under Executive Order 13224, the order that allows the United States to block their assets.

The listing puts the two gangs in the same US category as Mexico’s Sinaloa Cartel, which the State Department designated in February 2025. Delgado said in the same interview that Ecuador’s planning with the United States for a regional anti-cartel coalition should be complete by November, with Ecuador as its operations theater for the South Pacific.

He added that any operation involving US forces would run under the Joint Command’s planning, because the Americans do not act alone. He also said joint action with the United States in international waters had largely cut the refueling points that fast drug boats relied on.

US Terrorism Listings Los Choneros and Los Lobos: Ecuadorian gangs named in two State Department notices published on Friday, 5 September 2025.

Ecuadorian gangs named in two State Department notices published on Friday, 5 September 2025. Sinaloa Cartel: Mexican cartel named in a notice published on Thursday, 20 February 2025.

What It Means for You

For travelers, the State Department’s Ecuador advisory, issued on Tuesday, 18 August 2026, is Level 2, “exercise increased caution”, because of crime, terrorism, unrest and kidnapping. It sets Level 4, “do not travel”, for the Guayaquil districts of Nueva Prosperina and Pascuales and all areas south of Portete de Tarqui Avenue, and Level 3 for the rest of the city.

The Samanes bunker was in the north of the city, and the police did not say what the mines and explosives were meant for. The find therefore says nothing certain about risks to visitors.

A curfew between 00:00 and 05:00 in Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos, El Oro and Esmeraldas, set by Decree 519 for Sunday, 1 November to Tuesday, 10 November 2026, could affect travelers there. Anyone planning a Guayaquil trip for those dates should check local news and the State Department page before booking.

US companies that ship through Guayaquil or deal with Ecuadorian partners should take legal advice on the terrorism designations, which can block assets and restrict dealings with the named groups. The designations apply to the gangs, not to Ecuador or its businesses.

Before You Go Read the State Department advisory of 18 August 2026 for the current Level 4 and Level 3 areas of Guayaquil.

Check Decree 519 and local news for the rules of the 1 to 10 November curfew in five Coast provinces.

What Is Not Known

No official source The Rio Times could read gives the number of bunkers, their locations or how many firearms each held. It is also unknown which agencies made each seizure, which gangs owned the weapons and whether anyone was arrested.

Teleamazonas calls the weapons “weapons of war”, but its page does not say how many were rifles, how many were handguns or how many were new. Nothing public explains how the weapons reached the bunkers or whether any came from abroad.

It is also unclear whether the 100 counts only firearms or other items, since the Samanes find alone held 13 mines and 10 C4 charges. An official tally from the police, the Interior Ministry or the Joint Command would settle the question.

The police have not said whether the Samanes bunker is tied to a known gang, and prosecutors have not said whether a case is open. The Rio Times found no official statement on further bunker searches.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many firearms were seized in Ecuador’s bunkers?

Teleamazonas reported about 100 firearms in an offensive of under seven days. The Rio Times found no itemised official tally to confirm the figure.

What was found in the Guayaquil bunker?

Police found 13 Claymore mines, 10 C4 charges, a rifle, a shotgun and more than 690 cartridges in north Guayaquil on 21 October 2026. The police did not name a gang.

Why does it matter to the United States?

Washington designated Los Choneros and Los Lobos as foreign terrorist organizations in September 2025. Ecuador’s military chief says planning with the United States for a regional anti-cartel coalition should be complete by November.

Is it safe for Americans to visit Guayaquil?

The State Department rates Ecuador Level 2 overall, but parts of Guayaquil are Level 4, “do not travel”, and the rest of the city is Level 3. Read the advisory issued on 18 August 2026 before any trip.

Is another curfew planned?

Yes, Executive Decree 519 sets a curfew from 00:00 to 05:00 in Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos, El Oro and Esmeraldas from 1 to 10 November 2026. President Noboa says the September curfew came with 40% fewer crimes.

World.title: Kenya Opposition Leader Kalonzo Explained
World.content:
Kalonzo Musyoka in 2012, when he was Kenya’s vice president and home affairs minister (file photo). Photo: Raidarmax / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

KENYA · ANALYSIS

Kalonzo Musyoka is the former vice president who has backed Raila Odinga’s presidential bids three times and now says he is the man to beat President William Ruto in August 2027.

Key Facts — Who Former vice president Kalonzo Musyoka leads the Wiper Patriotic Front and the opposition Ukombozi Alliance.

— Record He backed Raila Odinga for president in 2013, 2017 and 2022 instead of running himself.

— Base Ukambani, his home region, held about 1.7 million of Kenya’s 22.1 million registered voters in 2022.

— The rival On Saturday 24 October 2026 Ruto praised him, and he answered that Ruto’s days are numbered.

— The vote The vote is set for Tuesday 10 August 2027, and the opposition has no single candidate yet.

Kalonzo Musyoka is a veteran Kenyan opposition leader who declared himself President William Ruto’s main rival on Saturday 24 October 2026, the day Ruto said God uses him to publicise government projects. This guide explains who he is, what he did in past elections, how many voters his home region holds and why the contest matters beyond Kenya.

Our news report on the exchange is “Kenya’s President Says God Uses His Rival”. The United States designated Kenya a major non-NATO ally in June 2024, so who wins in August 2027 matters to Washington.

In Plain English — Wiper Patriotic Front Kalonzo’s party, founded in 2006 as ODM-Kenya and renamed in 2025 from Wiper Democratic Movement.

— Ukombozi Alliance The opposition coalition he leads, renamed in September 2026 from Azimio la Umoja.

— United Opposition The group of opposition leaders around Kalonzo, including Rigathi Gachagua, Martha Karua and Fred Matiang’i.

— Ukambani The Machakos, Kitui and Makueni counties, Kalonzo’s home region.

Who Kalonzo Musyoka Is

Kalonzo Musyoka was Kenya’s vice president from January 2008 under President Mwai Kibaki, who appointed him after the disputed 2007 elections, Kenyans.co.ke reports. He held the post until Tuesday 9 April 2013, having run in that year’s election as Raila Odinga’s running mate, Capital FM reported.

In July 2019 President Uhuru Kenyatta named him special envoy to monitor peace in South Sudan, according to a Foreign Affairs Ministry letter dated 2 July, The East African reported. The same report says he had earlier been involved in mediation efforts in South Sudan and Somalia.

He leads the Wiper Patriotic Front, which the Registrar of Political Parties renamed in 2025 from Wiper Democratic Movement. Capital FM now describes him as leader of both that party and the Ukombozi Alliance, the coalition that was Azimio la Umoja until September 2026.

Free download · Expat checklist Get the free checklist as PDF Moving to Kenya 2026: the step-by-step checklist. This guide condensed into 3 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. Email address Get the PDF Free. We send a confirmation link first, and the same address then receives The Rio Times Brief, our daily briefing. Unsubscribe with one click at any time; see our privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

His Record in Presidential Races

Kalonzo was a presidential candidate in 2007 for ODM-Kenya, the party that later became Wiper. In 2017 he ran as Raila Odinga’s running mate, and in March 2022 he described backing Odinga again as the third time he had done so, Capital FM reported.

In 2022 Odinga chose Martha Karua rather than Kalonzo as his running mate, and Kalonzo left the Azimio coalition for about a month before deciding in early June to rejoin it, Capital FM reported. The Standard’s report on the launch of Azimio’s manifesto on Monday 6 June, which he attended, carried the headline “I pledge my unequivocal support for Raila Odinga.”

Odinga gave him the nickname “watermelon”, a jibe at his indecisiveness, Kalonzo told KTN in March 2022, Capital FM reported. In January 2024 he declared that he would contest the 2027 race and “will no longer support Raila or any other candidate,” The Standard reported.

Citizen Digital reported that he also told The Standard, “Nothing will stop me, not even Azimio member parties fielding candidates.” He added that in 2022 he decided not to run in favour of Odinga but does not “expect any payback from him.”

Where His Votes Come From

The electoral commission’s register for the 2022 election listed 687,565 voters in Machakos, 532,758 in Kitui and 479,401 in Makueni. Together that is 1,699,724 of the 22,102,532 voters on the county register, about 7.7%.

Voters on the 2022 County Register — Nairobi City 2,415,310 registered voters

— Kiambu 1,275,008

— Machakos 687,565

— Kitui 532,758

— Makueni 479,401

— Ukambani total 1,699,724 of 22,102,532, or 7.7%

At 7.7% of the register, Ukambani cannot elect a president on its own, although its three counties together hold more voters than Kiambu’s 1,275,008. Article 138 of the Constitution also requires a winner to take at least 25% of the vote in more than half of the 47 counties, so a candidate has to win well beyond a home region.

These are the 2022 figures, and the register for 2027 may differ. The Constitution also demands nominations from at least 2,000 voters in each of a majority of counties, which forces every campaign to build a national network.

The Opposition Field in 2027

Capital FM describes Kalonzo as a co-principal of the United Opposition alongside Rigathi Gachagua, Martha Karua and Fred Matiang’i. Gachagua, a former deputy president, unveiled the Democracy for Citizens’ Party, Karua rebranded her party as the People’s Liberation Party, and Matiang’i, a former interior minister, now leads Jubilee.

Former president Uhuru Kenyatta resigned as chair of the coalition’s council in a letter dated Monday 5 October 2026, after Matiang’i took over the Jubilee Party, Citizen Digital reported. Kalonzo replied that there was “no vacuum at the helm of Ukombozi” and that his own office as party leader was unaffected.

In June 2026 Kalonzo unveiled a 13-point presidential agenda that promises anti-corruption audits, tax reforms to ease the cost of living, police reform and 6,000 megawatts of electricity capacity. He said he chose to launch his own platform before involving his co-principals, Capital FM reported.

“Without any split, I can assure you that William Ruto is a one-term president.”

Kalonzo Musyoka at the launch of his 13-point agenda, June 2026

Why the Contest Matters Beyond Kenya

Kenya’s elections carry a heavy history: the International Criminal Court says its prosecutor contended that more than 1,000 people were killed and about 350,000 displaced in the violence after the 2007 vote. That is why a disputed result in August 2027 would be watched closely well beyond Nairobi.

Kalonzo’s record is regional as well as national, with envoy work on South Sudan under President Kenyatta. In February 2025 The Standard reported that he criticised Ruto’s role in the Congo peace talks and claimed Ruto failed to support Kenyatta when he was the East African Community’s peace envoy.

Ruto is seeking a second term, and Article 142 of the Constitution bars anyone from holding the presidency for more than two terms, so the winner in August 2027 could serve until the next scheduled vote in 2032. If no candidate clears the thresholds described above, Article 138 requires a fresh election within 30 days, in which normally only the two leading candidates stand.

What It Means for US Readers

Presidential Determination 2024-05, signed by then President Joe Biden on Monday 24 June 2024 and published in the Federal Register on Friday 12 July 2024, designates Kenya a major non-NATO ally under US arms-export and foreign-assistance law. That status signals close US security ties, so the identity of Kenya’s next president and the fairness of the vote matter to US planners.

“Exercise increased caution in Kenya due to crime, terrorism, civil unrest, and kidnapping.”

US State Department travel advisory for Kenya

The official campaign period runs from Saturday 29 May to Saturday 7 August 2027, so travellers heading to Kenya in mid-2027 should check the advisory and any US Embassy alerts before they book. Investors will watch whether the opposition unites behind Kalonzo or another leader, although Capital FM’s summary of his agenda gives no costings.

Kalonzo’s agenda promises an “interest-based approach” to foreign policy and deeper engagement in the East African Community and the African Union, Capital FM reported. The summary reviewed does not mention the United States, so how he would manage the security partnership is not known.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the opposition will back Kalonzo or another leader, or when it will decide. Ruto praised Kalonzo and Kalonzo answered that Ruto’s days are numbered, and no outlet reviewed reports a deal between them.

The Rio Times could not confirm Kalonzo’s 2007 vote share at an official source, so this guide gives no figure. Voter numbers here come from the 2022 register, and the commission has not published a 2027 register in the sources reviewed.

Kenya’s next election date also faces a legal footnote: a Malindi High Court judgment of Friday 7 August 2026 held that the presidential vote should have been held on Tuesday 11 August 2026, but its declaration was suspended until after the 2027 election, Capital FM and Kenyans.co.ke reported. Electoral commissioner Ann Nderitu said the suspension keeps Tuesday 10 August 2027 in force, Kenyans.co.ke reported, and the commission’s website still lists that date.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Kalonzo Musyoka?

Kalonzo Musyoka is a veteran Kenyan politician who was vice president from 2008 to 2013. He now leads the Wiper Patriotic Front and the opposition Ukombozi Alliance.

Has Kalonzo ever run for president?

Yes, he was a presidential candidate in 2007 for ODM-Kenya. In 2013 and 2017 he ran as Raila Odinga’s running mate, and in 2022 he again backed Odinga instead of running.

Is Kalonzo the opposition’s candidate for 2027?

The opposition has not named one candidate. Kalonzo calls himself Ruto’s main rival and has unveiled his own 13-point agenda.

When is Kenya’s next election?

Kenya votes on Tuesday 10 August 2027, according to the electoral commission’s website. A president needs more than half of all votes and at least 25% in more than half of the 47 counties.

How many voters live in Kalonzo’s home region?

Machakos, Kitui and Makueni counties had 1,699,724 registered voters in 2022, about 7.7% of the national total. That is not enough to win alone, so any candidate must win support in other regions.

Why does Kalonzo matter to Americans?

The United States named Kenya a major non-NATO ally in June 2024, so the 2027 result matters to US security and diplomacy. Kalonzo has also worked as a regional peace envoy for South Sudan.

World.title: Moody’s Says El Salvador Debt Stays High
World.content:
A Finance Ministry news conference in San Salvador. Undated file photo from an earlier government, not from this week. (Photo: Presidencia El Salvador, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons)

EL SALVADOR · ECONOMY · CREDIT RATING

Credit-rating agency Moody’s says El Salvador’s pension deal with the IMF lowers the risk of a cash crunch in 2027, but it still expects the country’s debt to pass 90% of its output that year.

Key Facts — The deal The state is to recognise about US$2.3 billion it owes private pension funds, in 2027.

— The debt Public debt is projected at 85.0% of output in 2026 and 89.2% in 2027.

— The rating Moody’s rates El Salvador B3, below investment grade, with a positive outlook.

— The loan The IMF released about US$138 million on Thursday 1 October from a US$1.4 billion programme.

— Still open The terms of the new pension certificates and the 2027 pension reform are not public.

Moody’s Ratings says El Salvador’s deal with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) over its pension debt will sharply reduce the risk of a cash crunch in 2027, but public debt will still pass 90% of economic output that year. The comment, published during the week of 19 October according to Bloomberg Línea’s report of Friday 23 October, matters to US investors because Moody’s rates El Salvador at B3, below investment grade, with a positive outlook.

The obligation at the centre is about US$2.3 billion, equal to 5.5% of the economy by Moody’s count, in unpaid interest and transfers that the state owes private pension fund managers. As that account describes the IMF’s framework, most of it could be turned into new long-term pension certificates, with regular payments starting at the end of 2027.

In Plain English Moody’s Ratings: a US agency that grades the debt of governments and companies. Its B3 grade for El Salvador sits below investment grade.

a US agency that grades the debt of governments and companies. Its B3 grade for El Salvador sits below investment grade. The IMF programme: a 40-month loan of about US$1.4 billion, approved on Wednesday 26 February 2025 and paid in instalments after reviews.

a 40-month loan of about US$1.4 billion, approved on Wednesday 26 February 2025 and paid in instalments after reviews. Pension fund managers: private companies, known as AFPs, that run workers’ retirement accounts and are owed money by the state.

private companies, known as AFPs, that run workers’ retirement accounts and are owed money by the state. Pension certificates: new long-term IOUs the state would issue so it can repay that debt slowly instead of in cash.

What Moody’s Said

Moody’s says the IMF agreement “will substantially reduce the risk” that the pension obligation becomes “a disruptive liquidity event” in 2027, in a Spanish-language account translated here. It calls the progress positive for credit because it lets the IMF programme continue and reduces uncertainty over that liability.

“The key consideration for El Salvador’s credit profile remains whether the government can maintain the fiscal discipline needed to put debt on a sustained downward path after the one-off increase in reported debt associated with the recognition of pensions.” Moody’s, as quoted in Spanish by Bloomberg Línea on Friday 23 October and translated by The Rio Times

The agency adds that the relief does not replace strict fiscal policy, and that the country must keep running budget surpluses before interest payments. It also says financing conditions have improved, liquidity buffers have strengthened and bond spreads have fallen from the distress of 2022.

Moody’s notes that the IMF already counted the operation in its baseline projections. About 30 percentage points of the debt-to-output ratio are tied to long-term pension obligations, the report says.

What the IMF Numbers Show

The IMF’s press release of Thursday 1 October puts gross debt of the non-financial public sector, including pension bonds, at 87.6% of output in 2025, 85.0% in 2026 and 89.2% in 2027. A note says the 2027 figures include the recognition of about US$2.3 billion in accrued but unpaid interest owed to private pension funds.

IMF Projections, Percent of Output 2025: debt 87.6%, budget deficit 2.9%, surplus before interest 1.9%.

debt 87.6%, budget deficit 2.9%, surplus before interest 1.9%. 2026: debt 85.0%, budget deficit 2.3%, surplus before interest 2.9%.

debt 85.0%, budget deficit 2.3%, surplus before interest 2.9%. 2027: debt 89.2%, budget deficit 7.7%, surplus before interest 3.7%.

The IMF’s note says the 2027 figures include that recognition, which would explain a deficit that jumps while the surplus before interest keeps rising. Moody’s expects debt above 90% that year, against the IMF’s 89.2%, and ContraPunto reported on Monday 7 September that Moody’s puts 2026 debt at 93.4%, against the IMF’s 85.0%, a difference the sources do not explain.

The IMF Board completed the second and third reviews of the programme on Thursday 1 October and released about US$138 million (SDR 101.96 million, the IMF’s own unit of account). It urged “timely pension and civil service reforms” and sustained fiscal consolidation to put public debt on a downward trajectory.

How the Pension Debt Built Up

Central Reserve Bank data published on Thursday 30 April show the state owed private pension funds about US$11.48 billion in March 2026, up from about US$11.24 billion in December 2025, Infobae reported. About US$8.39 billion of that sits in transition certificates that have paid no principal or interest since a reform approved by the Legislative Assembly in late 2022.

The US$2.3 billion at the centre of the Moody’s comment is the unpaid interest and transfers that built up during the grace period set by that reform, Bloomberg Línea says, not the full stock of debt to the funds. The same account says the grace period suspended payments of principal and interest on a large part of the debt until April 2027, while interest keeps accumulating.

Pension Debt Timeline Late 2022: the Legislative Assembly approves a reform; transition certificates stop paying principal and interest.

the Legislative Assembly approves a reform; transition certificates stop paying principal and interest. Tuesday 10 February 2026: original deadline for a pension reform proposal under the IMF programme.

original deadline for a pension reform proposal under the IMF programme. Thursday 3 September 2026: IMF staff update moves the reform to 2027.

IMF staff update moves the reform to 2027. Thursday 1 October 2026: IMF Board releases about US$138 million.

IMF Board releases about US$138 million. April 2027: the grace period on payments ends.

the grace period on payments ends. End of 2027: regular payments on the new pension certificates would start.

Earlier IMF documents called for a pension reform proposal by Tuesday 10 February 2026, a deadline the government missed, Infobae reported. The staff-level update of Thursday 3 September now expects a reform of the system’s parameters in 2027, elsalvador.com reports, without saying what the changes will be.

What It Means for You

For US bond investors, Moody’s view is that a liability once seen as a possible cash shock has become easier to manage, while the debt ratio is still set to rise in 2027. At B3, the country remains below investment grade.

The reports describe a Moody’s comment on the pension deal, not a change to the B3 grade or to the positive outlook, which Moody’s raised from stable in early February, according to Diario La Página. A positive outlook means the next move could be an upgrade, but the sources reviewed give no date for any rating decision.

For anyone following the IMF programme in Washington, the Board release says the transfer of majority control of the Chivo bitcoin wallet to a private operator is complete. It adds that “no further Bitcoin accumulation is envisaged beyond the documented donations.”

For Salvadoran workers, the pension reform expected in 2027 is the open question, since the IMF statement does not say what it will contain. Nothing in the sources reviewed says what it will mean for retirement ages or payments.

What to Watch The terms of the new pension certificates: interest rate, maturity and holders.

The content of the 2027 pension reform.

Whether Moody’s acts on its positive outlook, and whether the IMF review path stays on track.

What Is Not Known

The Rio Times could not open Moody’s own text, so it relies on the Bloomberg Línea report and on elsalvador.com’s repeat of it on Saturday 24 October. The terms of the new pension certificates, including interest rate, maturity and who would hold them, are not public in the sources reviewed.

The Finance Ministry’s news page listed no statement on the Moody’s comment or on the pension operation when the Rio Times looked on Sunday 25 October. It is also unknown when Moody’s might act on its positive outlook, and what the 2027 pension reform will contain.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Moody’s say about El Salvador’s pension deal?

Moody’s says the pension agreement with the IMF will substantially reduce the risk that the obligation becomes a liquidity shock in 2027. It still expects public debt to exceed 90% of output that year.

How big is the pension obligation?

The IMF puts the accrued but unpaid interest owed to private pension funds at about US$2.3 billion. Moody’s puts that at about 5.5% of El Salvador’s economic output.

What is El Salvador’s credit rating?

Moody’s rates El Salvador B3 with a positive outlook, according to reports of its comment. B3 is below investment grade.

Is El Salvador’s debt now under control?

Not yet. The IMF projects gross public debt at 89.2% of output in 2027, up from 85.0% in 2026, and Moody’s expects more than 90%.

What happens next with pensions?

The IMF expects a reform of the pension system’s rules in 2027, but its content has not been published. The terms of the new pension certificates are also not public.

World.title: Kenya Loses Billions to Illicit Money Flows
World.content:
Wooden vessels moored at the Old Town import dock in Mombasa, Kenya (file photo from March 2020). Trade mis-invoicing and smuggling are two of the ways Kenya is estimated to lose money. Photo: Martin Chomba, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

KENYA · NAIROBI · ECONOMY

Estimates of what Kenya loses each year to corruption, smuggling and false trade paperwork run from about US$1.9 billion to US$3.8 billion, and the newest headline figure does not match the study behind it.

Key Facts — What it is Illicit financial flows are money lost to corruption, smuggling, counterfeit goods and false trade invoices.

— The range Estimates range from US$1.9 to US$3.8 billion a year; Sh403.58 billion equals about US$3.1 billion.

— The biggest piece Illicit goods such as counterfeits are put at Sh153 billion (about US$1.2 billion) a year.

— The scale Losses are put at about 12% of Kenya’s national budget, more than health spending.

— The catch The three published figures do not match, and none is a directly measured total.

Kenya’s illicit financial flows cost it an estimated Sh403.58 billion (about US$3.1 billion) a year, The Standard of Nairobi reported on Sunday 25 October 2026, citing a new Amnesty International report. The documents behind the number differ: Amnesty’s own report gives US$3.8 billion, and the 2025 study it relies on gives about US$1.9 billion.

For US readers, the numbers matter because Kenya is a Major Non-NATO Ally of the United States, and money lost to corruption and smuggling cannot be taxed while the government services a public debt that Amnesty puts at Sh12.3 trillion (about US$95 billion). No single figure can be confirmed from the documents, so this article sets out what each source says.

In Plain English Illicit financial flows: money that leaves a country’s legal economy through corruption, tax evasion, smuggling or false invoices.

money that leaves a country’s legal economy through corruption, tax evasion, smuggling or false invoices. Trade mis-invoicing: declaring a wrong value on imports or exports to pay less duty or move money abroad.

declaring a wrong value on imports or exports to pay less duty or move money abroad. Amnesty International: a global human-rights group. It released the report with its Kenya office in October 2026.

a global human-rights group. It released the report with its Kenya office in October 2026. NTA and Oxfam Kenya: the National Taxpayers Association, a Kenyan watchdog, and an aid charity. They published the 2025 study.

What The Standard Reported

The Standard’s article, by Jacinta Mutura and dated Sunday 25 October 2026, says Kenya loses an estimated Sh403.58 billion (about US$3.1 billion) annually through corruption, trade mis-invoicing and illicit goods, according to a new report by Amnesty International. The opening paragraph of the article gives no calculation, and the rest of the text sits behind the newspaper’s paywall.

At 129.79 shillings per US dollar (house market data, close of Friday 23 October 2026), Sh403.58 billion is about US$3.1 billion. The newspaper’s tags include Kenya’s debt crisis and public debt servicing, which fits the report’s focus on how debt shapes the budget.

The Standard’s figure does not appear anywhere in the text of the Amnesty report, so its origin is unclear. For that reason this article attributes the figure to The Standard and does not present it as Amnesty’s own.

Email address Get the PDF Free. We send a confirmation link first, and the same address then receives The Rio Times Brief, our daily briefing. Unsubscribe with one click at any time; see our privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

What the Amnesty Report Says

The report, titled Human Rights Under Siege and announced by Amnesty International on Monday 19 October 2026, is mainly about Kenya’s crackdown on youth-led protests between 2023 and 2025 against high taxes, debt and living costs. It also has a section on debt and public spending, where it argues that illicit financial flows remain rampant and undermine the government’s ability to raise money at home.

In that section Amnesty writes that in 2025 Oxfam and the National Taxpayers Association estimated that corruption, trade mis-invoicing and illicit goods together caused an annual loss of US$3.8 billion. It adds that such losses equal about 12% of the national budget, more than the health or social-protection budgets.

Amnesty converts shillings at 129 per US dollar in its own report, and at that rate The Standard’s Sh403.58 billion would be about US$3.1 billion, well below Amnesty’s US$3.8 billion. The report also quotes the African Union’s Common African Position on Debt of March 2026, which says illicit flows lead to external borrowing to make up for lost revenue.

What the Original Study Found

The study is titled Study to Establish the Size of Kenya’s Illicit Financial Flows and was launched on Thursday 18 September 2025 by the National Taxpayers Association (NTA), a Kenyan watchdog, together with Oxfam Kenya. The NTA describes it as the first comprehensive attempt to estimate Kenya’s yearly losses from corruption, commercial malpractice and criminal activity.

Its headline finding is that Kenya loses an estimated Sh253 billion (about US$1.9 billion) a year through commercial and criminal activities such as bribery and corruption. A table on page 38 splits Sh243.15 billion (about US$1.9 billion) into corruption at Sh11.15 billion (about US$86 million), illicit goods at Sh153 billion (about US$1.2 billion) and trade mis-invoicing at Sh79 billion (about US$609 million).

The authors say they could only establish the size by consolidating available statistical figures, and they call for wider data integration. They also report that the gap between what Kenya and its trading partners declare grew from Sh1 billion (about US$8 million) in 2016 to Sh180 billion (about US$1.4 billion) in 2024, according to the study’s summary.

Why the Three Figures Do Not Match

Amnesty’s US$3.8 billion is about twice the study’s own total of Sh253 billion (about US$1.9 billion), and The Standard’s Sh403.58 billion (about US$3.1 billion) falls between them. The published documents do not show how either higher figure was reached from the study.

Possible explanations include different categories, different years or a different exchange rate, but none is stated in the documents. What the documents do support is a range of about US$1.9 billion to US$3.8 billion a year, with the study as the best-documented base.

The Three Figures Sh403.58 billion (about US$3.1 billion): The Standard, Sunday 25 October 2026, attributed to Amnesty International.

The Standard, Sunday 25 October 2026, attributed to Amnesty International. US$3.8 billion: the Amnesty report announced on 19 October 2026, citing the 2025 Oxfam and NTA study.

the Amnesty report announced on 19 October 2026, citing the 2025 Oxfam and NTA study. Sh253 billion (about US$1.9 billion): the study’s own headline estimate, in its executive summary.

the study’s own headline estimate, in its executive summary. Sh243.15 billion (about US$1.9 billion): the study’s own category table on page 38.

What It Means for US Readers

Kenya is a Major Non-NATO Ally of the United States under a presidential memorandum of 24 June 2024. The Financial Action Task Force (FATF), the global anti-money-laundering watchdog, placed Kenya under increased monitoring on Friday 23 February 2024 and still listed it in its latest statement, dated Friday 19 June 2026.

That statement says Kenya has improved its anti-money-laundering regime but must still improve supervision, beneficial-ownership data and money-laundering investigations. The same June 2026 meeting added Bosnia and Herzegovina and Iraq to the list and removed Algeria and Namibia.

The European Union added Kenya to its list of high-risk countries for money laundering in a regulation dated 10 June 2025, in force from 5 August 2025. The European Commission’s page on that list, which includes updates published on 9 January 2026, still shows Kenya.

For US companies and banks, these listings are a reminder that Kenya’s illicit-flow estimates are not only a domestic budget matter. The US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, which bars US persons and companies from paying foreign officials to win business, applies to dealings with Kenyan officials.

Read the companion piece in this cluster: Kenya Freezes Assets in US$1.9M Lands Case. Both articles are updated from the same verified sources.

What Is Not Known

It is not known how The Standard arrived at its figure of Sh403.58 billion (about US$3.1 billion), because the opening of its article gives no calculation and the figure does not appear in the Amnesty report’s text. Amnesty’s US$3.8 billion also does not match the totals in the study it cites, and neither Amnesty, the National Taxpayers Association nor Oxfam Kenya has explained the difference in the documents reviewed, which leaves readers with a range rather than a single answer.

No one has published a directly measured total, since the study itself says it could only consolidate available statistics. Amnesty’s report says it wrote to the Presidency, the police and other bodies in September 2026 and had received no response by publication, and no government comment on the illicit-flow estimates appears in the documents reviewed.

Kenya’s status after the FATF’s next meeting is also open, because its list page showed no statement newer than Friday 19 June 2026 when checked on Sunday 25 October 2026. The EU list is updated separately and still named Algeria and Namibia, which the FATF removed in June 2026, so the two lists can differ.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does Kenya lose to illicit financial flows?

Estimates run from about US$1.9 billion to US$3.8 billion a year, depending on the source. The Standard puts the figure at Sh403.58 billion, about US$3.1 billion, citing Amnesty International.

Where does the Sh403.58 billion (about US$3.1 billion) figure come from?

The Standard attributes it to a new Amnesty International report. That number does not appear in the report, which cites a 2025 study with different totals.

What are illicit financial flows?

They are money that leaves a country’s legal economy through corruption, tax evasion, smuggling, counterfeit goods or false trade invoices. The money is not taxed or accounted for, so the government loses revenue.

Is Kenya on a money-laundering watch list?

Yes. The Financial Action Task Force placed Kenya under increased monitoring on 23 February 2024 and still listed it in its latest statement, dated 19 June 2026.

Why does this matter to US readers?

Kenya is a Major Non-NATO Ally of the United States, and its place on international watch lists is part of the risk picture that banks and investors weigh. US companies that deal with Kenyan officials must also follow the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act.
