World.title: Police tackle underage drinking, illegal scooters in Tartu
World.content:
Police are cracking down on banned electric scooters and minors disturbing public order in Estonia's second-biggest city, Tartu, and carried out one of their largest recent operations targeting young people on Friday.

People out and about in Tartu in southern Estonia late on Friday night may have encountered an unusually large police presence.

Dozens of law enforcement officers were focused on light electric vehicle compliance in the Annelinn and Ülenurme areas. They identified two prohibited scooters, which can travel faster than the legal limit, and two cases of people riding two to a single electric scooter.

Officers also monitored helmet use and spoke with young people.

Kristo Kooskora, a senior inspector at the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA), said that the weather had worked against them this time.

"It rained to some extent throughout the evening, and we saw very few scooters, but that does not mean the problem has disappeared. Various scooter gatherings have also become popular recently, and we have been dealing with those as well. Our work in this area is not over," she told ERR's evening news show "Aktuaalne kaamera."

There was more activity in the city center after midnight.

Nearly 50 police officers patrolled Küüni tänav, which leads from Kaubamaja shopping center to the main square, in an unprecedented operation.

"The checks were conducted by officers simply moving in from both ends and checking everyone caught between the police teams until the officers eventually met in the middle," Kooskora said.

According to preliminary information, police identified nearly 30 intoxicated minors, including some who were severely intoxicated. There were also minors using e-cigarettes and cases involving suspected drug use.

Handcuffs had to be used in several cases because the young people became aggressive. Some also attempted to flee, but their attempts were unsuccessful.

Officers said the operation confirmed the problem with minors is serious. Checks should be carried out more frequently, including on weekdays.

World.title: Justice chancellor: Wild boar cannot be made to suffer when training hunting dogs
World.content:
The Ministry of Regional Affairs and the Ministry of Climate should establish clear legal rules for training hunting dogs using live wild boars to ensure animal welfare and legal clarity, the Chancellor of Justice's Office says.

Four years ago in May, the regional affairs minister issued a regulation on measures to prevent and control African swine fever, introducing an exemption under which the ban on keeping pigs outdoors does not apply to wild boars kept for training hunting dogs.

The Estonian Union for the Protection of Animals asked the chancellor of justice to examine whether the regulation complies with the Animal Protection Act. The organization also pointed out that the law provides no legal basis for using wild boars kept in artificial environments to train hunting dogs and that no detailed requirements have been established for such training.

Deputy Chancellor of Justice-Adviser Olari Koppel said the ban on keeping pigs outdoors is a biosecurity measure and that the minister has the authority to introduce exemptions, provided they comply with EU law and do not undermine animal disease prevention. Koppel therefore sees no reason to believe that the exemption for training hunting dogs violates these conditions.

However, he noted that the regulation only provides an exemption from the ban on keeping pigs outdoors. It does not provide a legal basis for using wild boars to train hunting dogs or authorize activities prohibited under the Animal Protection Act.

"The absence of a specific legal provision does not, however, mean that such an activity is prohibited, provided other applicable rules are followed," Koppel said, adding that it must be possible to conduct training without endangering the animal's welfare.

The law does not establish a specific legal basis or detailed requirements for training hunting dogs using live wild boars. The activity is primarily governed by the Nature Conservation Act and the general animal welfare requirements arising from it.

Under the Animal Protection Act, animals must not be subjected to suffering or pain. According to Koppel, if hunting dog training cannot be conducted without causing such harm, the executive branch cannot make the activity permissible through regulations, guidelines or administrative practices.

"In that case, only the Riigikogu can decide through legislation whether the objective of the training and the benefits it provides justify making an exception to the prohibition established by law," Koppel said.

Koppel said the lack of clarity in the regulations is a problem. To address it, the Ministry of Regional Affairs and the Ministry of Climate should establish the conditions for training hunting dogs in legislation rather than merely in guidelines or explanatory memorandums. This would ensure compliance with animal welfare requirements and provide legal clarity.

Wild boar. Photo is illustrative. Source: Kalmer Saar/minupilt.err.ee

World.title: Isamaa party promises to close the climate ministry and create scandals committee
World.content:
Isamaa leader Urmas Reinsalu said at the party's council meeting in Tallinn that the campaign for Estonia's parliamentary elections has begun and is intensifying.

"Those same three parties that, under SALK's leadership, have established a politics of lies under both Kaja Kallas' and Kristen Michal's governments are now maneuvering to escape political punishment and put up camouflage nets," Reinsalu said, referring to the coalition Reform Party and Eesti 200, as well as the opposition Social Democrats.

According to the Isamaa chairman, Eesti 200 is being pressured to withdraw from the elections so that its remaining voters will instead bolster the Reform Party and the Social Democrats.

"So much for political accountability," Reinsalu said. "With the prime minister's speech to the party council, the Reform Party has launched a new wave of fearmongering and lies. This is being dressed up in a marketing campaign whose underlying message is that, yes, we have failed, but we will do better in the future."

"The Reform Party is featuring a beloved actor in its campaign, while the Social Democrats have adopted a different tactic, attempting to conceal their complicity in the Kallas-Michal government by maneuvering to put forward the secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as their candidate for prime minister. This maneuver will not succeed!" the Isamaa chairman said.

Reinsalu summed up Isamaa's political plans following the 2027 Riigikogu elections with the words "Let the citizens decide."

The party plans to give citizens the right to initiate early elections, following the Latvian model, and to establish a commission of inquiry into scandals after the elections. Lying before the commission would be a criminal offense.

In the area of defense, the party plans to close the border with Russia.

Isamaa also pledged to introduce a supplementary budget that would cut spending.

"Cost-cutting starts at the top: parliamentary and ministerial salaries, closing the Ministry of Climate and a critical review of foundations and subsidies," the party pledged.

On taxes, Isamaa promised to abolish the motor vehicle tax and reduce value-added tax on basic foodstuffs (meat, fish, milk, fruit, vegetables and bread) to 13 percent starting July 1, 2027.

The party also promised to end what it described as the harassment of businesses. "The Climate Act will be thrown in the trash. Investment certainty and a stable operating environment will be restored for the resource-based economy."

The party pledged to carry out an artificial intelligence revolution with the same boldness that Estonia once demonstrated in building its digital state. "The goal is genuine productivity growth, exports and simpler government operations. Sovereignty risks will be taken into account."

Isamaa promised to protect fundamental freedoms and repeal unnecessary restrictions.

The party also pledged to ease the burden of raising children on families and protect teachers' incomes.

In the energy sector, the party will emphasize oil shale. "The energy sector will be provided with dispatchable generation capacity, domestic resources (including oil shale) and affordable prices. Efforts to render oil shale-based energy production unviable will be halted."

The party also promised stricter requirements for the use of Estonian in public spaces, a conservative immigration policy and the restoration of regional balance.

Parliamentary elections will take place in March 2027.

World.title: Passenger ferry traffic on Narva River in danger of being discontinued
World.content:
Passenger ferry service launched on the Narva River five years ago is at risk of shutting down as the riverboat Caroline has proved too large for the Port of Narva.

The riverboat Caroline made its final trip of the season from Narva to Narva-Jõesuu in late September. The vessel is currently docked at the Port of Sillamäe, but it remains unclear where it will go next or where it will spend the winter.

The Estonian Transport Administration discovered that Narva's river port is not authorized to accommodate vessels of Caroline's size.

"The Transport Administration conducted a port inspection and found that Caroline is not a small vessel, but the port is registered as a small craft harbor. The port must change its registration. The harbormaster must also hold a license to operate larger vessels rather than just a small craft operator's license," said Kert Süsmalainen, head of the Transport Administration's waterways and ports department.

According to the Transport Administration, the fact that Caroline had previously used the Port of Narva without any problems was due to an oversight by the port operator. Five years ago, the vessel's length was measured at the waterline. However, Caroline's actual length exceeds the permitted limit by 120 centimeters.

Narva River. Source: Jenny Va / ERR

The City of Narva is trying to resolve the issue quickly. The port's registration has already been amended and there are plans to establish a passenger waiting area. However, finding a qualified harbormaster for the passenger port could prove challenging.

"It's clear that there are no people with those qualifications in Narva. Language proficiency is another obstacle. Our concern, of course, is that if a harbormaster is hired solely because of our vessel, their entire annual salary costs will likely be passed on to us through port fees. That, in turn, raises the question of whether we can make the numbers work," said Caroline owner Kaspar Eisel.

Operating Caroline on the Narva River is becoming increasingly challenging financially. While the riverboat carried around 10,000 passengers per season in its early years, that number fell to just under 3,000 this summer.

Whether Caroline will operate on the Narva River next summer and under what conditions, will be determined through negotiations with the management of Narva's river port.

World.title: Rain showers and cloud cover forecast across provinces

Temperatures are expected to edge slightly higher across central and southern provinces while remaining near seasonal averages in the north, maintaining mild autumn conditions during daytime hours before turning cool overnight and early in the morning.

Monday will see fair to partly cloudy conditions nationwide, accompanied by light and variable winds and stable temperatures. World.title: ‘Call of Duty’ North Korea invasion edition tops sales charts in South
World.content:
Seoul – The latest instalment of the “Call of Duty” video game franchise, featuring a full-scale North Korean invasion of South Korea, has topped sales charts in the would-be target, even as real-life border tensions are ratcheting higher.

“Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4”, the latest edition of the globally popular franchise is set against a backdrop of tensions between the United States and Russia.

Its Friday release comes on the heels of an explosion inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) that injured three South Korean soldiers, further straining ties on the peninsula.

The game follows several parallel storylines: a squad of young American and South Korean soldiers fighting for survival, a former serviceman driven by revenge, and a power struggle surrounding a new North Korean leader — a character players can also take on.

The new edition has generated considerable interest in South Korea, where able-bodied men are required to serve between 18 and 21 months in the military, depending on the branch.

The title has topped both the global and South Korean sales charts on Steam, one of the world’s largest digital distribution platforms for PC games.

The campaign begins with a surprise invasion of South Korea by North Korean forces, who deploy paratroopers and infiltrate through an underground tunnel to catch South Korean and US troops off guard.

In reality, the US stations about 28,000 troops in South Korea to help deter the nuclear-armed North. Seoul and Pyongyang remain technically at war because the 1950-53 Korean War ended in an armistice rather than a peace treaty.

Reactions among South Korean gamers have been largely positive, with some posting hashtags featuring a Korean slogan meaning “exterminate communism” on social media and others saying they were considering upgrading their computers or buying new consoles to play the title.

“I cried so much playing the game to a point I almost got dehydrated. It reminds me so much of my grandfather, who fought in the Korean War,” a Threads user with the handle b_yeol_t said.

Another user, posting under the handle ireozima_zebal, described the experience as “horrifying” because of its implications for a potential conflict on the Korean peninsula.

“This is what would unfold if the North launched an invasion, with the border province of Gangwon overwhelmed within an hour and our defence line pushed back right on the edge of Seoul,” the user said.

But the game has also drawn criticism for turning the fraught history between North and South Korea into entertainment.

The title raises the “question of whether it is appropriate… to present the tragedy of the Korean War and the current antagonism between South and North as something to be consumed for entertainment”, Kim Sung-jae, chairman of the Kim Dae Jung Peace Center, wrote in the Hankyoreh newspaper last month.

On Saturday, North Korean state media said leader Kim Jong Un had urged his military to become the strongest in the world at a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang last week.

World.title: ‘Tech debt coming due’: AI-found flaw signals chaos ahead
World.content:
Washington – Companies and government agencies rushed this week to patch two critical flaws in PHP, the programming language that runs a large share of the world’s websites.

The vulnerability to potential hackers was found by using a powerful model from OpenAI in one of the most high-profile demonstration of AI’s cyber capabilities.

AFP spoke with Michael Daniel, president of the Cyber Threat Alliance and a former White House cybersecurity coordinator under former US president Barack Obama, about what the episode means as AI tools find software flaws faster than ever.

The interview has been edited for length and clarity.

Q: What does the PHP episode tell us?

A: This is the beginning of a pretty chaotic period, given the abilities of the advanced models. I’ve been saying for years that the logical conclusion of these AI models being able to find vulnerabilities at speed and at scale is that there’s going to be a flood of these vulnerabilities.

Rob Joyce [former cybersecurity director at the US National Security Agency] has referred to it as the great cleansing forest fire of old software. I’ve talked about our tech debt coming due.

The incentives have been for people to keep software as long as possible, and we don’t really factor these risks into the cost of having the software. You’re not incurring a direct cost on your books for this old software, but in reality you are, only it’s an implicit cost until something like this happens.

Q: What should organizations be doing?

A: Preparing to get your software updated, be prepared to keep it updated, and be prepared to implement patches when they come out.

There’s going to be a flood of vulnerabilities, a flood of patches and a flood of mitigations, and not all of them will be created equal.

For a lot of smaller organizations that don’t have a lot of internal capacity, what you’ve got to do is shift your organization to be able to accept the vendor updates as fast as you can.

Q: Is every flaw dangerous?

A: Historically, the exploitation rate for vulnerabilities has been five or six percent, and there’s no indication that number is going up. But now when bad guys exploit a vulnerability, they’re able to do so much more quickly.

It used to take a month or two for a proof of concept to come out, and then another month or two for it to show up in exploit kits (used by bad actors). That’s now measured in hours or days.

Q: What does that mean for large companies?

A: Most businesses essentially ran a zero-risk tolerance for breaking things, so they would test the hell out of a patch before they put it into production. Now they don’t have that time.

If the risk of breaking something by putting this patch into place is one percent, but the risk of being attacked could cost me 50 million dollars…now I’ve got an interesting trade-off.

Q: Are advanced AI tools reliable at finding real flaws?

A: There’s a lot of noise. The PHP one is a prime example of a real one, but there’s an awful lot out there that are either not real or are on software that’s never exposed to the internet. We’ve got to improve our triage system.

Q: Where does this lead us in two or three years?

A: We’re going to turn these AI tools on software that hasn’t been deployed yet, so one would hope we start to deploy software that has fewer vulnerabilities to begin with. You burn out all the old stuff, and it makes way for new growth that’s more secure from the beginning.

It’s not like this solves our cybersecurity problem, but it does change the nature of it going forward.

World.title: Fed expected to hold rates steady days ahead of US midterms
World.content:
Washington – The US Federal Reserve appears set to hold interest rates steady at its meeting next week, analysts say, despite stubbornly high inflation and with markets pricing in at least one rate hike before year-end.

The central bank’s Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will meet over two days, announcing its decision at 2:00 pm local time (18:00 GMT) on Wednesday.

The Fed has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, and at its last meeting in September the FOMC voted to raise the key federal funds rate for the first time in three years, lifting the target range to 3.75 percent to 4.0 percent.

The Fed’s meeting comes days ahead of key midterm elections in the United States on November 3, with the Democratic Party seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from US President Donald Trump’s Republicans.

Trump frequently berated and criticized Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s predecessor Jerome Powell over interest rates — which he deems to be too high — but has so far refrained from targeting the man he appointed to replace him over the issue.

The Fed’s preferred gauge for inflation, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, hit a pandemic-era peak of 7.2 percent in 2022, before a series of interest-rate hikes tamed it to around 2.2 percent by late 2024.

Trump’s economic policies — including his upending of the global trade order using tariffs and his war on Iran — fuelled it once more, and it hit a three-year high of 3.9 percent in May.

Since the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February, global energy prices have skyrocketed, with Tehran’s retaliatory actions sharply curtailing oil and gas supplies through the Gulf.

Higher energy prices have begun to cascade through into other goods and services, fuelling inflation in the United States, with prices a key issue for voters as they head to the polls.

– ‘Based on the economics’ –

Loretta Mester, former regional head of the Cleveland Fed, told AFP that the timing of the meeting just days ahead of the election would not be a factor for policymakers.

“The Fed doesn’t take into account any kind of political issues in that FOMC room,” she said. “It really is based on the economics.”

Mester argued that the fundamentals call for continuing to raise interest rates.

“The data that’s come in continue to show a stable labor market and continue to show inflation above target,” she said, adding that there was no evidence that it was on a path downwards towards the target.

“The economics would suggest then you need to continue raising rates.”

Still, she thought that most policymakers seemed keen to avoid moving too quickly, and may hold rates at this meeting, waiting to tighten the screws until the following meeting in early December.

Wendy Edelberg, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, believes central bankers would rather not put themselves in the middle of the political debate ahead of the midterms.

“It’s unhelpful for everyone if the Fed gets wrapped up in all the political discourse right before an election,” she told AFP.

Edelberg said that “there wouldn’t be huge economic implications” if policymakers raised rates in December as opposed to October.

She saw such a decision less as a “nod to Trump” — who has aggressively demanded lower rates to spur economic activity — and more a way to avoid being the potential target of political barbs.

Since returning to power last year, the US president has waged an unprecedented assault on the Fed’s independence, launching a criminal probe against Powell and attempting to unseat Fed Governor Lisa Cook.

The probe against Powell was dropped to smooth the way for Warsh’s Senate confirmation, but the battle to fire Cook continues despite a Supreme Court decision nullifying an earlier attempt to do so.

Last week, Cook declined to attend a hearing in the White House’s probe into mortgage fraud allegations, which she denies.

World.title: Obama blasts Trump’s ‘chaos and cruelty’ while campaigning for Democrats
World.content:
Washington – Former US president Barack Obama delivered scathing criticisms of his successor, Donald Trump, at rallies Saturday in Ohio and Michigan to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

Democrats are attempting to wrest back control of one or both chambers of the US Congress, which are currently controlled by Trump’s Republican party.

The former president retains considerable popularity among the Democratic base, which he is keen to leverage to support his Democratic Party’s candidates.

In both states, the 65-year-old former president blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern amid soaring fuel prices.

“The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” Obama said in Ohio, where he rallied in support of former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown.

“Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for.”

“After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough,'” Obama declared in Cleveland. “We are voting for change right here in Ohio.”

Later, in Michigan, Obama campaigned for Abdul El-Sayed, from the party’s left wing, who is in a close race with Republican Mike Rogers for the US Senate.

“Imagine the power duo of Abdul and Elissa,” Obama said, referring to the incumbent Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin, who is not up for election this year.

“You got a Muslim man, you got a Jewish woman fighting for you in the United States Senate. That’s something, Michigan, you can be proud of.”

Obama also urged voters to cast their ballots as soon as possible since early voting is already open in both states.

“Don’t procrastinate, don’t equivocate,” Obama said.

In Ohio, Brown will attempt a comeback against incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while the race for governor will be contested between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate in 2024.

Polls for Ohio give Democrats a slight lead in both those races, but the results are expected to be close.

Obama also took digs at Trump’s renovation projects across the US capital, including his botched renovation of the National Mall’s Reflecting Pool, his construction of a massive White House Ballroom and the guilded decorations he has adorned the Oval Office with during his second tenure.

“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said, referring to popular but indulgent American restaurant chain.

Nationally, polls also suggest that Democrats could regain control of the House of Representatives but face a much more competitive contest for the Senate.

World.title: Antonelli storms to US Grand Prix pole on weekend he can take title
World.content:
Austin – Runaway world championship leader Kimi Antonelli showed no nerves as he stormed to pole position with a perfectly-measured fastest lap in qualifying on Saturday for the United States Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old Italian will wrap up the drivers’ championship if he wins in Austin on Sunday, his Mercedes teammate George Russell finishes outside the top eight and Lewis Hamilton finishes outside the top four.

Antonelli secured his seventh pole of the season and his first in eight races with a fastest lap in 1min 34.035sec to outpace Max Verstappen, his nearest challenger, by 0.179sec with Verstappen’s Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar a career-best third.

Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc was fourth ahead of Russell, in the second Mercedes, and seven-time champion Hamilton in the second Ferrari.

Antonelli leads Russell by 102 points in the championship and is aiming to become Formula One’s youngest champion and Italy’s first since Alberto Ascari of Ferrari in 1953.

“We got pole so we’ll try to win tomorrow,” said Antonelli. “Max has been very quick and did an incredible job in qualifying so it’s not going to be easy.

“Hopefully, we’ll be leading into Turn One and we’ll try to set the pace — even though it’s going to be very tight.

“I’m very happy with qualifying, but Q3 was very tough with the wind, gusty and unpredictable, but I’m happy to stick it on pole.”

Verstappen, who won this race from pole last year and will go in search of his fifth victory in Austin, said: “Q3 was not good. Q1, Q2 it was nice, but for whatever reason with both sets of tyres, I just didn’t have the balance. No mistakes, but just no grip.”

McLaren duo Oscar Piastri and reigning world champion Lando Norris qualified seventh and eighth ahead of Racing Bulls’ rookie Arvid Lindblad, who has a five-place grid penalty, and Liam Lawson.

The session took place in hot and cloudy conditions, the two Cadillacs leading out ahead of fellow Americans Haas before Leclerc clocked a marker time of 1min 35.200sec to set the pace ahead of Verstappen.

After seeing 207 laps deleted on Friday and 42 in final practice, all the drivers knew how important it was to avoid exceeding track limits in the qualifying hour – a problem that left Alpine’s Pierre Gasly requiring a late lap, with seconds to spare, to survive the first qualifying session after losing his earlier time.

The top ten shootout began with Antonelli quickest on the opening runs ahead of the two Red Bulls and Leclerc back in fourth, Ferrari seemingly unable to find the progressive speed needed to stay on the pace of Mercedes and their young tyro.

As so often this year, the precocious Italian found the speed he needed as he prepared for his final run and delivered pole with his now customary elan.

World.title: Bolsonaro leads Lula in final Brazil election polls
World.content:
Sao Paulo – Two separate polls published on Saturday gave Flavio Bolsonaro a two-point lead over President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on the eve of Brazilian elections.

Bolsonaro, the son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro, is the narrow favorite to win Sunday’s runoff after nabbing 47 percent of the vote over Lula’s 45 percent in the first round.

Saturday’s polls published by the Datafolha institute and Quaest give Bolsonaro 51 percent of voting intentions, while Lula has 49 percent.

Both polls show a difference between the candidates that falls within the margin of error, locking them in a statistical tie.

No first-round loser in the history of Brazilian democracy has bounced back to win the runoff, but Lula’s campaign has regained momentum with massive protests and an intense digital campaign since the shock result.

The pair took part in a final televised debate on Friday, during which they mostly focused on policy proposals after a first debate that quickly deteriorated into a barrage of insults.

The Datafolha poll was conducted between Thursday and Friday and does not specify whether interviews were carried out after the program.

The Quaest poll was conducted between Friday and Saturday, when both campaigns staged massive rallies in a last bid to sway voters.

Most polls did not foresee Bolsonaro’s first-round victory, instead projecting a narrow Lula win.

World.title: Apologetic Alvarez fires Atletico to win against Deportivo
World.content:
Madrid – Julian Alvarez continued on his road to redemption by scoring as Atletico Madrid beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0 on Saturday, closing the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona to two points, and apologising to the club’s supporters for trying to leave this summer.

Diego Simeone’s side are second, with champions Barca hosting Real Madrid, third, in the Clasico at Camp Nou on Sunday.

Alvarez netted for the second consecutive game, having grabbed his first of the season in Atletico’s 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart in midweek.

Atletico supporters hounded Alvarez during his first appearances this season after he tried to force his way out of the club in the summer, but the tension has gradually cooled.

After the game Alvarez apologised to the fans and said it was a “mistake” on his part.

“I understand people’s anger, I would have been angry too,” Alvarez told Movistar.

Simeone was pleased that the Argentina international had apologised.

“It’s not easy to say sorry, I’m very happy for him, he will feel very at peace,” said the coach.

“We need him. If the club wants to reach where the fans dream, we need a very good Julian Alvarez.”

Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak believes Alvarez will earn the love of supporters again, over the weeks ahead.

“I’m happy for him, he’s giving the best of himself, a lot of effort, and I’m sure bit by bit he’ll win over the fans again,” Oblak told Movistar.

“He’s a great player, he’s shown it already and he’s on the road to showing it again — we need him in the best form possible.”

Home fans at the Metropolitano stadium directed a few whistles at the team in general after a slow start, with Deportivo having the best chance of the first half.

Oblak saved well from Lorenzo Amatucci, while at the other end Simeone’s side lacked spark.

Early in the second half Alvarez found the breakthrough.

Alejandro Grimaldo fired in a dangerous low pass towards the far post, where the Argentina international turned it over the line.

Alvarez came close to a second after a slick team move, with Alex Baena slipping him in, but Depor goalkeeper Leo Roman saved the striker’s attempted lob with his face.

The former Manchester City striker looked much closer to his best form in this outing after struggling with some fitness problems earlier in the campaign.

After apologising to Atletico’s fans for trying to depart this summer, Alvarez said he was slowly improving.

“I’m starting to feel good… I’m grateful to all my teammates because they’ve supported me. They’ve really stuck by me throughout this whole time,” said Alvarez.

“I’m working to improve. I’ve felt better in these last few matches.”

Deportivo forward Kevin Sanchez spurned two fine chances in stoppage time.

“In the first half we played quite badly, in the second better but then we dipped at the end again,” added Oblak. “We had a bit of luck.”

– Mikautadze strikes late –

Earlier, Georges Mikautadze snatched a late 2-1 win for Villarreal in a derby clash against Valencia, who had midfielder Harvey Elliott sent off as both sides finished with 10 men.

The Yellow Submarine came from behind to triumph, climbing into mid-table and leaving Javier Aguirre’s Los Che 19th, in the relegation zone.

Pepelu sent Valencia ahead from the penalty spot in the first half before American defender Alex Freeman headed the visitors level at Mestalla stadium after 69 minutes.

Inigo Perez’s Villarreal had Pape Gueye sent off when the Senegal international hit Jose Gaya in the face with his elbow.

However, English midfielder Elliott, on loan from Liverpool, was soon dismissed for two quick yellow cards for apparent dissent.

Villarreal striker Mikautadze broke through in stoppage time, racing through and finishing with aplomb to claim the three points.

World.title: Watch: IAF’s Tejas steals the show at ‘Wings over Ganges’ aerial display in Varanasi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and defence minister Rajnath Singh witnessed the Indian Air Forceâs aerial display at the âWings over Gangesâ event in Varanasi on October 25, as the city hosted the 94th Indian Air Force Day celebrations.

The display featured the IAFâs LCA Tejas, Sukhoi-30MKI,

and Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, alongside the Sarang Helicopter Display Team. Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Army also participated, showcasing coordination among the three services.

Uttar Pradesh governor Anandiben Patel and Chief minister Yogi Adityanath were also present at the event.

The event came amid the IAFâs emphasis on jointness and integration as the armed forces prepare for future multi-domain conflicts.

IAF chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh has said the three services would need to operate more closely and that theatreisation should focus on employing air power effectively within an integrated structure.

âWe are not viewing theaterisation as an exercise to permanently divide fighter assets geographically,â Singh told news agency PTI. He said future conflicts would be multi-domain by nature and require closer coordination among the three services.

World.title: ‘Give priority to local artisans’: PM Modi’s festive shopping appeal as Diwali approaches
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Sunday urged people to prioritise products made by local artisans while shopping for festivals, saying their purchases would strengthen the âVocal for Localâ campaign and help realise the vision of a self-reliant India.

Addressing the 139th edition of his monthly radio programme

, PM Modi said the campaign was helping Indian products reach international markets, citing the export of makhana from Bihar to Greece and arhar dal from Karnataka to the Maldives.

The prime minister noted that people typically purchase gifts and other items for their families and loved ones during festivals, and called on them to support local artisans through their shopping choices.

âThis time too, while shopping, please give priority to products made by local artisans. Your purchases will boost their enthusiasm,â he said.

PM Modi said greater participation in the âVocal for Localâ campaign would accelerate the progress towards a self-reliant India.

âTherefore, I personally urge you to give priority and prominence to products crafted by local artisans,â he added.

PM Modi stresses packaging, highlights traditional skills

The prime minister also emphasised the importance of packaging in attracting consumers and helping products find a place in the market.





âOften, when we see something in the market, good packaging makes us pick it up, and we want to learn more about the product. Understanding this, greater emphasis is now being laid on packaging,â he said.

During the broadcast, PM Modi also highlighted efforts to revive traditional skills and farming practices, including an initiative to promote natural cotton cultivation in Punjabâs Malwa region.

He said the organisation Kheti Virasat Mission had been working to revive organic farming and had launched an initiative called âNav-Trinjanâ to encourage natural cotton farming.

The initiative also started a weaving school a few years ago to pass the traditional skill on to younger generations.

âYou can imagine how great a help this is for the environment. Friends, a few years ago, 'Nav-Trinjan' also started a weaving school with the goal of passing on the skill of weaving to the new generation,â PM Modi said.

Heval river rejuvenation , e-Sanjeevani consultations highlighted

PM Modi also spoke about efforts by residents and the local administration in Uttarakhandâs Tehri Garhwal district to revive the Heval river.

He said the riverâs water level had begun to fall some time ago, while natural water sources in the surrounding areas were drying up. In response, villagers and the administration launched conservation efforts that included rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and large-scale tree planting.

âToday, these efforts have given the Heval river a new lease of life while also helping rejuvenate dozens of natural water sources,â the prime minister said.

He also highlighted the use of technology in healthcare through the e-Sanjeevani telemedicine service, which enables people to access medical consultations remotely.

âIt brings me immense satisfaction to share that nearly 50 crore tele-consultations have been conducted through it so far. This is a massive figure and a prime example of the power of technology, the service-mindedness of our doctors, and the trust of our citizens,â he said.

PM Modi added that the serviceâs extensive network enabled it to reach even the most remote parts of the country, with beneficiariesâ experiences offering examples of its reach.

PM calls 12-year journey of Mann Ki Baat a âpilgrimageâ

The Sunday broadcast also marked 12 years of Mann Ki Baat. PM Modi described the programmeâs journey as a âpilgrimageâ, saying it had allowed him to learn about citizensâ efforts and acknowledge their contributions.

âSince then, our journey has been continuing without interruption.

You are both fellow travellers and guides on this journey,â he said, recalling that the programme began on Vijayadashami 12 years ago.

The prime minister said the broadcast had given him an opportunity to highlight the hard work, courage, dedication and spirit of service shown by ordinary people across the country.

World.title: 'Don't be spectator, show leadership': EAM Jaishankar to UN on terrorism, global crises
World.content:
NEW DELHI: External affairs minister

on Sunday urged the United Nations to take a stronger leadership role in tackling global crises, saying it must not remain a spectator to conflicts and other challenges facing the world.

Speaking at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan on the occasion of UN Day, Jaishankar called for reforms in multilateral institutions, arguing that large parts of the world could not be excluded from decision-making.

âThe UN must show leadership, not be a spectator to global crises,â he said, adding that the case for reformed multilateralism was growing stronger by the day.

Jaishankar also described

as a major threat to global peace, rejecting its use as an instrument of statecraft.

âIts usage as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable. It can never be justified, it can never be rationalized,â he said, calling for stronger international resolve to counter terrorism in all its forms.

The minister said some countries continued to allow political calculations to take precedence over the fight against terrorism, despite the lessons of history.

Global South faces '4F crisis'

Jaishankar highlighted the challenges confronting developing countries, describing the Global South as facing a â4F crisisâ involving finance, fuel, food and fertiliser.





He said developed countries also had a stake in finding solutions and called for urgent steps to reduce risks in the international economy and provide nations with more diversified options.

âMarket distortions through constriction and choke points only add to suffering. A genuine dialogue in this regard is overdue,â he said.

World.title: Centre rushes 250 RAF personnel to Arunachal after violent protests over hydropower project
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has sent two companies of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to Arunachal Pradesh following violence in Pasighat during protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, officials said on Sunday.

The ministry of home affairs (MHA) directed on Saturday that the two companies, comprising around 250 personnel, be airlifted from Navi Mumbai aboard an Indian Air Force transport aircraft. The units are expected to reach Pasighat and be deployed by Sunday, officials told news agency PTI.

The RAF is a specialised anti-riot unit of the CRPF whose personnel wear blue uniforms.

Several CRPF units are already deployed in the violence-hit areas.

Arunachal Pradesh also has a permanent deployment of around two to three CRPF battalions.

Officials said CRPF personnel had effectively handled the protests since Friday and prevented the violence from escalating. Several police and central forces personnel were injured during the clashes, they added.

On Friday night, a mob torched an NHPC office and a police station and vandalised the residences of three political leaders, including the state BJP president, in East Siang district, according to Arunachal Pradesh Police officials.





Arunachal chief minister Pema Khandu said the right to peaceful protest was an essential part of democracy, but stressed that demonstrations must remain within the bounds of the law and should not lead to property damage or disruption of public order.

Describing the incidents in Pasighat as regrettable, Khandu appealed to all sections of society to maintain peace.

According to a statement issued by the chief minister's Office (CMO), a 12-hour bandh in Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts over the proposed power project remained largely peaceful on Friday.

However, violence broke out in Pasighat after the bandh ended and continued until 3.30 am on Saturday.

Protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) turned violent in Pasighat, East Siang district, on Friday night, with "Gen Z" protesters allegedly setting fire to the NHPC office and a police station and vandalising and looting the residences of two MLAs and the state BJP president, police said.

The violence continued in waves for nearly nine hours into Saturday morning, leaving "over 40 police personnel injured in stone-pelting", police said. A protester was hit in the leg by a tear gas shell and admitted to hospital.

Following the violence, the East Siang district administration imposed restrictions on public gatherings and processions in Pasighat, Mebo and Ruksin, citing fears of vandalism, arson and a possible breach of law and order amid protests and bandh-related activities.

Indiaâs proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, planned across three districts of Arunachal, is being pitched as a strategic counter to Chinaâs mega dam upstream. But the plan has faced resistance from indigenous tribes, who fear the reservoir could submerge villages and sever their deep-rooted ties with the river.

Known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, the Siang enters Arunachal Pradesh near Gelling and flows for 294km before meeting the Dibang and Lohit rivers at Sadiya in Assam to form the Brahmaputra.

World.title: 'Not less than a pilgrimage’: PM Modi marks 12 years of Mann Ki Baat - top quotes

Drawing a parallel with India's longstanding tradition of pilgrimages, PM Modi said the programme had given him an opportunity to understand people's efforts closely and pay tribute to their contributions.

âOur country has had a tradition of pilgrimages for centuries. For me, âMann Ki Baatâ is not less than a pilgrimage, a journey to closely understand the efforts of people of the country and to pay tribute to their contributions,â he said.

With Diwali and Chhath approaching, the Prime Minister urged people to maintain cleanliness in their surroundings and at places where they live.

âThe sacred festivals of Diwali and Chhath are just a few days away. Cleanliness campaigns are being run from place to place. It's important that we keep those places clean where we live,â PM Modi said.

World.title: ‘Foreign-funded conspiracy to destabilise India’: Telangana BJP chief targets Congress over Jamia graffiti
World.content:
Rao claimed that the opposition was encouraging students to act against national interests

Jamia protests trigger political row

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao on Sunday accused the Congress and the INDIA alliance of encouraging anti-national activities, alleging that the controversy over graffiti at Delhiâs Jamia Millia Islamia was part of a broader conspiracy to destabilise the country.Speaking to ANI, Rao claimed that radical networks within student groups were being supported by opposition political parties. He also alleged that the campus demonstrations were part of a foreign-sponsored effort to create unrest in India, though he did not provide evidence to substantiate the claim.âWriting on the walls of Jamia Millia University in Delhi, all these things are now being exposed because there are people who are part of the âTukde-Tukdeâ gang and anti-national gangs who are among the students, and they are in support of Sharjeel Imam, who has actually been involved in several anti-national activities,â Rao said.Targeting the Congress and other INDIA alliance parties over their alleged silence on the controversy, Rao claimed that the opposition was encouraging students to act against national interests.âThis slogan shows that the Congress and the INDIA alliance, which are silent on this issue, show how they are inciting students and everyone in the country to go against the interests of the nation and indulge in anti-national activities,â he said.Rao further alleged that the protests were designed to create anarchy and were being sponsored by a foreign country to destabilise India.The BJP leaderâs remarks come amid heightened tensions at Jamia Millia Islamia, where university authorities recently shifted classes to an online format, citing student safety amid ongoing campus demonstrations.The controversy has also drawn Congress leaders into the dispute. Congress MP Imran Masood, who visited the university to meet protesting students on Friday, denied that slogans calling for a âfree Kashmirâ had been raised during the demonstrations. Delhi Police detained Masood during his visit.âNo slogans calling for a âfree Kashmirâ were raised there, not a single one. I stood up in front of everyone and strongly condemned such slogans, stating that Kashmir is an integral part of India,â Masood told ANI.Since Oct 12, students have been on a sit-in and hunger strike, which has grown into Jamia's biggest student protest since the anti-CAA agitation. Jamia has not had an elected union since 2006, when it was dissolved following violence. It is one of Delhi's few central universities without an elected union.

World.title: Iran says resumption of war would not change its stances
World.content:
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday (October 25, 2026) that a potential resumption of war with Israel and the United States would not change his country's positions.

The remarks come amid mounting U.S and Israeli threats of renewed attacks on Iran, as President Donald Trump said on Friday (October 23, 2026) that Washington "may do another little Epic Fury," referring to the U.S-Israeli campaign on Iran that began on February 28.

"Recently, there has been talk of a new war, but I am already thinking about the post-war period. Whether there is war or not, our policies remain the same," said Mr. Araghchi during a televised event in Tehran.

"They have already done so twice and have seen the results. If they want to try again, they know they will achieve no different outcome from those of the past," he added.

An April 8 ceasefire between Iran and the United States put an end to the most intense fighting, apart from sporadic exchanges of fire in and around the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global energy supplies.

These military flare-ups have lulled in recent weeks.

Iran has claimed control over Strait of Hormuz since the outbreak of the war and has regularly targeted vessels that attempt crossing without its authorisation, moves strongly opposed by Washington and countries in the region.

In response, the U.S has been maintaining a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.

In June, Iran agreed with the United States to a memorandum of understanding laying out a pathway to a permanent settlement of the conflict, only for the deal to later unravel as each side accused the other of violating it.

Tehran has since called for a return to the accord to end the conflict.

"The current war has changed everything. We must accept that new realities are taking hold. Shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz will no longer be the same, and the management of the strait will no longer be the same," said Mr. Araghchi.

"To achieve peace and stability, our region must move towards the complete absence of foreign forces," he added.

World.title: ECI hiding information on ECINET software as it will reveal manipulation: Congress
World.content:
The Congress on Sunday (October 25, 2026) accused the Election Commission of India of hiding information about the controversial ECINET software and claimed that the poll body is repeatedly refusing to provide this because it will reveal the reality of the "massive, centralised manipulation" that has taken place in the "disastrous" SIR.

The opposition party also reiterated the demand that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar must go as well as the SIR be suspended forthwith.

Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh shared a media report which claimed that the Election Commission of India (ECI) has declined to disclose the name and version of the software it used to identify errors and anomalies in voter rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, stating that the information relates to "commercial confidence, trade secrets and intellectual property" and is exempt under the Right to Information (RTI) Act.

In his post on X, Mr. Ramesh said the Election Commission of India continues to "hide" information about the controversial ECINET software at the "heart of the disastrous SIR, that has been used to centralise manipulation of the electoral rolls".

"Today, a leading national daily revealed that the ECI has refused to provide information on the software being used in the SIR in its response to a Right to Information (RTI) application. Using flimsy excuses, the ECI has refused to name the software being used in the SIR, or confirm whether AI is being used and what safeguards are in place," Mr. Ramesh said.

The lack of transparency around the ECINET software and the use of AI has damaged the credibility of the entire process among citizens, he said.

The ECI is repeatedly refusing to provide this information because it will reveal the reality of the massive, centralised manipulation that has taken place, Mr. Ramesh said.

Why did Indians find out from disclosures of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) that they developed the ECINET software and why has this not been transparently disclosed by the ECI, he asked.

Why has the ECI repeatedly denied the use of AI in the SIR and electoral roll revision, when it is clearly being used, Mr. Ramesh questioned.

The ECINET software and the IT Division of the ECI were the focus of several objections raised by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, he pointed out.

The complaints even reached the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), which comes under the Prime Minister himself, he said.

"The public knows that massive manipulation has taken place. Gyanesh Kumar must go. The SIR must be suspended forthwith," Mr. Ramesh said.

Mr. Ramesh's remarks come amid a raging row after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Mr. Sandhu and Mr. Joshi objected on record at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders mostly related to the process of the SIR of electoral rolls.

The EC has said that differing views and observations are a part of deliberations in any institution and all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.

World.title: Delhi High Court upholds policy to give cash to EWS students for school uniforms
World.content:
The Delhi High Court has refused to interfere with the Delhi government’s decision to provide cash to students admitted under the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and disadvantaged groups categories in private schools to buy their uniforms.

A bench of Justices Subramonium Prasad and Renu Bhatnagar dismissed a review petition filed by NGO Justice For All, seeking reconsideration of the court’s January 23 judgment upholding the policy.

The petitioner argued that the Delhi government should provide uniforms to students belonging to EWS and disadvantaged groups in aided and unaided private schools, rather than cash, under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act.

The Delhi government had earlier submitted that its Cabinet considered the procurement and distribution of uniforms unfeasible due to operational constraints. It subsequently introduced a policy in June 2025 to provide students with a suitable amount of money to purchase uniforms.

In an order dated October 12, the bench said the grounds raised in the review petition amounted to an attempt to reargue the case in its entirety. It observed that a policy decision could not be interfered with unless it was so arbitrary, whimsical or capricious that it shocked the conscience of the court.

Also Read : Parents can reach me in case of EWS quota violation: Sood

“The decision of the government that it shall provide cash to the students instead of providing uniforms because of the difficulties faced by the government cannot be said to be completely arbitrary, whimsical or capricious,” the court said.

It added that the material submitted by the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD), including the policy dated June 10, 2025, and the note for the Council of Ministers, had been considered before the court concluded that the policy did not violate the statute.

On January 23, the high court had upheld the government’s decision to provide cash directly to eligible students for purchasing uniforms, observing that processing individual orders for each student’s uniform would pose genuine difficulties for the authorities.

It had held that providing a uniform subsidy through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) was not contrary to the Right to Education Act or its rules and would help ensure that students received their uniforms on time.

“Undoubtedly, it would be impossible to carry out the exercise of taking measurements of every student, placing orders for different kinds of uniform cloth on the GeM portal, after procurement of the material getting the uniforms stitched as per the measurements and finally distributing the uniforms in schools before the commencement of a new session,” the court had said.

World.title: PM Modi witnesses IAF air show in Varanasi
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (October 25, 2026) attended the Indian Air Force’s air show 'Wings over Ganges' at Namo Ghat in Varanasi and witnessed a display of aerial manoeuvres by the IAF's premier display teams.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Uttar Pradesh Governor Anandiben Patel and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accompanied Mr. Modi on the final day of the three-day air show held to commemorate the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force.

According to Air Force officials, the show features fighter aircraft, including the Sukhoi-30 MKI, indigenous Tejas and LCH Prachand, along with helicopter displays.

Three Kiran aircraft flew in a 'V' formation, creating a spectacle in the colours of the national flag, while Mi-17 helicopters carrying the tricolour participated in the Omkar formation.

The Surya Kiran aerobatic team showcased precision flying and coordinated manoeuvres, while the Sarang helicopter display team enthralled spectators with its aerial stunts.

Mr. Modi's presence at the event generated considerable enthusiasm among residents, with large numbers of people gathering along the route from the police lines to Namo Ghat to welcome the Prime Minister.

BJP workers and local residents greeted Mr. Modi with rose petals, traditional musical performances and cultural programmes at designated points along the route.

These points, many of them with tents, were erected at the Police Lines main gate, Police Lines crossing, Yes Bank on Khajuri-Maqbool Alam Road, Hukulganj Tirumuhani, Chowkaghat wood market, City Railway Station, Gol Gadda crossing, the railway underpass and the CNG station near Namo Ghat.

People raised slogans of "Har Har Mahadev" and "Jai Shri Ram" as the Prime Minister stood on the footboard of his vehicle to acknowledge the crowds.

Spectators expressed pride at witnessing the air show in the Prime Minister's presence.

Divakar Singh, who attended the event, said it was a matter of great pride for Varanasi.

"It is a memorable experience to watch the Indian Air Force's air show at Namo Ghat in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The spirituality of Kashi, combined with the might of fighter aircraft in the sky, fills us with pride," he said.

He added that the event would inspire children and young people to develop respect for the country and a spirit of national service.

Another spectator, Govind Pandey, said it was the first time he had witnessed an air show of this scale.

He said watching the event alongside Mr. Modi, who represents Varanasi in Parliament, had made the experience particularly memorable. Such displays could inspire young people to join the Indian Air Force, he added.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Modi inaugurated a new garment manufacturing unit of Arvind Ltd in the Mirzamurad area of Varanasi.

Officials said the facility aims to promote industrial development in the region and strengthen India's textile and garment manufacturing sector. During the visit, the Prime Minister also interacted with around 300 women.

Officials said the new unit is expected to generate employment opportunities, particularly for women, and accelerate local economic activity.

The initiative is also expected to connect garments manufactured in Varanasi with international customers through access to global markets.

Mr. Modi arrived at Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport in Varanasi on Sunday (October 25, 2026) morning and travelled by helicopter to Mirzamurad for the inauguration. He subsequently flew to the Police Lines before proceeding by road to Namo Ghat.

World.title: Cyclone over Bay of Bengal to bring heavy rain across South India, Odisha, West Bengal; red alerts issued in multiple States | LIVE
World.content:
A severe cyclonic storm brewing over the Bay of Bengal is set to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 with winds of 115-125 kmph, triggering red alerts in Kerala, Odisha and heavy-rain warnings in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu.

Odisha has mobilised NDRF and ODRAF teams and ordered school closures in five districts, while Kerala has shut institutions in three red-alert districts amid continuing waterlogging. Last year’s Montha was classified as a ‘severe cyclonic storm’.

The Odisha Government on Saturday (October 24, 2026) activated its disaster response and mitigation machinery. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi reviewed the State’s preparedness and directed officials to prioritise public safety, evacuation and emergency response, stressing a zero-casualty objective.

World.title: At least 22 killed in Kenya bus crash near site of previous fatal accident
World.content:
A bus collided with a truck on Kenya's main highway on Sunday (October 25, 2026), killing at least 22 people, police said.

The crash came three weeks after 17 people died in another accident along the same highway linking the capital, Nairobi, with the coastal city of Mombasa.

Several others were injured in the Sunday morning crash and were receiving treatment, police said. The passengers were reportedly returning from a funeral when the accident occurred.

Makueni County Commissioner Abdullahi Khalif said that the death toll could rise.

The circumstances surrounding the crash remain unclear. Speeding and poor road conditions have previously been cited as contributing factors in road accidents in Kenya.

Kenya's National Transport and Safety Authority said the stretch of the highway where the crash occurred is a designated “accident black spot” and that recommendations had been made to address safety concerns.

World.title: Bangladesh seeks details from Saudi Arabia on execution of two citizens: report
World.content:
Bangladesh has sought detailed information from Saudi Arabia about the execution of two of its citizens in the Makkah region, including the charges against them, court verdicts, manner of execution, whereabouts of their bodies and whether they had legal representation during their trials, according to a local media report.

The Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah sent a diplomatic letter to the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs' branch in Makkah on October 19, seeking answers to six questions, according to a report by Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo published on Saturday (October 24, 2026).

Bangladesh's Consul General in Jeddah also raised the matter with a senior Saudi foreign ministry official during a meeting the same day, the report said.

The two Bangladesh nationals, a man and a woman, were executed on October 14, after being convicted of committing an “indecent act” inside a mosque in Makkah.

The diplomatic letter seeks details of the offences, when and where they allegedly took place, the dates of arrest and certified copies of the court verdicts, the report said.

It also asks whether the death sentences were carried out by beheading or another method, where the bodies are being kept and whether they will be repatriated to Bangladesh or have already been buried in Saudi Arabia.

Bangladesh has also sought information on whether lawyers represented the two during the investigation and trial and whether they had requested legal assistance, the report said.

According to Prothom Alo, Bangladeshi officials said the country's missions did not have detailed information about the proceedings leading to the executions, including whether the two had legal representation.

A list of Bangladeshi prisoners shared by Saudi authorities in September reportedly contained allegations of adultery and an information technology-related offence involving the two, but did not specify their sentences.

Dhaka is seeking clarification on the discrepancy between those entries and the Saudi Interior Ministry's public explanation of the executions.

Bangladesh had also raised the executions with the Saudi ambassador in Dhaka, according to the Dhaka Tribune.

Bangladeshi officials said the government had not received detailed official information from Saudi authorities before learning that the executions had been carried out, the newspaper reported last week.

Bangladesh has also sought information about 20 other citizens whose names appeared on the Saudi prisoner list as convicted but whose sentences were not specified, according to The Daily Star.

Saudi authorities had yet to respond to the consulate's latest diplomatic communication, Prothom Alo reported, citing Bangladeshi officials.

World.title: When safety slips through a gaping hole in Chennai’s MRTS stations
World.content:
When the Mass Rapid Transit System (MRTS) was proposed in the 1970s for Chennai, it was envisioned as the first mass public transport corridor to run on an elevated section in the country, years before the Metro Rail was even an idea in India. In anticipation of good patronage, humongous railway stations were built in one go, along with various passenger amenities such as escalators, lifts, and toilets.

Built in phases, the full MRTS service from Beach to Velachery was launched in November 2007. It was extended to St. Thomas Mount this year. The MRTS project, including the extension, had suffered delays of several decades.

Futuristic model

Envisioned as a futuristic model of mass public transport for easy and fast movement, the MRTS now stands as an example of poor maintenance, with passengers left with inadequate operational, civic, and security amenities. Particularly, on the security front, the MRTS has earned a bad reputation among women commuters after incidents of sexual assault and theft at a few stations, including Perungudi, Taramani, Thiruvanmiyur, and Indra Nagar.

The latest incident is the death of a 55-year-old woman at the Thirumayilai station. The woman, Vijaya, a resident of Pallikaranai, had travelled on an MRTS train along with her daughter and got down at Thirumayilai on October 8. Wanting to answer nature’s call and finding the toilet shut, the woman tried to relieve herself by entering one of the many abandoned rooms on the platform. The room being pitch dark, she fell to her death through a huge gap on the floor. Her body was found only after four days; that too, because of the foul smell that drew the attention of officers of the Railway Protection Force (RPF) station housed on the ground floor.

Sprawling facilities

Having built sprawling railway stations in the MRTS section, Southern Railway realised that it required a large workforce and huge funds to maintain the amenities. So it drew up a security plan in 2013. It decided to close one of the two entrances at 14 elevated stations, including Perungudi, Taramani, Thiruvanmiyur, Indra Nagar, Kasturba Nagar, Kotturpuram, and Chintadripet. It also closed the access ways leading to these entry and exit points on the elevated platforms with grill gates and shut several rooms on the platforms built for commercial units and vendors that remained empty.

Also Read: Issue with ticketing gate poses inconvenience to some Metro Rail commuters

At the Thiruvanmiyur, Indra Nagar, and Kasturba Nagar stations, mezzanine floors, originally apportioned for commercial use, were closed with grill gates. Large, empty stations were soon being used by the homeless, especially at Perungudi, Taramani, Light House, and Thiruvallikeni.

R.K. Prabhu, a resident of Baby Nagar in Velachery, who has been using MRTS services since the full services were launched, complains that anti-social elements take over portions of the Perungudi station at night for consuming alcohol and playing cards. Though officials had shut down a portion of the station with concrete slabs, the wall has been broken open, and that space is still being used for drinking and dumping garbage.

Regular commuters say that except at a few stations, toilets are not usable at all.

The Thiruvanmiyur station is another station that has a haunted feel after sunset. “Several rooms around the station have remained unoccupied for years. Liquor bottles, garbage, and other discarded items can be found here. Many youngsters also use the premises for drinking and smoking,” said workers cleaning the station. Located right next to Chennai’s Information Technology Corridor, the station is being used by a significant number of women commuters.

“Those working in Tidel Park, Ramanujam IT Park, and the IIT Madras Research Park get down here. After 7 p.m., this place looks unsafe. Some of us take the overbridge to the station. A security person should be stationed at this bridge,” suggested S. Ragini, who works at a prominent IT company in Tidel Park. Other commuters from the IT park say there are stray dogs on the bridge at times and even on the station premises. While Southern Railway has posted RPF personnel to man the platforms of each railway station, the security officials face difficulties in patrolling the stations effectively.

Commercial exploration

Right to Information activist Dayanand Krishnan says it is a surprise that the vast spaces could not be commercially exploited by setting up offices, food plazas, and other business establishments. He said Southern Railway should have organised a stakeholder meeting with big commercial establishments before commencing the construction of such buildings. They would be ideal for housing supermarkets.

Mr. Krishnan says the quality of space plays an important role in attracting not only business establishments but also consumers. The MRTS stations are not “inviting places”, he added. Additionally, the poor quality of construction is a deterrent for vendors — roofs leak even after light rain and rainwater stagnates on the platforms and the ground floors.

Former Director-General of Police C. Sylendra Babu says, “Chennai’s massive elevated MRTS stations have become poorly policed spaces, allegedly sheltering petty criminals and drug-users, with incidents of alcohol and drug consumption and sexual harassment reported over the years. The vast, deserted ground-floor areas, multiple entry and exit points, and lack of a dedicated security detail have made these stations vulnerable to anti-social activities.”

‘GRP is understaffed’

He says the Government Railway Police (GRP), which is legally responsible for passenger safety, is understaffed, while the RPF primarily focuses on safeguarding railway property. He called for establishing GRP police stations at major MRTS stations, with the Railways and the State government sharing the cost equally.

Mr. Babu added that the Railways had failed to utilise the enormous spaces commercially for decades, leaving them neglected and vulnerable to misuse. As the MRTS readies itself for merging with the Chennai Metro Rail limited (CMRL) network, administratively, it is important that the issue of space utilisation is sorted out first.

Former Superintendent of Police (GRP) V. Pon Ram also says Chennai’s MRTS network continues to face security challenges owing to inadequate police deployment, poorly lit stations, and vast, underutilised spaces.

Merger with CMRL

With commuters already losing direct train services from Velachery to Avadi, Tiruvallur, Arakkonam, and Gummidipoondi, after the fourth line between Egmore and Beach came into use, calls to hand over the MRTS to the CMRL, without delay, have been renewed. The Railway Board has given the go-ahead for handing over the service to CMRL.

Commuters say safety and security, besides amenities, in the CMRL network are far superior to those available at the MRTS stations. Prasanna Kumar, a frequent commuter on the MRTS system, says, “I hesitate to take an MRTS train late in the evening because I don’t feel safe. It is equally challenging for women passengers. The access pathway to the station itself is not well lit. This is why I’m eagerly anticipating the CMRL’s take-over of the MRTS. The CMRL stations have CCTVs and people don’t have to be anxious about their safety.”

While talk of the take-over has been in the pipeline for nearly 15 years now, the approval from the Railway Board came only this year and the signing of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Tamil Nadu government and Southern Railway is expected to happen within two months. The transition period of the take-over will begin slowly, with the CMRL introducing security and housekeeping services initially. “Improving passenger-related issues and services will be the priority. Meanwhile, upgradation of station structures and systems will follow,” an official said.

Purchasing new trains for this system may take a minimum of two years. In those two years, officials have said, the MRTS will see some significant changes in the maintenance of stations and their surroundings.

Southern Railway holds safety audit

In the week since the accidental death, the Chennai Division of Southern Railway undertook a comprehensive review of building safety plans at all the MRTS stations and took steps to prevent such accidents.

A senior official of the Chennai Division said all shaft openings identified at stations, including Thirumayilai and Perungudi, were closed. Vacant, unused rooms were locked and stickers were pasted, restricting access. Permanent closure of the restricted areas is in progress. Signage for commuters will come up soon. As for station security and passenger assistance, the official said a Station Master and support staff had been deployed at important stations, including Thirumayilai, Chepauk, and Velachery. Commercial staff members are being deployed for ticketing services and for assisting passengers at the stations, the official added.

Additional security personnel have been deployed at the stations and for patrolling trains, the official further said.

(With inputs from R. Sivaraman, Sunitha Sekar, and Sangeetha Kandavel)

World.title: 500,000 Chromebooks to be distributed among students across country over 2 years, announces PM Shehbaz
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced on Sunday that the government would distribute 500,000 Chromebooks to students nationwide over two years.

He said this at the launch of the Prime Minister’s Youth Chromebook Scheme at ceremony in Islamabad.

At the outset of his address, the premier stressed that it was his duty and the state’s “collective responsibility” to provide youth with modern technology.

“Our boys and girls are the true assets of Pakistan,” the prime minister remarked. He added that the Chromebooks were being distributed based on the youth’s hard work and ability.

He hoped students would be able to “attend school remotely [..] and find themselves amongst the most educated people” with the help of the device.

More to follow

World.title: Why are Pakistan wearing a pink jersey today?
World.content:
Pakistan’s second match against England in the ongoing tri-nation series is underway, and while fans will take heart from the spirited fielding effort shown by Pakistan so far, it is not the only thing of note about the fixture.

That is because today, the Green Shirts are wearing pink.

Pakistan has sported pink jerseys today in lieu of the usual green national kit, due to the Pakistan Cricket Board observing Breast Cancer Awareness day.

“The initiative, being organised as part of Pinktober, the global Breast Cancer Awareness Month, aims to highlight the importance of early detection, regular screening and timely treatment while encouraging greater awareness of the disease across the country,” said a PCB media release rearding the topic.

As part of the initiative, not only is the Pakistan team coloured pink, but members of the English cricket team, match officials and commentators are also wearing pink ribbons for the cause, in order “to demonstrate solidarity with breast cancer patients and survivors”.

The initiative also includes the stumps used in the match being branded pink, relevant graphics and branding all across the stadium, as well as a series of digital promotional material by the PCB rolled out before the fixture.

“Cricket provides a powerful platform to connect with millions of people and through this initiative, we aim to translate that reach into meaningful awareness and engagement around breast cancer,” said PCB Director Commercial Ali Adnan Zaidi in the media release, while Chief Operating Officer Sumair Ahmed Syed “recognises the responsibility that comes with the immense following and influence of cricket in our country.”

This is not the first instance of a team sporting a pink jersey for this cause. South Africa hosts a “Pink Day” One-day International every year at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg, where the home team wears pink kits to raise awareness about breast cancer.

The last two of these pink clashes between South Africa and Pakistan have been memorable as well, with Pakistan notching a 36-run win in the 2024 clash, and the 2021 fixture featuring a sublime innings of 193 by Fakhar Zaman that went in vain as the hosts won by 17 runs.

Pakistan hosted a similar pink day last year as well, as part of the T20I series against South Africa.

The Sydney Cricket Ground (SCG) hosts the Pink Test every year as part of the Australian summer, in support of the McGrath Foundation - a cancer care charity founded by Jane McGrath and her husband, Australian pace-bowler Glenn McGrath.

World.title: Terrorist commander killed during IBO in Balochistan's Qila Saifullah: state media
World.content:
Security forces killed a terrorist commander during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Balochistan’s Qila Saifullah, state-run Radio Pakistan reported on Sunday, citing security sources.

The slain terrorist was identified as Adil Shah alias Darvesh in the state broadcaster’s report, which said he belonged to Fitna-al-Khawarij — a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

“Security forces are actively carrying out operations against terrorists in Balochistan under ‘Operation Radd-ul-Fitna-3’. According to security sources, the terrorist commander had been associated with Fitna-al-Khawarij since Dec 2020 and had been managing the financial affairs of the group since 2024,” the report said.

The commander was also involved in facilitating permanent residences for “foreign terrorists” in Balochistan’s Zhob, Sherani, and Shaban, the report quoted the sources as saying. It added that the slain terrorist had been involved in attacks on security forces and kidnapping for ransom since 2022.

Nineteen first information reports were registered against him and a bounty of Rs2.5 million was placed on his head, the report further stated.

Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti said in a post on X that his killing showed the security forces’ “professional expertise and readiness”

The province has witnessed terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time.

On October 19, an army major was martyred, and four terrorists were killed during IBOs in Balochistan.

A day before that, security forces killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during IBOs conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan.
